body: Improves the plate-selection UX for multi-plate `.gcode.3mf` uploads. Two fixes. ## Fix 1 — numeric plate ordering (was 1, 10, 11, …, 2) `findPlateGcodes` sorted `Metadata/plate_N.gcode` with a bare `.sort()` (lexicographic: `plate_10` < `plate_2`). Now sorts NUMERICALLY by the plate integer, so `listPlates` and the palette chips come out `plate_1, plate_2, …, plate_10, …`. (`listPreviewPlates` already sorted numerically — left alone.) ## Fix 2 — show each plate's thumbnail so users can SEE what to select A printable multi-plate export ships a per-plate render (`Metadata/plate_N.png`) for every plate but strips the 3D mesh, so the per-plate PNG is the practical way to identify a plate. **Backend** - `extractPlateThumbnail(threemf, plate)`: returns `Metadata/.png` bytes, falls back to `Metadata/top_.png`, else `null`. Bounded, never throws. - `GET /api/queue/:id/thumbnail?plate=plate_N` → serves that plate's PNG; 404 if absent. ### Thumbnail route contract - **No `plate` query** → unchanged overall-thumbnail behaviour (byte-for-byte). - **`?plate=plate_N`** → `extractPlateThumbnail`; `image/png` 200, or 404 when that plate has no PNG. - The plate is folded into the ETag (`artifactETag(path, "thumb", "plate:")`, like the mesh route) so `plate_1` vs `plate_2` never share a cache validator. `cache-control: no-cache` (revalidate) as before. **Frontend** - `renderConfirmPanel` threads `job.id` into `renderPlateSelect`. Each palette chip is now a small card: the plate's thumbnail (``) above the label + eta. - The `[data-plate-seq]` container carries `data-job-id`; `app.js` `makeSeqRow` builds the same small thumbnail next to each built sequence row (so `B,O,B` is visually readable). - Graceful fallback: a plate with no PNG removes its `` and the label alone remains. Palette stays horizontally scrollable. ## Note (not fixed here) The 3D mesh preview only works for a PROJECT `.3mf`; a sliced `.gcode.3mf` strips `3D/Objects`, so a future g-code toolpath preview is the way to show real geometry for printable files. Not implemented now — this PR is per-plate thumbnails only. ## Gates - `bun run typecheck` ✅ - `bun run test:ci` ✅ (707 pass, 0 fail) - full `bun test` ✅ (707 pass, 0 fail) - e2e selectors (`[data-plate-add]`, `[data-seq-item]`, `[data-seq-list]`, 全追加, 確定) unchanged. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Problema (detectado probando en producción)

La ejecución puntual del job de Argenprop devolvió **0 avisos**, pero el diagnóstico con `debug-fetch` sobre la misma URL **2 minutos después** trajo la página completa (20 avisos parseados perfectamente). Conclusión: Argenprop sirve páginas vacías/bloqueo de forma **intermitente** (probablemente según User-Agent o rate-limiting), no es un problema del parser.

## Fix

En `BaseScraper.search()`: si la **página 1** no parsea ningún aviso, se reintenta una vez tras 2-4 s con **sesión y User-Agent nuevos**. Aplica a todos los portales; las páginas siguientes no reintentan (una página 2 vacía significa fin de resultados).

## Testing

- 35 tests (1 nuevo): página 1 vacía → reconstruye la sesión, reintenta y devuelve los avisos del segundo intento.

author: dckallos
body:
This pull request introduces several improvements to the orchestration layer's engineering standards, testability, and developer guidance. It adds comprehensive documentation for both human and AI contributors, enforces a consistent docstring style, introduces a new GitHub Actions workflow for orchestration tests, and updates the dbt project configuration for local developer workflows.

**Developer and Agent Guidance**

* Added `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` to clearly define contributor roles, non-negotiable standards (especially for AI agents), and the prime directive: all orchestration behavior must be YAML-configured, never hardcoded in Python. These documents also detail the workflow, guardrails, and common pitfalls, with explicit instructions for both human and Claude-based agents. 
* Expanded `CODE_STANDARDS.md` with detailed engineering standards for typing, modularity, error handling, testing, and style (including docstring format), ensuring the orchestration layer remains YAML-driven, typed, and testable.

**Testing and CI/CD**

* Added `.github/workflows/orchestration-tests.yml` to run unit and integration tests for the Dagster orchestration layer in CI. This workflow installs dependencies, runs tests in a clean venv, and ensures no Snowflake credentials are required for offline testing.

**Code Style Enforcement**

* Updated `.pre-commit-config.yaml` to add a manual pre-commit hook (`normalize-docstrings`) that enforces the house-style docstring format (triple quotes on their own lines), as described in the documentation. This is opt-in and can be run on demand to incrementally normalize the codebase.

**dbt Project Configuration**

* Updated `artwork_pipeline/dbt_project.yml` to clarify local developer schema handling and profile linkage. The profile is now set to `dbt_daniel` for local development, and custom schema logic for staging and marts is documented to explain local vs. Snowflake behavior. 

These changes collectively enforce high engineering standards, improve testability, and provide clear, actionable guidance for all contributors, ensuring the orchestration layer remains robust and maintainable.

## Summary
P0-2 of the blast realtime-gap analysis. When a rider matches with a **different** driver (blast `select`/`pull-up`), the server notifies losing drivers with `blast_taken` on `user:{driverId}:notify` — but **nothing on mobile handled it**, so the stale blast card lingered on the loser's feed until the next ~20s `/drivers/requests` poll.

## Change
- **`feed.tsx` `onMessage`**: drop the card optimistically on `blast_taken` (`setRequests` filter by `blastId`) — mirrors the existing `blast_expired` handler exactly.
- **`contexts/notifications.tsx`**: new `blast_taken` case — decrement the unread-request badge + `triggerFeedRefresh()` so the card clears **app-wide** (not only when the driver is on the feed), plus a low-key **"BLAST FILLED"** closure banner, suppressed when they're already watching the feed (same `onFeedRef` suppression as `direct_booking_request`).

Losers are always drivers, and the server sends this via `notifyUser` (no OS push), so no `routeFromPush` case is needed.

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` clean (mobile). Mirrors the proven `blast_expired` code path; mobile UI components have no unit-test harness (web vitest covers `lib/` only).

## Rollout
JS-only mobile change → reaches devices via the next EAS build (batched with the Apple Pay button, #463). Preview OTA fires on merge.

author: tobyleeder-blip
body:
## What

Anonymous users can no longer use Amadi indefinitely. They explore freely at first, get recurring nudges to connect (or create) a Bluesky account as they engage, and eventually hit a hard wall.

### Connect/create modal (design: Toby's artifact)
- One dialog, three pages: a chooser ("I'm new to Bluesky" promoted first / "I already have an account"), a create page, and the existing handle sign-in one level deep.
- **In-flow account creation**: the create path starts OAuth against the bsky.social entryway with `prompt=create` (advertised in its `prompt_values_supported`), landing users on Bluesky's hosted signup. They return through the normal `/oauth/callback` already linked. No more external bsky.app links.

### Gate model
- Usage is derived live (feeds created, posts seen, chat refinements, days of use), no counters to drift. Config in `src/lib/account-gate.ts`, env-overridable (`GATE_NUDGE_*`, `GATE_WALL_NUDGES`, `ACCOUNT_GATE_DISABLED=1`).
- Nudges recur per metric: every 3 feeds, 100 posts seen, 10 refinements, 2 days. Marked shown at display time (server-persisted per user, multi-session safe).
- After 3 nudge popups, the next threshold crossing raises a **non-dismissible wall**, enforced server-side: chat, feeds POST/PATCH, branch, template, feed-preview, swipe return 403 `account_wall`; reads stay open so the wall screen renders. Sticky marker so pruned `seen_posts` can never reopen the wall.
- Linked users (by `bluesky_did`) are exempt before any counting; expired-token users get the existing "Reconnect" UX, never the wall.

### Action resume
Like/repost/reply/quote/publish attempts while unlinked open the modal with the action stashed (sessionStorage, 10 min TTL). After the OAuth round trip the action auto-completes; any mount without `?bsky_connected=1` discards the stash, so abandoned flows never fire it.

## Migration

`apps/web/sql/013_account_gate.sql` (additive, idempotent) must be applied to prod feed-db before/with deploy:
```sql
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS gate_nudges_shown jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb;
```

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` clean; lint at repo baseline (+3 `set-state-in-effect` errors of the same class/files main already has 47 of).
- Verified against a local feed-db: fresh user `free` → nudge at each interval crossing → marking shown suppresses reload re-trigger → 4th crossing after 3 shown walls with sticky marker → `POST /api/chat` 403 `account_wall` while `GET /api/feeds` stays 200.
- Verified in-browser: chooser/create/sign-in pages, nudge + wall variants, action-triggered modal, wall error-toast suppression.
- `prompt=create` confirmed against real bsky.social from local dev (lands on the signup screen, not login).

author: jongio
body:
## Problem

`.github/workflows/pr-build.yml` scoped its concurrency group by `github.ref`:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

For `pull_request_target` events (and `workflow_run`), `github.ref` resolves to `refs/heads/main` (the base/default branch), **not** the PR head branch. So every PR's preview build shared a single concurrency group: `PR Build-refs/heads/main`.

With `cancel-in-progress: true`, whenever GitHub queued a batch of PR events, all but the last-queued run got cancelled — showing red **Check Build Permission** / **Build PR Preview** checks on ~10 PRs at once.

Verified in run history: batches at 22:24 and 23:55 UTC on 2026-07-02 each cancelled ~10 different `idea/*` PRs, leaving only the last-queued run alive.

## Fix

Scope the concurrency group to the PR head branch, with fallbacks:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref || github.event.workflow_run.head_branch || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

- `pull_request_target` → `github.event.pull_request.head.ref` (PR head branch)
- `workflow_run` → `github.event.workflow_run.head_branch` (same branch, so it shares a group with the `pull_request_target` path for the same PR — which also prevents those two trigger paths from racing on the same release tag)
- `push` (prbuild) / `workflow_dispatch` → `github.ref`

This isolates each PR into its own concurrency group so different PRs no longer cancel each other, while still cancelling superseded in-progress runs *within* the same PR. `cancel-in-progress: true` is unchanged.

Unblocks the batch-cancelled `idea/*` PRs whose preview checks were showing red.

author: mattjj
body:
When reverse-mode differentiating a gather with the operand's cotangent accumulated into a ref (via jax.vjp + with_refs), the backward pass previously materialized a dense zeros array, scatter-added into it, and dense-added the result into the ref. Now:
* gathers that look like NumPy-style advanced indexing over leading axes (e.g. from `x[idx]`, like embedding lookups) become a single in-place indexed add-update on the gradient ref: `ref[idx] += ct`;
* all other gathers (clip mode, batched dims from vmap, etc.) become a scatter-add onto the ref's current value, which still avoids materializing dense zeros.

We only accept gather modes whose out-of-bounds transpose semantics match ref addupdate's (drop, not clamp), so clip-mode gathers take the general path.

author: jacquardlabs
body:
## Summary
- `.vbadge` had `flex-shrink: 0` and no width cap. That's harmless in review mode, where badge text is always a short verdict (`approved`/`changes`/`info`), but in Q&A mode the badge holds the raw selected choice text. A long choice claimed its full unwrapped width, squeezing the sibling title column to near zero and forcing one-word-per-line wrapping, with the badge visually overlapping the title.
- `.choice-chip` had no `text-align` override, so it inherited the browser's default centered `<button>` alignment — long choices that wrap to multiple lines rendered off-center instead of flush left.

## Fix
- Cap `.vbadge` to `max-width: 45%` with `overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis`, so long Q&A choices truncate instead of stealing the row.
- Add `text-align: left` to `.choice-chip`.

## Test plan
- [x] Reproduced both bugs against the pre-fix code with a synthetic `qa-input.json` carrying a long choice string, driven headlessly via Playwright — confirmed the one-word-per-line collapse and centered wrapped choice text.
- [x] Re-ran the same repro against the fix — title wraps normally, badge truncates with `…`, choice text left-aligns.
- [x] `python3 tests/test_server_qa.py`

author: lan496
body:
## Summary

Replaces `PeriodicKdTree` (backed by kiddo's `ImmutableKdTree`) with `PeriodicNeighborSearch`, a pure safe-Rust uniform bin grid over Cartesian coordinates, and drops the `kiddo` dependency entirely.

## Motivation

- **Suspected heap corruption in the magnetic symmetry search** (lan496/spinforge-dev#88): long noncoplanar magnetic-structure runs nondeterministically die with SIGTRAP / macOS malloc freelist corruption, with the native backtrace inside `PeriodicKdTree::new` → `PrimitiveMagneticSymmetrySearch` → `iterative_magnetic_symmetry_search` (`MoyoNonCollinearMagneticDataset`). It reproduces on both moyopy 0.7.9 and 0.13.0. moyo itself contains no `unsafe`; kiddo's `ImmutableKdTree` is the only unsafe-heavy code in that call path, so this removes the suspected source of the out-of-bounds write.
- **Confirmed wrong-results bug in kiddo v5's `ImmutableKdTree`** (sdd/kiddo#258: incorrect indices/distances from best-n queries), fixed only in the unreleased 6.0.0-alpha rewrite. A silently wrong nearest-neighbor index would corrupt `solve_correspondence` permutations, so moving off it is worthwhile independently of the crash.

## How it works

Each point is registered in every bin its `symprec`-ball overlaps — at most 8 bins, because the bin size is at least `2 * symprec` — so `nearest()` inspects only the single bin containing the query position: any point within `symprec` of the query has registered itself there. Construction is O(N), queries are O(1) expected. The periodic-image enumeration (offsets in `[-1, 1]^3` with padding, exact for Minkowski-reduced bases) is unchanged. The `PeriodicNeighborSearch` docstring explains this invariant with a 2D cross-section figure.

The random lattice rotation that worked around kd-tree axis-alignment pathologies is no longer needed and is removed.

## Performance

Full `cargo bench --bench translation_search` (criterion defaults, Apple M1), run on `main` (kiddo kd-tree) and on this branch (bin grid). Median times:

| n (atoms) | kd-tree (`main`) | bin grid (this PR) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (1) | 424 ns | 3.48 µs | 0.12× |
| 2 (8) | 4.70 µs | 11.9 µs | 0.40× |
| 3 (27) | 45.2 µs | 41.0 µs | 1.1× |
| 4 (64) | 285 µs | 112 µs | 2.5× |
| 5 (125) | 1.19 ms | 0.29 ms | 4.1× |
| 6 (216) | 3.67 ms | 0.72 ms | 5.1× |
| 7 (343) | 9.93 ms | 1.73 ms | 5.8× |
| 8 (512) | 22.9 ms | 3.78 ms | 6.1× |

Break-even around 27 atoms, then 2.5–6.1× faster from 64 atoms up; the small-cell regression is microsecond-scale construction overhead (the grid builds a hash map where the kd-tree builds a flat array). The `naive` benchmark, identical code on both branches, serves as a control: it agrees within noise between the two runs (e.g. 53.6 ns vs 53.5 ns at n=1, 78.0 ms vs 77.6 ms at n=8), so the comparison is not skewed by machine load.

## Other changes

- Adds `rustc-hash` (FxHashMap) for fast bin hashing; removing kiddo drops 145 lines of transitive dependencies from `Cargo.lock`.
- Adds a regression test cross-checking `solve_correspondence` against the naive O(n²) solver on an axis-aligned n×n×n grid cell (many sites sharing coordinate values on every axis — the historically pathological input for the kd-tree).
- Renames the stale `PeriodicKdTree` references in `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/layer_architecture.md` to `PeriodicNeighborSearch`.
- `cargo test --workspace` passes; no new clippy warnings in touched files.

author: squiggler-app[bot]
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @sanity/pkg-utils@10.9.0

### Minor Changes

- [#2955](https://github.com/sanity-io/pkg-utils/pull/2955) [`935f6f6`](https://github.com/sanity-io/pkg-utils/commit/935f6f688f95d4285cedadd245a8e2563c458a45) Thanks [@stipsan](https://github.com/stipsan)! - Enable `transpileTemplateLiterals` by default in the `babel.styledComponents` transform, so unused styled components can be tree-shaken.

  The `pure: true` default has been emitting `/*#__PURE__*/` annotations in front of tagged template expressions, a position no bundler supports (see [rollup#4035](https://github.com/rollup/rollup/issues/4035)), so the annotations were dropped and unused styled components were never tree-shaken - not by pkg-utils itself, and not by the bundlers of apps consuming the published package. Transpiling `` styled.button`...` `` to `styled.button(["..."])` turns the styled component initializer into a plain call expression, which pure annotations are defined for:

  ```js
  const UsedButton = /*#__PURE__*/ styled.button.withConfig({
    displayName: 'UsedButton',
    componentId: 'sc-1fal5wv-1',
  })(['cursor:pointer;'])
  ```

  With this shape, unused styled components are now removed from the build output, and the annotation survives into the published output so app bundlers (rollup, webpack, esbuild, etc) can drop exported styled components that the app never imports.

  To restore the previous output, set `babel: {styledComponents: {transpileTemplateLiterals: false}}` in `package.config.ts`.

### Patch Changes

- [#2927](https://github.com/sanity-io/pkg-utils/pull/2927) [`46495fb`](https://github.com/sanity-io/pkg-utils/commit/46495fb8b74aec099c8d89ca2a34a1b4ef29a95b) Thanks [@squiggler-app](https://github.com/apps/squiggler-app)! - fix(deps): update dependency browserslist to ^4.28.4

## 관련 이슈 번호

Closes #845

## 배경 및 문제

`/ux` 는 UX_FLOW/UX_REFINE 공개 진입점으로 남아 있었지만, 구현 직전 목업 기준 확보는 `/impl` 의 canvas-design 분기가 담당하게 됐고 epic 급 화면 흐름은 `/design` 이 담당하게 됐습니다. 그 결과 `/ux` 의 독자 산출 계약과 positioning 이 최신 canvas SSOT 규약과 어긋났습니다.

## 원인 (해당 시)

`/ux` 가 이전 디자인 시안 전달 흐름을 자체 계약으로 유지하면서, #843에서 도입된 `docs/design-variants/` 확정본 승격 + canvas 등록 규약을 얇게 감싸지 못했습니다. ux-flow 화면 인벤토리도 hi-fi 목업 대상 여부를 표시하지 않아 전 화면 목업화 비용과 drift 위험이 남았습니다.

## 작업내용

- `/ux` 를 구현 없이 목업과 흐름을 먼저 탐색하는 utility로 재정의하고, 내부 `canvas-design` wrapper를 통해 drafts 반복 → 사용자 PICK → 확정본 승격 + canvas 등록으로 끝나도록 정렬했습니다.
- public-surface gate와 README / positioning / init 안내에서 `/ux` 를 advanced에서 utility로 이동했습니다.
- `ux-flow.md` 화면 인벤토리에 `hi-fi 목업 필요` 열을 추가하고, designer 지침은 `필요` 화면만 목업화하도록 제한했습니다.
- module-architect 입력 표현과 design 규격 문서를 확정 목업/canvas SSOT 계약에 맞췄습니다.
- 관련 회귀 테스트를 추가·갱신했습니다.

## 결정 근거

`/ux` 를 삭제하지 않고 utility로 낮추면 기존 사용자가 직접 선행 디자인 탐색을 요청하는 경로는 유지하면서, 목업 확정본의 변경 경로는 `canvas-design` 하나로 수렴합니다. hi-fi 필요 플래그는 핵심 화면만 목업화하게 만들어 비용과 산출물 drift를 줄입니다.

## 배포 경로 검증 (plug-in 영향 시)

- plug-in 본체 경로: `skills/ux/**`, `skills/canvas-design/SKILL.md`, `agents/designer/**`, `agents/ux-architect/**`, `agents/module-architect/**`, `commands/init-dcness.md` 변경은 plugin update로 사용자 환경에 도달합니다.
- 사용자용 SSOT 문서: `docs/plugin/design.md`, `docs/plugin/positioning.md` 변경은 plugin update로 도달합니다.
- init-dcness 복사 seed 신규 추가 없음. 기존 활성 프로젝트는 `claude plugin update dcness@dcness` 로 지침/skill 변경을 받으면 되고, 별도 `/init-dcness` 재실행은 필요 없습니다.

## 신규 surface justification (새 public skill/command/agent/gate 추가 시만)

N/A — 신규 public 발화 추가 없음. 기존 `/ux` 를 advanced에서 utility로 재분류하고 역할을 축소했습니다.

- [x] node scripts/check_cross_refs.mjs

## Summary
This PR adds a new "Important Information" legal page and updates messaging across the site to clarify ShoreVest's underwriting approach, shifting from "margin of safety" and "downside protection" language to more precise terminology around collateral coverage, legal protections, and downside scenario analysis.

## Key Changes

**New Pages:**
- Added `important-information.html` (English) and `important-information_cn.html` (Chinese) with standard legal disclaimers about investment risks and regulatory compliance

**Messaging Updates:**
- Replaced "Margin of safety" with "Entry discipline" on strategy pages to better describe low LTV/cost-to-value entry approach
- Changed "Downside protection" to "Risk management" and "Underwriting approach" to more accurately reflect how risks are considered
- Updated meta descriptions across multiple pages to emphasize "collateral coverage, legal protections and downside scenarios" rather than "margin of safety" and "downside protection"
- Refined language in strategy sections to clarify that recovery "remains subject to legal, commercial, and enforcement risk" rather than implying guaranteed multiple resolution paths
- Updated firm description from "first-lien downside protection and margin of safety" to "first-lien underwriting focused on collateral coverage, legal protections and downside scenarios"

**Footer Updates:**
- Added "Important Information" link to footer navigation across all pages (English and Chinese versions)
- Updated `shared-footer.js` to include the new Important Information page link

**Content Refinements:**
- Clarified that underwriting "considers multiple resolution paths rather than relying on any single route"
- Changed "downside controls are embedded" to "downside scenarios are considered" for more precise language
- Updated collateral-focused underwriting description to emphasize it's "not around interest spreads, refinancing or market direction"

## Implementation Details
- Both new HTML pages follow the existing legal page template structure with proper language attributes and metadata
- Pages include the standard tracking token injection script and shared header/footer components
- All footer updates maintain consistency across English and Chinese versions
- Meta description updates align with the refined messaging throughout the site

author: patdhlk
body:
## What

Changes the allocator-test strategy: **verified** zero-allocation (counting-global-allocator differential tests) is required pre-1.0 only in **executor scope** (REQ_0104) and **connector scope** (REQ_0328). medkit drops its zero-alloc mandate.

- **ADR_0133** (new, `spec/architecture/medkit/index.rst`) records the decision, the rejected alternatives (harden the harness / `#[ignore]` on noisy platforms), and the ❌ consequence: a medkit hook-path allocation regression is no longer CI-caught; re-verification is a 1.0 hardening item.
- **REQ_0925** softened: the non-blocking / bounded / SPSC clause stays mandatory; allocation-freedom becomes design intent (it holds by construction per ADR_0114). Re-anchored to **TEST_0913** (live-executor integration) so the `req-implemented-has-test` schema gate keeps holding.
- **TEST_0914** retired (`:status: rejected`, precedent: TEST_0401) and `hook_no_alloc.rs` deleted, plus its now-unused `taktora-bounded-alloc` dev-dep.
- Existing no-alloc guards outside the two mandated scopes (motion, DLT logging) stay while quiet — per ADR_0133 they are regression guards, not requirements, and get dropped rather than stabilised if they flake.

## Why

The counting-allocator differential harness counts every thread's allocations in the tracking window and is inherently flake-prone (the GH #132 class — intermittent 1-vs-0 on macOS). medkit is pre-1.0 diagnostics tooling; paying a flaky CI gate for a guarantee it doesn't need yet is the wrong trade.

## Verification

- `uv run sphinx-build -W -b html` (strict needs-schema gate) — passes
- `./scripts/check-duplicate-need-ids.sh` — passes (ADR_0133 also avoids the IDs claimed by in-flight `feat/medkit-build-identity`, which claims ADR_0132)
- `cargo test -p taktora-medkit-binding-executor-tests` — passes

## Note on branch history

A concurrent M3-connector agent session found this work uncommitted in the shared checkout and quarantined it with a mis-attributed "UNAUTHORIZED" draft commit. The changes were authored deliberately in the taktora-cc3 remote session at the maintainer's request; the commit was rewritten with an accurate message (same tree, validated as above).

author: raymond91125
body:
Persists the neurotransmitter reconciliation and adds a second cited transmitter source, per request.

## New source: Wang et al. 2024 atlas (`data/wang-neurotransmitter-atlas/`)
- **"A neurotransmitter atlas of C. elegans males and hermaphrodites"** (Wang, Vidal, … Hobert lab), eLife reviewed preprint, **doi:10.7554/eLife.95402.2**, crawled **2026-07-03**.
- Pinned **Table S2** supplement (`TableS2_expression.xlsx`, sha256 recorded) + reproducible `parse_atlas.py` → **302 per-neuron assignments** (`assignments.csv`), from the consolidated "Neurotransmitter(s)" column (CRISPR reporter atlas).

## Persisted reconciliation (`analysis/`)
`reconcile_neurotransmitters.py` (reproducible) compares **neurons.json vs WormAtlas vs Wang** per cell class → `neurotransmitter_reconciliation.{csv,md}`.

**117 classes compared; ~101 agree.** Findings:
- **Robust discrepancy → likely `neurons.json` error:** **HSN** `nt`=glutamate,serotonin, but **both** WormAtlas **and** Wang say **ACh**(+serotonin) — glutamate unsupported.
- **`neurons.json` gaps the atlas fills:** ALA/AVF/AVJ→GABA, AWA/RIP→ACh, I4→glutamate, ASI→betaine (blank in neurons.json).
- **Not real conflicts:** Wang’s consolidated column is the *primary* transmitter, so dual-transmitter cells (ADF, RIH, VCn, RIM, RIB) look reduced; and **AIM**’s ACh is the male/post-L3 phenotype (WormAtlas fn 4) — hermaphrodite AIM matches neurons.json.

Caveats (sex/stage/evidence footnotes; Wang primary-column granularity; class-level matching) are documented in the report and script headers.

`ruff` + `pytest` (59) green locally.

author: viperjuice
body:
## Summary

- `chunker/metadata/languages/javascript.py`'s `optional_parameter` branch of `_parse_parameter` read the parameter name but never its `type_annotation` child, unlike the adjacent `required_parameter` branch which does. TS `foo(x?: string)` parses `x?` as an `optional_parameter` node whose `type_annotation` child holds `: string` — the type was silently dropped.
- Confirmed at scale on real gp source: **564/2,153 (26%) of extracted params are optional, and 0 kept their type** before this fix.
- Fix mirrors the `required_parameter` branch exactly (same `type_annotation` lookup, same `.strip(":").strip()` normalization, same output shape) so an optional param now keeps its type.
- This type flows straight through to `signature_text` (`chunker/core.py::_format_signature_text`) and from there into the Boundary IR `signature` field (`chunker/boundary/adapter.py`), so the fix reaches every consumer of the extracted metadata/Boundary IR, not just the raw parameter list.
- Version bumped `3.2.1` → `3.2.2` (patch/bugfix) since this changes parser output for any TS/JS source that uses optional typed parameters.

## Verification

- Added a regression test, `TestTypeScriptMetadataExtraction::test_extract_optional_parameter_type` in `tests/test_metadata_extraction.py`, asserting `foo(name?: string, age: number)` keeps `parameters[0]["type"] == "string"`. Confirmed red-without / green-with the fix (stashed the source change, reran — test failed with `type == None`; restored — passed).
- Ran the repo's Boundary IR golden regen (`scripts/regenerate_boundary_goldens.py`) — **all 12 language goldens report `unchanged`**. This is expected, not a gap in the fix: none of the current `tests/fixtures/boundary_ir/repos/{javascript,typescript}/*` fixtures happen to contain an optional typed parameter (`x?: T`), so the fixture corpus can't exercise this bug either way. I did not hand-edit the fixtures to add one — doing so would ripple into `test_boundary_ir_fixture_inventory.py` and related count/inventory assertions for marginal benefit versus the direct unit test above, which is a precise, minimal repro of the exact bug. Flagging the gap explicitly: **the Boundary IR determinism gate does not currently have coverage for optional typed parameters in any language**, so a future regression here would not be caught by goldens alone.
- Ran `tests/test_metadata_extraction.py`, `tests/test_javascript_language.py`, `tests/test_typescript_language.py`, `tests/test_boundary_ir_*` (golden snapshots, determinism, semantic contract, schema, language parity) — all pass.
- Ran the full fast CI-equivalent suite (`scripts/run_ci_smoke.py`) — 360 passed.
- `ruff check` and `black --check` — clean.
- `uv lock` — regenerated to match the version bump.

### Pre-existing gap noticed, left out of scope

While comparing branches: `required_parameter` with a typed default (e.g. TS `age: number = 18`) does **not** capture the default value — only `optional_parameter` and bare `assignment_pattern` do. That's a separate, narrower gap unrelated to this fix; not touched here.

## Downstream consumers that will need attention on upgrade

- **`spec`'s `spec-engine/realized/adapter.py` E(C) pipeline** — this is the consumer named in the task. It pins to `treesitter-chunker==3.2.0` by version string in code/docstrings (`EC_SOURCE`, docstrings referencing "GENUINE treesitter-chunker 3.2.0 Boundary IR"), and `spec-engine/realized/test_realized.py:70-71` hard-asserts `ec1["provenance"]["tsc_version"] == "3.2.0"` / `X.tsc_version() == "3.2.0"`. **These version-string assertions will break on any bump to `3.2.2` regardless of output content** — that's a required update independent of this fix.
- **Golden/digest regen in `spec`**: I checked (`grep -rnE '[A-Za-z_]\?:' spec-engine/realized/sample* spec-engine/**/*.json`) and **none of spec's current sample fixtures or correspondence/graph JSON contain an optional typed parameter**, so **no actual golden/digest content in spec needs regenerating from this specific fix** — only the hardcoded version-string pins above need updating. If spec's fixtures grow an optional typed param later, this fix will change output for it and any pinned digest would need regen at that point.
- Not touched: no other repo scanned (`Code-Index-MCP`, `governed-pipeline`, `portal`, etc.) had a live pin exercising this code path at the time of this check.

**Do not merge — isolated worktree, opened for review per instructions.**

body:
## Summary

The Critic always runs — `run_revision_loop()` calls `review()` unconditionally on every cycle — but a clean pass produced zero console output. The only visible signal tied to the Critic was the per-field "The critic flagged '...'" echo inside `_make_pm_followup_fn`, which only fires when there *are* findings. From the CLI, a session where the Critic ran and passed cleanly looked identical to one where it hypothetically didn't run at all.

- `orchestrator.py`: `run_revision_loop()` gains an optional `on_review: Callable[[list[CriticFinding]], None] | None = None` parameter, invoked with the findings from every `review()` call (each cycle, plus the post-loop cap check). Kept as a plain callback so `orchestrator.py` stays free of any `typer`/CLI dependency — same pattern already used for `pm_followup_fn`.
- `cli.py`: new `_on_critic_review()` echoes `"Critic reviewed the draft: no issues found."` whenever a pass comes back clean (on any cycle, not just the first), and does nothing on the flagged path since that's already covered by the existing per-field echoes.

Now all three outcomes are visible: clean pass, flagged findings (existing per-field messages), and cap-reached escalation (existing message).

- [x] `hatch run test` — 79 passed (new: two `orchestrator.py` tests asserting `on_review` fires with the right findings per cycle; one CLI integration test asserting the confirmation string appears in output for a clean run)

author: silverstein
body:
## What

Fixes the concrete #369 packaging blocker found in #395/#397: opt-in `engine-sherpa` builds produced binaries referencing `@rpath/libsherpa-onnx-c-api.dylib` and `@rpath/libonnxruntime.1.17.1.dylib` that nothing bundled — apps crashed at launch, installed CLIs died with dyld "Library not loaded".

## Fix

**macOS: link sherpa-onnx statically.** `sherpa-rs` moves to per-target deps: macOS uses `default-features = false, features = ["download-binaries", "static"]` (upstream ships osx static archives; dropping defaults also drops unused `tts`). No bundling, no rpath surgery — binaries are self-contained.

**Linux/Windows: dynamic, as before.** sherpa-rs-sys's `static` panics in build.rs on Linux without a global `RUSTFLAGS` relocation hack, and CI deliberately builds the `engine-sherpa` gate on all three platforms. Docs now state the platform split plainly (macOS copy-anywhere; Linux/Windows run from the cargo target layout).

Also: two `tracing::info` success logs in `sherpa_engine` (recognizer load, transcription complete) so a real sherpa run is distinguishable from the whisper fallback — the same honesty principle as #396 — and `install-dev-app.sh --target-only` for packaging verification without touching `~/Applications`.

## Verification (real runs, both platforms)

macOS (maintainer machine):
- `MINUTES_BUILD_FEATURES=parakeet,metal,vad-ort,engine-sherpa ./scripts/install-dev-app.sh --target-only`: bundle builds, seal verifies, **zero** `@rpath`/sherpa/onnxruntime refs in app binary, bundled sidecar CLI, and standalone CLI.
- Launched the built app from target/: process alive >10s.
- Copied the CLI to a temp dir and ran a **real sherpa transcription** of `crates/assets/demo.wav` with a temp config: correct transcript, `sherpa-onnx transcription complete` in logs, **no** "falling back to whisper".
- Re-verified after the per-target split: build clean, still 0 dangling refs.

Linux (this box):
- The exact CI gate `cargo build -p minutes-core --no-default-features --features engine-sherpa` fails on `static` (upstream panic), passes with the per-target scoping — including `--locked` and the combined `diarize,vad-ort,engine-sherpa` build.

Plus: 911 core tests green, fmt clean, llms.txt in sync, default builds verified unchanged (no sherpa in default feature graph, no new refs).

## Review provenance

Implemented by a codex session on the maintainer's macOS machine against a full acceptance-criteria brief; cross-platform CI risk caught and fixed in review here (Linux static panic); fresh-context codex adversarial review then verified Cargo semantics/`--locked`/tts-drop/`--target-only` and flagged the doc gaps fixed in the final commit. NOTICE/third-party attribution for the statically embedded runtime is deliberately tied to the #369 release decision (nothing distributes the feature yet).

## What this unlocks / what stays open on #369

Local macOS opt-in builds (`MINUTES_BUILD_FEATURES=parakeet,metal,vad-ort,engine-sherpa`) now produce working apps and CLIs — the dev-app SOTA batch testing path is real. Still open on #369: whether release binaries ship sherpa (size/notarization/NOTICE), Linux/Windows install packaging, and sherpa-live (does not exist; live remains whisper/parakeet).

author: timoffex
body:
Removes the finalizer because the code it calls acquires a lock, which can deadlock during GC. In general, finalizers should never acquire locks or perform IO, and should be very very simple.

Unfortunately, this means we need a different way to clean up API instances. For now, this creates a small memory leak (the `WandbAPI` objects in wandb-core will not get cleaned up).

author: brettcurtis
body:
## What

Corrects the cluster management ADR from the misleading 'One Cluster Per Zone with Five Add-on Layers' to the accurate 'Team-Owned Regional Clusters with Zone-Based Node Pools'.

## Why

The old title and framing were wrong in two ways:

1. **'One cluster per zone'** — the correct model is team-owned clusters. Teams declare their cluster locations in Logos (`platform_managed_project.kubernetes_engine`). The zone-per-node-pool topology is an implementation detail, not the defining characteristic.

2. **'One cluster per team — Rejected'** was listed in alternatives — this is backwards. Team-based cluster ownership IS the decision. The old text was rejecting the correct architecture.

## Changes

- Page intro and Components table updated to reflect team-owned framing
- ADR title updated
- ADR context reframed around team ownership and Istio locality routing
- Decision section separates regional control plane rationale from zone-based node pool rationale clearly
- Alternatives section removes the incorrect rejection; keeps the two valid alternatives
- Consequences updated to reflect team autonomy over cluster lifecycle

author: ken-jo
body:
Closes the project directory browser (ProjectRootsBrowser, right-hand Workspace rail) UX gaps in one atomic PR, split into area commits. Scope excluded per direction: multi-root simultaneous display, `.gooseignore` handling.

## Areas

### 1. Remove root (`cb25a38d`)
- New IPC `workspace.removeRoot` drops an additional root from `permissions.additionalDirectories` (the executor Layer-1 read allow-list SOT). Trash button in the toolbar, shown only for non-default roots.
- **Security**: removal can ONLY target a path already in `additionalDirectories` (canonical/case-folded match), NEVER an arbitrary renderer path; the default root (`process.cwd()`) is hard-refused (`cannot-remove-default`). The scope shrink is audited (redacted path), mirroring `persistValidatedRoot`.
- Files: `src/ipc/domains/workspace.ts` (`removeRoot` handler + `WorkspaceRemoveRootResult`), `src/contract/app-contract.ts:333`, `src/preload/internal-surface.ts:1741`, `src/ui/renderer/types.ts` (`LvisWorkspaceApi.removeRoot`), `src/ui/renderer/components/ChatSidePanel.tsx` (`removeActiveRoot` + button).

### 2. Right-click context menu + reveal IPC (`2e122a82`)
- Each row wrapped in a Radix `ContextMenu`: Open / Reveal in Finder|Explorer / Copy path / Copy relative path (ActionPanel per-row pattern). Open + Copy are renderer-local; only Reveal adds an IPC channel.
- **Security**: `workspace.reveal` re-validates the renderer path with the SAME guard `listDir` uses (`assertReadableFilePath`) and passes only the main-owned `verdict.resolved` realpath to `shell.showItemInFolder` — never the raw renderer string. `showItemInFolder` selects the location only (never opens/executes), consistent with `canOpenExternal:false`.
- Files: `src/ipc/domains/workspace.ts` (`reveal` handler), `ChatSidePanel.tsx` (`renderEntries` menu + `toRelativePath`), i18n platform-branched labels.

### 3. Keyboard nav + ARIA tree widget (`24ab7718`)
- Converted to WAI-ARIA APG tree: each row is now a focusable `role=treeitem` div (was a button inside a treeitem — nonconforming), children wrapped in `role=group`, with `aria-level`/`aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-selected`.
- Single `onKeyDown` on the tree: Up/Down roving focus, Right expand-then-descend, Left collapse-or-parent, Enter/Space open-or-toggle, Home/End, and a 500ms type-ahead over the flattened visible order. `pendingFocusRef` gates imperative `.focus()` to keyboard moves (no focus theft on mount/mouse); a clamp effect keeps the roving pointer valid across collapse/reload/root-switch. Keyboard focus (`activeItemPath`) is intentionally separate from the opened-file highlight (`selectedPath`).
- Files: `ChatSidePanel.tsx` (sole file).

### 4. Completeness polish (`9d4feca3`)
- (a) Collapse-all button; (b) empty-state → "Add folder" CTA; (c) per-child inline loading / error-with-retry / empty-folder placeholders (+ active-root error now retryable); (d) truncated-listing flag (main already returned `truncated`; the browser was dropping it); (e) empty-folder placeholder; (f) extension-aware file row icons (`File` = domain default, not a fallback); (h) drag-drop a folder + Cmd/Ctrl+O (panel-scoped) to add a root.
- **Security (drag-drop)**: a dropped path is renderer-supplied with NO native-dialog gesture, so `workspace.addRootByPath` NEVER persists it — it validates (`validateDirectoryAddition` + is-a-directory) and mints a one-time `ackToken`; the existing `pickRoot({ackToken})` path performs the re-validated persist. A drop therefore surfaces the same confirmation panel a warned pick does and can never silently widen the read scope. A dropped FILE is rejected (`not-a-dir`; no renderer-side dirname guessing — No-Fallback).
- Files: `src/ipc/domains/workspace.ts` (`addRootByPath`), `ChatSidePanel.tsx` (a–h), `src/ui/renderer/format-ipc-error.ts` (new codes mapped), i18n.

### 5. E2e (`a85fca1c`)
Real packaged-Electron coverage for ARIA tree + keyboard expand/collapse + role=group + context menu + collapse-all + default-root-has-no-remove-button.

## Deferred (own follow-up — out of this atomic scope)
Double-click-to-pin a file into a workspace TAB (design item g). It requires a `WorkspaceTabContentRef` union `fs` variant (its own Field-Addition Sweep across `contentKey`/`normalizeContentRef`/`contentKind`), a new fs content-tab viewer in `ContentTabView`, and prop-drilling the workspace-tabs store into `FileBrowserWorkspace` — a cross-cutting change orthogonal to the read/navigate/reveal/remove gaps this PR closes. Single-click preview already works.

## Verification
- `bun run typecheck` — 0 errors
- `bun run build` — OK (i18n catalog 7 locales, tls/opacity/color-token, no-inline-channels gates all pass)
- `bunx vitest run` — 7623 passed / 9 skipped, 0 failed (incl. wire-lock snapshots `preload-shape` + `channel-inventory` updated for the 3 new channels, and `format-ipc-error-coverage` for the new codes)
- New tests: 10 IPC handler tests (`workspace-preview.test.ts`: removeRoot scope/default/unauthorized, reveal path-guard/dir/sensitive/unauthorized, addRootByPath ack-gate/file-reject/unauthorized) + 11 component tests (`ChatSidePanel.test.tsx`: ARIA roles, ArrowDown roving, Enter-expand, type-ahead, ctx reveal/copy, remove-root, collapse-all, empty-folder, truncated, drag-drop ack gate)
- Playwright e2e (real Electron): 6 workspace-rail specs pass incl. the new ARIA/keyboard/context-menu test; screenshots captured (extension icons, expand chevrons, collapse-all, Korean context menu).

author: matheusbatista1
body:
Rodada 2 — Fase E: correções de cálculo/UX surgidas do uso real.

## Fixes
- **"Fatura atual" = fatura ABERTA.** New `computeCardOpenBill`/`computeCardOpenBills` resolve the open cycle per card (`cardBillMonth(today)`) and delegate to `computeCardBillForMonth`. Replaces `computeCardBill` (which summed every non-installment charge across all past/future cycles and never netted paid faturas → e.g. Caixa read R$3.287 instead of the ~R$1.171 open bill). Applied on the dashboard MiniCard/"Próximos vencimentos" and the Cartões screen.
- **"Fim do mês" projection.** Now subtracts **overdue** payable obligations (boleto/empréstimo/financiamento) that are unpaid with competence before the current month — they never debit a balance and were outside the `[currentMonth…]` window, inflating the figure. Card faturas are **excluded** (a pre-current fatura is presumed paid, the same assumption `computeCardOutstanding` uses; only boleto/loan/financing have explicit `isPaid`). *(An adversarial review caught a first attempt that dragged the floor to the oldest card charge via `isPaid` — a no-op for cards — over-subtracting presumed-paid faturas; the shipped version avoids that.)*
- **Visão mensal Entradas/Saídas/Resultado** now count the amount actually **paid** for a settled obligation (`settledItemCents`/`settledItemShareCents`), matching the dashboard "Economia do mês" (the page used face value before).
- **Toggle Geral↔Apenas-meu animation.** `use-count-up` now tracks the live displayed value as the tween origin, so a fast toggle that interrupts an animation resumes correctly and always lands on the latest target (no more stuck/wrong numbers).

## Checks
`typecheck · lint · test` (403, incl. new open-bill + overdue-projection + card-charge-guard tests) `· build` green. Adversarially reviewed; the one confirmed finding was fixed + locked with a guard test.

## Validação (você)
Rode `scripts/validate-finances.ts` e confira o novo **fim do mês** (deve descontar boletos/empréstimos vencidos não pagos) e a **fatura atual** de cada cartão no dashboard/Cartões.

author: prozak
body:
Rebase of the June 19 branch onto current master (clean auto-merge with the recent insmod-resolution changes to the wrapper).

The wrapper's locator functions hardcoded ~/.local/share/uml-veristat/, the install dir used only by the default (patched) build. A --clean build installs to ~/.local/share/uml-veristat-clean/, and partial/custom builds to other -SUFFIX dirs, so on a box with only a suffixed flavor the wrapper failed with "UML kernel not found" despite a usable install. resolve_install_dir() now picks one shared install dir up front (UML_INSTALL_DIR, then the unsuffixed default, then the most recently built suffixed dir containing a kernel), all three locators read it so artifacts never mix across flavors, and a non-default selection prints the active flavor.

Since this touches uml-veristat/**, the PR exercises the full 5-distro package matrix.

author: tamnd
body:
Pass B propagates contamination over the program to a fixpoint, taking Pass A's local verdicts and returning the verdicts that hold once cross-unit effects are accounted for. It stacks on the call graph.

The load-bearing property is containment. The naive rule, a compiled unit that calls an interpreted unit must itself be interpreted, is wrong and would collapse the whole program into the engine: a compiled unit calls an interpreted one perfectly well by paying a boundary crossing, so an ordinary call never contaminates. Pass B does nothing along ordinary call edges, and a test pins that a compiled caller of an interpreted callee stays compiled.

Contamination flows along exactly two edges instead. This slice realizes the control-inversion edge from section 4.4. A compiled function handed to an untyped callback position, an any or unknown parameter, can be called back from interpreted or unknown code with arguments of the wrong static type, so it needs entry guards, which makes it Speculative rather than Interpreted. The detection walks each unit body for a bare function reference passed into an argument position and reads the resolved signature to decide whether that position is typed. A concretely typed callback position, like the parameter of Array.map, does not invert, because the type system models exactly how the callback is called. A function that is called rather than passed by reference sits in callee position and never inverts. Only a cleanly compiled unit is promoted; a unit Pass A left interpreted for a hard blocker cannot be rescued by guards and is left alone.

One known imprecision: a call carrying explicit type arguments or a spread can misalign the argument-to-parameter mapping. The mapping is only ever read to decide whether a position is untyped, so a misalignment can add a guard, never drop one, which stays on the sound side. A later slice tightens it.

The other edge, the value-identity edge that drives boxing through escape analysis, is the second Pass B lattice and lands in its own slice over the call graph.

Tests drive real compiles: containment across an ordinary call, promotion through an any callback, no promotion through a typed callback, no promotion for an ordinary call, and no promotion of a hard-blocked unit.

author: rafay99-epic
body: ## Problem Desktop widgets were immovable, un-resizable, and un-closable in real use, and piled up on top of each other after connecting/disconnecting monitors (#—user report). ## Root cause (verified empirically with synthetic mouse drags on a Dev build) 1. **Desktop-pinned widgets never received mouse events.** With *keep on top* off (the default), panels sat at `desktopWindow + 1` — **below Finder's full-screen desktop-icons window** (layer −2147483603), which absorbs every click. A synthetic drag moved a floating widget (even with the app inactive) but a desktop-pinned one never budged (even with the app active). This is why it looked channel-dependent: Dev testing happened with floating widgets, Stable ran desktop-pinned. 2. **Nothing handled display changes.** `.stationary` panels aren't rescued by the system and saved frames were restored blind — during testing, the *combined* widget restored to CG y=986 on a 982-pt-tall screen: fully off-screen and unreachable. ## Fix - Desktop level is now `desktopIconWindow + 1`: still under every app window, still composites with the desktop on Space switches, but clickable. - `WidgetManager` observes `didChangeScreenParametersNotification` (debounced 0.6 s): a widget whose saved spot exists again snaps back to it; a stranded widget is re-tucked into the default top-right cascade. Saved spots are only written by a user drag, so unplug → replug round-trips every widget to where the user put it. - Launch-time restore clamps through the same geometry (`WidgetPlacement`, pure + unit-tested: 6 new tests). ## Verification - `swift test` green (all suites + 6 new `WidgetPlacementTests`). - Post-fix Dev build: desktop-pinned panels confirmed at layer −2147483602 via the window server; synthetic-drag verification of the desktop-pinned case was interrupted by concurrent real mouse input — manual confirmation pending on the Dev build. --- ## Summary by cubic Makes desktop-pinned widgets clickable and keeps them on-screen across display changes. Preserves the user’s placement by nudging partly off‑screen widgets back into view. - **Bug Fixes** - Place desktop widgets at `desktopIconWindow + 1` so they receive clicks while staying under app windows and compositing with the desktop. - Use `WidgetPlacement.rescued` for launch restore and display-change realign: keep fitting frames, nudge partly off-screen (e.g., Dock/resolution changes), and cascade only when fully stranded; debounce `didChangeScreenParametersNotification` by 0.6s. - **Refactors** - Add `WidgetPlacement` (pure geometry) with unit tests to lock placement rules. Written for commit 00475fa418ca98422ccf6bdd40732c0d3d02d550. Summary will update on new commits.

author: clarkse-he
body:
TITLE: DSMC molecular internal degrees of freedom (Borgnakke-Larsen rotation + vibration)

BASE: development   HEAD: Helion-Energy:dsmc-internal-dof
COMPANION: Helion-Energy/warpx-data  (adds MCC_cross_sections/D2/neutral_elastic.dat used by the tests)

## Summary
Adds molecular internal degrees of freedom (rotational + vibrational) with a Borgnakke-Larsen (BL)
energy-exchange model to the particle-particle DSMC collision operator. Previously DSMC was
translational-only; for molecular gases (H2/D2/N2 ...) this mispredicts temperature and Mach number
because a real diatomic stores a large fraction of its enthalpy in rotation (and, when hot, in
vibration). Rotation is treated as a classical continuous mode; vibration as a quantum harmonic
oscillator (so it stays frozen at low T and activates correctly when hot).

## What's added
- `DSMC/InternalDOF.H` — Larsen-Borgnakke samplers (classical rotational, quantum-harmonic
  vibrational), energies stored per-particle in eV.
- `DSMC/SplitAndScatterFunc.{H,cpp}` — BL redistribution in the elastic branch: with probability
  1/Z_rot (1/Z_vib) exchange energy between relative translation and each partner's internal modes,
  conserving the total collision energy; per-species BL parameters resolved host-side and captured
  into the kernel. (Rebased onto the recent ScatteringProcess::Executor refactor, #7001.)
- Runtime real components `E_rot` / `E_vib`, registered + initialized (Boltzmann at the species
  temperature) in `ParticleCreation/DefaultInitialization.H` and `AddParticles.cpp`, carried by
  SmartCopy + Redistribute.
- Per-species inputs on `PhysicalParticleContainer` / `WarpXParticleContainer`:
  `<species>.internal_dof = none|rotational|rovibrational` (+ `.theta_rot/.Z_rot/.rotational_dof`,
  `.theta_vib/.Z_vib`, `.rot_init_temperature/.vib_init_temperature`).

## Bug fix included (flux injection + resampling)
- `AddParticles.cpp`: runtime components are now communicated through the flux-injection temporary
  container's `Redistribute`. They were added with `communicate=false`, so particles migrating
  during that redistribute lost them (NaN internal energy). This also affects QED optical-depth /
  user attributes under flux injection generally.
- `PhysicalParticleContainer.cpp`: allow `leveling_thinning` resampling with internal DOF (survivors
  keep all attributes); only merging thinning remains guarded.

## Tests (`Examples/Tests/collision/`)
- `test_3d_dsmc_rotational_relaxation` — 0-D relaxation; asserts total (trans+rot) energy
  conservation and translation<->rotation equipartition.
- `test_3d_dsmc_rovibrational_relaxation` (labeled **slow**) — asserts rot/trans equipartition and
  quantum-suppressed vibrational energy (<E_vib> < kB T_eq).
- `test_2d_dsmc_rotational_flux` — flux injection + leveling-thinning resampling on a multi-box
  domain; asserts the E_rot runtime component survives Redistribute (guards the bug fix above).
All gate on physics (energy conservation / equipartition), not platform-dependent checksums; fast
variants run in ~1 s.

## Companion data
Elastic collisions in the tests use a D2 hard-sphere cross section added to warpx-data at
`MCC_cross_sections/D2/neutral_elastic.dat` (constant sigma = 2.642e-19 m^2). That one-file
warpx-data PR must merge first (or alongside) for CI to find the table.

## Not included (follow-ups)
- Weight-averaging E_rot/E_vib in merging (velocity-coincidence) resampling.
- C++ RotationalTemperature/VibrationalTemperature reduced diagnostics.
- Threading internal energy into the cross-section lookup; dissociation channel; QK reactions.

author: vocksel
body:
## Problem

An agent with no prior context has no way to bootstrap itself onto a gateway: the BindableFunction's name and parent are consumer-chosen, nothing marks it as an AgentGateway, and the protocol is only documented outside the place. Wrong guesses return terse errors (`unknown method "nil"`) that teach nothing. Meanwhile `inputSchema` is dead metadata — the library never validates params against it, so every consumer hand-rolls defensive `asTable`/`getStringField` boilerplate (see flipbook-labs/flipbook#604), and the example plugin's gateway shares the name `FlipbookAgentGateway` with the real Flipbook gateway, so installing both has them destroy each other's bindable.

## Solution

Shrink what an agent must be told down to one universal convention, make the gateway itself teach the rest, and move the repeated consumer work into the library:

- **Discovery:** every gateway is tagged with the `AgentGateway` CollectionService tag and carries `Description`, `Usage` (one-line protocol summary), and `ProtocolVersion` attributes. An agent still learns to look for the tag from instructions (the new `use-agent-gateway` skill, a consumer repo's docs, or the user's prompt) — the tag's job is to make that required knowledge a single convention shared by every gateway, independent of names, parents, or which plugins are installed. `TAG` and `PROTOCOL_VERSION` are exported constants.
- **Self-describing protocol:** the `list` manifest now returns `{protocolVersion, name, description, instructions, actions}`; `Config` gains `description` and `instructions` (agent-facing prose). Every malformed-request error restates the full request grammar; unknown-action errors list the valid names.
- **Library-side params validation:** required/type/enum enforcement with unknown-param rejection, quoting the schema in every error (e.g. `invalid params for openStory: missing required param "story" (string) — Path to a .story ModuleScript`). Schemas themselves are validated at registry construction. Actions receive a guaranteed table.
- **Result guard:** non-JSON-encodable action results become a clear `ok = false` error blaming the action instead of failing on the agent's side of the boundary.
- **Protocol version is library-owned** (`PROTOCOL_VERSION = 2`) instead of consumer-passed.
- **Docs:** new generic `.agents/skills/use-agent-gateway` skill (Studio MCP setup/troubleshooting, discovery, protocol reference) for consumer repos to reference; the e2e skill moved from `.claude/skills/` to `.agents/skills/` and updated; root `CLAUDE.md` index added; README rewritten.
- **Example plugin** renamed to `ExampleAgentGateway` and slimmed to domain-only validation.

## Testing

- `lute run lint`, `lute run analyze`, `lute run build`, and `lute run build-example` all pass locally.
- New/updated jest specs cover the tag/attributes, enriched manifest, teaching errors, the full validation matrix (`validateParams.spec.luau`), and the JSON-encodability guard — they need Open Cloud, so CI runs them.
- The pure-Luau validation modules were additionally smoke-tested under Lute locally (16 checks, all passing).

## Notes for reviewers

Breaking changes throughout (v0): `Config.protocolVersion` is gone, `run` now receives a guaranteed params table, and the manifest shape changed. flipbook-labs/flipbook#604 has follow-ups planned to adopt this (move its `getInstructions` action into `Config.instructions`, delete validation boilerplate, use schema `enum`s).

## Summary
Fixes tests/spec/commit-signing.bats test case "G-SEC05: adjusted unsigned-Anteil auf main (ohne Bot) ist <= 5%", which fails on current origin/main.

## Root cause
`BOT_EMAIL` in the test only matched the canonical `<id>+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com` noreply address. `.github/workflows/codebase-memory-regen.yml` configures git with the bare `github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com` form (no numeric id prefix) for its auto-commit step. Those bot commits are unsigned and leaked into the "non-bot unsigned" bucket, pushing the ratio above the 5% G-SEC05 threshold.

## Fix
Narrowed `BOT_EMAIL` to the common suffix shared by both noreply email variants (`github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com`). `grep -F` substring-matches, so this now excludes bot commits under either email format, matching the SSOT intent (exclude all github-actions[bot] commits from the unsigned-signing metric) rather than one specific address string.

author: ciaranm
body:
Third slice of the fluent constraint-options cleanup (#299), after linear (#451) and arithmetic (#452).

## What changes

The Element family's `bounds_only` bool becomes a consistency choice:

```cpp
// before
p.post(Element{var, idx, &array, /*bounds_only=*/true});
// after
p.post(Element{var, idx, &array}.with_consistency(consistency::BC{}));
```

- `with_consistency()` takes `ElementConsistency = std::variant<consistency::GAC, consistency::BC>` → unsupported level is a compile error.
- `bounds_only` only affects the propagator, never `define_proof_model`, so the "consistency never changes the OPB encoding" rule holds.
- **Behaviour-preserving:** the per-type defaults are kept — `Element`/`Element2D` default to GAC, `ElementConstantArray`/`Element2DConstantArray` to BC. Each wrapper passes its own default to the protected base ctor (mirroring how linear keeps `flipped_cond` internal). No call site anywhere passed `bounds_only` explicitly, so nothing else changes.
- The `element_test` var path now drives `with_consistency(consistency::GAC{})` end-to-end (a no-op vs the default, so the `checking_gac` assertion stays valid).

## ⚠️ Query for review (not addressed here)

The catalogue flagged the **default flip** as a footgun: `Element` defaults to GAC but `ElementConstantArray` defaults to BC, so same-looking calls propagate differently. I've **preserved** that flip because unifying the defaults is a *functional* change, out of scope for this API-cleanup pass. If you'd like the defaults unified (e.g. everything GAC by default), that's a small separate PR — flag it and I'll do it.

## Verification

- Full `cmake --build` of all targets — clean.
- `ctest -R element` → 12/12, including cake chain-verify `scp_chain_element*`.
- clang-format 21 clean.

author: davidobando
body:
Fixes #1638

Five call sites in `src/Core/CodeAnalysis/Binding/ExpressionBinder.Calls.cs` (ctor, static, instance, inherited-instance, imported-extension) each ran their own copy of the CLR call-argument-construction sequence (`RebindFormattableInterpolationArguments` -> `ApplyInterpolatedStringHandlers` -> delegate rebind -> `BindClrParameterConversions`). The copies had drifted apart: some skipped steps.

## What changed

- Extracted a single shared helper, `BuildResolvedClrCallArguments`, that runs the four-step pipeline once. All five call sites now call it.
- `RebindFormattableInterpolationArguments` gained an optional `receiverArgCount` parameter so it can be applied safely to the extension path's receiver-offset argument shape.
- Added a `ClrCallDelegateRebindMode` enum (`Full` / `NumericWideningOnly`) so the extension path's intentional narrower delegate rebind (issues #1150 / #1334, avoids an ilverify StackUnexpected mismatch on generic LINQ dispatch) is preserved through the shared helper instead of being lost.

## Drift bugs fixed (with proving tests)

- **Ctor path**: never ran the delegate-rebind step, so a value-returning arrow-lambda argument could not target a delegate-typed (`System.Action`) constructor parameter. Fixed by routing through the full pipeline. Proven by `Ctor_ArrowLambda_ValueReturning_ToActionParameter_VoidizesAndRuns`.
- **Inherited-instance path**: never ran the interpolation-rebind step, so an interpolated-string argument could not target an `IFormattable`/`FormattableString` parameter of a member inherited from an imported CLR base class. This also required passing `interpolatedStringArgs` into that path's `OverloadResolution.Resolve` call (a companion, pre-existing gate that was rejecting the candidate before the pipeline ever ran) — matching the flag already passed at the ctor and instance call sites. Proven by `InheritedInstance_InterpolatedString_ToFormattableStringParameter_Rebinds`.

## Intentional divergences preserved (not drift)

- Extension path's numeric-return-widening-only delegate rebind (issues #1150/#1334) — kept via `ClrCallDelegateRebindMode.NumericWideningOnly`.
- Instance path's split between the enumerable-normalized receiver type fed to delegate rebind and the raw receiver type fed to parameter conversions — kept via a `conversionReceiverType` override parameter on the helper.

## Out of scope (flagging, not deferring)

While tracing the `interpolatedStringArgs` resolution flag, found it is also missing from the static-path and extension-path `OverloadResolution.Resolve` calls (and the static path's deeper `classSymbol.TryLookupFunction` resolution mechanism). That's a related but distinct gap, not part of the four-step pipeline this issue names, and touches shared resolution internals used well beyond these five sites. Left as-is here; worth a follow-up issue if interpolated-string-to-FormattableString static/extension calls turn out to need it too.

## Testing

- `dotnet build GSharp.sln -c Release` — 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `dotnet test test/Core.Tests/Core.Tests.csproj -c Release` — 5215 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (`RegenerateBaseline`, confirming the IL baseline is unchanged for the already-correct static/instance paths).
- `dotnet test test/Compiler.Tests/Compiler.Tests.csproj -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Interpolat|FullyQualifiedName~Extension|FullyQualifiedName~Ctor|FullyQualifiedName~Constructor"` — 163 passed, 0 failed.
- Two new regression tests added, proving the two drift-bug fixes above.

author: basnijholt
body:
## Problem

Every dev-mode session with `__ENABLE_SERVICE_WORKER__` enabled (e.g. the lab deployment) logs:

```
dev-sw.js?dev-sw:1 Uncaught SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module
```

and silently runs without a service worker (registration failure is swallowed by design). Two stacked bugs, both dev-only and pre-existing (not from #44 — last touched by the mobile-shell commit):

1. **Classic registration of an ES-module worker.** vite-plugin-pwa's `devOptions.type` is `'module'`, so `dev-sw.js` is served with bare `import` statements, but `src/index.tsx` registered it without `type: 'module'` → the reported SyntaxError.
2. **Empty precache manifest kills evaluation.** Even registered as a module, the dev worker failed: dev injects `precacheAndRoute([])` and `createHandlerBoundToURL('index.html')` throws for non-precached URLs at evaluation time.

## Fix

- Register with the matching worker type per mode (`classic` for the built `sw.js`, `module` for `dev-sw.js`).
- Gate the navigation fallback on a non-empty precache manifest; the media-auth fetch handler works without it in dev.
- Source-guard test updated to pin the new shape including the dev-evaluation guard.

## Verification

- Driven live against the dev server via CDP: classic registration reproduces the exact SyntaxError; after the fix, the app's own boot path registers `dev-sw.js?dev-sw`, it activates, and controls the page.
- Production `dist/sw.js` verified intact after `npm run build`: 17 precache entries, `index.html` fallback and denylist present.
- `npm test` 2,346 passed · typecheck · lint at 18-warning baseline.

body:
Final connector slice for **FEAT_0036**, on the merged M2b (#174). Adds the real `rumqttc` backend, TLS, username/password, and a broker-in-CI integration job. The mock stays the default backend; a plain build pulls no `rumqttc`.

Closes #170.

## Built (test-first)
- **`RealMqttSession`** over `rumqttc 0.24` behind default-off `rumqttc-integration` — builds `MqttOptions` (credentials on CONNECT, keep-alive, clean-session), maps `MqttQos`→`rumqttc::QoS`, and pumps the `EventLoop` which **owns reconnect** per ADR_0128 (ConnAck→Up + counter reset, connection error→Connecting + backoff, auth-reject→terminal Down). Inbound routes through the existing `InboundRouter` seam; no `connector.rs` changes (it monomorphizes over the real session). — REQ_0257, REQ_0255
- **TLS** via `rustls` behind default-off `tls` (= `rumqttc/use-rustls`); `TlsConfiguration::Simple` with a CA PEM; client-cert deferred. — REQ_0256
- **Broker-in-CI** (`.github/workflows/ci-mqtt.yml`) — mosquitto via `namoshek/mosquitto-github-action@v1` (1883 + 8883), password file + self-signed CA/cert generated at job time (**no keys committed**); runs `real_broker.rs` (plain round-trip, auth accept/reject, TLS handshake) with `rumqttc-integration,tls`. Tests skip when `MQTT_TEST_BROKER` is unset, so they no-op locally.

## Requirements
REQ_0255, REQ_0256, REQ_0257.

## 👀 Human review focus
- **`.github/workflows/ci-mqtt.yml`** (new) — first live-broker CI job + cert generation. Minor: `mosquitto.conf` uses `allow_anonymous true`; auth-reject still works, but `allow_anonymous false` would be stricter.
- `src/real.rs` — the event-loop pump self-spawns via `tokio::spawn` on the caller's runtime (rumqttc idiom); `connect()` must be called inside a tokio runtime.

## Verify — all gates green locally
fmt · test `--all-features` (broker tests skip) · `--no-default-features` · clippy `--all-features` · `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc` · complexity · check-publish-deps · lean-default (0 rumqttc in default tree). **Independently ran the broker tests against a real mosquitto (docker): plain round-trip + auth accept/reject pass.**

author: karlheitmann
body:
### Task: ###

- https://linear.app/signinsolutions/issue/VMC-589/update-tractionguestscim-rails-gem-to-use-rails-8

### Stacked PRs: ###

- ➡️ Part 1 PR: #73
- Part 2 PR: #74

### Description: ###

ParameterService validates incoming params against the user schema and rejects anything it doesn't recognize. It was missing the SCIM query parameters attributes and excludedAttributes (RFC 7644 3.9), which control the shape of the response rather than being writable attributes.

Because attributes wasn't in `KEYS_TO_IGNORE`, the `check_allowed_parameters!` before-action rejected requests like `PATCH /Users/:id?attributes=userName` with a 400 Unknown fields before `patch_update` could run, so the endpoint never returned 200 with the user resource, and its test failed.

Two related PATCH tests in `scim_users_request_spec.rb` were also failing. Both expected 200 but the endpoint now returns 204: commit a7a3299 ("Return HTTP 204 unless attributes requested") changed `patch_update` to return 204 No Content unless `?attributes=` is requested, and it updated `scim_users_controller_spec.rb` but never updated the request spec. One assertion predated that change (left stale), and the other was added afterward in `b11f242` with the wrong expectation. Both were corrected to 204.

Fixing the status assertion exposed a second issue in the "maps attributes by type" test: `get_multi_value_attrs` only ran its type-based mapping when `operation["value"].is_a?(Hash)`, but in a real request that value is an `ActionController::Parameters` (not a Hash), so the mapping was silently skipped and emails were assigned by array position instead of by SCIM type. `get_multi_value_attrs` now also accepts `ActionController::Parameters`.



###  Changes: ###

- Add attributes and excludedAttributes to ParameterService::KEYS_TO_IGNORE.
- Update two stale 200 → 204 PATCH assertions in scim_users_request_spec.rb.
- Accept ActionController::Parameters (not just Hash) in get_multi_value_attrs so email type-mapping runs on real requests.


- Bump gem version to v0.10.1.

author: gandy2025
body:
## Problem
`first-tree-welcome` delegates repo creation / binding / seeding to `first-tree-seed`, which runs in a **tree-less** spawned build-tree chat (it exists precisely because no Context Tree binding exists yet). The runtime installer shipped `first-tree-seed` and `first-tree-write` only via `TREE_SKILL_NAMES`, which `agent-bootstrap.ts` installs only `if (contextTreePath)`. So in the tree-less build-tree chat, seed was never on disk → the delegation broke → the agent fell back to raw `gh`.

## Fix
- Move `first-tree-seed` and `first-tree-write` from `TREE_SKILL_NAMES` to `CORE_SKILL_NAMES` (always installed, tree or not).
  - `first-tree-write` must move with `first-tree-seed`: `first-tree-seed/SKILL.md` loads `../first-tree-write/SKILL.md` by relative reference and inherits its Hard Rules. Installing seed without write leaves a dangling reference in the tree-less chat.
  - `first-tree-read` stays tree-only — there is nothing to read without a bound tree.
- Guard `reconcileTreeSkillState` so it never removes a `CORE_SKILL_NAMES` member. For an existing tree-bound agent whose `managed.json::skills` still lists seed/write under the old TREE tier, `installCoreSkills` installs them first; without the guard the tree reconcile would delete them immediately after.
- Sync two now-stale rationale comments (`agent-bootstrap.ts`, `agent-briefing.ts`) that assumed tree-less agents have no skill payloads on disk (they now do).

## Tests
- Retarget the multi-skill installer-engine describe block to `installCoreSkills` (now a 3-skill set) to preserve engine coverage (fast-path skip, VERSION drift, content drift, missing-VERSION reinstall, clobbered-symlink repair, partial failure).
- Add an `installFirstTreeIntegration (tree-only skills)` describe covering the `first-tree-read` happy path + per-skill failure log.
- Add a `skills-state-reconcile` regression proving core skills listed in prior managed state survive the reconcile (mutation-verified: fails without the guard).
- `@first-tree/client`: 1191 tests pass; `typecheck` + `biome` clean.

No DB / schema / API changes. Implementation-only — makes the already-documented `welcome → seed` delegation actually work; no Context Tree PR needed.

- **Scrollable live preview** — the preview now always renders below the composer and is reachable by scrolling, so it stays visible while the keyboard is open instead of being gated behind the keyboard state (matches iOS, where the whole screen scrolls).
- **iOS-style corner tag** — a small "Preview" pill sits flush in the top-right corner inside the preview box, rather than crowded under the username.

Since the bottom nav is already hidden while composing, `imePadding` alone lifts the column correctly.

body:
## Objectif

**Consolidation** des 3 PR web qui modifiaient toutes `Manoir - Exploration.html` depuis la même base (elles se seraient mises en conflit au fur et à mesure des merges), **+ un 4ᵉ lot « vie du manoir »**. Une seule PR web propre. Remplace **#218**, **#220**, **#221**.

## Contenu (4 lots)

### 1. Réglages UI (ex-#218)
- **Joystick masqué pendant un dialogue** (il recouvrait la carte de dialogue).
- **Minimap réduite** : `160×140 → 118×103` px (canvas interne inchangé).

### 2. Sortie de l'Exploration (ex-#220)
- Bouton **« ‹ »** en haut-gauche → retour à l'écran d'accueil/routines du profil courant.
- Libellé de salle décalé pour ne plus passer sous la bannière de mission.

### 3. Mission 2 « La Salle des miroirs » (ex-#221)
Deuxième mission guidée avec **6 garde-fous** : halo Lampyre permanent · 3 éclats de miroir lumineux (biblio/galerie/atelier) · réplique de Lampyre par éclat · minimap révèle la Salle des miroirs après 2 éclats · indice du puzzle conservé · **récompense : luminosité du Grand Hall indexée au nombre de verres d'eau bus** (via l'énigme optique déjà codée). Machine à états `ombrelune_mirror_quest`. `Compagnon - Énigme optique.html` marque la victoire (`data-act="win"`).

### 4. Vie du manoir — PNJ + interactivité (nouveau, « Vague 1 »)
Le manoir paraissait grand et vide : on le **peuple** (ambiance d'abord, liaison aux routines prévue en Vague 2).
- **4 PNJ décoratifs animés (Canvas)** : Sylvain le majordome (balai), Doria la liseuse (livre), Vétch le jardinier (arrosoir), Ombeline la gouvernante. Halo chaud, idle animé, accessoire de métier → POI **« Parler à … »** (réplique de Lampyre).
- **4 points d'observation « Observer »** sur le mobilier existant (télescope, portraits, puits, trophées) : léger scintillement à repérer → réplique.
- Chaque spot ouvre un petit trou de brouillard pour être découvert en explorant. POI de **plus basse priorité** : n'interfère ni avec l'eau, ni avec les miroirs, ni avec les escaliers.

## Fichiers

- `web/manoir-td/Manoir - Exploration.html`
- `web/manoir-td/Compagnon - Énigme optique.html`

## Contraintes

- **100% Canvas 2D / vanilla**, aucune dépendance ajoutée. Réutilise le moteur POI + dialogue Lampyre existant.
- Store partagé `ombrelune_*` + event `storage` (sync live eau ↔ jeu). Rétrocompatible Mission 1.

## Vérification (headless Playwright)

Parcours complet + PNJ validés, **0 erreur JS** :
- Mission 2 : `dark → seeking → found → puzzle → solved`, minimap révèle la salle à 2 éclats, Grand Hall éclairé selon l'eau.
- PNJ/observation : 8 spots (4 PNJ + 4 points), POI « Parler »/« Observer » → dialogues ; aucune interférence avec les missions.

Déploiement auto au merge (Firebase Hosting) — aucun build Flutter requis.

author: aarongrace978
body: The scene was already computed from the real sun and moon. This makes everything else in it real too — still zero dependencies, zero network calls at runtime, all solved live in the browser: - **Real tides.** A 28-constituent harmonic tide prediction for Boston Harbor (NOAA station 8443970), fitted against NOAA's own published predictions for 2026–2027. Agreement: ~1.5 cm RMS; high/low times within 1–3 minutes of the official tables. The water level in the scene now rises and falls with the actual tide — the seawall drowns at high water and bares at low. New almanac card shows current height, direction, and the next high/low. - **The real stars.** A ~1,000-star catalog (Yale BSC, mag ≤ 4.6) embedded and rotated with sidereal time, with color from B-V index and extinction near the horizon. Orion genuinely rises over the harbor in winter. Twenty constellation stick figures fade in during deep night. - **The real planets.** Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn positioned by solving Kepler's equation from JPL's approximate elements — verified against JPL Horizons to under 0.5°. Labeled faintly in deep night; new almanac card reports where each one is. - **Meteor showers on schedule.** On the real peak nights (Perseids Aug 12, Geminids Dec 13, and seven others) the sky's meteor rate jumps and the status line notes it. Verification (all done before this PR): - Tide model vs NOAA predictions API: 1.5 cm RMS over 17,520 hourly points, extremes within 3 min / 1 cm. - Planet RA/Dec vs JPL Horizons for 2026-07-03: all four within 0.5°. - Headless-browser screenshots across July night, pre-dawn, Perseids peak, December (Orion up): no console errors, reduced-motion still works.
