author: reissbaker
body:
Previously, scrollbars had to be rendered in JS. This is annoying and silly, since every app that used `overflow: scroll` needed to rebuild scrollbars from scratch; and if you want a *really* nice scrollbar, you'd need to even build the click-and-drag handling yourself.

Not only that, but some scrolling features aren't even possible to build within JS. For example, since text selection is implemented in the native Rust engine, selecting-and-dragging inside of scroll views is painful to make correct: in a browser or native window, typically that causes the scroll to move and text to continue selecting. That's hard to do right in JS if Rust is unaware of scrolling dynamics, since text selection happens on the Rust side of the border (since it requires layout knowledge + hit testing).

This implements native scrolling in Rust. The scrollbars are rendered in Rust but are styleable with CSS `scrollbar-color` (to set the thumb and track color: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/scrollbar-color) and `scrollbar-gutter` (to determine whether the layout engine always reserves space for the scrollbar, or if it only reserves space when there's overflow content: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/scrollbar-gutter), just like an ordinary web brower.

author: bgi-pres
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #497 (`docs/institutional-elevation-report-2026-07-03.md`) — this closes the **#1 highest-priority P0** from that audit: the public data room's NDA/password/email gate was client-side theater.

**Before:** `app/dataroom/[token]/page.tsx` shipped every ready document's full content, team member emails, and track-record figures in the initial server-rendered payload **regardless of gate config**. A client-side `gatePassed` boolean decided whether to blur it — skippable via `localStorage`, and the real content was already readable from view-source without ever entering a password or accepting the NDA. The document-open route (`d/[id]/route.ts`) checked only token validity/expiry, never the gate itself or the share's `allowed_sections` whitelist.

**After:** gate-passage is a server-verified fact, checked *before* any confidential query runs — not a client claim hidden behind CSS.

## What changed

- **`lib/data-room-gate.ts`** (new) — a signed, HttpOnly cookie recording which gates (password/NDA/email) a visitor has satisfied for a *specific* share. It is only ever written by code that has independently verified the corresponding gate:
  - `pwd` — set after a real password comparison succeeds
  - `nda` — set after an NDA signature row is actually inserted
  - `email` — set after a syntactically valid email is captured (data capture, not a secret)
  
  Nothing trusts a client-supplied "I already did this" claim. Tamper and expiry are rejected — covered by `lib/data-room-gate.test.ts` (10 tests: satisfied-gate matrix, cross-share isolation, signature tamper detection, TTL expiry).

- **`verifySharePassword` / `recordNdaSignature` / new `passEmailGate`** — each now grants its gate via the signed cookie on real server-side success, instead of just returning a boolean for the client to act on unilaterally.

- **`app/dataroom/[token]/page.tsx`** — the gate check now runs *before* the org/thesis/track-record/team/entities/documents queries. An ungated visitor gets a minimal branding-only render (name/logo/accent — not confidential) plus the gate UI; only a server-verified pass unlocks the real data fetch and full props. There is no longer any confidential data in the payload to leak.

- **`app/dataroom/[token]/d/[id]/route.ts`** — now enforces the same gate check plus the share's `allowed_sections` whitelist before redirecting to a document, closing the direct-link bypass the prior version had.

- **`components/dataroom/{DataRoomViewer,ViewerGate}.tsx`** — the client now renders purely off a `contentReady` prop from the server. Passing the gate calls `router.refresh()` so the Server Component re-fetches with the now-valid pass, rather than a local boolean unblurring content that was already present in the payload. Also drops the spoofable `localStorage`-based stage-skipping in favor of the server-side pass (which naturally covers "returning visitor" without a client-side mechanism a visitor can forge).

## Testing
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx next lint` — clean
- `npx jest` — **125 suites / 1461 tests green** (10 new)
- `npx next build` — succeeds

author: jake-sh
body:
## Summary
Delivers a push notification to every **other** project member when a chat message is sent — working while the PWA is backgrounded **or fully closed**, on both Android and iOS 16.4+ (PWA installed to home screen).

### Client
- `src/lib/messaging.ts`: FCM token register/unregister via `getToken` (VAPID key), bound to the existing service worker. Gracefully no-ops where push isn't supported or the VAPID key isn't configured.
- **Settings → Notifications toggle** now requests browser permission and registers/removes this device's token. Tokens are stored per-device under `users/{uid}/fcmTokens/{token}`.
- `PushTokenSync` refreshes the token on app open for already-opted-in users (FCM tokens rotate; never prompts).
- `public/sw.js`: added `push` + `notificationclick` handlers. The server sends **data-only** messages so the SW always builds/shows the notification itself (iOS requires a notification per push) and focuses/opens `/chat` on tap. Cache bumped `v3 → v4`.

### Server (`functions/`)
- Cloud Function `sendChatNotification`: a Firestore `onDocumentCreated` trigger on `projects/{projectId}/messages/{messageId}`. Because it's event-triggered serverless, it fires on the message write **no matter how long the app has been idle** — there's no server to keep awake / spin down. It excludes the sender, skips members who turned notifications off, fans out to their device tokens via `sendEachForMulticast`, and prunes tokens FCM reports as permanently invalid.
- `firestore.rules`: owner-only read/write on the `fcmTokens` subcollection (the function reads them via the Admin SDK, which bypasses rules).
- `tsconfig.json` / `eslint.config.mjs` exclude `functions/` (it has its own Node toolchain and build output).

## ⚠️ Required manual steps to go live (outside the Vercel deploy)
1. **Enable the Firebase Blaze plan** on `co-work-fd9d3` (Cloud Functions require it; there's a large free tier of invocations, but a billing account must be attached).
2. **Generate a Web Push certificate** (Firebase console → Project settings → Cloud Messaging → Web configuration → *Web Push certificates* → generate key pair) and set it as `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_VAPID_KEY` in the **Vercel** project env (then redeploy). Without it, push registration is silently disabled.
3. Deploy the backend (not part of Vercel):
   ```
   firebase deploy --only functions,firestore:rules
   ```

## Test plan
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` passes (app)
- [x] `functions` package compiles (`npm --prefix functions run build`)
- [x] `npm run lint` passes (no new errors; `functions/` excluded)
- [x] `npm run build` compiles successfully — `firebase/messaging` bundles fine (prerender failure is the pre-existing missing-Firebase-env-var issue in this sandbox, unrelated)
- [ ] After the manual steps: install the PWA on an Android device and an iOS 16.4+ device, enable Notifications in Settings (grant permission), fully close the app, have another member send a chat message → notification arrives and tapping it opens the chat
- [ ] Toggle Notifications off → that device stops receiving push

author: angriff36
body:
## Manifest 3.x native migration + schema truth campaign

48 commits taking capsule-pro from manifest 2.22.0 glue to 3.1.3 native, and — the bulk of the work — making the generated Prisma schema **structurally identical to the real database**.

### Schema truth (the headline)

An `information_schema` reconciliation of the generated schema against the live database found **~1,114 structural drifts** across seven classes. End state:

| Class | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Nullable-in-schema over NOT NULL columns | 826 | **0** |
| Required-in-schema over nullable columns | 28 | **0** |
| Schema columns missing from the DB | 179 | **0** |
| Type mismatches | 81 | **10** (D27-owned PrepTaskPlanWorkflow jsonb fields, deliberate) |

- **Root cause was upstream**: the Prisma projection ignored the DSL's own `?` nullability marker. Fixed in manifest **3.1.0** (with json literal defaults and string-safe json store coercion), then **3.1.1** (Prisma 7.8 config shape, `@db.Money` expressible), **3.1.2** (dead `request` param in 159 generated routes), **3.1.3** (OpenAPI documents json as objects).
- Sources now declare truth: 1,198 properties gained `?` (one `SoftDeletable` mixin edit covered 103), 41 jsonb-backed fields became `json` (several **crashed live pages** as raw text: invoice detail, public proposal view, event summaries, RolePolicy reads+writes), 88 missing domain fields + 46 missing `deletedAt` mixins applied from a live-DB-derived spec, 22 money columns annotated `@db.Money`, `KitchenTask.tags` became the `text[]` it always was.
- **Migration `20260703005048_schema_truth_additive`** (applied to dev, prod via deploy workflow): 6 new tables, missing columns, `SET NOT NULL` on 33 engine-owned timestamps (with defensive backfill), scalar-list NULL repair (`events.accessibility_options` had 2,524 NULL rows). Idempotent throughout — a partial first apply proved `migrate deploy` ran statements non-transactionally here.

### Runtime wiring

- **Engine outbox events now reach SSE**: the engine wrote to `manifest_outbox_entries`, which nothing drains. The legacy-table adapter (built for this, zero call sites) is now wired — after fixing a zero-UUID tenantId bug, channel-vs-name eventType, and a wrong status enum (pinned by new unit tests). The one double-publishing route dropped its hand-written outbox block.
- **Async-reaction queue actually drains**: no cron existed and the drain route was POST-only while Vercel Cron only sends GET. GET now drains when cron-authorized; every-minute cron added.
- **Phase 6 realtime**: engine publishes committed event batches to per-tenant Redis channels (`manifest:events:{tenantId}`); the SSE route subscribes per stream. No-ops until `REDIS_URL` is set.
- `manifest/runtime` was still pinning manifest **2.22.0** (missed in the 3.0.0 bump — two library copies in the tree); fixed.

### Verification (all fresh, this branch tip)

- Full-monorepo typecheck: **2,340 errors vs 2,354 at the merge base — zero new-on-branch** (branch peaked at +1,232 during the migration).
- `manifest:ci` fully green end-to-end, including `audit:strict` with its baseline **shrunk by 55 healed entries**.
- `manifest/runtime` tests: 527/527 (six pre-existing failures fixed — mixin-base entities excluded from structural conformance by IR-derived rule; timecard tests used lowercase role names against case-sensitive `roleAllows`).
- `prisma validate` + `generate` green; all five drift gates no-drift.

### Parked owner decisions (documented, not blocking)

- D27: the 10 PrepTaskPlanWorkflow jsonb fields stay `string` until the bespoke store migrates.
- `versionProperty` design: `version`/`versionAt` columns exist in the DB but no source declares them (16 fields).
- Duplicate DSL entities (QACorrectiveAction≈CorrectiveAction, QATemperatureLog≈TemperatureLog, LogisticsRoute≈DeliveryRoute, BankAccount≈infra `employee_bank_accounts`): their declared tables now exist (empty); dedupe is a design call.
- Prod `manifest_outbox_entries` backlog count + eventual DROP (table is now vestigial).
- Engine events can arrive twice (Redis bus instantly + outbox cron ≤60s); SSE consumers refetch idempotently.

author: obi1kenobi
body:
Previously, adding a generic param to a parent `impl` scope could cause
the normalized generic params of functions in that `impl` to get
renumbered, making it look like those functions' signatures had
themselves changed as well.

This PR separates the normalization for parent, item, and higher-ranked
generics so that they all use separate namespaces, and can grow and
shrink independently. This will cut down on unnecessary (and expensive!)
type checks and will make `cargo-semver-checks` lints more efficient.

Supersedes #1086 which was irreversibly closed due to what appears to be
a GitHub bug.

author: eurus7895
body:
## Why

`musubi setup`'s console-GUI install ran `npm install` and checked the Rust/MSVC toolchain, but never generated the desktop icons. Tauri's `beforeDevCommand` runs only vite, so on a fresh clone `npm run tauri:dev` fails inside the Windows build script on a missing `icons/icon.ico` (the `.ico`/`.icns` are generated artifacts, not committed). This surfaced in real use: a fresh clone could not launch the GUI locally without an undocumented manual `npx tauri icon` step.

A second papercut: the linker check hard-failed when `link.exe` wasn't on `PATH`, even on machines where MSVC was installed — cargo finds the linker via `vswhere`, so a `PATH` miss is a false negative.

## What changed

`install_console_gui` (`musubi/setup_wizard.py`) now runs the whole `npm run tauri:dev` prerequisite chain:

- `npm install` (unchanged)
- Rust-toolchain check (unchanged)
- **MSVC linker check made robust** — falls back to `vswhere` (querying the `VC.Tools.x86.x64` component) when `link.exe` isn't on `PATH`, instead of hard-failing.
- **New: `npx tauri icon src-tauri/icons/icon.png`** — generates `icon.ico` / `icon.icns` from the source PNG, closing the gap that broke `tauri:dev`.

The icon step is best-effort and guarded (skips if `npx` or the source PNG is unexpectedly absent); a non-zero `tauri icon` exit reports a clear, actionable message. `vswhere` is looked up with `os.path` rather than `pathlib` so the existing `os.name`-monkeypatched tests don't try to instantiate a `WindowsPath` on the test host.

## Tests

- Updated the missing-linker test for the new message wording.
- Added `test_install_console_gui_generates_icons_when_toolchain_ready` (asserts the `npx tauri icon` invocation and success message).
- Added `test_install_console_gui_reports_icon_generation_failure` (asserts the failure path surfaces the exit code).
- `pytest musubi/tests/test_setup_wizard.py` → 34 passed; full `pytest musubi/tests` → 1230 passed, 1 skipped. No new ruff findings.

body:
## Summary

Brings the app's location + notification stack to working order, adds three user-facing sighting features, packages the backend as a zero-install server, and fixes the critical gaps found in a full requirement audit.

## What's included

**Config / infrastructure**
- Align Firebase config to the `wild-cat-watch-1e4f2` project (app + backend now share one project; fixes SenderIdMismatch on push).
- LAN auto-discovery via mDNS: the backend advertises `_wildcat._tcp`; the app discovers it at startup and on network change, so it keeps working across Wi-Fi changes with no config edits (`bonsoir` + `zeroconf`).
- Zero-install standalone server: a double-click `WildCatServer.exe` (PyInstaller) that switches to SQLite, auto-migrates, creates a default admin, advertises on the LAN, and serves via waitress. No Python/pip/MySQL/terminal needed.

**Features**
- Own reported sightings: new `GET /api/sightings/mine/` (+ `is_mine`/`status`); map shows your last-7-day reports as green markers; profile lists your report history with pending/verified badges.
- Adjustable alert radius from the profile (`sighting_radius_km`); the nearby endpoint and push notifications both respect each user's own radius.
- Clearer map: a single "alert zone" circle around you (your radius) instead of a circle per sighting; de-duplicated, colour-coded markers.

**Critical fixes (from the audit)**
- C1: serve uploaded sighting images in every mode (Django `static()` only served media when `DEBUG=True`, so images 404'd in the packaged server).
- C3: auto-verify reported sightings (`AUTO_VERIFY_SIGHTINGS`, default on) so nearby users are alerted in real time; admin verify still works.
- C4: refresh the user's location every 5 min while the app is open and widen the backend freshness window to 120 min, so recipients aren't silently dropped.

## Testing
- Backend: full suite green (35/35), incl. a new real-time auto-verify test. Also fixed a pre-existing positions-lookup test that broke once seed data was added.
- App: `flutter analyze` clean.
- Packaged exe verified end-to-end: register → login → report-with-image → auto-verify → mine/nearby → image served → radius.

## Notes
- Secrets stay out of git (`.env`, `firebase_service_account.json`, the exe, runtime data, and dev `media/` are all ignored).
- The standalone exe embeds the Firebase credential for zero-touch use (intentional; not for public distribution) and also accepts an external `firebase_service_account.json` next to the exe.

## Summary

- apply the CSS HMR shared-stylesheet de-duplication behavior from #14580 to the built-in CSS `exportType: "link"` runtime
- keep one HMR stylesheet load per resolved CSS URL while preserving all chunk ids that share that stylesheet
- add an e2e case for `exportType: "link"` where `main` and the split CSS chunk both resolve to `static/style.css`

Example: when `output.cssFilename` is fixed to `static/style.css`, a hot update can list both `main` and `style` chunks for the same stylesheet. Before this fix, the link runtime could fetch the same stylesheet more than once and leave extra `<link rel="stylesheet">` elements after repeated updates. Now the runtime groups those chunk ids by URL, loads the stylesheet once, and still applies CSS module data for every affected chunk.

author: garethclarridge
body:
This PR implements a performance optimization in the `StructureShadowReportCommand`.

### 💡 What
Replaced `query()->get()` with `query()->lazy()` in the loop iterating over `MediaProcessingLog` records.

### 🎯 Why
The `media_processing_logs` table accumulates a record for every media processing run. Iterating over this entire table using `get()` loads all matching models into memory simultaneously, which will eventually lead to memory exhaustion as the application history grows.

### 📊 Impact
Reduces the memory footprint of the `structure:shadow-report` command from O(N) to O(1) relative to the number of logs being processed.

### 🔬 Measurement
Verified via `tests/Feature/Console/StructureShadowReportCommandTest.php`. The command continues to aggregate agreement metrics correctly while processing records in chunks.

author: seijikohara
body:
Adds two user-selectable display settings — **Album name** and **Cover art** — that hide the album name and/or the album artwork on both the compact music card and the full-screen Now Playing player. Requested in #231 (comment: an option to remove "Album" from the player), extended to the cover art.

## What it does

- **Settings → Panels** gains two switches ("Album name", "Cover art"), both default ON, mirroring the existing Music-spectrum switch. Toggling either takes effect immediately on both surfaces.
- **Album name off**: the album line is dropped entirely (no em-dash placeholder) on the card and the player.
- **Cover art off**: the whole artwork block is dropped; the metadata column / player controls take the freed space.
- **Card entry stays reachable**: the source-eyebrow row (icon + source label) becomes an unconditional tap-to-expand affordance for the full-screen player — so the player is reachable even when the art (the other expand affordance) is hidden. This mirrors the calendar/weather card header-tap entry. Distinct content descriptions keep the eyebrow-tap and art-tap addressable; the whole-card tap still opens the source app.

Title and artist are never hidden (they identify the track).

## Implementation

Mirrors the `musicSpectrum` static-boolean pattern end to end: DataStore (`DisplaySettings`/`DisplayPreferences`, default `true`) → `SettingsViewModel`/`SettingsUiState`/`SettingsAction` → two `PanelsSection` switches → threaded as two Boolean composable params from `MainActivity` through `HomeRoute → HomeScreen → DashboardScaffold → DashboardContent → FloatingCardColumn` into `MusicCard` and the `NowPlayingPanel` invocation. The leaf composables gate the album `MetaLine`/`MarqueeMetaLine` and the `AlbumArt` block.

## Testing

- **Unit**: DataStore round-trip for the two keys (+ reset-parity intact); `SettingsViewModel` write/default tests.
- **Instrumented (TBox-Mock emulator)**: card album-hide, art-hide, eyebrow-tap-expand (distinct from art-tap), panel album-hide — all pass at runtime.
- **Roborazzi**: one new golden `nowplaying-head-unit-853x512-minimal` (both toggles off) recorded on CI. Existing music-panel goldens are byte-identical (both settings default true → default rendering unchanged); dashboard goldens are untouched.
- `spotlessCheck` / `lint` / `test` / `assembleDebug` green locally. The Compose `ModifierParameter` lint baseline stays at 1 (unchanged).

## Notes for review

- **Unconditional eyebrow tap-to-expand** is intentional (an approved design decision), not art-hidden-only: with art shown, the card now has two expand affordances (art tap + eyebrow tap, distinct labels) and the whole-card tap opens the source app. When art is hidden, the eyebrow is the sole expand path; its tap zone is under the 64 dp automotive floor — accepted as it mirrors the merged calendar/weather header-tap entry (the card itself remains a 64 dp+ target). The eyebrow's `contentDescription` does not mask the source label for TalkBack.

## Merge

Rebase + squash. Squash subject: `feat(music): add album-name and cover-art visibility toggles`.

# Release Notes: v0.36.3 — OCR Fast-Follow: Messaging & Feedback

## Release Theme

Complete the OCR-disable story from v0.36.2: tell users honestly when image/scanned-document reading is off, everywhere it's off, and ask if they want it back.

## Key Features

**🔔 Consistent "OCR Temporarily Unavailable" State**
- Added a shared notice component used identically across all three OCR-gated flows: New Note/Edit Note upload, bulk import, and the photo-to-Study-Pack quick capture.
- Bulk import treats each failed file independently — an OCR-disabled file gets the paused-feature treatment while a sibling failure in the same batch still renders as a normal error.
- A lightweight "Yes, I'd like this back" affordance on the notice, tracked through analytics so real demand is visible before OCR is ever re-enabled.

## Polish & Fixes

- Fixed a real bug: New Note/Edit Note upload was swallowing the backend's actual "temporarily unavailable" message into a generic "We couldn't extract text from this file" failure. It now surfaces the real message.
- No change to the v0.36.2 kill-switch itself — `studysnap.ocr.enabled` stays the single source of truth; this release only changes how the frontend responds to it.
- Adopted a new rule to prevent Codex prompt files from being committed to the repo going forward — they're local planning material, not a shipped artifact.

author: igorshevchik
body:
## Зачем

Вы заметили: холостая работа очередей «как будто есть нет». Причина — демо-нагрузка была **редкой** (3 джоба раз в 5 мин) и **мгновенно разгребалась** (backlog = ждут+в работе ≈ 0 → линия графика лежит в 0). Этот PR делает демо **наглядным**, чтобы утренний тест сразу показал живые очереди.

## Что сделано

- **Секундная каденция.** Демо-крон вбрасывает поток каждые `DEMO_TICK_SEC` секунд (по умолчанию 5), а не раз в `CRON_INTERVAL_MIN` минут. Реальный опрос остаётся на минутной каденции (пуст до стадии 5).
- **Видимый backlog.** Демо-джобы держат искусственную паузу обработки `DEMO_DELAY_MS` (по умолчанию 600 мс) — **только для демо-счётов** (`isDemoAccount`): `fetchStatement` и `findCompany` в `worker.ts`. Реальные джобы **не тормозятся**. `DEMO_DELAY_MS=0` → мгновенный разгреб.
- Чистые хелперы `demoTickMs`/`demoDelayMs` (клампы, тесты). Env `DEMO_TICK_SEC`/`DEMO_DELAY_MS` проброшены в оба compose + `.env.example`.

## Безопасность / нагрузка (проверено ревью)

- **Реальные джобы никогда не паузятся** — двойной гейт по `isDemoAccount` (R1: NO BLOCKERS).
- **Самоограничено на дефолтах** — crm-sync ~72% занятости; `removeOnComplete/Fail` (1000/5000) кап Redis (R2: NO BLOCKERS). Условие: `DEMO_LOAD_N × 2 × DEMO_DELAY_MS ≤ DEMO_TICK_SEC × 1000` (задокументировано; `N≥5` при 5-сек тике переполнит — но в проде демо off).
- **Head-of-line**: демо делит concurrency=1 воркер с боевыми — реальный джоб может подождать за паузой демо. Сейчас неактуально (боевой опрос пуст до стадии 5, в проде `DEMO_LOAD_N=0`); при сосуществовании — отдельная демо-очередь. Задокументировано.

## Проверки

`lint`✅ `typecheck`✅ `test` 548/548 ✅. Панель 5 ревьюеров (гейтинг/безопасность · сайзинг/runaway · тесты/env/доки + предыдущие) — без блокеров; правки (устаревший коммент, дубль строки, стамп, сайзинг-гайд, head-of-line) внесены.

> Живой график этой демо-нагрузки нельзя снять статикой (нужен backend+Redis) — проверяется на сервере: поднять с `DEMO_LOAD_N=3`, открыть `/queues` (без `?preview=1`).

author: ommsharravana
body:
## Varnam Vizha — organiser self-serve layer

Makes the festival platform **self-serve for the committee** — every module that was read-only is now writable from the dashboard, so organisers run the programme without a developer. Built by 6 parallel worktree agents (non-overlapping sections), merged, then verified end-to-end in a real browser as the demo chair with every write confirmed in the DB.

### What organisers can now do
- **Events** — create / edit / cancel events from the dashboard: dates (blank end = +2h), venue, capacity + waitlist, paid + ticket link, featured. Cancelled events stay publicly visible with a badge.
- **Registration form builder** — design per-event sign-up questions (text / phone / long answer / dropdown / checkbox, required flags, reorder, max 12). Public form renders them; answers stored on each registration; required rules enforced server-side.
- **Registration ops** — event-day check-in (idempotent) + undo, waitlist promotion with live capacity check ("Event is still full." when at cap), status filter chips, CSV incl. status + check-in time.
- **Sponsors & budget** — add/edit sponsors (soft delete), create budget, add allocations, record spend with automatic parent-budget rollup; DB CHECK constraints pre-validated with friendly messages.
- **Team** — chair adds committee members (yi_directory person + app='varnam' role; reactivates previously-removed members), deactivates with a last-chair guard.
- **PWA** — shared "Install Yi Connect" prompt suppressed on /varnam-vizha routes (Varnam has its own scoped manifest).

### Verification (all click-tested in a real browser + DB-confirmed)
Create "Nila Soru" event → edit capacity → cancel (throwaway) → build a required dropdown question → public register: guard fires, retry keeps typed values, answer stored → waitlist join on a full event → promote refused at cap → promote succeeds after capacity raise → check-in stamped → sponsor added → budget spend rolls up → team member added + deactivated. `tsc --noEmit` = 0 errors.

Two bugs found & fixed during verification: React 19 form auto-reset wiping typed values on validation error (inputs now controlled); `events.end_date` NOT NULL vs optional end time (defaults to start + 2h).

### Notes for reviewers
- Every server action re-checks `getVarnamAccess()` server-side; explicit denials, no silent redirects; writes verified with select-back (no false-success).
- Registration PII stays chair/admin-only (page + actions use the same gate).
- Agent-verified live-schema corrections: `sponsors.contact_phone` (not `contact_person_phone`); `budget_allocations.allocated_amount > 0`.
- New person added to Team gets access once their yi_directory `user_id` links on first sign-in (hint shown in UI).

author: vchelaru
body:
## Summary

Ports `SpriteRuntime.RenderTargetTextureSource` to raylib — a Sprite can now display another container's baked render target (item 3 of #3434, explicitly deferred out of #3436/#3448 when the raylib render-to-texture core landed).

- `MonoGameGum/GueDeriving/SpriteRuntime.cs`: the `RenderTargetTextureSource` get/set property widens from `#if XNALIKE` to `#if XNALIKE || RAYLIB`. `IRenderTargetTextureReferencer` (`RenderingLibrary/Graphics/Sprite.cs`) stays XNA-only — its `Texture` member is typed to XNA's `Texture2D`, which raylib doesn't have and doesn't need: raylib resolves the source directly.
- `Runtimes/RaylibGum/Renderables/Sprite.cs`: new `RenderTargetTextureSource` property. `Render()` resolves the baked `RenderTexture2D` each frame via the existing `Renderer.TryGetBakedRenderTargetFor` seam (added in #3436 for exactly this), and draws it with a negative-height source rect — an RT is stored bottom-up in GL, so this flips it upright, mirroring the same idiom `Renderer.TryCompositeRenderTarget` already uses for the container→screen composite. `TextureWidth`/`TextureHeight` fall back to the source's dimensions, matching the MonoGame `Sprite.cs` pattern.
- No renderer-ordering changes were needed: raylib's `Draw()` already bakes every `IsRenderTarget` container across all layers in one pre-pass before the main compositing walk, so by the time any Sprite renders, a visible source is already baked — same-tree and cross-container references both just work.
- **Known limitation, matching MonoGame parity gaps intentionally left alone:** a Sprite referencing an *invisible* source container won't see it baked (raylib's bake pass, like the pre-#1643 MonoGame behavior, only bakes visible `IsRenderTarget` containers). Porting the "collect referenced invisible render targets" pass MonoGame added for #1643 is a natural follow-up if invisible-source usage comes up, but is out of scope here. Also, "cross-layer" doesn't apply to raylib today — `RaylibGum`'s `Renderer` has no multi-layer API (`AddLayer`) yet, unlike MonoGame's.
- Adds a demo cell to `Samples/raylib/Screens/RenderTargetScreen.cs` (and wires nothing new in `Program.cs` — the existing "Render Target" nav button already routes here): a Sprite shows a sibling container's bake, scaled up and rotated, proving it's a live texture reference and not a duplicated draw.

## Tests

- `Tests/RaylibGum.Tests/Rendering/RenderTargetTests.cs`: two new tests.
  - `Draw_SpriteWithRenderTargetTextureSource_PreservesVerticalOrientation` — a top/bottom split-color source pins the Y-flip (a uniform-color source couldn't distinguish flipped from not).
  - `Draw_SpriteWithUnbakedRenderTargetTextureSource_DrawsNothing` — a Sprite referencing a container that never became a render target draws nothing rather than crashing on a null lookup (covers the new early-return branch).
- Full `RaylibGum.Tests` suite: 375/375 green.
- `MonoGameGum.Tests` Sprite-filtered tests and a `SkiaGum` build both pass/succeed with no new warnings — confirms the shared `SpriteRuntime.cs` widening didn't disturb the other two platforms.

author: petemoore
body:
This is the first corpus-level proof of the Z80 parser front-end (src/asmparse.asm): TestAsmParseCorpus drives parse_run over all 93 corpus fixtures (tests/{core,format,operands,symbols,paged}/sources/*.s) and byte-matches the emitted PARSE_RECS output against serializeIR(frontend.Translate(src)), the same wire framing helper pass1_ir_test.go uses.

To fit the corpus, the two large buffers are relocated to low RAM under a new ASMPARSE_CORPUS_BUFS build define (set alongside ASMPARSE_STANDALONE in the asmparse-z80 Makefile target): LEX_TOKS moves to an equ at &0100 (1024-token capacity, 14336 B, ends &3900) and PARSE_RECS to an equ at &3A00 (10752 B, ends &6400). Both lie in the flat harness's unused low-RAM region (&0100–&63FA). LEX_SRC and LEX_STRPOOL grow to 4096 B each. The default asmlex.bin and all non-corpus builds are unaffected.

Because equ constants don't appear in the pyz80 mapfile, the existing parseZ80 helper switches from mac.Sym("PARSE_RECS") to the hardcoded addrPARSE_RECS constant (documented with the "drift = silent corruption" comment the pass1_ir_test.go constants use).

Host-side capacity guards are computed and loud (i253): source length, IR wire length, token count (via refLex), and SYM_NAMES interned-name bytes are all checked before the Z80 run. The single oversize fixture (in_long_source.s, source 16474 B and IR ~16484 B) is in the reviewed parseKnownOversize exclude-list. Result: 92 fixtures matched, 1 reviewed-excluded, stale-entry guard clean.

Completes i48c-b8g.

body:
## 개요

경찰 관련 뉴스를 자동으로 모아 보여주는 웹앱입니다. 서버 비용 없이 GitHub Actions(수집) + GitHub Pages(호스팅)만으로 무료로 돌아갑니다.

## 주요 기능

- **매시간 자동 수집**: 매일 KST 05:00~23:00 매시간, 구글 뉴스 RSS에서 경찰 관련 키워드로 기사 수집 (API 키·외부 패키지 불필요)
- **🔥 오늘의 주요 이슈 TOP 5**: 제목 유사도로 같은 사건 기사를 묶어 보도 언론사 수를 집계하고, 많이 보도된 순으로 랭킹 표시
- **하루 누적 병합**: 시간이 지나도 아침에 수집된 기사가 유실되지 않음
- **날씨 브리핑**: 서울 3일 예보 (open-meteo, 무료)
- **텍스트 복사**: 메신저·단톡방에 붙여넣기 좋은 브리핑 텍스트 포맷으로 복사

## 구성

| 경로 | 역할 |
|---|---|
| `scraper/scrape.py` | 수집·클러스터링·랭킹 (파이썬 표준 라이브러리만 사용) |
| `.github/workflows/scrape.yml` | 매시간 cron, 결과 자동 커밋 |
| `docs/index.html` | 웹앱 (날짜별 조회, 주요 이슈, 복사 기능) |
| `docs/data/` | 날짜별 브리핑 JSON (현재는 샘플 데이터) |

author: stackotter
body:
WinUIBackend applies a fix to wire up stdout/stderr to the parent process's console, which allows applications to print debug info to the console etc. That fix is required for any Windows applications that are compiled as GUI apps (which don't get consoles by default).

Before this PR, that fix was only applied once WinUIBackend.runMainLoop got called by SwiftCrossUI, which meant that early print statements in App.init didn't get routed to the console, which made debugging issues during the early phases of startup tricky.

This PR adds a static `earlySetup` requirement to `BackendFeatures.Core` that backends can use to run early setup code before the app's `init` gets invoked. It also adds a WinUIBackend implementation of that method, with the console fix code that previously lived in `runMainLoop`.

author: jstoup111
body:
## Why

Recovery steps (rebase, remediate, debugging) perform judgment-heavy reasoning where wrong decisions produce silent failures: wrong semantic merges silently revert merged work, false HALTs waste context, and wrong root-cause diagnoses produce band-aid fixes. Fable's longer reasoning chains guard these critical paths.

## What Changed

- **HARNESS.md model table** — updated `debugging`, `remediate`, and `rebase` rows from Opus to Fable with specific rationales
- **SKILL.md frontmatter** — updated `model: fable` in skills/debugging/SKILL.md, skills/rebase/SKILL.md, skills/remediate/SKILL.md
- **resolved-config.ts** — updated DEFAULT_STEP_MODELS (rebase, remediate) and DEFAULT_STEP_EFFORT (rebase to max)
- **Interim fallback documented** — added note in HARNESS.md clarifying that Fable pins assume #186 availability; users can override per-run with `--model` flag or `steps.<step>.model` config
- **CHANGELOG** — added entry under Changed section with issue references (#189)

## Testing

- `npx vitest run test/engine/resolved-config.test.ts` — all 23 tests pass
  - New test: recovery steps default to fable with correct effort levels
  - New test: user config overrides fable default on rebase
  - New test: collateral-drift guard confirms finish/build unaffected
- Existing test suite: 2698 passed (1 pre-existing unrelated timeout)

## Notes

- These three recovery steps are intentionally pinned to Fable (highest reasoning capability available) due to the severity of mis-judgment in each
- Interim mechanism: until #186 (model availability ladder) ships, users can override with per-step config

Closes jstoup111/ai-conductor#189

author: adrianantico
body:
Description
Summary
This PR allows bundled R Shiny applications to use packages that are not published on CRAN.
Supported package sources include:
Public or private GitHub repositories
Local R package directories
Local source archives such as .tar.gz files
Example
dependencies:
  r:
    packages:
      - github::owner/package@v1.2.0
      - CustomName=github::owner/repository@main
      - InternalPackage=local::../packages/InternalPackage
      - Reports=local::../packages/Reports_2.1.0.tar.gz
Relative local paths are resolved from the Shiny application directory.
Implementation
Uses pak::pkg_install() when constructing the bundled R library.
Separates build-time package specifications from runtime package names.
Removes local paths and GitHub references from the packaged runtime manifest.
Supports GITHUB_PAT and GH_TOKEN for private GitHub repositories.
Does not embed repository credentials in the resulting application.
Requires runtime_strategy = "bundled" for GitHub and local packages.
Supports both single-app and multi-app builds.
Adds documentation and tests covering package specifications, manifests, and path resolution.
Motivation
Many Shiny applications depend on internal packages or development versions that are intentionally not published to CRAN. These packages should be installable while constructing the application’s private R library.
Once built, end users do not need:
R installed
Access to the GitHub repository
The original local package directory
Build credentials
Validation
Dependency-handling tests pass.
Diff whitespace validation passes.
Runtime-mocking tests were skipped locally because mockery was unavailable.
Network-backed system-requirement checks warned because network access was unavailable.
This PR is intentionally separate from the sitrep crash investigation and Node PATH fix.

author: patricksun93
body:
## Summary

Closes the design-vs-implementation gaps found in the full-codebase goal audit. The core commerce spine was already sound; this PR fixes the seams — real bugs, dead admin sections, and the storefront's un-localized post-purchase flow.

Produced by a multi-agent fix workflow (22 parallel fix agents) + hand-finishing the one agent that hit a usage limit. **Net diff is 55 files** (the ~6.7k deletions are dead admin sections removed).

## Backend correctness
- **Oversell fix** — `orderRoutes` now decrements `inventory` inside the order transaction with a guarded UPDATE (`WHERE quantity_available >= qty`; 0 rows → 409 rollback), preventing race oversell. Stripe webhook confirmed to decrement exactly once.
- **Privilege fix (staff ≠ admin)** — staff no longer inherits `isAdmin`. `authMiddleware` gains `staffOrAdmin`; `AuthContext` lets staff into the dashboard without admin powers.
- **Chinese search** — product search now matches `product_translations` for the active locale (was English-only → non-English queries returned nothing). Autocomplete phantom columns fixed.
- **Analytics** — `inventory-status` was querying columns that don't exist (`stock_quantity`/`is_active`/`cost_price`); rewritten against the real `inventory`+`products` schema. Now returns 200 with real data.
- **sitemap** — `http.request` instead of `fetch` (port 6666 is a fetch bad-port that silently failed, dropping product URLs from the sitemap).

## Admin dashboard
- `AnalyticsDashboard` + `BulkUploadView`: relative `/api` proxy + cookie/CSRF auth (were hitting browser-blocked `localhost:6666` with `Bearer null`).
- Removed dead **Reports / Content / Security** sections (UI calling backend routes that don't exist — verified absent).
- Brand `Bed Texture` → `Noiraé` (titles, footers ×4 locales).

## Storefront i18n (11 new namespaces, EN/中文/FR/ES full parity, 0 missing keys)
checkout success, order confirmation, order detail, returns request + detail, CartDrawer, SearchBar, newsletter, order tracking, reviews, silk/cashmere collections, category page. Also: orders status colors → design tokens (dark-mode safe).

## Verification
- Storefront `next lint && next build` — ✅ pass (warnings only). Admin build — ✅ pass. 6 changed backend files `node --check` — ✅.
- i18n: per-key check, every `t('key')` in the 11 components exists in the catalog; all namespaces present in all 4 locales.
- **Runtime smoke** (live backend): admin login `isAdmin=true`; **staff login `isAdmin=false`/`isStaff=true`** (privilege fix proven); Chinese search "超柔" → results; analytics `inventory-status` → 200 with real data.

## Audit corrections
The audit flagged the approval-status route and inventory-adjust routes as "missing" — they already exist in `adminRoutes.js` (audit false-negative from a BSD-grep `\|` bug). Verified present; only the genuine backend bug (analytics phantom columns) needed fixing.

## Not done / deferred (intentional)
- Inventory decrement is code- + transaction-verified but **not exercised with a live end-to-end order**.
- API v1 versioning, multi-currency service, product-bundle routes/UI, SEO slug URLs + `generateMetadata` — larger scope, deferred.
- git-history local-dev password — left for a conscious history-rewrite decision (not done here).
- The 4 adversarial verify agents hit the usage limit; substituted with the build + runtime smoke above.

author: subhashb
body:
## Summary

Committed `.protean/ir.json` baselines churned on every regeneration because `protean ir show` writes a volatile `generated_at` timestamp — a value that is already excluded from both the content checksum and `ir diff`. Every `make ir` produced a one-line-per-file timestamp diff even when nothing about the contract changed, training contributors to ignore baseline diffs and hiding genuine contract changes.

This adds a **canonical, no-timestamp baseline output**:

- **`protean ir show --canonical`** strips `generated_at`, retaining `$schema`/`ir_version`/`checksum`/`elements` (version markers and content-derived keys, all already ignored by `ir diff`/`ir check`). A canonical baseline changes *only* when the domain contract changes.
- **One shared serializer** (`canonical_ir()` / `canonical_ir_json()` in `protean.ir.constants`) is the single source of truth for baseline rendering. **Every baseline writer routes through it** so they emit byte-identical output:
  - `protean ir show --canonical`
  - the `--fix` staleness pre-commit hook (`_regenerate_ir`)
  - `protean schema generate` (`write_ir`)
- **Stale-baseline hint messages** across `ir diff`, `ir check`, and the staleness hook now recommend `--canonical`, so following the printed guidance no longer reintroduces churn.
- **Schema relaxed**: `generated_at` is now optional, keeping canonical baselines schema-conformant. This is a strict relaxation — every existing full-IR document still validates.

Staleness and diff are unaffected: both already ignore `generated_at` (staleness compares only `checksum`; `diff_ir` walks content sections). Upgrading produces a one-time `.protean/ir.json` diff on the next regeneration (dropped timestamp, sorted keys), functionally harmless.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/protean/ir/constants.py` | `CANONICAL_EXCLUDED_KEYS`, `canonical_ir()`, `canonical_ir_json()` |
| `src/protean/cli/ir.py` | `--canonical` flag on `ir show`; `--canonical` in stale hints |
| `src/protean/cli/hooks.py` | `--fix` hook writes canonical baseline; hint updated |
| `src/protean/ir/generators/schema_writer.py` | `write_ir` writes canonical baseline |
| `src/protean/ir/staleness.py` | usage-docstring hint updated |
| `src/protean/ir/schema/v0.1.0/schema.json` | `generated_at` moved out of `required` |
| `docs/` | `ir`/`schema` CLI reference + compatibility-checking guide |

## Test plan

- [x] `--canonical` omits `generated_at` and retains content keys; negative control confirms default output keeps it
- [x] All three baseline writers produce byte-identical canonical output
- [x] Canonical baseline still reads as FRESH under `ir check`; `ir diff` sees no change vs live IR
- [x] Canonical output validates against the (relaxed) IR schema
- [x] `--canonical` is a no-op with `--format=summary`
- [x] Core suite (`protean test`) passes; `ruff` + `mypy` clean
- [x] Adversarial revert check: every behavioral test goes red when the strip is neutralized

Closes #1064

author: dwgoon
body:
## Release 0.3.0

Modernizes jpegio end to end. Verified locally (Windows, both backends, Python
3.9 and 3.13) and in CI (Linux/macOS/Windows, CPython 3.9-3.13, all green).

### libjpeg-turbo 3.2.0
- Bundle libjpeg-turbo 3.2.0 and build it from source with CMake on every
  platform (SIMD auto-enabled when NASM is present); the old per-platform
  prebuilt binaries are removed.

### Robustness and correctness
- A corrupt or truncated JPEG raises a Python exception instead of calling
  `exit()` and killing the interpreter.
- GPT-5.5 review fixes: NumPy view lifetime (per-read owner that survives
  re-read / drop, in both backends), integer overflow on large dimensions,
  marker invalid-free, quant/Huffman table-slot preservation, Huffman write,
  bounds/error checks, and a num_components validation on write.

### Two binding backends
- A hand-written CPython C-API backend (default, no Cython needed) and the
  Cython backend, selectable via `JPEGIO_BACKEND`.

### Steganography tooling
- All markers (APP0..APP15 + COM) preserved with read/write access; more JPEG
  properties exposed (encoding-relevant ones writable; comp_info edits honoured
  on write); a `jpegio.tools` module (zigzag, DCT histograms, nnz / embedding
  capacity, coefficient/marker helpers).

### Packaging
- `src/` layout; vendored library under `third_party/`; Apache-2.0 with the
  bundled libjpeg-turbo BSD licenses (`NOTICE`, `license-files`); Python
  3.9-3.13; cibuildwheel wheels + sdist for Linux/macOS/Windows.

author: zoza1982
body:
## What

Browse a local **`.tar` or `.zip`** like a directory: `Enter` on it descends in, `..` at the archive root pops back out to the containing folder, and copying files out works through the normal copy/move flow. Read-only — no writing into archives. Recognized by **magic bytes, never extension**.

Delivers the archive-browsing half of your original ask. Compressed tar (`.tgz/.txz/.tbz2/.tzst`) is the next phase (P5).

## How

- **New crate `cairn-backend-archive`** — `ArchiveVfs` impl `Vfs` (caps `LIST | READ | RANDOM_READ` only; mutating methods keep the `Unsupported` default; `local_path` stays `None`). One `ArchiveOps` trait implemented twice: **zip** via the central directory, **plain tar** via a one-pass offset index over the seekable file. Both decode in `spawn_blocking` (the codecs are sync-only). `zip` uses `deflate-flate2-zlib-rs` (pure-Rust inflate, no write-only zopfli, no FFI); `tar` 0.4.
- **Mount model (ADR-0012):** a mount is an ephemeral registry connection. The P1 sniff gains `FileKind::Archive`; `FileSniffed{Archive}` → `AppEffect::MountArchive` → the runner resolves `local_path` (v1 requires a local file), builds `ArchiveVfs`, mints a `ConnectionId`, inserts it, and the pane navigates in. `PaneState.mount_stack` records the origin `(conn, cwd)` so `leave_dir` at the archive root pops back out (generalizes to nested archives). `Scheme::Archive` added.

## Security (untrusted archive bytes) — security-review: **PASS, no blockers**

All 10 MUST-BLOCK invariants verified: a **counting reader** (`Read::take`) makes declared sizes advisory-only; per-member (64 MiB) + cumulative-session (512 MiB) byte caps; zip decompression-ratio bomb guard with a floor; entry-count cap (100k); path-traversal / absolute / UNC / drive-letter / NUL rejection via `VfsPath`; symlink/hardlink members **inert** (never resolved to a host path); device/FIFO/socket + setuid/setgid/sticky skipped; checked/saturating arithmetic on all header fields; no panics on crafted input; `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, pure-Rust decode path.

## Review gates — findings applied

- **CRITICAL** (code-review): removed a stray `>>>>>>>` CHANGELOG conflict marker the rebase left.
- **HIGH** (bug-bot): a full-member read that the caps would truncate now **errors** (`archive_member_too_large`) instead of silently returning a short buffer — a copy-out of an over-cap member previously produced a truncated file that even `VerifyPolicy::Size` accepted (data loss). Regression test added.
- **Important** (code-review): fixed the `wanted` byte-range formula (`offset + declared` → clamped to real length), the zero-byte-read-at-cap edge, and the zip feature slimming. Added `open_read`-level tests (full / ranged / over-cap-errors).

**Deferred with tracked follow-ups** (both reviewers agree these are bounded/low): zip entry-count-cap fires after the central-directory parse (bounded by file size ~46 B/record); tar inflated-header adjacent-member read; `ArchiveMounted` staleness/dedup guard; session-cap TOCTOU under concurrent reads; unmount-on-leave (per-session fd/memory); tar seek-to-offset for `RANDOM_READ` efficiency; bidi/zero-width display-name sanitization (repo-wide, best solved at the render layer).

## Testing

The archive crate's tests build adversarial fixtures **in memory** (no binary blobs committed): a `..`-traversal member, a symlink member, a setuid/special member, a hand-crafted lying-`u64::MAX` tar header, a real deflated zip bomb, an over-entry-count archive, plus the new `open_read` full/ranged/over-cap cases. All 7 CI commands green locally (fmt, clippy lean + all-features, tests lean + all-features, rustdoc, fmt-check).

## Docs

RFC-0013 (new), ADR-0012 (new, mount model + `Scheme::Archive`), CHANGELOG, README, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.

author: ahhda
body:
## Summary
- `balances-watcher-linea` has been crash-looping in staging (56 restarts over ~8h, alerted via `PodCrashLooping`). The container isn't actually erroring — it's killed by the k8s liveness probe because `/health` repeatedly returns 503.
- Root cause: `block_watcher`'s stall-detection window is `block_time * STALL_TIMEOUT_BLOCKS` (3). Linea's declared `block_time` was `2s`, giving a 6s stall timeout. But polling the live OVH Linea node directly, real block-to-block gaps of 8-10s are routine (the sequencer batches blocks rather than producing them on a steady clock). Every gap over 6s triggers a false "stream stalled" → resubscribe → `/health` failure, and three consecutive failures over the 30s liveness period kills the pod.
- Fix: bump Linea's nominal `block_time` from 2s to 5s, raising the stall window to 15s — comfortably above the observed 8-10s gaps. This constant has exactly one call site (the stall-timeout calculation), so the change is isolated to Linea's reconnect behavior and doesn't affect any other network.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo check` passes (via rustc 1.91, required by `alloy@2.0.4`)
- [x] `cargo test` — all 4 existing tests pass
- [ ] After merge + deploy to staging, confirm `balances-watcher-linea` stops restarting and `stream stalled` log lines drop to near zero

author: yixiaod
body:
## Summary
Adds a comprehensive evaluation harness to measure and validate the trigger rates of 8 SAS-related skills against their trimmed descriptions. This ensures that description optimizations don't cause regressions in skill invocation reliability.

## Key Changes

- **`measure.py`**: Core evaluation script that:
  - Runs queries against Claude with installed skills using `claude -p`
  - Parses streaming JSON output to detect which skills are invoked via the Skill tool
  - Measures trigger rates across multiple runs per query
  - Generates per-skill result JSON with pass/fail metrics (threshold: ≥0.5 for positive queries, <0.5 for negative)
  - Supports concurrent execution with configurable workers and timeout

- **`run_all.sh`**: Bash orchestration script that:
  - Registers all 8 skill descriptions as project commands from SKILL.md files
  - Drives evaluation across the skill set with configurable model and run counts
  - Writes per-skill JSON results to `results/` directory

- **Eval sets** (8 JSON files): Domain-specific test queries for each skill:
  - `sas-programming-core.json`: General SAS programming (catch-all)
  - `sdtm-qc-programming.json`: SDTM domain QC validation
  - `adam-dev-programming.json`: ADaM dataset development
  - `adam-qc-programming.json`: ADaM QC validation
  - `tfls-dev-programming.json`: Table/figure/listing development
  - `tfls-qc-programming.json`: Table/figure/listing QC
  - `sas-log-clean.json`: SAS log diagnostic and cleanup
  - `vscode-sas-setup.json`: VS Code SAS extension configuration
  
  Each eval set includes positive queries (should trigger) and negative queries (should not over-trigger) to test disambiguation boundaries.

- **`README.md`**: Documentation covering prerequisites, usage, and optimization workflow for regressed descriptions

- **`.gitignore`**: Excludes `results/` directory from version control

## Notable Implementation Details

- Uses unique session IDs per query invocation to prevent concurrent `claude -p` calls from colliding
- Stops parsing after 4+ tool uses to focus on initial skill selection phase
- Supports partial skill name matching (e.g., "adam-qc" matches "adam-qc-programming")
- Filters environment to exclude `CLAUDECODE` to prevent interference
- Integrates with existing `skill-creator/scripts/run_eval.py` for optimization workflows

author: alvaroliger
body:
## The bug

When a user edited their website via WhatsApp, `applyChange()` saved the updated HTML/CSS/JS to the database and replied:

> _"Tu web publicada se actualizará en unos segundos."_

But `deployToLiveDomain()` was never called, so the live static site (on the user's custom domain or Pagepolis subdomain) was never updated. Users were told their change went live — it didn't.

`EditorController::save()` and `AiController::update()` both call `deployToLiveDomain()` after every save. The WhatsApp path was the only write path that omitted it.

## The fix

One line added after `$project->update([...])` in `WhatsAppController::applyChange()`:

```php
$project->deployToLiveDomain();
```

`deployToLiveDomain()` is a no-op for projects without an active custom/subdomain domain, so there is no risk for draft or path-served sites.

## Verification

New test suite `WhatsAppDeployTest` (6 tests, all green):

| Test | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `test_whatsapp_edit_deploys_to_active_custom_domain` | `DeploySite` job dispatched |
| `test_whatsapp_edit_deploys_to_active_subdomain` | `DeploySite` job dispatched |
| `test_whatsapp_edit_without_domain_does_not_deploy` | `DeploySite` NOT dispatched |
| `test_whatsapp_edit_with_path_domain_does_not_deploy` | `DeploySite` NOT dispatched |
| `test_whatsapp_edit_saves_content_to_database` | DB row updated |
| `test_whatsapp_edit_increments_ai_quota` | `ai_calls_today` incremented |

```
php artisan test --filter WhatsAppDeployTest
→ 6 tests, 6 passed
```

## Note on phpunit.xml

Also adds `APP_KEY` to `phpunit.xml` (pre-existing missing env var that caused all feature tests to error with "No application encryption key"). This overlaps with open PR #39 — the conflict is trivially resolvable (same single-line addition).

author: baijum
body:
## Problem

`tests/scheme/srfi/srfi18.scm` has hung indefinitely with zero output since at least v0.10.0; `run-all.sh` masked it as a 60s-timeout SKIP, so the suite stayed green.

Sampling the hung process showed the main thread blocked in `pthread_join` (from `thread-join!`) while the child OS thread spun forever in the dispatch loop. Root cause: `thread-terminate!` only set cooperative-fiber-scheduler flags (`fiber.terminated`, `wakeWaiters`) that a child **OS thread** spawned by `thread-start!` never observes. The test's `(let loop () (thread-yield!) (loop))` thunk ran forever (`thread-yield!` is a no-op in a schedulerless child VM), and the parent's `thread-join!` blocked forever. The file hung at its `thread-terminate!` test and, since it only prints on failure or at the end, produced no output.

## Fix

- `vm.zig`: new `VMError.Terminated`; new `VM.terminate_flag: ?*bool` pointing at the shared parent-heap `fiber.terminated` flag for child OS threads.
- `vm_dispatch.zig`: poll the flag (atomic load) at the **existing** 1024-instruction safepoint next to the timeout check — no new cost in the hot dispatch path. On termination the child unwinds with `Terminated`, the OS thread exits, `pthread_join` returns, and `thread-join!` raises `terminated-thread-exception` per SRFI-18. Works even for pure busy loops with no yields.
- `primitives_srfi18.zig`: the thread entry wires up the flag; `thread-terminate!` stores it atomically.

## Test file repairs

Two tests in `srfi18.scm` could never work as written — they captured a mutex/condvar inside an OS-thread thunk, but OS threads run on isolated heaps and sync primitives are deliberately uncopyable (`gc_deep_copy.zig`):

- Mutex contention and condvar signal are now exercised on the cooperative fiber path (`spawn`), including a real holder/waiter blocking sequence.
- New test pins the OS-thread semantics: capturing a mutex in a thread thunk raises `uncaught-exception` at join.
- The file now fails via `(exit 1)`: a top-level `(error ...)` exits 0, so the old ending could never fail `run-all.sh` anyway.

## Regression test

`tests_srfi18.zig` terminates a pure busy-loop OS thread and joins it. Verified it catches the bug: with the safepoint check removed, `zig build test` hangs indefinitely; with it, the test passes in milliseconds.

## Verification

- `zig build test`: 451/451 pass (after rebase onto main)
- `bash tests/scheme/run-all.sh`: 240 Scheme files pass, 0 fail, **0 skip** (srfi18.scm was previously the only SKIP); R7RS suite 1395/1395
- `srfi18.scm` alone: 43 passed, 0 failed, exit 0, ~2s

## Follow-ups noticed (not in this PR)

- `run-all.sh` counts timeouts as SKIP and still exits 0 — this is what hid the hang for months.
- Top-level `(thread-yield!)` from the main fiber corrupts the top-level form's value (a spawned fiber's result leaks through `runWithScheduler`) and aborts top-level `define` with `error.Yielded`.

author: wuchendi
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #56: makes `.github/workflows/deploy-flnk.yml` the canonical deploy path and closes the gaps the audit remediation left around deployment.

- **Worker secret sync on every deploy**: a pre-deploy step feeds `LIBSQL_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ALLOWED_EMAILS`, and `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (runtime, for Analytics Engine SQL) into `wrangler secret bulk` from GitHub repository secrets. Empty values are skipped, so an unset GitHub secret never wipes an existing Worker secret. All secret values flow through `env:` — no `${{ }}` interpolation inside `run:`.
- **`ALLOWED_EMAILS` removed from `wrangler.jsonc` vars**: a var shadows the same-named Worker secret on every deploy, which would silently reopen registration. It now exists only as a Worker secret (prod) / `.dev.vars` entry (local).
- **Real D1 `database_id` and KV namespace `id` committed**: they are resource identifiers, not credentials, and CI deploys from a clean checkout must bind the right resources.
- Docs: README deploy section now points at the workflow; `.dev.vars.example` gains `ALLOWED_EMAILS`.

## Required repository secrets (before first workflow run)

| Secret | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `FLNK_LIBSQL_AUTH_TOKEN` | Turso auth token — without it the deployed Worker loses DB access |
| `FLNK_ALLOWED_EMAILS` | Sign-in allow-list; empty keeps open registration |
| `FLNK_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` | Analytics Engine SQL token (optional; stats degrade gracefully) |

`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` / `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` (deploy auth) are unchanged.

## Verification

- Workflow YAML parses cleanly; secret-sync step is idempotent and skips when no secrets are provided.
- Staged diff scanned for token patterns — none present (`LIBSQL_URL` remains a placeholder; only resource ids were added).

author: lewricka
body:
## Resumen

- Reporte del dueño en prod: la app se recargaba sola tras un deploy y perdía formularios a medias (crear reto/momento). Causa: #498 dejó `registerType: 'autoUpdate'` + `skipWaiting`/`clientsClaim` incondicional + sondeo de `registration.update()` cada 60s — cualquier deploy tomaba el control del SW y recargaba TODAS las pestañas abiertas al momento. Anoche hubo 18 deploys.
- `registerType: 'prompt'` (`web/vite.config.ts:82`) + `web/src/sw.ts` ya no hace `self.skipWaiting()` incondicional al instalar: el SW nuevo se queda **en espera** hasta que `main.tsx` manda `{ type: 'SKIP_WAITING' }` (lo hace `updateSW(true)` de `vite-plugin-pwa`/`workbox-window`).
- El sondeo de 60s se mantiene (objetivo de #498: no quedarse en versión cacheada en un SPA que no navega).
- `web/src/main.tsx`: `registerSW({ onNeedRefresh, onRegisteredSW })`. Al detectar versión nueva:
  - Pestaña **oculta** (`document.hidden`, ya sea en el momento del `onNeedRefresh` o después vía `visibilitychange`): se aplica en silencio, sin que el usuario note nada al volver.
  - Pestaña **activa**: banner discreto "Hay una versión nueva · Actualizar" (`web/src/ui/UpdateBanner.tsx`), que aplica al pulsarlo.
- `docs/operativa.md` §5.0: documenta el comportamiento nuevo.

## Decisión de arquitectura del banner

`UpdateBanner` se monta en su **propio root de React** (`createRoot` sobre un `<div>` añadido a `document.body` desde `main.tsx`), FUERA del árbol de `<App/>`. Justificación:
- En el punto del arranque donde `registerSW` decide mostrar el banner aún no existe ningún componente de producto al que engancharlo de forma natural.
- `ToastProvider` (`web/src/ui/ToastProvider.tsx`) no soporta una acción persistente con botón — solo mensajes efímeros con auto-dismiss. Ampliarlo se salía del área de esta issue (UI kit compartido, usado en todas las features) para un aviso que solo aparece tras un deploy.
- Montar un mini-root evita tocar `App.tsx`/`ToastProvider` (fuera de mi área: `web/src/main.tsx`, `web/src/sw.ts`, `web/vite.config.ts` y un componente nuevo).

Visualmente: pill flotante centrada abajo, mismo "recipe" que `Toast.module.css` (papel + hairline + `shadow-lg`, `.t-caption`), en `--z-toast`. Centrada (no anclada a una esquina) a propósito: los FABs de la app viven en esquinas distintas según la pantalla (crear viaje y "＋" del viaje a la derecha; compartir clasificación a la izquierda en `GroupPage`) — no hay una esquina libre en todas partes, pero el centro nunca coincide con ninguna.

## Hallazgo sobre la restauración del hash (#g=x&add=reto) — FUERA de mi área

El síntoma "tras recargar mid-formulario, aterriza en la home del viaje" tiene una causa **independiente** del auto-reload, en `web/src/features/auth/useDeepLinkJoin.ts` (fuera de mi área, `features/**`; lo reporto con puntero exacto):

- `App.tsx:194-196` llama a `joinIfGroup(window.location.hash)` en un efecto que se dispara en **cada montaje** de `LoggedIn` cuando `route.group && user?.id` (o sea, en cada recarga de una URL `#g=…`).
- `useDeepLinkJoin.ts:48` normaliza el destino con `normalizeGroupHash(route.group, route.challenge)` (línea 62-66), que solo reconstruye `#g=…(&c=…)` — **descarta** `add`, `v` y `from`.
- `useDeepLinkJoin.ts:49-51`: si `window.location.hash !== normalized`, sobreescribe `location.hash` al valor normalizado.

Resultado: CUALQUIER recarga estando en `#g=X&add=reto` (o `&add=recuerdo`, o `&v=marcador`) hace que este efecto reescriba el hash a `#g=X` sin esos parámetros, y el router (`App.tsx:277` / `:305`) cae a `TripPage` (home del viaje) en vez de reabrir `CreateChallengeFlow`/`AddMoment`. No es un efecto del Service Worker: pasaría con **cualquier** recarga (F5 manual incluido) mientras se está creando un reto/momento.

Sugerencia para quien lo arregle (no incluida aquí, fuera de mi área): `normalizeGroupHash` debería preservar `add`/`v`/`from` cuando ya están presentes en el hash actual, o el efecto de `App.tsx:194-196` no debería re-ejecutar `joinIfGroup` en cada montaje si el usuario ya es miembro (solo hace falta el auto-join una vez).

## Verificación

Desde `web/` en el worktree (tras `npm install` y copiar `.env.local`):
```
npm run format && npm run lint && npm run type-check && npm run test && npm run build && npm run design-lint
```
Todo en verde (106 archivos de test, 755 tests incluyendo los 2 nuevos de `UpdateBanner`). Verificado en `dist/sw.js` que el `self.addEventListener('message', ...)` es la ÚNICA vía a `self.skipWaiting()` (no hay llamada incondicional) y que el chunk de `workbox-window` (con `SKIP_WAITING`) está presente en el bundle, confirmando que `registerType: 'prompt'` se aplicó.

Closes #549

This PR establishes a minimal, reusable repository baseline intended for sharing common assets across multiple servers. The goal is to make shared config/script management explicit and safe from day one.

- **Repository purpose and operating model**
  - Expanded `README.md` from a placeholder into a concise baseline guide for cross-server use.
  - Added clear scope: centralizing shared files, versioning updates, and keeping server environments aligned.

- **Initial structure contract**
  - Documented a recommended top-level layout:
    - `config/` for shared configuration
    - `scripts/` for operational scripts
    - `docs/` for operational documentation
  - Added short usage flow for clone/edit/sync across servers.

- **Safety guardrails**
  - Added a root `.gitignore` with defaults for editor/OS artifacts, temporary files, and common secret-bearing files (`.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`).

author: keithkatale
body: ## Problem `prisma.intelDocument.findMany()` (and all other Prisma calls) were failing in the deployed containers with: > Unable to require `/app/node_modules/.prisma/client/libquery_engine-linux-musl.so.node`. The Prisma engines do not seem to be compatible with your system. ## Root Cause The `binaryTargets` in `packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma` included `linux-musl` and `linux-musl-arm64-openssl-1.1.x`, which are Prisma engine binaries compiled against OpenSSL **1.1.x**. Both `Dockerfile` (web) and `Dockerfile.wealth-manager` use `node:20-alpine` as their base. Alpine 3.18+ (shipped with `node:20-alpine`) uses **OpenSSL 3.0.x**. At runtime Prisma selects the `linux-musl` binary, which cannot load against OpenSSL 3.0.x, causing the crash. ## Fix Removed the OpenSSL 1.x musl targets (`linux-musl`, `linux-musl-arm64-openssl-1.1.x`) from `binaryTargets`. The OpenSSL 3.0.x equivalents (`linux-musl-openssl-3.0.x`, `linux-musl-arm64-openssl-3.0.x`) were already present and are the correct targets for all current Alpine-based deployments. ```diff - binaryTargets = ["native", "linux-musl", "linux-musl-openssl-3.0.x", "linux-musl-arm64-openssl-1.1.x", "linux-musl-arm64-openssl-3.0.x"] + binaryTargets = ["native", "linux-musl-openssl-3.0.x", "linux-musl-arm64-openssl-3.0.x"] ```

author: bigbirdreturns
body:
Docs-only. The **answer memo** to the resource-spend gate (#30). It decides the invariant rather than asking questions — code may touch `resolveChallenge` only after this is accepted. Still no implementation.

### The invariant (decided)
> Resource spend may reduce variance or protect downside on an **already-plausible** attempt. It may not create success for an unqualified party, bypass role requirements, bypass authored difficulty, rescue a failed result after the fact, or become purchasable power.

"Already-plausible" is defined, not vibes: a party that meets the contract's **count + role gates** (`countOk`/`rolesOk`). Spend operates only *inside* the authored risk envelope; it never moves the envelope.

### Explicitly rejected
post-failure retry payments · spend-to-guarantee-success · spend-to-ignore-role-requirements · spend-to-skip-risk · purchasable tokens · daily scarcity pressure · opaque bonus math. The invariant exists to make these *unrepresentable*, not merely discouraged.

### Engine invariant the resolver must guarantee (with required property tests)
1. **Gate independence** — zero effect on `countOk`/`rolesOk`; a hopeless party resolves identically with or without spend.
2. **No mean lift past entitlement** — variance/downside only; the failure floor never rises.
3. **Determinism preserved** — same arc + seed + assignment (incl. `tokensSpent`) → same run.
4. **Authored, not global** — magnitude authored per contract/arc, never hidden global behavior.

### First allowed shape
pre-commit · authored per contract · visible before resolve · receipt-recorded · non-purchasable · refused below the contract's minimum requirements. Becomes the 4th taxonomy row only once the resolver honors it under the invariant and the property tests pass.

### Control question
Can tokens become an honest risk-management lever while the engine still refuses hopeless parties, preserves authored difficulty, and records exactly what the player spent and why?

### Sequence
accept this memo → arc-first engine-design pass (resolver variance modifier + property tests, reviewed on its own) → encounter-shell surface, gated like difficulty-mode choice.

body:
## What & why

Removes the #441 durable-credential gate that blocked anonymous users from creating groups (rules + client service + client screen), per Decision 0 of the A+ grade sprint plan. Post-#648 an anonymous user can already join groups and add expenses on a discardable UID ("gate creation, not participation"), so the create gate no longer protects its founding invariant — it only guaranteed creator durability, at the worst UX moment in the app (a blocking "Link Google" modal on first create, whose "Not now" silently aborted creation).

Anonymous users now create groups exactly like durable users, **with one carve-out**: add-people-by-name (shadow members) stays durable-only — `addShadowMember` already hard-rejects anonymous callers server-side (unchanged), and this PR additionally gates the three client affordances (create-screen chips, group-detail #807 shortcut, group-settings members section) on `isDurableUserProvider` so an anonymous creator never reaches a reject they can't act on. Anonymous creators still grow their group via the invite code (join is already un-gated). The existing #285 `AccountBackupNudge` becomes the primary link-your-account prompt post-create — no new nudge UI was built.

## Linked issue
Refs #818 — this is Wave 2 (create-gate removal) of a larger multi-wave issue; other waves are separate PRs.

## Scope check
- [x] One concern only — no bundled cleanup, opportunistic refactors, or dep bumps
- [ ] Linked issue's acceptance criteria reconciled — **partial**, this PR covers only the create-gate removal wave; #818's other waves are tracked separately.

## Gate (required if the change touches any of these — see CLAUDE.md → The Gate)
- [x] `security/firestore.rules` or Cloud Functions auth/validation

→ Spec authored via `superpowers:writing-plans`, ran through `/run-the-gate`: **v3, GATE-APPROVED** — Round 1: 1 P1 / 1 P2 / 3 P3 (applied). Round 2: 0 P1 / 3 P2 / 3 P3 (stop condition, all folded in). Round count: 2.

## Spec (link if Gate-category)
Spec: `docs/plans/2026-07-03-remove-anon-create-gate.md`

## Verification

**RED (before the rules edit)** — inverted the two #441 denial tests in `firestore-rules-publish-readiness.test.ts` to expect success (renamed to `#818 anonymous provider can create groups (durable-credential gate removed)`), then ran the emulator suite against the *unmodified* rules:

```
$ cd functions && npx firebase-tools emulators:exec ... jest firestore-rules-publish-readiness.test.ts

  ● Publish readiness Firestore rules › #818 anonymous provider can create groups (durable-credential gate removed) › anonymous provider can create a group (valid-shaped)

    FirebaseError: 7 PERMISSION_DENIED:
      false for 'create' @ L223, false for 'create' @ L380, false for 'update' @ L223, evaluation error at L381:24 for 'update' @ L381, false for 'create' @ L223, false for 'create' @ L380

  ● Publish readiness Firestore rules › #818 anonymous provider can create groups (durable-credential gate removed) › anonymous provider can create the group + inviteCode batch

    FirebaseError: 7 PERMISSION_DENIED:
      false for 'create' @ L223, false for 'create' @ L380, false for 'update' @ L223, evaluation error at L381:24 for 'update' @ L381, false for 'create' @ L223, false for 'create' @ L238, false for 'update' @ L223, false for 'update' @ L247

Test Suites: 1 failed, 1 total
Tests:       2 failed, 199 passed, 201 total
```

Both fail for the right reason: `isDurableSignIn()` still rejects the anonymous sign-in provider.

**GREEN (after removing `isDurableSignIn()` + both call sites)**:

```
Test Suites: 1 passed, 1 total
Tests:       201 passed, 201 total
```
All 201 pass, including the full #814 `validActivityMetadata` suite (unrelated hardening merged to `origin/main` just before this branch was cut — confirmed via the spec's mandatory pre-step: `grep -c validActivityMetadata security/firestore.rules` = 2, both before and after the rules edit).

**Full verification suite**:
- [x] `flutter analyze` — clean, no issues found
- [x] `flutter test` — **2902 passed, 0 failed** (full suite)
- [x] `bash tool/check_theme_purity.sh` — PASS (touched `create_group_screen.dart`, `group_detail_screen.dart`, `group_members_section.dart`, `shadow_member_chips_field.dart`)

## Security

---

### Notable implementation details
- `GroupService.stageGroup` is now anonymity-blind: deleted `_isCurrentUserAnonymous`, `_isAnonymousOverride`, and the `isAnonymous` ctor param (would otherwise strand an `unused_field` / vacuous test seam per Gate r2 P2).
- `DurableCredentialRequiredException` deleted from `durable_credential_exception.dart` (lost its only thrower + test references); `GoogleLinkConflictException` in the same file is unrelated and untouched.

author: gregflint
body:
## ⚠️ RABBIT-HOLE FLAGGED — solo PR

Phase 1 is the **core proof** and carries the project's trickiest correctness invariants: **determinism** (byte-identical re-runs), **no `eval` of stored code** (declarative AST + owned interpreter), **decimal money** (no float drift), and **per-charge 310 currency** (never defaulted). Review these four specifically.

## Shaped work item — [86e24cy5r](https://app.clickup.com/t/86e24cy5r)

- **Problem:** Turn an EDI invoice into either a carrier kickback or a dollar scorecard, deterministically (§5, §13). Everything downstream (AI authoring, disputes, recovery) sits on this.
- **Appetite:** L
- **Solution:** Build the deterministic engine — **STANDARD tier only, no AI, no cascade**. 210 (motor) + 310 (ocean) as first-class peers.
- **No-gos (respected):** no AI/discovery/extraction, no CLIENT/CONTRACT tiers or resolver, no disputes/payment/recovery, no Temporal, no rate recomputation. None appear in this PR.

## What's in the PR

| Area | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Ingestion | `ingestion/x12.ts` | Dependency-free X12 reader; **delimiters read from ISA**, never hard-coded. |
| | `ingestion/parse-210.ts` | 210 adapter (GS01=IM): B3 header + L1 charges → `charge_fact`. |
| | `ingestion/parse-310.ts` | 310 adapter (GS01=IO): **per-charge currency (L1-20), never defaulted USD**. |
| | `ingestion/charge-fact.ts` | Shared normalized charge shape; decimal money helpers; crosswalk-categorize boundary + quarantine. |
| Rule engine | `rule-engine/ast.ts` | Declarative predicate AST (stored in `rule_version.ast`) — **never raw JS**. |
| | `rule-engine/interpreter.ts` | **Owned pure/total interpreter.** No I/O, no `Date.now`; decimal.js; `UNASSESSABLE` not throw; evaluated tree = explanation. |
| Rubric/eval | `rubric-resolver/standard-rubric.ts` | Hand-authored STANDARD criteria (3 gating, 2 scoring); footing tolerance as a parameter. |
| | `evaluator/evaluate-invoice.ts` | **Gate→score:** GATE (COLLECT_ALL → REJECTED_REWORK+kickback) → SCORE (skipped on hard-gate fail) → scorecard. |
| | `evaluator/snapshot.ts` | Stable-key rubric content hash (reproducibility pin). |
| | `evaluator/fact-bundle.ts` | Resolves invoice → fact bundle **before** eval (keeps eval pure). |
| | `evaluator/persist.ts` | Thin DB boundary: writes through `withTenantTx`, append-only respected. |

## Acceptance criteria → tests

| Criterion | Test(s) |
|---|---|
| Golden 210/310 parse to hand-checked charge facts | `AC1` (unit ×2) + `AC1 e2e` (→ charge_fact rows) |
| Malformed → `REJECTED_REWORK` + **all** failed gates (COLLECT_ALL) + citations | `AC2` (×3, incl. two-gate collect-all) + `AC2 e2e` |
| Valid → `SCORED` + per-criterion scorecard | `AC3` + `AC3 e2e` |
| Same invoice + snapshot → **byte-identical** | `AC4` (deep JSON equality + stable rubric hash) |
| Decimal-edge money, no float drift | `AC5` (0.1+0.2=0.3; approx tolerance boundary) |
| HARD gate failure → SCORE phase does NOT run | `AC6` (no findings/scorecard on rejected) + `AC2 e2e` |

## Local run results (ephemeral container Postgres, non-superuser role)

- `npm test` (unit+e2e): **13/13** (11 new pure + 2 existing)
- `npm run test:db`: **18/18** (15 existing incl. Phase 0 + 3 new persistence)
- `npm run lint` / `typecheck` / `build`: **clean / clean / exit 0**

## What to check

1. **Determinism** — `evaluateInvoice` is a pure function of (invoice, rubric); the rubric hash uses stable-key serialization. `AC4` asserts byte-identical output.
2. **No `eval`** — rules are the JSON AST in `ast.ts`, run by `interpreter.ts`. No `eval`/`new Function` anywhere.
3. **310 currency** — `parse-310` reads L1-20 per charge, falls back to C3, and leaves currency empty (→ gate failure) rather than defaulting USD.
4. **Gate→score ordering** — a hard-gate failure returns before the SCORE phase; `UNASSESSABLE` on a hard gate fails **closed** (blocks), which is the safe default for footing/currency.
5. **Crosswalk boundary** — audit logic reads `category === 'FUEL'`, never a raw code; unknown codes quarantine.

## Uncertainties / deliberate scope calls

- **STANDARD scoring criteria are pass/fail integrity checks**, so the scorecard's `$` over/under rollups are 0 here — the columns exist for the dollar-variance criteria that arrive with contract data (Phase 2+). Called out so the zero isn't read as a bug.
- **`UNASSESSABLE` on a hard gate blocks (fails closed).** Defensible default (can't certify footing you can't assess); flagging in case the intended policy for a specific gate differs.
- **EDI fixtures are hand-authored golden minimal invoices**, not captured carrier files — sufficient to pin the acceptance criteria; real carrier-variability fixtures (PRO-number placement, parcel CD3/L9) are follow-up hardening, consistent with the "ocean thinner/slower to harden" note.
- **Parser covers the L1 charge triad** needed for the criteria; the full L0/L3 weight/rate detail and N7/V1/R4 ocean segments are not parsed (not required by any acceptance criterion; would be dead code now).
