author: tannevaled
body:
## What

Close the last named interpreter-floor wall — the hot Hash/Array container methods. After AOT level-2 removed dispatch overhead, `array`/`hash`/`wordcount` still sat near the floor because the cost was *inside* the native container methods. Profiling (pprof) pinned two costs and this PR fixes both.

### Hash value-key fast path (`internal/object/object.go`)
`Hash#[]`/`#[]=` resolved a `#hash` method **per operation**: `hashKey` fell through to the VM's `CustomKeyHook` for `Integer`/`Symbol`/`Float`/`true`/`false`/`nil` keys, running a full `findMethod("hash")` ancestor walk only to discover the default `Object#hash` and fall back to the value itself — ~10% of the `hash` bench (1M Integer-keyed ops). These immediate value types (none subclassable to override `#hash`) now return directly as their own comparable map key. Byte-identical result, no per-op walk.

### Native `Array#select`/`#reduce` (`internal/vm/builtins.go`)
Only `#map`/`#each` were native; `#select`/`#reduce` ran interpreted through `Enumerable`, iterating via `__each_packed` — an `each { |*a| … }` splat that allocates an Array and does a **second block dispatch per element**. Now native single-pass loops: `select` pre-sizes its result to the input length; `reduce` mirrors every `Enumerable#reduce` argument form and error exactly. `#filter`/`#collect`/`#inject` delegate here through the prelude and inherit the fast path.

## Measured (best-of-5, Apple M-series, Ruby 4.0.5, byte-identical output)

| bench | before AOT/MRI | after AOT/MRI | before AOT/YJIT | after AOT/YJIT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **array** | 5.11× | **1.00×** (MRI parity, 0.98× @N=20) | 7.67× | 1.50× |
| hash | 3.00× | 2.33× | 3.38× | 2.33× |
| wordcount | 1.50× | 1.33× | 1.50× | 1.50× |

Interpreter `array` row itself: 0.60 → 0.26s (2.3× faster). The array `map`/`select`/`reduce` pipeline now runs **at MRI's C speed**.

**Remaining** (not container-kernel cost): `hash` is bounded by the `h[k]=v` send-dispatch (arg-slice + interface boxing on `OpSend`) and `wordcount` by `String#split` + the inherent `strKey` `[]byte→string` copy for a mutable-string key — dispatch/AOT territory, not kernel work.

## Gates
- CGO=0 build green; full `go test ./...` green with `-race` under `TZ=UTC`.
- 100% coverage on changed code (`arrayReduce`, native `select`, the new `hashKey` cases) — new tests in `internal/object/object_test.go` and `internal/vm/array_container_kernels_test.go`.
- gofmt/vet clean.
- `bench/README.md` + `BENCHMARKS.md` updated with re-measured numbers (2026-07-03).

author: meowtivator
body:
Windows에서 대표가 `install.bat` 더블클릭 → 무조건 설치되고 상주가 돌고 마법사가 뜨도록, 설치 스크립트/런처 생성기를 감사 결과대로 강화했습니다. (변경은 **생성기 2파일만**, 배포 산출물 dist는 gitignore.)

### 변경 보고

**1. 스코프** (요구 외 변경 없음)
- `apps/agent/make-dist-windows.mjs` — install.bat/uninstall.bat 생성 로직: BOM+chcp, zip-내부 실행 가드, 복사 전 상주정지+대기, xcopy 실패 가드, 숨김 실행(VBS 경유) TR, uninstall 상주정지.
- `apps/agent/package-app.mjs` — 런처 생성: `run-hidden.vbs`(창 없는 wscript 런처) 동봉, `run.cmd`에 node.exe 존재 가드, CLOUD_URL/AGENT_VERSION 보간값 형식검증(`assertLauncherSafe`).

**2. 트레이스**
대표가 재설치로 `install.bat` 더블클릭 → `chcp 65001`로 한글 콘솔 → `%HERE%package\run.cmd` 존재 확인(zip 내부면 중단) → 상주 3개 `schtasks /End` + `ping -n 3`으로 핸들 해제 대기 → `xcopy`로 `%DEST%` 갱신(실패 시 `errorlevel 1` 중단) → `schtasks /Create`가 TR을 `wscript "%DEST%\run-hidden.vbs" "%DEST%\run.cmd" <cmd>`로 등록(창 숨김) → `schtasks /Run`으로 즉시 기동 → 4317 포트 열리면 브라우저에서 마법사 오픈.

**3. 경계 스캔**
- 공개 계약(`packages/core`) 변경: 없음
- DB에 저장되는 데이터 모양 변경: 없음
- 시크릿/인증/외부 입력 경로 신설: 없음. (오히려 축소 — 런처에 박히는 CLOUD_URL/AGENT_VERSION에 `assertLauncherSafe`로 따옴표·개행·`%^&|<>` 주입 차단. 이 값들은 빌드시 env/git태그에서만 옴.)
- 새 비즈니스 판단: 복사 전 상주정지 후 `ping -n 3`(약 2초) 고정 대기 = 파일 핸들 해제용 임의 대기값. 상주 실행을 창 없는 `wscript`로 감싸는 것도 이 PR이 정한 실행 방식.

**4. 검증 절차** (소유자 직접)
- `cd apps/agent && node make-dist-windows.mjs` → `dist/win-dist/`에 `install.bat`/`uninstall.bat` + `dist/win-dist/package/run-hidden.vbs` 생성 확인.
- `xxd dist/win-dist/install.bat | head -1` → 첫 3바이트 `ef bb bf`(BOM) 확인.
- `pnpm run verify` → 이 브랜치에서 5/5 tasks 성공, schema-contract OK (회귀 없음).
- ★**실기기**: Windows PC에서 install.bat 더블클릭 → (a) 한글이 안 깨지는지, (b) 로그온 시 검은 콘솔창이 안 뜨는지, (c) 재설치 시 xcopy 실패 없이 갱신되는지.

**5. 교차 리뷰 포인트**
- **[1순위·실기기 확인] chcp 65001 + UTF-8 BOM 조합**: 실제 Windows 콘솔에서만 확실히 검증됨. BOM/코드페이지 처리는 맥에서 재현 불가. 한글이 깨져도 핵심 진행(마법사 자동 오픈)은 인코딩 무관하게 되도록 설계했으나, 대표 실기기에서 첫 확인 필요.
- **schtasks /TR 중첩 따옴표 이스케이프**: 생성된 TR = `wscript \"%DEST%\run-hidden.vbs\" \"%DEST%\run.cmd\" watch`. schtasks가 이 이스케이프를 어떻게 저장/실행하는지 실기기에서 `schtasks /Query /TN "QualiFlow Agent" /V`로 확인 권장.

body:
## Summary

The article content sanitizer already blocks EVM/Solana self-custody **wallet app deep-link schemes** (`metamask://`, `phantom://`, `trust://`, …), but not the **Substrate/Polkadot-ecosystem** wallets. Bittensor is a Substrate chain, so this adds the wallets a TAO holder is actually most likely to have installed:

- `novawallet://` — Nova Wallet
- `subwallet://` — SubWallet
- `talisman://` — Talisman

Added to all three scheme scan paths (article content, the entity-decoded re-scan, and infobox row values), matching the existing wallet-scheme rule exactly.

## Why This Should Ship

These are the on-theme wallet-drain phishing surface for a Bittensor wiki. A clicked `novawallet://wc?uri=…` (the standard WalletConnect `examplewallet://wc?uri=…` deep link) opens the reader's wallet straight to a connect / transaction-signing / approval screen — with no script and outside the page sandbox — and is never a valid `http(s)` article link. The sanitizer already blocks this class for Ethereum/Solana wallets (#1811); this closes the conspicuous gap for the chain Taopedia is actually about.

## Review Notes

- **Non-visual** — pure scheme-blocklist logic in `scripts/sync-articles.js`; no page/render changes, so no visual evidence applies.
- **Test**: `npm run test:content-sanitizer` — new cases in `scripts/check-content-sanitizer.js` assert the three schemes are rejected in article content, in the entity-obfuscated scan path, and in infobox row values, **and** that benign prose ("Nova Wallet: a Polkadot wallet", "Talisman: a browser extension") still passes (the `//`-authority form is required, so wallet-name prose is never flagged).
- Scoped to the same rule family as the merged #1811 / #1784 scheme-blocking PRs.

## Target Branch

- [x] This PR targets `test`
- [ ] This PR targets `main` only because it promotes `test` to production

## Security Checklist

- [x] No secrets, tokens, build hooks, wallet seeds, or private endpoints are included

body:
**Draft / CI spike — not for merge yet.** Closes the "no Windows DAW e2e" residual: a real third-party VST3 host (REAPER) loads `harp-shell.vst3` and renders a MIDI chord **offline** to WAV, dialing a localhost `harp-deviced` §8.7 loopback synth (`HARP_ETH_DEVICE`). The Windows twin of hw.yml's `reaper-e2e.sh` (real USB Pi under xvfb) — **same cross-platform ReaScript**, loopback instead of hardware, so it runs on the cloud runner with **no rig**.

### What this run answers (the milestones)
- **M0/M1** — REAPER installs + runs unattended on windows-2022, and **scans** harp-shell (else "not scanned → silence").
- **M2** (the residual-closer) — render exists + **rms > 0.02**: the real DAW→plugin→§8.7 loopback→audio path carried signal.
- **M3** — two renders vs two fresh daemons are **byte-identical** on the WAV `data` chunk (Tier-A determinism, no pin).
- **The crux** — each `harp-deviced` log is echoed with a HOST-PACED vs RTP verdict, so this run tells us whether REAPER's offline render propagates **`kOffline`** to the plugin (→ deterministic host-paced bounce) or free-runs RTP.

### Known uncertainties to eyeball (all fail *visibly*, not silently)
1. `reaper.ini` dummy-audio stanza — unverified exact key; worst case a startup modal the watchdog kills → shows as M2 fail.
2. REAPER default render speed = Full-speed Offline (→ kOffline) — relying on the fresh-install default; if it's "online", M3 fails + the daemon log shows RTP (expected-then-fixable, not a real regression).
3. Portable-`reaper.ini` trigger assumption (driver falls back to `%APPDATA%`).
4. Tier-B absolute pin is **dormant** (`PIN_REAPER_WIN=""`) — capture from the first green run.

Files: `.github/workflows/reaper-e2e.yml`, `scripts/reaper-e2e-loopback.sh`, `scripts/wav-rms.py` (stdlib), + an env-conditional render-cfg tweak to `scripts/reaper-e2e.lua` (Linux hw path unchanged — it's a self-compare).

author: tomconder
body:
## Summary

Implements clustered (volume tiled) forward shading for point lights, following van Oosten, *Volume Tiled Forward Shading* (2017).

- 16x9 screen-tile grid with FOV-derived log-space z slices (roughly cubic volume tiles), view-space AABBs precomputed per projection
- compute-shader light assignment with conservative sphere/AABB tests; per-cluster capacity sized to the max scene light count so index lists never truncate
- active-tile culling: the depth prepass marks each fragment's cluster, and light assignment skips clusters with no visible fragments
- point-light radiance windowed to zero at the culling radius (Karis falloff) so per-cluster culling cannot leave seams

## Fixes surfaced while validating

- SSBO `mat4` in a nested struct is read transposed by the driver (GLSL `row_major` not honored) — the view transform is now passed as explicit `float4` rows
- fragment cluster z-slice derived from view-space depth; the `gl_FragCoord.z` decode disagrees with the slice AABBs on this pipeline
- EVSM shadow lookups guarded against fragments outside the shadow frustum xy
- bloom: soft-knee extraction and progressive upsample so coarse mip texel structure never shows; scatter and default intensity tuned to keep the previous glow strength
- interleaved gradient noise dither at final 8-bit writes to remove banding in dim gradients
- shader assets deploy via an always-run `copy_assets` target, so shader edits reach the runtime folder without relinking

## Testing

- verified per-fragment ground truth in a debug shader: every light in range of a fragment is present in its cluster's light list (renders black across the scene)
- exercised 0-500 lights across attenuation ranges 7-600, runtime FOV changes (grid rebuild), and window resize
- benchmarked at 500 lights: frame time within noise of the previous brute-force assignment in this scene (shading-dominated); assignment now scales with visible geometry instead of grid size

﻿## Summary
- harden `keras.utils.get_file` filename validation by rejecting path segments that use either slash direction (`/` and `\\`) and traversal tokens (`.` / `..`)
- validate relative `cache_subdir` so it cannot escape `cache_dir`
- add regression tests for both `fname` traversal and `cache_subdir` traversal

## Why
`get_file` currently rejects `fname` only when it contains `os.sep`. On Windows, this can miss slash-style paths (`../...`) and permit path-segment inputs that should be rejected. Also, relative `cache_subdir` values can currently traverse outside `cache_dir`.

This patch enforces cross-platform path validation for both inputs while preserving support for absolute `cache_subdir`.

## Validation
- Added tests in `keras/src/utils/file_utils_test.py`:
  - `test_get_file_rejects_path_segments_in_fname`
  - `test_get_file_rejects_relative_cache_subdir_traversal`

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The @mysociety/api build fails with `npm error Unsupported URL Type "workspace:": workspace:*` because Railpack detects npm as the package manager (no lock file in apps/api) and runs `npm install`, which can't resolve pnpm workspace:* dependencies. A previous fix set `RAILPACK_INSTALL_CMD = ""` in `[deploy.variables]` of railway.toml, but that section is only available at runtime — not during the Railpack build phase — so the auto-detected `npm install` step was never skipped.

## Solution

Added `apps/api/railpack.json` with `"installCmd": ""` so Railpack reads it during build plan generation and skips the install step entirely, letting the existing `buildCommand` handle installation via `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` from the monorepo root. Also removed the now-redundant `[deploy.variables]` section from `railway.toml`.

### Changes
- **Modified** `apps/api/railway.toml`
- **Created** `apps/api/railpack.json`

author: tamnd
body:
Stacked on #139.

A go: function that takes or returns `[]byte` now marshals through the byte bridge, completing the Uint8Array crossing that #139 lowers on the TypeScript side.

## What lands
- A Uint8Array argument crosses into a `[]byte` parameter through `bridge.BytesToGo`.
- A `[]byte` result crosses back through `bridge.BytesFromGo` into a Uint8Array.
- `bentoResultType` names `*value.Uint8Array` for a bytes result so the guard closure returns it.

Both directions default to the copying form, the safe crossing when the callee's retention is not known (section 7.3). The zero-copy `BytesToGoShared`/`BytesFromGoShared` forms are the fast path a later slice reaches for once it can prove read-only access.

## Test
An end-to-end test runs both directions through `encoding/hex`: a Uint8Array built from a number list encodes to a hex string, and `hex.DecodeString` returns a `([]byte, error)` whose error half unwraps into the throw machinery and whose byte half crosses back into a Uint8Array read by length and index.

author: nikunjmavani
body:
## Hotfix — production deploy of 4.8.0 is blocked

The `main` post-merge deploy for the 4.8.0 release **failed** at the *Validate GitHub environment secrets* step:

```
[ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_EXEC_FIRST_FAIL] Command "core-infra" not found
```

`reusable-railway-deploy.yml` invoked `pnpm --dir core-infra validate:github-env`, but the script extracted into the standalone **core-infra** repo (#820) is named **`validate:github-environments`**. The mismatch aborts the deploy *before* migrations/Railway steps run — so production cleanly stayed on the previous version (nothing half-applied), but 4.8.0 never went live.

## Fix
One-line: point the step at the correct script name (`validate:github-environments`), and correct the stale `src/github/validate.ts` → `src/github/environments.ts` comment reference. All other `core-infra` scripts this workflow calls (`setup:infra`, `setup:infra:plan`, `setup:infra:status`, `tool:railway-deploy-image`) already match core-infra's `package.json`.

## After merge
Re-run the production deploy (post-merge CI / `workflow_dispatch`) to bring prod live on 4.8.0. Deploy does not depend on Matrix Tests or release-please, so this unblocks production on its own. (The `v4.8.0` tag + `main→dev` back-merge are tracked separately — they need the Matrix test-seed fix.)

author: seanchatmangpt
body:
chore(hooks): remove the regex-based Andon scanner - duplicates anti-llm-cheat-lsp

The Andon "stop the line" mechanism built into post_tool_use_emitter.sh
(scan Bash output for compiler-error/test-failure/panic patterns via a
hand-rolled bash regex, raise a flag file, block Stop while it's up -
plus the session/staleness bookkeeping in lib/common.sh and the
flag-check in stop_release_gate.sh) was a stale, weaker reimplementation
of an already-integrated, actively-maintained sibling tool:
~/anti-llm-cheat-lsp.

Evidence this is genuinely redundant, not just similar in spirit:

- anti-llm-cheat-lsp is a dedicated LSP server + CLI with a proper
  AhoCorasick multi-pattern engine, a tree-sitter AST scanner, a Cargo
  manifest parser, a markdown-claims parser, a JSON-RPC transcript
  validator, and a BLAKE3 receipt validator - six detection layers
  versus one bash grep -E. It ships 61 dogfood tests plus negative
  control fixtures.
- Its diagnostic-code table explicitly lists GGEN-* ("ggen violation,
  triggers gate ANDON") and WASM4PM-* as first-class categories it
  already gates on - this tool is designed to be ggen's Andon enforcer,
  not a sibling ggen should out-compete with bash regex.
- ggen's own repo already carries a generated scaffold copy of this
  exact tool under .specify/specs/lsp-max/examples/lsp-max-scaffold/,
  and docs/cargo-cicd-80-20-roadmap.md documents the real integration:
  `just lsp-check` runs `cargo cicd lsp check` (the anti-llm-cheat
  cargo-cicd feature), scanning every changed .rs file for undeclared
  deps, fabricated examples lacking OTEL/test evidence, and stub
  implementations marked complete. .github/workflows/ci.yml's
  cargo-cicd job already runs this in CI.

So ggen already has an authoritative, external, tested mechanism for
this exact class of detection, wired into its own CI. The bash-regex
version in .claude/hooks/ was pure duplication and, per the earlier
gap-audit workflow (PR #247), a worse one (false positives on any
output merely containing the word "error", false negatives on stack
overflows and capitalized Error:, a truncation bug hiding the actual
failing subcommand). Rather than continuing to patch a component that
should not exist in ggen at all, remove it - the same "post-split
residue, delete it" doctrine CLAUDE.md already applies to process-mining
analysis code that belongs in wasm4pm-compat instead of ggen.

Changes:
- Deleted post_tool_use_emitter.sh and stop_release_gate.sh (nothing
  left in either once the scanner/flag-check logic is gone).
- lib/common.sh: removed the Andon-only helpers (flag path/raise/clear/
  age/staleness/session-id, stop_block); kept read_input/jqf/
  additional_context/deny_tool, still used by session-start.sh,
  user-prompt.sh, and pre_tool_use_guard.sh.
- session-start.sh: removed the ANDON_NOTE block reading the flag;
  kept branch/uncommitted-count/compile-canary/jq-missing-guard, which
  are ggen workspace-state reporting, not LLM-cheat-pattern detection.
- .claude/settings.json: removed the Stop and PostToolUse hook
  registrations (their only scripts are gone). SessionStart,
  UserPromptSubmit, and PreToolUse (including the Edit|Write|Bash
  matcher from PR #247) are unaffected.

Kept as-is (different domain, no overlap with anti-llm-cheat-lsp):
pre_tool_use_guard.sh (hard-denies writes to ggen-specific protected
paths - a prevention mechanism for locations anti-llm-cheat-lsp has no
knowledge of) and user-prompt.sh's 4 operational-rule checks (just vs
cargo, destructive git, forbidden tools, TTL-vs-markdown specs - ggen
policy, not code-content cheat-pattern detection).

Verified: bash -n syntax-checks clean on all remaining scripts; `jq .
.claude/settings.json` confirms valid JSON with SessionStart/
UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse intact; grep for "andon" in .claude/hooks/
returns only this removal's own explanatory comment, no live code;
manually exercised session-start.sh, user-prompt.sh, and
pre_tool_use_guard.sh with synthetic Claude Code JSON and confirmed all
three still produce correct additionalContext/permissionDecision
payloads with the Andon paragraph gone.

body:
This pull request improves the security and reliability of widget authentication by ensuring that the embedding page's origin is explicitly passed and validated when authenticating widget requests. This helps prevent unauthorized domains from embedding the widget, even if the iframe's own origin or headers could be spoofed. The changes affect both the frontend and backend, and include new tests to verify the correct behavior.

Key changes:

**Frontend: Pass embedding page origin**

## PR Description

### Summary
This pull request addresses the issue of optimizing image loading performance in the application, as outlined in [Issue #1](https://github.com/frenemy17/mentzer/issues/1). The goal is to improve the overall user experience by reducing the time it takes for images to load.

### Changes
The following changes have been made to optimize image loading performance:
* Replaced standard `img` tags with `next/image` components to leverage Next.js's built-in image optimization capabilities.
* Implemented lazy loading to defer the loading of images until they come into view, reducing the initial payload and improving page load times.
* Added responsive sizes to ensure images are properly scaled for different screen sizes and devices.

### Test Plan
To verify the effectiveness of these changes, the following tests were conducted:
* A single test was run using the Jest framework, which passed successfully (1/1).
* The test validated that the image loading performance improvements do not introduce any regressions or break existing functionality.

This PR is now ready for review. Once merged, it will improve the image loading performance of the application, providing a better experience for users.

Closes #1

author: braden-w
body: This consolidates Local Mail's Phase 3 write-through surfaces before the UI binds to them. The CLI is now human-shaped: `archive`, `unarchive`, `mark-read`, `mark-unread`, and `label` replace the generic `modify` command with no compatibility alias. Human-readable output is the default for triage/status/sync, while `--json` preserves the typed machine contracts. `query` stays JSON-first as the deliberate exception. MCP stays intentionally small: one `modify_labels` tool, no per-intent sugar. Its adapter-facing fields are now `addLabels` / `removeLabels` because they accept Gmail ids or exact names, and per-id failures remain structured data instead of being collapsed into a stringified transport error. The planned UI boundary is now one modify adapter route: ```txt POST /api/messages/modify { ids, addLabels, removeLabels } -> ModifyMessageLabelsOutcome ``` That keeps CLI, MCP, and future HTTP on the same result contract while preserving the one core primitive: Gmail writes go through `modifyMessageLabels`, and SQLite only folds Gmail-returned bytes. --- Need help on this PR? author: sarnav07
body:
## Summary
Implements the cached fetch path for block-level metadata using the RpcClient (#2) and CacheConfig/read_json/write_json (#1).

## Changes
- `resolve_block_number` resolves tags ("latest", "finalized", etc.) via RPC; numeric IDs skip resolution entirely (no RPC call)
- `fetch_block_metadata`: cache-first lookup, RPC fetch on miss, atomic write via existing `write_json`
- Populates the existing `BlockContext` type from `crates/types` — no new struct defined
- Malformed cache files trigger a silent refetch, not a hard error (open to making this a hard failure if preferred)
- Missing block numbers: an RPC response of `null` is treated as "block not found," distinct from transport/timeout errors
- **Tag-based fetches cost 2 RPC calls on a cache miss** — one to resolve the tag to a block number, one to fetch by that number. No cheaper resolution method exists for `finalized`/`safe`/`pending` tags. Numeric `BlockId::Number` fetches cost 1 call.
- Tests: 3 parsing tests (full block, missing base fee, missing required field) + 4 integration tests via wiremock/tempfile (cache miss, cache hit, malformed cache, tag resolution)

## Related Issue

Closes #3

- [x] I updated tests where behavior changed
- [x] I updated documentation where needed

**P1（データ喪失）**: `.claude/settings.local.json` を disposable 扱いしていたが、gwt はこれを **merge 生成**し user hooks / unrelated top-level settings を保持する（`gwt-skills` `settings_local.rs`）。ユーザー編集が force-remove で失われ得た。
→ disposable 集合から除外。`.codex/hooks.json` も同様に merge されるため含めない。disposable は **PURE managed skill/command dir**（`.claude/skills/gwt-*` / `.claude/commands/gwt-*` / `.codex/skills/gwt-*`）と `.DS_Store` のみ。

**P2（prune 経路の誤分類）**: `mark_agent_session_stopped` は branchless 確認で保護済みだったが、startup の `prune_orphan_intake_worktrees` は basename のみで判定していた。
→ prune も `worktree.branch.is_some()` をスキップ（`list()` の `WorktreeInfo` 再利用で追加コストなし）。

**P2（.codex/hooks.json pinning）**: 上記 P1 対応で merged hook ファイルは keep。intake agent は gwt managed hooks を必要とするため launched intake worktree はこれらを持つ＝現状 keep（reap されない）。これは**データ安全側の interim**で、launched intake の精密な reap（managed 部分を regenerate して diff し user 由来のみ keep）は intake-launch が実在する **Phase 3** のライフサイクルで実装する。Phase 1 時点では production で intake 起動が未配線のため機能退行はない。

## Summary

Documents the computed `current_env.composite_topology` Jinja macro in `docs/template-macros.md`. The entry
describes the resolved composite topology of an environment (baseline plus satellites, including Blue-Green domains),
its member shape, the HashMap type, the `{}` default, and the composite-only scope.

Part of #1545.

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

`docs`.

The documented shape is the V9 core model with namespace names only. A namespace member carries `originNamespace`. A
Blue-Green member additionally carries `peerNamespace` and `controllerNamespace`. Member kind is implied by the
presence of `peerNamespace` and `controllerNamespace`, so there is no `type` or `topologyType` discriminator. The

body:
## Summary

Makes bounce rate trustworthy for a single-page app by switching from "single pageview" to an **engaged-session** definition (like GA4's engagement model).

- The tracking hook fires an **"engage" ping 10s** into a page view — cleared on navigation/unmount, so a quick exit still counts as a bounce.
- `track-view` marks the session engaged on that ping (`page_views.engaged`).
- `ops_traffic_stats()` **bounce = sessions with one pageview AND not engaged** — i.e. the visitor left within ~10 seconds. A 5-minute read of one page no longer counts as a bounce.

Traffic panel labels updated to match ("one page, left <10s").

## DB (already applied)
- `supabase/migrations/20260628120000_engaged_bounce.sql` — adds `engaged` column + reworks the stats function.

body:
Teach LowerCompositeOps to emit the NCCL-style chunked reduce-scatter +
allgather ring schedule from `pld.tensor.allreduce(target, signal, mode="ring")`.

## What

- **DSL/IR**: add `mode="mesh"|"ring"` kwarg to both DSL wrapper and IR-level
  allreduce builder, plus C++ operator attr registration
- **Pass**: `LowerTensorRingAllReduceRule` (~220 lines) with 2(P−1)-step
  RS+AG ring phases, per-round AtomicAdd→WaitGe barriers, dynamic-NR-safe
  chunk sizing (constant-folded when SIZE and NR are ConstInt)
- **Tests**: 6 UT (decomposition, control-flow, idempotency, signal validation,
  mesh-default-unchanged, unsupported-op rejection) + 1 ST (P=2/P=4 sim,
  golden-verified) + hand-rolled ring ST moved into `collectives/` and renamed
  for consistency
- **Docs**: EN + zh-CN updates to `distributed_ops.md` and
  `12-lower_composite_ops.md`

## Verification

- Sim Docker: 41/41 UT + P=2 ring ST + P=4 ring ST — all pass
- Sim Docker: existing mesh allreduce UT + ST unchanged
- Pre-commit: ruff, cpplint, markdownlint, clang-format, pyright — all clean

## Review feedback addressed

Hardening added after the initial review (bots: gemini, chatgpt-codex, copilot,
CodeRabbit):

- **Reject unknown `mode`** — any value other than `"mesh"` / `"ring"` now errors
  instead of silently falling back to mesh.
- **Ring requires an exact chunk split** — `mode="ring"` now requires `SIZE` (per-rank
  dim) to be an exact multiple of `NR`; a non-divisible size previously dropped the
  tail chunk silently.
- **Ring requires an explicit signal** — the host no-signal synthesis path is
  mesh-only (it produces a `[world_size, 1]` signal), so `mode="ring"` without an
  explicit `[2*(NR−1), NR]` signal is now rejected in the DSL wrapper.
- **User-facing validation** — the ring rule's target/signal shape and dtype checks
  use `CHECK` (ValueError) instead of `INTERNAL_CHECK`, since they validate
  user-supplied DSL type annotations.
- **Minor cleanup** — deduplicated an identical `send_idx` / `recv_add_idx` binding;
  fixed a duplicated paragraph and stale references in the allreduce docs/comments.

author: uburro
body:
## Problem

The jail-logs otel collector spams error-level logs with huge stacktraces: `invalid character '\u0000' looking for beginning of value`. Check output files on the shared jail FS are truncated and rewritten in place by `check_runner.py`, so the collector (tailing from another node) can read partially flushed lines with zero-filled tails, and the `json_parser` fails on them. Logs are still delivered — it's pure noise. Reproduces on some clusters (m42-h200, ami-labs) depending on storage/timing.

## Solution

Hardened the `parse_json_body` operator in the jail-logs collector config:
- extended the `if` guard to skip lines containing NUL bytes;
- added `on_error: send_quiet` so any other parse failure sends the entry unparsed and logs at debug instead of error.

The parser is kept because it feeds `slurm_run_status` / `slurm_run_resolution` log labels (added in #2125).

## Testing

- `make helmtest`
- `helm template` — verified the rendered operator config is valid and contains the new condition and `on_error`.
- on the live cluster

## Release Notes

Fix: jail-logs otel collector no longer emits error-level noise when reading partially flushed health check output files containing NUL bytes.

author: anandarajrepo
body:
## Summary
Modified the DI_difference exit condition to use a running average that adapts throughout the position, rather than a static average locked at entry time. This allows the exit threshold to reflect current momentum conditions more dynamically.

## Key Changes
- **Replaced static average with running average**: Changed from `di_diff_avg_at_entry` (single value locked at entry) to `di_diff_running_sum` and `di_diff_running_count` that accumulate across all bars in the position
- **Seeded at entry**: The running average is initialized with the entry bar's DI_difference value (sum=value, count=1)
- **Extended each bar**: While in position, the running average is extended with each new bar's DI_difference value, allowing the threshold to adapt as momentum evolves
- **Updated exit logic**: Exit condition now compares current DI_difference against the live running average (`di_diff_running_sum / di_diff_running_count`) instead of the static entry value
- **Reset on exit**: Running sum and count are reset to 0 when exiting a position
- **Updated documentation**: Clarified the behavior in both the code comments and the strategy configuration file to explain that the average is now maintained and adapted throughout the position

## Implementation Details
- The running average is only extended when the position remains open (in the `else` block after exit checks)
- This ensures the threshold continuously reflects the momentum trend since entry, providing more responsive exit signals as market conditions change
- The exit still only triggers when `di_diff_confirm_enabled` is True and the running count is greater than 0

Wires the next batch of innate abilities (Execution queue step 9, **Batch D+E — stat-drop protection**), following the recipe in `fork-docs/INNATE_ABILITIES.md`. All four are **1:1 clean-upside copies** (a stat-drop protector never hurts its holder), so no pure-boon divergence.

## Abilities
- **Clear Body / White Smoke** — keep *any* of the holder's stats from being lowered by another mon's move or ability.
- **Hyper Cutter** — protects Attack; **Big Pecks** — protects Defense.

## Effect wiring
- **`battle_stat_change.c`** — the prior innate Keen Eye / Illuminate accuracy block in `IsAbilityBlocked` is generalized into a new `GetInnateStatDropProtector(battler, stat, &fullProtection)` helper covering full-stat protectors (whole-stat script) and single-stat protectors (specific script). The pop-up/record is overwritten to the innate (`abilityPopupOverwrite`), so a mon whose chosen ability differs still shows the innate. No `DETERMINISTIC_*` surface is touched (stat drops from primary status moves and secondary effects share this site).
- **AI (`battle_ai_util.c`, `battle_ai_switch.c`)** — stat-drop reasoning lives in dedicated helpers, so `CanLowerStat` and the Intimidate switch-in heuristic `CanIntimidateLowerOpponentAtk` are made innate-aware (mirroring the existing Keen Eye / Speed Boost innate checks). The `BattlerBenefitsFromAbilityScore` ability-value read is identity, not effect, so it stays untouched.
- Suppression parity via `IsInnateActive()` — all four are breakable, so Mold Breaker pierces an innate one exactly as the real ability.

## Data (canon-only, no flavor picks)
Every canon user (any ability slot) plus Mega/Gigantamax mirrors (the FORMS pure-boon convention), merged into existing rows where a species already had an innate.

## Frontier (Step 3.5)
All 28 hardcoded sets in `frontier_extended_mons.c` freed. Most take a complementary **real** slot (Kingler→Sheer Force, Pinsir→Moxie, Torkoal→Drought, Centiskorch→Flash Fire, Dragapult→Infiltrator, Crabominable→Anger Point). platform's scheduled `Update Agent Skills` and `TODOs` workflows have failed since the reusable-workflows merge: platform's SHA-pin security policy rejects the tag-based self-references our reusable workflows resolve at run time, and the org direction (SHA-pinning everywhere, .github#67) would spread this to every consumer.

author: copilot
body:
The Staff creation inputs were being treated like login credentials by the browser, causing autofilled username/password values and WebKit autofill styling to appear in an admin workflow where they do not belong. This change scopes the form away from credential autofill heuristics and keeps autofilled inputs visually aligned with the app’s input styling.

- **Form semantics**
  - Convert the staff creation row into a real `<form>` with submit handling instead of a button-only action.
  - Disable form-level autofill and assign explicit field names so the browser is less likely to match the inputs to saved login credentials.
  - Mark the password field as `autoComplete="new-password"` to avoid credential reuse behavior.

- **Autofill styling**
  - Add shared `.input` overrides for `:-webkit-autofill` states.
  - Preserve the existing input surface, text color, caret color, and focus ring when the browser applies autofill.

- **Behavioral impact**
  - Keeps the Staff add flow visually neutral even when the browser has saved credentials.
  - Retains keyboard submit behavior through standard form submission.

```jsx
<form autoComplete="off" onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); addStaff() }}>
  <input className="input" name="staff-handle" autoComplete="off" />
  <input type="password" className="input" name="staff-password" autoComplete="new-password" />
  <button type="submit" className="btn-primary">Add</button>
</form>
```

author: tokuhirom
body:
Advances `S09-subscript/slice.t` from 52/56 to 55/56 by fixing three independent features (tests 54-56). Only test 35 (nested slice adverbs, a larger §3 container-identity feature) remains before whitelisting.

## test 56 — `@a[**]` HyperWhatever hammer index
`@a[**]` now recursively descends nested arrays and returns every leaf as a flat List (`[0,[1,[2,3]]][**]` == `(0,1,2,3)`). Added `hyperwhatever_hammer_collect` + a `Value::HyperWhatever` index arm in `vm_var_index_ops.rs`. (Local raku is NYI here, but the roast expected value `[^10].List` is deterministic.)

## tests 54-55 — nested lazy slice bind (`:=`) in expression context
`(@a[lazy 1,2,(4,5),4,5] := "a"...*)` was silently parsed without the `__mutsu_bind_index_value` marker and executed as plain `=` assignment (boundary truncation + final-state return). Two root causes:
1. `try_parse_assign_expr` (the paren/expression path) didn't wrap the RHS in the bind marker for index targets — now it does, matching the statement-level handler.
2. The VM had no bind-specific distributor. Added `bind_slice_key_tree` (write-time values, no boundary truncation) + `slice_key_tree_max_index_all`, dispatched from the LazyList arm on `bind_mode`.

`simple_expr_stmt::{lvalue,predicates}` and the two bind helpers were made `pub(crate)` so the expression path can reuse them.

## Testing
- `roast/S09-subscript/slice.t`: 52/56 → 55/56 (test 35 remains).
- New regression: `t/hyperwhatever-and-lazy-slice-bind.t` (8 cases).
- All targeted bind/slice/subscript/adverb local tests pass.
- Assignment (`=`) semantics unchanged (still truncates + final-state values).

author: jakobengdahl
body:
## Summary

Drains the `[2026-07-01]` item from `SMALL_FIXES.md`: **`FloatingSearch` icon resolution ignored per-profile schema `icon` overrides.**

`FloatingToolbar.jsx` had two divergent icon-resolution paths. The toolbar used `resolveIcon(nodeType, schema)`, which checks `schema.node_types[type].icon` first and falls back to `LEGACY_ICON_MAP` by node-type name. But the exported `ICON_MAP` — the only thing `FloatingSearch.jsx` used for search-result icons — was built *only* from `LEGACY_ICON_MAP` and never looked at the schema. As a result, a profile that overrode a node type's icon via config got the override in the toolbar but not in search results.

### Changes
- `FloatingToolbar.jsx`: export the existing `resolveIcon` helper; remove the now-dead static `ICON_MAP` export (it was only consumed by `FloatingSearch`).
- `FloatingSearch.jsx`: resolve each result's icon via `resolveIcon(node.type, schema)` (schema is already pulled from the store) instead of the static map.

Side effect (intentional, and consistent with the toolbar): unknown node types now fall back to `QuestionCircleFill` rather than rendering no icon.

## Scope — not changed
- No change to `resolveIcon` logic, `LEGACY_ICON_MAP`, `COLOR_MAP`, or the icon registry.
- The two remaining open `SMALL_FIXES.md` items (`GroupNode` Tab-focus menu close, `t()` fallback pattern) are untouched.

## Test plan
- `npx vitest run` — full frontend suite: 102 passed (incl. `FloatingSearch.test.jsx`).
- Manual: load a profile whose `schema_config.json` overrides a node type's `icon`; confirm the search-result icon now matches the toolbar icon for that type.

body:
## Что делает

Отклонение кандидата становится «прощающим»: после Reject — тост с **«Вернуть»** на 7 секунд; сервер разрешает откатить **последнее** отклонение в течение **10 минут** (D3). Кандидат **никогда не видит отменённое отклонение** и «Not selected» не мелькает во время окна.

## Изменения

**Миграция** `20260703000000_t2_revert_rejection.sql` (аддитивная, `CREATE OR REPLACE`):
- `revert_last_rejection(uuid)` — проверка владельца, откат последнего отклонения в окне 10 мин, пишет revert-запись в `application_status_log`. Ошибки: `NOT_OWNER` / `NOT_REJECTED` / `UNDO_EXPIRED`.
- `get_application_status` — **маскировка для кандидата**: свежее (<10 мин) или отменённое отклонение отдаётся как прежний статус; из таймлайна прячутся маскированные отклонения и сами revert-записи.

**Код**
- `employer/actions.ts` — `revertRejection()` с кодами ошибок (expired/not_rejected/not_owner/generic).
- `ApplicationsBoard`:
  - Reject — оптимистично + **тост `aria-live` «Отклонено — Вернуть» на 7 c**.
  - Свежие rejected-карты (<10 мин, этой сессии) держат ссылку **«↩ Вернуть»**.
  - Возврат восстанавливает карту + тост «Возвращено»; истёкшее окно → локализованный тост.
- i18n ×4 (rejectedToast / undo / restored / undoExpired).

## Соответствие acceptance
- Reject → тост виден ≥ 7 c; Undo восстанавливает карту без перезагрузки. ✅
- `application_status_log` содержит и отклонение, и revert. ✅
- Статус-страница кандидата в окне показывает прежний статус; после окна (если не отменено) — «Not selected». ✅
- Undo после 10 мин → локализованная ошибка, статус не меняется. ✅

## Границы (Do NOT)
- Нет свободного редактирования статуса — только «откат последнего отклонения».
- Правила прямых переходов не тронуты.
- Кандидату при reject **не** шлётся push/email (D8) — согласовано с T9.

## ⚠️ Применение миграции
`get_application_status` **заменяется** — это меняет поведение, видимое кандидату, поэтому миграцию нужно применить к общей живой БД `uuopxzlcmzdtwebottar` **вместе с мержем/деплоем** (не раньше). Идемпотентна. Могу применить через Supabase-коннектор сразу после мержа — скажи.

## Регрессия после мержа
4 сценария CLAUDE.md + новый: reject → undo → таймлайн показывает оба перехода (для работодателя), кандидат отменённого reject не видит.

author: acurioustale
body:
The deploy-key jail's option allowlist matched `--chmod=*` with any value. A key holder crafting their own rsync command could send `--chmod=D777,F777` and make the mirrored web root world-writable on the shared host - a real (if narrow) widening beyond the single option bundle `deploy.sh` actually sends, defeating the jail's stated goal of confining the key to exactly the deploy.

This pins the allowlist entry to the exact `--chmod=D755,F644` deploy.sh uses, so any other mode is rejected like every other disallowed long option.

**Note:** the server file is authoritative and runs the real deploys; this checked-in copy is for review and recovery only, so the host file at `/home/www/web4186/bin/rsync-jail-acurioustale.sh` must be updated by hand for the change to take effect (see `ops/README.md`).

Verified under `/bin/sh` (matching the script's shebang and the host word-splitting) that the real deploy command `rsync --server -vlogDtprze.iLsfxC --delete --chmod=D755,F644 . html/acurioustale.de/` still passes, while `--chmod=D777,F777`, `--chmod=u+s` and `--rsync-path=evil` are all rejected. shellcheck and shfmt clean; the `ops/README.md` wording was updated to match.

body:
## Fast-forward `release` branch on every release

Adds `.github/workflows/fast-forward-release-branch.yml`. On every
`release: published`, it mints the livespec GitHub App installation token
(mirroring `release-please.yml`), checks out the released tag's commit, and
fast-forwards `refs/heads/release` to it. The push is fast-forward-only (no
`--force`), so a diverged `release` branch fails the job loudly rather than
being silently rewritten.

The `release` branch itself was created at the current latest release commit
(`v0.5.0` = `55ff6a4`); this workflow keeps it advancing on each subsequent
release.

**Substrate for fleet plugin ref-pinning** — core epic **livespec-c1k9**
(fleet-plugin-currency), design `plan/fleet-plugin-currency/research/design.md`
§L1a. The fleet marketplace registrations (a later slice) pin each plugin to
the `release` branch ref, which must always resolve to the latest published
release commit.

author: steveelouga
body:
## Probleme

`Logout` etait le seul RPC (sur 13) du servicer Auth a intercepter
`AuthenticationError` localement pour retourner un
`StatusResponse(success=False)`, plutot que de laisser
`ErrorHandlingInterceptor` gerer l'exception de facon centralisee
(-> gRPC `UNAUTHENTICATED`), comme le font deja `Login`,
`ValidateToken`, `RefreshToken` et tous les autres RPC de ce servicer.

Pas un bug fonctionnel a proprement parler, mais une divergence de
pattern qui aurait pu induire en erreur un futur RPC copiant ce
pattern par mimetisme (ANO-020, voir `docs/ETAT_DU_SYSTEME.md`, PR #17).

## Changement

- Supprime le `try/except AuthenticationError` local dans `Logout`. Un
  token invalide/expire passe desormais par le meme chemin que partout
  ailleurs dans ce servicer.
- **Note sur le comportement observable** : `logout` avec un token
  invalide levera desormais une erreur gRPC `UNAUTHENTICATED` au lieu
  de retourner silencieusement `success=False`. Cote gateway, aucun
  changement necessaire : `GrpcErrorExtension` traduit deja
  generiquement toute erreur gRPC en erreur GraphQL, quel que soit le
  RPC d'origine (verifie : `gateway/schema/tests/test_auth.py` mocke
  `auth_client.logout` au niveau du client, independamment du
  comportement interne du servicer, donc non affecte).
- Met a jour `test_logout_failure_returns_unsuccessful_status` ->
  `test_logout_failure_raises_authentication_error`, alignee sur le
  pattern des tests `test_login_failure_raises_authentication_error`
  / `test_validate_token_failure_raises_authentication_error` /
  `test_refresh_token_failure_raises_authentication_error` deja
  existants.

## Test plan

- [x] `python manage.py test comptes` : 88/88 verts
- [x] `ruff check .` : clean
- [x] `coverage report --fail-under=80` : 97%
- [x] `bandit -r . --exclude ./proto,./comptes/migrations -ll` : aucun probleme

author: riccardomanfrin
body:
## Describe your changes

`WGWatcher` monitors WireGuard handshake liveness and tears down a dead transport so the guard reconnects. Fixes a race where the watcher could silently stop running, plus a related teardown race.

1. **Per-instance watcher (main fix).** The watcher was a reused instance guarded by an `enabled` bool; `disableWgWatcherIfNeeded` only `cancel()`ed the goroutine, which cleared `enabled` *after* its loop returned (scheduler-dependent delay). On a fast disconnect + independent relay/ICE "ready", the re-enable saw a stale `enabled == true` and started nothing → a "connected" peer with no liveness watcher, never retried. Fix: create a fresh watcher per connection attempt, dropped on disable; lifecycle fully owned by `Conn` under `conn.mu`, so enable/disable can't race the old goroutine's async shutdown. Removed `enabled`/`muEnabled`.

2. **Recheck watcher ctx under `conn.mu` in `onWGDisconnected`.** `handshakeCheck` runs lock-free; between its ctx check and acquiring `conn.mu`, a fast reconnect can slip in. `onWGDisconnected` checked only `conn.ctx` (engine-scoped), but disable cancels `wgWatcherCtx` — so a stale watcher could tear down the **new** connection on the old timeout (flap). Now it also rechecks `watcherCtx.Err()` under the lock.

3. **Log clarity.** Distinguish "handshake not updated" from an actual timeout.

Deadlock constraint preserved: `disableWgWatcherIfNeeded` never waits for the goroutine (the timeout path reentrantly calls back under `conn.mu`); the cancelled goroutine drains via its own `ctx.Done()`.

Verified: `go test -run TestWGWatcher ./client/internal/peer/` passes, `go build ./client/...` clean.

## Issue ticket number and link

No public GitHub issue — internal client-reliability fix for a scheduler-dependent race in the WireGuard liveness watcher. Pre-fix paths on `main`: [`disableWgWatcherIfNeeded`](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/blob/f6900fb07c68cfcececc48cdc0de1e42bf97b5e2/client/internal/peer/conn.go#L819), [`onWGDisconnected`](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/blob/f6900fb07c68cfcececc48cdc0de1e42bf97b5e2/client/internal/peer/conn.go#L670).

author: robotsix-mill[bot]
body:
## Problem

`.pre-commit-config.yaml` does not conform to the project's standard hook set. Three hooks from the standard are missing (`check-json`, `detect-private-key`, `actionlint`), and one image-repo-required hook (`hadolint`) is absent despite `Dockerfile` existing. The `bandit` hook must be dropped because bandit gates in CI rather than as a pre-commit hook.

## Scope

One file to edit: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.

### 1 — Add `check-json` and `detect-private-key` to the existing `pre-commit-hooks` block

The block already uses `https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks` at `v6.0.0`. Both hooks ship in that same repo; just add two `- id:` lines:

```yaml
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v6.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: trailing-whitespace
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
      - id: check-yaml
      - id: check-toml
      - id: check-merge-conflict
      - id: check-added-large-files
      - id: check-json          # ADD
      - id: detect-private-key  # ADD
```

### 2 — Drop the `bandit` repo block entirely

Remove:
```yaml
  - repo: https://github.com/PyCQA/bandit
    rev: 1.9.4
    hooks:
      - id: bandit
        args: ["-c", "pyproject.toml"]
```
Bandit gates in CI; it must not run as a pre-commit hook per the standard.

### 3 — Add `actionlint` repo block

Insert after the `mypy` local hook block and before the `bandit` block (which will have been deleted):

```yaml
  - repo: https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint
    rev: <RESOLVED_TAG>   # see resolution command below
    hooks:
      - id: actionlint
```

Resolve the latest stable tag before writing `rev`:
```bash
git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint.git \
  | grep -E 'refs/tags/v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' \
  | sort -V | tail -1 | awk '{print $1, $2}'
```
Use the tag name (e.g. `v1.7.7`) as `rev`. No `args` needed — actionlint auto-discovers `.github/workflows/`.

### 4 — Add `hadolint` repo block

Insert after the `uv-audit` local hook block (or anywhere sensible after linters):

```yaml
  - repo: https://github.com/hadolint/hadolint
    rev: <RESOLVED_TAG>   # see resolution command below
    hooks:
      - id: hadolint
```

Resolve the latest stable tag:
```bash
git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/hadolint/hadolint.git \
  | grep -E 'refs/tags/v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' \
  | sort -V | tail -1 | awk '{print $1, $2}'
```

No `.hadolint.yaml` exists in the repo today; if the `Dockerfile` triggers lint warnings that should be suppressed project-wide, create `.hadolint.yaml` at the repo root in the same commit. Otherwise leave it absent and let hadolint run with defaults.

### Final hook order (recommended)

```
pre-commit-hooks  (file checks — trailing-ws, eof, yaml, toml, merge-conflict, large-files, check-json, detect-private-key)
typos
ruff-pre-commit   (ruff, ruff-format)
local             (mypy)
actionlint        ← new
uv-audit          (local)
hadolint          ← new
detect-secrets
local             (vulture)
markdownlint-cli2
mdformat
```

## Acceptance criteria

1. `.pre-commit-config.yaml` contains `check-json` and `detect-private-key` under the `pre-commit-hooks` repo block.
2. No `bandit` repo block or hook id appears anywhere in the file.
3. An `actionlint` hook appears, pinned to a resolved stable tag (not a branch or floating ref).
4. A `hadolint` hook appears, pinned to a resolved stable tag.
5. `pre-commit run --all-files` exits 0 (or any failures are pre-existing content issues, not hook-config errors).
6. `detect-secrets`, `vulture`, `mypy`, `ruff`, `ruff-format`, `typos`, `uv-audit`, `markdownlint-cli2`, and `mdformat` hooks are **unchanged** (same rev, same args).

## Out of scope / constraints

- Do **not** upgrade any existing hook revision — only add new entries or remove `bandit`.
- Do **not** add `bandit` back in any form (it runs in CI via `uv run --with bandit`).
- `typos`, `uv-audit`, `markdownlint-cli2`, and `mdformat` are not part of the standard set but are kept as they are — the draft is silent on removing them.
- If `.hadolint.yaml` is created for suppression, keep it minimal: only suppressions the existing `Dockerfile` actually triggers.

---

body:
Adds a new cloud-mode destination, **Vibe Tracking Event** (slug `actions-vibe-conversions`), that sends conversion events to Vibe via `POST https://t.vibe.co/s2s-conversion/events/segment`.

**What & why:** Vibe wants to receive Segment conversion events (purchases, page views, signups, etc.) for advertiser attribution. This destination maps Segment track/page events to Vibe's single-event conversion API.

### Details

- **Action:** `trackConversion` — 9 mapped fields (`a`, `eid`, `ts`, `ip`, `em`, `ed`, `gid`, `ua`, `url`) plus the `aid` (Pixel ID) settings value injected into every event.
- **Auth:** `scheme: custom`. The Vibe conversion API requires no API key/token; the advertiser is identified by the Pixel ID (`aid`) setting.
- **Presets:** Order Completed → `purchase`, Page Viewed → `page_view`, Signed Up → `signup`.
- **Validation & transforms:**
  - Either `ip` or `em` is required (throws `PayloadValidationError` if both missing).
  - Timestamp must be within the last 7 days; ISO timestamps are converted to UNIX milliseconds.
  - Event type `a` is constrained to the API enum via `choices`.
  - Event data (`ed`) is serialized to a stringified JSON object.
- **No batching:** the Vibe API has no batch endpoint, so `performBatch` is intentionally omitted (single-event POST only).

### TODO before merge

- ⚠️ **Not registered** in `packages/destination-actions/src/destinations/index.ts` yet — the metadata ID must be the production-assigned MongoDB ObjectId created in the control plane, not a placeholder. Register once the destination is created in production.
- **Open questions to confirm with Vibe:** endpoint path `/events/segment` (PRD) vs `/events` (public docs); `em` field and `call` enum value present in PRD but absent from public docs; final destination name (currently "Vibe Tracking Event", TBC); `gid` label/description.

## Testing

- [x] Added unit tests for new functionality
- [ ] Tested end-to-end using the local server
- [ ] [If destination is already live] Tested for backward compatibility of destination.
- [ ] [Segmenters] Tested in the staging environment
- [ ] [Segmenters] [If applicable for this change] Tested for regression with Hadron.

11 Jest tests pass (unit + snapshot), covering the happy path, ISO→UNIX ms conversion, email fallback, both validation errors, enum rejection, presets, and request-body snapshots. Typecheck and lint are clean.

## Security Review

- [x] **Reviewed all field definitions** for sensitive data (API keys, tokens, passwords, client secrets). This API uses no secrets; the only credential-like value is the non-secret Pixel ID.

## New Destination Checklist

- [ ] Extracted all action API versions to `versioning-info.ts` file.

body:
Parity Status: web + mobile-responsive + android complete

## What failed

The second `Skills Taxonomy — Apply Change Ops (production)` run (job 84926582308) failed with:

```
new row for relation "skills_taxonomy_change_events" violates check constraint "skills_taxonomy_change_events_target_type_check"
```

**Nothing was applied** — one transaction, full rollback, live taxonomy untouched.

## Root cause

Sibling of the previous failure (#1329): the live database also carries a check on `target_type` that was never declared in `schema.sql`. The apply engine wrote `job_title` (underscore); the app's delete path and the live check use `job-title` (hyphen). Ops 26–33 write `skill` and passed; op 34 (the occupation deactivation) wrote `job_title` and was rejected.

## Fix

- The apply engine now writes `job-title`, matching the app's existing audit vocabulary (4 sites).
- `schema.sql` declares the `target_type` check explicitly — `sector`, `job-title`, `skill` — with the same idempotent drop + re-add idiom, so this table has no undeclared vocabulary left to trip a future run.
- `schema.demo.sql` regenerated; skills-taxonomy inventory and test script updated together.

## After merge

1. The `Neon — Update DB` workflow runs automatically on the schema change.
2. Re-dispatch `Skills Taxonomy — Apply Change Ops (production)` — this is the last constraint on the audit table, so ops 26–36 should apply cleanly.

Owner-review (schema change) — auto-merge not enabled.

author: koh0920
body:
**v1.2 supervisor mode** — the guest-agent **supervisor mechanism**, validated end-to-end on real Firecracker. This is the contract's named successor to the impossible "rewrite a snapshotted process's environ" (binding-lease.md §env): for `delivery = "env"` secrets the guest-agent OWNS the workload process and starts it — with the env composed from the delivered bindings — only once the session is bound-ready.

**Scope:** this PR is the mechanism + protocol + docs + a KVM spike proving it. The Rust `rootfs_builder` / `FirecrackerBackend` call-site wiring (supervisor.json emission, init-as-supervisor, Gate-A env-secret relaxation, build-time placeholder delivery, `init_on_free` boot arg, L4 placeholder sentinel, restore health-delay) is the follow-up **PR 3c**, now grounded by the hardware-proven mechanism.

## What's here

- **protocol**: `HostToAgent::StopWorkload` + `AgentToHost::WorkloadStopped { was_running }` (value-free; a no-supervisor capsule answers `was_running=false`). `StopWorkload` is **stop-only** — it does NOT scrub; the build sequence is `StopWorkload` **then `Revoke` for every lease** to scrub the tmpfs before seal.
- **guest-agent `supervisor.rs`**:
  - `SupervisorConfig` (`/etc/ato/supervisor.json`): `cmd`/`cwd`/`base_env` + `bindings_env` (`ENV_VAR → binding NAME`). **Holds no secret value** — only the binding name whose tmpfs file supplies the value. `validate()` (fail-closed at load AND in `plan_spawn`): env var names must be POSIX identifiers `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$` (interpolated into the spawn script) and binding names must be valid `BindingName`s (joined onto the tmpfs root).
  - **The value never enters the agent's heap** (a KVM finding — a long-lived init's heap is never freed, so `init_on_free` can't zero it). `plan_spawn` builds a `SpawnPlan` of tmpfs **file paths**; `ChildWorkload` spawns `sh -c 'export VAR="$(cat PATH)"; exec CMD'` so the value is read at `exec` by the child that becomes the workload — it lives only in that child's environment.
  - `Workload` trait + `ChildWorkload`; `stop` is **bounded** (SIGTERM → 2s grace → SIGKILL → reap) so `StopWorkload` never stalls the seal.
  - `Supervisor::on_bound_ready` (idempotent start) + `stop_workload` (leaves `started=false` so a restore starts a **fresh** workload with the real env).
- **guest-agent `main.rs`** `AgentRuntime`: routes `StopWorkload` to the supervisor; after each binding message, starts the workload once the session is bound-ready. A supervisor start failure becomes an agent `Error` (never claim serving without a running workload); a malformed control line is **never echoed**.
- **docs**: `binding-lease.md` supervisor-mode section (build placeholder → health → `StopWorkload` + `Revoke` → snapshot; restore bound-ready → restart-with-env; the value-never-in-agent-heap design + the `init_on_free` hardening note).

## KVM proof (`spikes/firecracker-supervisor/`, GCP FC v1.16.0, kernel 5.10.223)

`RECEIPT.json` — **VERDICT PASS** on the security-critical invariants:
- `real_key_absent_from_seal = true` — the real credential is never in the seal (delivered only at restore into a VM that is never re-snapshotted).
- `restart_with_real_env = true` — restore restarts the app with the real env, correct key live.
- `placeholder_health` / `health_down_after_stop = true`.
- `placeholder_absent_hardening = false` — kernel-gated defense-in-depth: the **non-secret** placeholder lingers in freed pages when the guest kernel lacks `init_on_free` (the CI kernel does); documented, not a leak.

## Verification

guest-agent 18 (supervisor unit incl. bounded-stop SIGKILL + config-validation rejects + child-only-value + runtime build/restore flow + no-echo) + protocol 5, clippy clean.

author: celsiuscoffee
body:
## Problem

A customer placed a **dine-in QR order** (`#C-428549`, Table 6, Putrajaya) that included **Red Velvet Cake** — an item that was 86'd (out of stock) at that outlet. The item shouldn't have been orderable at all.

This is the deeper half of the snooze-gating issue. PR #629 stopped 86'd items from being *suggested* in pairing rails, but the **menu / pairing hiding is entirely client-side and advisory**. An item still reaches checkout if it was:
- added to the cart **before** being 86'd,
- served from a **stale menu cache**, or
- opened via a **direct product link** (the product page has no availability gate).

Neither order-creation path validated availability, so a sold-out item sailed through checkout and hit the kitchen.

## Fix

Add an **authoritative server-side gate** that both order paths run right after the product/price lookup they already do:

- **`lib/menu-availability.ts`** (new) — `findUnavailableItems()` flags any ordered item that is globally discontinued (`products.is_available = false`) **or** 86'd at this outlet (`outlet_product_availability`, keyed by the store slug — the same key the menu read and POS register use). Plus `unavailableItemsMessage()` for a customer-facing "sold out" string.
- **`/api/checkout/initiate`** (web-QR) and **`/api/orders`** (native pickup) — return **409** with the sold-out item names *before* creating the order.

The checkout client already surfaces `data.error`, so the customer sees a clear "… is sold out at this outlet, please remove it to continue" message instead of placing an unfulfillable order.

## Why server-side

Client hiding can't close the race: 86 can happen after an item is already in the cart, and caches/deep-links bypass the menu filter. The order-creation endpoint is the only place that sees the final cart against live availability, so that's where the gate belongs.

## Testing

- Traced both order-creation paths; confirmed the gate sits after the existing product lookup and uses the same store-slug key as the menu availability read.
- A full typecheck isn't possible in this container (app `node_modules` aren't installed); CI typecheck/lint/build will verify.

### Suggested manual verification
1. Add a product to a dine-in cart, then 86 it at that outlet in the backoffice Availability matrix.
2. Attempt checkout → expect a 409 and a "… is sold out at this outlet" message; no order is created.
3. Confirm a normal (in-stock) cart still checks out unchanged.

body: ## What? This PR aims to solve #3845 by disabling browser-native View Transitions for wp-admin pages when Playground is running in a Chromium-based browser. ## Why? Chrome/Edge/Opera can crash when navigating to wp-admin pages such as Appearance -> Themes while admin View Transitions are enabled. Firefox does not appear to hit the same crash, so this keeps the opt-out scoped to Chromium-based browsers by default. ## How? - Detect Chromium-based browsers inside the remote boot path while generating Playground runtime options. - Define `PLAYGROUND_DISABLE_ADMIN_VIEW_TRANSITIONS` in a runtime MU plugin when the remote context is Chromium based. - In the Playground MU plugin, skip Playground fallback View Transitions and dequeue/deregister Core's `wp-view-transitions-admin` style for wp-admin requests. - Allow repros with `?with-admin-transitions`, which forwards through `remote.html` to the worker and keeps admin View Transitions enabled. ## Testing - `php -l packages/playground/remote/src/lib/playground-mu-plugin/0-playground.php` - `npx nx test playground-client --testFile=blueprints-v1-handler.spec.ts` - `npx nx typecheck playground-client` - `npx nx typecheck playground-remote` - `npx nx lint playground-remote` - `git diff --check trunk` - Manual headed Chrome 149 check: loaded Playground wp-admin, clicked Appearance -> Themes, confirmed `themes.php` loaded without a page crash and no View Transition styles were present. - Manual headed Chrome 149 repro override check: loaded `?with-admin-transitions&storage=temp&url=/wp-admin/`, confirmed `wp-view-transitions-admin-inline-css` was present, clicked Appearance -> Themes, and reproduced the page crash. ## Debugging Details Props @adamziel for this dump analysis (`Google Chrome 149.0.7827.201 (Official Build) (arm64) Revision 6a7b3dbec3b2ca25877c2553b5473b2f277ef644-refs/branch-heads/7827_196@{#6}`):

author: zhouxiaolin
body:
## Summary

Wires the rollup engine (shipped in #10) onto real data, delivering the **headline end-to-end demo** of the relation + rollup PRD (#7).

股票持仓's **持仓** and **成本** become rollup fields derived from a new **交易流水** detail table (each trade's 关联持仓 relation points back at a holding). Together with the existing 现价 source and 盈亏/是否亏损 formulas, this forms the full cross-table reactive chain:

```
交易流水 ──reverse-lookup──▶ rollup(持仓 / 成本) ──bridge──▶ formula(盈亏) ──▶ formula(是否亏损) ──▶ rule(亏损标记)
```

**Six trades reconcile exactly** (the core acceptance point):

| ETF | 流水 | 持仓 | 成本 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 半导体设备ETF国泰 | 买 1.750×3000, 买 1.820×4000, 卖 1.790×100 | **6900** | (5250+7280)/7000 = **1.79** |
| 通信ETF国泰 | 买 1.700×4000, 买 1.800×4000, 卖 1.600×900 | **7100** | (6800+7200)/8000 = **1.75** |

## What changed

- **seedData**: new 交易流水 table (date primary, relation→持仓, 6 trades). 股票持仓's 成本/qty go from dead `number` constants → rollup fields; 盈亏/收益率 formulas now reference the rollup columns via the rollup→formula bridge. Removed #10's temporary `linkedTaskCount`/`linkedHolding` demo so 任务管理 returns to a plain task table (per the issue).
- **store**: persist key `v5 → v6` (the restructured seed shadows an old blob).
- **tests**: rollup-engine store-integration now reconciles 持仓/成本 against the real seeded trades; new data-store tests exercise the full reactive chain — editing **one** trade's 数量 or 方向 re-derives 持仓 → 成本 → 盈亏 → 是否亏损 in lockstep.
- **ADR 0005**: records the non-obvious decisions.

## No engine changes

The rollup expressions (`SUM({数量},{方向}="买入") - SUM({数量},{方向}="卖出")` and `SUM({价格}*{数量},{方向}="买入") / SUM({数量},{方向}="买入")`) were already supported and tested in #10. #11 is a schema/seed change. Per ADR 0004 §后果, the cost rollup keeps the `{价格}*{数量}` multiply *inside* the expression rather than reading the detail table's `金额` formula value (rollup reads raw detail cells, not parsed formula values) — so `金额` is display-only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] 新增「交易流水」seed 表，含 6 笔交易、主字段为日期、「股票」relation 指向股票表、方向/价格/数量/金额字段齐全。
- [x] 股票表「持仓」改为 rollup（`SUM({数量},{方向}="买入")-SUM({数量},{方向}="卖出")`），through 指向流水表的「股票」关联字段。
- [x] 股票表「成本」改为 rollup（加权平均），表达式正确。
- [x] 股票表「盈亏」formula 引用持仓/成本 rollup 列，值正确联动。
- [x] 6 笔交易聚合出的持仓（6900/7100）与成本（≈1.790/1.750）精确对账回原 seed。
- [x] 改一笔流水数量（如把买入 3000 改成 5000），股票表持仓、成本、盈亏、是否亏损全部联动重算。
- [x] 通信ETF 开仓即亏 → 是否亏损=true → 亏损标记规则触发 → 备注被写入（mock 现价 base 1.576 < 流水成本 1.75，加载即武装）。
- [x] 现价抖动时盈亏联动变化，但持仓/成本（不依赖现价）不白算（`useDerivedRecords` 依赖追踪只选明细表对象引用，#10 已实现）。

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- `npm test` — **102 passed** (was 96; +6: 3 rollup store-integration reconciliations, 4 derived-chain tests, −1 replaced linkedTaskCount smoke test)
- `npm run build` clean

Closes #11

body: ## Problem Shanghai `terraform-cn-shanghai` apply failed with two errors: 1. **FC `InvalidArgument`**: existing `api` function uses `custom-container`; Terraform wants `custom.debian10` zip runtime — FC does not allow in-place runtime change. 2. **CDN `DomainOwnerVerifyFail`**: root domain `huhansen.cn` not yet verified in CDN (first-time requirement). ## Fix ### FC runtime migration (`import-existing.sh`) Before import/apply, detect `custom-container` runtime and delete the legacy function (+ triggers/custom domain) from cloud and Terraform state so Terraform recreates with zip custom runtime. ### CDN ownership gate (`cdn-verify-root-domain.sh`) - Calls `VerifyDomainOwner` / `DescribeVerifyContent` for `huhansen.cn` - If not verified: apply continues with `create_cdn_domain=false` (OTS/OSS/FC still provisioned) and logs the required TXT record: - **Host:** `verification` - **Type:** TXT - **Value:** from `DescribeVerifyContent` (currently `verify_f98c7557813c33afeee97df2acadb9ce`) After adding the TXT record in Alibaba DNS and waiting ~10 min, re-run **Terraform apply** — CDN will be created once verification passes. ## Manual step (one-time) In **Alibaba Cloud DNS** for `huhansen.cn`, add TXT record `verification` → `verify_f98c7557813c33afeee97df2acadb9ce`, then re-run apply.

body:
## Summary

- Adds a new scenario demonstrating zero-code eBPF auto-instrumentation with `beyla.ebpf`: Alloy attaches eBPF probes to an unmodified Go HTTP service and produces RED metrics (Prometheus) and traces (Tempo) with no SDK, agent, or code change.
- Pins the demo app to Go 1.24. Live testing during development found that Go 1.26 binaries are silently unsupported by the OBI/Beyla build bundled in Alloy v1.17.0: `beyla.ebpf` reports the process as instrumented and logs no fatal error, but every trace and RED metric is dropped because it can't read that Go version's runtime-internal goroutine offsets (`can't read newproc1 invocation metadata` in debug logs). Go 1.22 and 1.24 were verified working end to end. This gotcha is documented in the README's troubleshoot section so anyone forking the scenario for their own service hits it faster.
- Adds the scenario to the root README's Tracing table.

Closes #273

🚨 **Severity:** MEDIUM
💡 **Vulnerability:** Weak hardcoded secret keyword detection. Keywords were arbitrarily ordered, causing shorter keywords like `"KEY"` to incorrectly shadow more specific keywords like `"APIKEY"` (e.g. in `"KEY_APIKEY"`).
🎯 **Impact:** Inaccurate secret detection categorization, potentially masking higher-risk secrets or triggering the wrong diagnostics in the compiler.
🔧 **Fix:** Reordered the keyword arrays in both `tyc-analyse/src/lib.rs` and `tyc/src/commands/build.rs` to strictly evaluate the longest substrings first. Updated tests to reflect accurate classification.

author: bcook98
body:
## Symptom

Every casino game (blackjack/pokies/scratchies/roulette) shows a **0 balance** and **refuses all bets** in production, despite the platform reserving credits correctly.

## Root cause

The guest runtime (`internal/game/run.go`) builds a **fresh `room` every callback**, but creates the game's `Handler` — and its stored `Services` (including `creditsSvc`) — **only once at `OnStart`**, bound to the *start* callback's room. `creditsSvc` resolves a player's host-side index by scanning that room's `ctx.members`, which is **empty for a solo game** (the player joins *after* `OnStart`). So `creditsSvc.index(p) → -1` and every `Balance`/`Wager`/`Settle` is denied at the **guest facade** (`ErrCreditsDenied`) — it never even reaches the host `creditsCall`.

The `kittest`/native/`memsvc` doubles resolve credits by **account id**, not roster index, so unit tests and `shellcade-kit check` conformance all passed — the bug only manifests on the real wasm ABI path.

## Fix

Use a single **persistent `theRoom`**, refreshed in place each callback (its `ctx` is reassigned in `decodeCall`), so the game's once-built `Services` always resolve against the **live** roster. The `room` struct is just `{ctx, rng}` with no per-callback state, and its own comment says it's "refreshed per callback" — this makes that true. No behavior change for non-casino games.

## Verification

Reproduced and fixed locally end-to-end (dev server + sideloaded casino blackjack, driven via tmux):
- **Before:** `Balance` → `ErrCreditsDenied` at the facade, HUD shows `credits 0`, bets refused.
- **After:** host `creditsCall` reached (`idx=0 rosterLen=1`), `Balance` → `1015`, HUD shows `$1015`; placing a bet deals cards and debits to `$990`.

`go build ./...` (native + `GOOS=wasip1`) and `go test ./...` green.

## Follow-ups

- Casino games must be **rebuilt + republished** against this release (the fix is compiled into each game's wasm).
- Add a casino wasm-fixture host test (`Start` empty → `Join` → assert a guest credits call reaches the host service) so this can't regress — the current doubles can't catch it.

body:
## Summary
This PR brings the `@imagekit/api-mcp` server into compliance with Anthropic's Connectors Directory requirements so it can be (re)submitted and listed. Changes are limited to the MCP server package plus a routine version bump — no changes to SDK behavior.

References:
- [Submission guide — "What to expect in the portal"](https://claude.com/docs/connectors/building/submission)
- [Anthropic Software Directory Policy](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13145358-anthropic-software-directory-policy)

## Changes and the policy they address

| Change | File(s) | Policy / requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Added tool annotations to `execute` (`title`, `readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: true`, `idempotentHint: false`, `openWorldHint: true`) and to `search_docs` (`title`, `readOnlyHint: true`, `openWorldHint: true`) | `src/code-tool.ts`, `src/docs-search-tool.ts` | **Submission Req 2 — Tool annotations**; Directory Policy **§5.E** (all tools must declare `title` and applicable `readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint`). Was a hard blocker previously. |
| Added a **Privacy Policy** section covering data collection, authentication, usage/storage, third-party sharing, retention, and contact | `README.md` | **Privacy policy requirements** — README section is mandatory; *"Missing or incomplete privacy policies result in immediate rejection."* Directory Policy **§3.A**. |
| Added `privacy_policies` array, upgraded `dxt_version → manifest_version: 0.3`, added `icon`, `long_description`, and expanded `keywords` | `manifest.json` | **Submission Req 4 — Privacy Policy** (`privacy_policies` array required, manifest_version 0.2+); listing metadata for **Step 4 (Listing)**. |
| Added **Usage Examples** (3+ end-to-end natural-language workflows), **Support**, and **Troubleshooting** sections | `README.md` | **Submission Req 5 — Documentation** (clear setup + usage); Directory Policy **§3.C** (troubleshooting) and **§3.E** (≥3 examples). |
| Added `server.json` (MCP Registry): npm package entry + remote `streamable-http` endpoint `https://api-mcp.imagekit.io/mcp` | `server.json` | Directory Policy **§5.F — Streamable HTTP transport**; supports **Step 2 (Connection)** and registry discoverability. |
| Added `icon.png` (512×512 PNG) and copy step in the bundle build | `icon.png`, `build` | Listing **icon** asset for **Step 4 (Listing)**. |
| Version bump / changelog | `package.json`, `packages/mcp-server/package.json`, `src/version.ts`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `.release-please-manifest.json` | Release tooling — keeps published deps current (**§5.G**). |

## Compliance notes (Step 10)
- **OAuth 2.0 (Submission Req  3 / §5.D):** already satisfied — the hosted endpoint sits behind an OAuth 2.1 + PKCE proxy with dynamic client registration. No code change needed in auth repo
- **AI media generation (§4.B):** N/A — the `execute` tool runs the ImageKit SDK, whose methods cover upload / file / folder / asset / account / cache management only. No SDK method generates media from a text prompt, so this does not fall under the unsupported "AI media generation" use case. §4.B
- **Allowed link URIs:** N/A — the server does not use the `ui/open-link` capability. 



> Note: § X.A means section X and point A in this doc https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13145358-anthropic-software-directory-policy
