author: gitrgoliveira
body:
## Summary

- Team standings now show a **"DH" badge** on the team that won a *daihyosen* (representative play-off), so operators and spectators can see why two teams with identical pool stats finish at different ranks.
  - **Pool standings** (mixed format): badge every DH winner.
  - **League standings**: badge every DH winner (same policy as pools). The backend only injects daihyosen bouts for ties that affect advancement, so the badge never clutters inconsequential rows.
  - **Brackets**: already covered by the existing "DH" decision chip; no change.
  - **League Overview preview**: the compact "Final standings" summary on the Overview tab now carries the same DH badge as the full League tab (it previously showed the tied rows with no badge).
- **Admin Pools tab now reuses the public `PoolsViewer`.** It previously rolled its own standings table with an editable `#` rank input and no rank badge, so pool rows read inconsistently with the public viewer. The operator console now renders pool standings via the same shared `window.PoolsViewer` that the shiaijo view already uses: rows in **draw order**, `#` = **draw position**, rank surfaced as a **badge** (1st/2nd/…), plus the **DH** badge. Match clicks route through `enrichPoolMatchWithComp` to the scorer (team sheet for team bouts, individual **rep editor** for pool-DH/TB bouts). The **manual rank override** is removed (rankings now come only from results and the daihyosen), deleting `RankInput`/`decideRankCommit`/`orderStandingRows`/override handlers/the per-pool detail view and their tests (net -834 lines).
- The badge is a **glossary-linked term**: tap/focus "DH" to define *daihyosen* (touch- and keyboard-accessible), matching the bracket's DH chip.
- **Daihyosen is now band-aware (engine fix).** Per the FIK/EKC rules a daihyosen is a *single pairwise* supplementary ippon-shobu bout, played only to decide a ranking that matters. The pool engine previously injected a supplementary bout for **every** tied group regardless of whether it changed the outcome, so teams level below the qualifying places still generated daihyosen matches. Injection is now gated on the advancement cut (`tieAffectsAdvancement` over `EffectivePoolWinners`): a tie within `[1..poolWinners]` (advance/seed) gets a bout, a tie entirely below the cut shares its rank with no bout. A two-way consequential tie yields exactly one pairwise bout. Applied to both the team `-DH-` and individual `-TB-` paths; team leagues already gated via `LeagueTiebreakCandidates`.
- **Chusen (drawing lots) resolver.** When 3+ tied teams play a round of daihyosen that still ends level (a cycle: each beats another), the FIK/EKC last resort is chusen. The Pools tab now shows a focused **"Chusen (drawing lots) required"** panel (only when a cycle exists) listing the tied teams with a position input each; recording the drawn order settles the tie and lets the competition advance. Engine `ChusenCandidates` surfaces exactly those groups via a shared `groupNeedsChusen` predicate that `dhCycleExists` also delegates to; resolution reuses the existing `override-rank` endpoint (writes `PoolRanks`). This is the **only** hand-set-rank path, and only when the bouts cannot decide it (the general always-on override table stays removed).
- Broadened the *daihyosen* glossary definition to cover **tied team pools**, not just knockout matches.
- Added engine **regression tests** pinning the standings *order* after a DH (previously only completion was tested).
- **Operator surface parity (shiaijo + schedule editors).** A pool daihyosen is a *representative* bout (one player per team), but it only presented as such when opened from the Pools tab. Opened from the **shiaijo** (or the schedule score editor) it appeared as a plain team-vs-team match with no label and no rep-player pickers. Both surfaces now reuse the existing `enrichPoolMatchWithComp` enrichment, so a pool DH there shows:
  - a glossary-linked **"DH"** tag on the queue cards (Up Next / Upcoming / Completed) and a **"Daihyosen · representative tie-break bout"** caption in the scorer;
  - the **representative-player pickers** ("Shiro rep · Team / Aka rep · Team"), populated from each team's roster. The chosen reps persist to `MatchResult.RepPlayerA/RepPlayerB` (already supported by the backend for pool-DH/TB ids — no server change).

- **Server-authoritative team IV/PW in every summary.** Team-match results now render `IV shiro-aka · PW shiro-aka` everywhere a team result appears (bracket, pool/league match lists, schedule, shiaijo chip), instead of a bare IV number. The IV and PW values are computed **server-side** and attached to every match on the wire (HTTP + SSE `match_updated`) via `MatchResult.MarshalJSON`, so the client renders them verbatim and never re-derives points from ippons. `engine.ComputeTeamSummary` delegates to the same `state.TeamResultFrom`, so the tie-break math and the displayed summary share one source of truth and cannot drift. The summary renders **IV over PW on two lines** (newline + `white-space: pre-line`) so both totals stay legible in the narrow centre score cell.
- **Mobile-legibility pass on `PoolsViewer`** (from an `/impeccable critique`): team standings drop the three lowest-order tiebreakers (IL/IT/PL) below 480px so cells stay readable on a phone (desktop keeps all 10 columns); match rows meet the 36px shared / 44px coarse-pointer tap target; a table `<caption>` disambiguates the `#` column and names the table for assistive tech; long IV/PW summaries wrap rather than starving the name columns. (The rank badge sizing is intentionally left per spec.)
- **Leagues render via a distinct standings path, never pool-style.** A league is not a pool, so leagues now have their OWN endpoint and viewer (mirroring Swiss) and no longer route through `PoolsViewer`. Backend: `engine.LeagueStandings` + `GET /competitions/:id/league/standings` (public; returns the single league group rank-ordered; 404 for non-league). Frontend: `api.leagueStandings()` + a new **`LeagueStandingsViewer`** that fetches the dedicated endpoint and renders rank-ordered (`#` = the authoritative rank with override `*`, **no** rank badge, DH badge on daihyosen winners, caption "Ranked by standings"). Leagues get their own `league` tab in the viewer and the admin surface; `PoolsViewer` is reverted to **pool-only** (draw order, `#` = draw position, rank via badge, "Listed in draw order"). This also fixes the earlier divergence where a league showed different orderings on the League tab vs the Overview summary.
- **Shiaijo team score card fix.** The queue-card team score prefixed an `IV` label in front of a value that already self-labels as `IV s-a · PW s-a`, rendering a doubled "IV IV 0-0 · PW 0-0". Dropped the redundant prefix for the team case (engi keeps its "Flags" label).
- **DH pill placement + broadcast signal.** In the score-summary rows the winning-team DH pill now sits on the **inside** edge (toward the centre score) for both sides - on the right-aligned Aka side the pill moves before the name so it no longer lands on the far-right outside edge. The **streaming overlay** (OBS/vMix lower-third) now shows a **"DAIHYOSEN"** chip when the running match is a daihyosen bout (a pool/league `-DH-` rep bout, a team match on its daihyosen sub-bout, or a pending daihyosen), so stream viewers know a tie-break bout is on court.
- **Tri-review hardening pass** (3-lens review + adversarial verification, 8 confirmed findings fixed): public read endpoints (league/swiss standings, `/tournament`) return an opaque `internal error` on 500 instead of leaking wrapped OS error text; `TeamResultFrom` honours its nil contract when the sub-results hold only the daihyosen placeholder (regression-tested); `ChusenCandidates` propagates the `LoadOverrides` error; shared `dhWinnerName` + `StandingsTableHead` helpers de-duplicate the standings viewers; DH badge policy unified (any DH winner, no rank cap); `teamSize > 0` guard form normalized. **C

author: teng-lin
body:
## What & why

The experimental REST server (`src/notebooklm/server/`) lagged the mature MCP server despite both being thin adapters over the same `_app/` core. A 4-lens gap review (2 Claude + Codex + agy — committed at `docs/notes/rest-vs-mcp-gap-review-2026-07-02.md`) found the gap was **almost entirely one-directional**: REST lacked ~11 capabilities MCP had (and was the softer target on safety), while MCP lacked ~zero that REST had. This PR closes those gaps and lifts the shared projections into `_app/` so **both** adapters share one implementation (Option B), rather than REST duplicating MCP's helpers.

Planned + reviewed with oracle+momus across claude/codex/agy (2 rounds to convergence); each phase went through a claude+codex+agy triple-review polish gate before commit.

## What shipped

**Shared `_app` lifts** (MCP refactored onto them — output byte-identical, pinned by tests):
- `notebooklm/_redact.py` — home-path / signed-token redaction (both adapters)
- `_app/views.py` — share enum→label, `source_view` (`kind`/`status_label`), `ask_result_view` (strips `raw_response`)
- `_app/pagination.py` — pure slice + bound validation
- `_app.source_content.execute_source_read`, `_app.source_add.safe_upload_name`, `_app.research.poll_sources_for_import`, `_app.errors.CATEGORY_HINTS` + `is_retriable`

**REST — new capability (17 endpoints):** source-content read; deep-research router (start/status/cancel/import); `chat/configure`; studio `DELETE`/`retry`; PATCH renames (notebook/source/artifact); `sources/wait`; `suggested-prompts`; `/server/info`; artifact prompt; `sources/drive` + `sources/batch`; per-kind generate-option validation + mind-map `instructions` forwarding; opt-in **non-breaking** pagination.

**REST — hardening (parity with MCP):** uniform `{category, message, retriable, hint}` errors + home-path redaction; `--token` argv refusal (`--token-file`/env only); loopback enforced on the unspoofable peer address (`request.client.host`, `proxy_headers` off); multipart `Content-Length` 411 gate; disconnect-safe download cleanup; `notify` default flipped to `false`.

> Sharing **widening-confirm** is intentionally deferred — it landed MCP-side in #1748; a follow-up can share that gate via `_app` so REST and MCP use one idiom. Fail-loud `chat_configure` (#1744) and the research reliability work (#1741) are already inherited through the shared cores.

## Verification
- Full suite: **11,515 passed** (2 failures are `--extra browser`/playwright env-only, proven passing against the same code with playwright present).
- ruff + mypy clean; module-size, server-boundary, and architecture-freshness guardrails green.
- Rebased onto current `main` (past the #1741/#1744/#1748 MCP work) — no conflicts, semantics re-verified.

## Review notes
Each phase's triple review caught and fixed real bugs before commit: uppercase-full-UUID mind-map mis-route on PATCH/DELETE, batch swallowing shared auth/notebook failures, non-finite `wait` timeout, a `GenerationState` enum/str `.value` crash, and a half-applied error contract on hand-raised HTTP errors.

author: edvallm
body:
# 🔧 bugfix: missing-coverage remediation — #275 (CI-11) + #285 (CI-13)

> Two AGENTS.md "MUST" coverage gaps assigned to @edvallm, bundled on one `bugfix-*` branch (bypasses ownership — `main.ecs.js` is Track A and #275 spans D/C). #275 hardens + tests `prefers-reduced-motion`; #285 adds the dev-mode DOM budget assertion.

## Required checks

- [x] I read AGENTS.md and the agentic workflow guide.
- [x] I ran `npm run policy` locally.
- [x] Branch name follows `<owner>/bugfix-<slug>` (`medvall/bugfix-coverage-275-285`) — bugfix branch, ownership bypass.
- [x] Changes are within scope; cross-track files (`main.ecs.js`) carried under the bugfix bypass.
- [x] Ran unit + e2e for the touched paths.
- [x] Checked security sinks, architecture boundaries, dependency impact (none).
- [x] Requested human review.

## Layer boundary confirmations

- [x] `src/ecs/systems/` unchanged (no DOM added).
- [x] `assertDomElementBudget` is an app-boundary guard in `main.ecs.js` (the composition root), not an ECS system; it only reads `document.querySelectorAll` and throws — no simulation coupling.
- [x] Untrusted UI content still uses safe sinks; the budget breach is surfaced via the existing `renderCriticalError` `textContent` path (no HTML injection).
- [x] No framework imports or canvas APIs introduced.

## What changed

### #275 (CI-11) — `prefers-reduced-motion` hardening + test
- **`styles/animations.css`**: added a universal reduced-motion safety net inside the existing `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block — `*, *::before, *::after { animation-duration/transition-duration/*-delay: 0s !important }`.
- **`tests/e2e/reduced-motion.spec.js`** (new): emulates `reducedMotion: 'reduce'`, then asserts (a) no element in the `#overlay-root` menu subtree declares a non-zero animation/transition, and (b) no element site-wide declares a non-zero transition (during gameplay + boot).

### #285 (CI-13) — dev-mode DOM budget assertion
- **`src/main.ecs.js`**: added `DOM_ELEMENT_BUDGET = 500` and `assertDomElementBudget({ documentRef, limit })`, which throws a descriptive error when `document.querySelectorAll('*').length` exceeds the budget. Wired a `isDevelopment()`-gated call right after `runtime.start()` (initial board is in the DOM); the breach throws and is surfaced by the existing startup `catch` → `renderCriticalError`.
- **`tests/unit/main.ecs.test.js`**: 4 new cases (budget constant, boundary = 500 passes, 501 throws a visible descriptive error, custom limit).

## Why

- AGENTS.md §Accessibility (MUST): non-gameplay motion must respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. AGENTS.md §Performance budget (MUST): "DOM ≤ 500 total after level load. Assert in dev-mode startup." The reduced-motion rule was checked nowhere in tests; the DOM budget was checked only in e2e, never asserted in the app itself.

## Tests

- `npx vitest run` — **1298 passed** (incl. 4 new `assertDomElementBudget` cases).
- `npx playwright test tests/e2e/reduced-motion.spec.js` — **2 passed**.
- `npm run check` — clean. `npm run policy` — green modulo the pre-existing e2e timing-flake cluster (documented in prior PRs; unrelated to this change).

**TDD note (honest):**
- **#285** followed failing-test-first: the new unit tests failed (function absent) → implemented → pass.
- **#275** did **not** reproduce as a failure — the per-animation handling in `animations.css` already existed and the new e2e passed against unmodified code. Rather than fabricate a failure, this PR **locks in** the contract with the (passing) regression test and **hardens** it with the universal override so compliance no longer depends on incidental quirks (an unused `.overlay` transition; a malformed `.overlay__btn` transition-duration) or on every future selector being hand-added to the block.

## Audit questions affected

- **F-19/F-20/F-21** (paint/layers/promotion) — unaffected; reduced-motion only zeroes durations. **F-17/F-18** (frame budget) — the DOM budget guard is dev-only, no production/runtime cost.
- Accessibility (reduced-motion) and the DOM-budget performance MUST now have explicit automated coverage.

## Security notes

- No new sinks. Budget breach message is plain `textContent` via `renderCriticalError`. No untrusted input; the count comes from the live DOM.

## Architecture / dependency notes

- `assertDomElementBudget` lives at the app composition root, not in an ECS system; dev-gated so production startup is unchanged. No dependency or lockfile changes.

## Risks

- Low. The reduced-motion override is additive and scoped to the reduce media query. The DOM assertion runs only under `isDevelopment()` and only throws on a genuine >500 breach (surfaced, not silent) — production builds are unaffected.

author: davidgershony
body:
## Summary

Reduce mnemonic exposure by adding zero-allocation `ReadOnlyMemory<char>` accessors and fixing `PsbtOperations` to use the cached ExtKey instead of re-reading `.Words`.

## Changes

- **WalletWords.cs**: Add `WordsMemory` and `PassphraseMemory` properties that expose the backing `char[]` without creating new string copies. Add security documentation to the `Words` getter.
- **PsbtOperations.cs**: Replace `_hdOperations.GetExtendedKey(walletWords.Words, walletWords.Passphrase)` with `walletWords.GetOrDeriveExtKey(_hdOperations)` to use the cached key and avoid extra mnemonic string allocations.

## Rationale

Every call to `.Words` creates a new `string` on the managed heap that cannot be deterministically zeroed. By preferring `GetOrDeriveExtKey()` (which derives once and caches), we minimize the number of mnemonic string copies that linger in memory.

## Testing

All 154 shared tests pass.

author: ahmedelbanna80
body:
Fixes #201. Also folds in #202 (same class, tiny diff).

## What

`operator-supply-chain.yml` had the same publish-before-scan ordering flaw PR #200 fixed for the app image (#199): `docker/build-push-action` published the operator image to GHCR at build time — BEFORE the SBOM + Trivy HIGH/CRITICAL gate — so a scan-failed operator image could land at a stable tag, unsigned, as the newest published digest.

### Ordering fix (the proven #200 pattern)

```
build (load: true, never publish) → syft SBOM → Trivy gate (fail HIGH/CRITICAL, enforced on the default branch)
  → GHCR login → publish the EXACT scanned bytes (digest captured fail-loud, refuse to sign a guessed digest)
  → cosign sign + attest + verify on the published digest
  → dist/install.yaml digest-pin → operator-latest release attach
```

### Release-asset gating verdict (asked in the issue)

The installer-pin + release-attach steps were **already positioned after the Trivy gate** in the old file, so job-order alone kept a scan-failed run from attaching a new `install.yaml`. But they consumed **`steps.build.outputs.digest` — the pre-gate build/push digest**. Both now consume **`steps.push.outputs.digest`** (the post-gate published digest), so the bundle can only ever bake in a digest that passed the gate, was published, signed, and verified. Locked in by a dedicated release-attach-after-gate guard test.

### CVE state (issue task 2)

Local `docker build` of `packages/kn-next-operator` + `trivy image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed` is **CLEAN — 0 findings** (debian 13.5 distroless base and the `manager` gobinary; `trivy fs` on `go.mod` also 0). No drift since #155, **no dep/base bumps needed** — the first post-merge run on the default branch should be the operator's first green scanned→published→signed→release-attached run.

### #202 folded in

`aquasecurity/trivy-action` and `anchore/sbom-action` are now **SHA-pinned in BOTH workflows** (`ed142fd0…` = v0.36.0, `e22c3899…` = v0.24.0, provenance comments, SHAs verified against upstream tags). The scan gate previously ran from a mutable `@master` ref inside a job holding `packages: write` + `id-token: write`. The other item in #202 (app-image buildkit-provenance restore via OCI-layout + crane) is **not** done here — it needs its own tracking, as the issue itself notes; #202 can be closed for the pinning half or retitled.

### Trade-off carried over from #200

`provenance: false` on the operator build too (the local `docker` exporter can't carry a provenance manifest list). `docs/security/threat-model.md` Repudiate/Info-disclosure rows updated honestly.

## Tests (TDD)

`tests/operator-supply-chain-workflow.test.ts` — written first, 9/11 failing against the old workflow, all green after:
- build is local-only (`load: true`, no `push:` input), nothing publishes before the Trivy gate
- Trivy gate stays fail-loud (HIGH/CRITICAL, exit-code 1, `continue-on-error` PR-only)
- push step main-gated, `id: push`, digest output, fail-loud on unresolvable digest
- sign → verify ordering, both parameterized by `steps.push.outputs.digest`; `steps.build.outputs.digest` banned file-wide
- **release-attach invariant**: installer pin + `softprops/action-gh-release` come after gate/push/sign/verify and bake in the pushed digest
- SHA-pin guard for trivy-action + sbom-action in **both** workflows (#202)

Full root suite: 14 files / 292 tests green. YAML parse-checked, biome clean.

Note (stacked-PR CI gating): repo CI gates run on `main` only for some jobs — vitest, biome and the local operator build+trivy scan were run locally as above.

author: tutkli
body:
## Summary

- Part of [#1145](https://github.com/tutkli/forty-cdk/issues/1145) (item 3). In `'popper'` mode the listbox's initial focus — whose implicit scroll is what reveals the selected option — runs after the portal move but **before** `@floating-ui/dom`'s async `computePosition` resolves and the `size` middleware constrains the surface to its `max-height`. So the surface isn't a scroll container yet when focus lands, and once `size` bounds it the `scrollTop` is 0: a selected option far down the list stays below the fold on open. Combobox already documents and fixes this via the positioner's `onFirstPosition` hook (#1066); select never adopted it.
- Adds `scrollSelectedOptionIntoView()` to [select.ts](projects/forty-cdk/select/src/select.ts) and wires it to the `'floating'` positioner's `onFirstPosition` in [select-content.ts](projects/forty-cdk/select/src/select-content.ts) — the one moment both prerequisites hold (surface portaled + `size`-constrained). It re-scrolls the selected option into view, safe-called (`?.`) to match every other `scrollIntoView` call site. No-op while virtualizing (the navigator owns that scroll via `scrollToIndex`) and when nothing is selected (initial focus lands on the first option, already at the top). `'item-aligned'` and `modal` modes are untouched: item-aligned centers the selected option by construction, and the modal surface is a CSS-sized scroll container from first paint, so neither races.
- Vitest ([select.spec.ts](projects/forty-cdk/select/src/select.spec.ts)): the selected option's host is scrolled into view once the positioner resolves; no scroll fires when nothing is selected. Both confirmed to fail on the pre-fix behaviour (the hook was never wired, so `scrollIntoView` was never called).
- E2E ([select.e2e.ts](projects/forty-cdk-harness/e2e/select.e2e.ts) + a `?many=1` mode on the fixture): with 60 options, a `size`-middleware-constrained height, and `item-45` selected, opening reveals it inside the scroll viewport (`scrollTop > 0`, option within the content rect); a top selection (`item-0`) leaves `scrollTop` at 0. The reveal case was confirmed to fail without the fix. The fixture constrains height via `var(--for-available-height)` (not a static `max-height`) precisely so the scroll container only exists after positioning — the exact race the fix addresses.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm lint` passes.
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes.
- [x] `pnpm test` — 4342 tests passing (2 new vs. main).
- [x] `pnpm build` — library compiles cleanly via ng-packagr.
- [x] `pnpm exec playwright test --project=chromium select.e2e.ts` — 21/21 (2 new). WebKit not run locally (known Windows harness hang); CI covers it.

body:
## Problem

`add_expense` failed on monthly tabs that lack the G/H summary block. It looked up a category label (訂閱費 / 基本房租生活費 / 交通中餐等等雜支 / 本月額外雜支) in column G and spliced the new expense's E-cell into that category's `=sum(...)`. **7 月 2026 (the current month) has no G/H block**, so the tool errored with `Could not find the category label "本月額外雜支" in column G`.

The block is also redundant: the per-row 類別 tag (column C) is the categorization actually in use, and `month_summary` already reports per-類別 totals from it. Vincent confirmed the G/H block is **deprecated** — it's being removed from 8 月 / 9 月 and future months won't have it.

## Change

The tailored tools no longer read or maintain the G/H block.

- **`add_expense`**: logs the expense into the `花費總額` SUM window only; the total picks it up automatically (an insert at the window's edge auto-extends the range). Removed the `category` parameter and the sum-splice logic. Now works on every monthly tab, with or without a block.
- **`month_summary`**: dropped the block-derived `categories` field; kept the per-類別 `tags` breakdown.
- **`start_month`**: dropped the category `#REF!` scrub (no category sums remain to repair).
- **`conventions.ts`**: removed `CATEGORIES` / `DEFAULT_CATEGORY` and the `categoryLabel` / `categoryFormula` columns; `CONVENTIONS_TEXT` now marks the block deprecated and tells callers to ignore any lingering one.
- Removed the now-dead helpers `spliceIntoSum`, `adjustColumnRefsForInsert`, `stripRefErrors` (each existed only to maintain the block) and their tests.
- Added `docs/2026-07-03-summary-block-deprecation.md`.

No other formulas are touched — `花費總額`, `剩餘`, `上月透支` cross-tab references, and USD GOOGLEFINANCE conversions are unaffected.

The G/H block still physically exists on 8 月 and 9 月 (`G5:H10`). Once this is deployed, `add_expense` ignores it, but a lingering block goes stale. Clearing `G5:H10` on those two tabs finishes the deprecation. Repo owner is handling this manually.

author: claudespice
body:
## Summary

Documents two new generic CDC replication-progress acceleration metrics in the observability metrics reference. They are emitted for every CDC-accelerated dataset (Postgres replication, MongoDB streams, DynamoDB streams) as each coalesced change burst applies:

- `dataset_acceleration_cdc_replication_lag_ms` — wall-clock now minus the upstream commit timestamp of the latest applied batch. Low/zero = caught up; growing = falling behind. For multi-shard sources (e.g. DynamoDB) this tracks the slowest shard.
- `dataset_acceleration_cdc_applied_commit_unix_time_ms` — upstream commit timestamp (Unix epoch ms) the accelerator has caught up to. Pair with wall-clock now to compute lag on your own clock.

Both verified against source: registered in `crates/runtime/src/accelerated_table/metrics.rs` (i64 gauges, unit `ms`) and recorded in `crates/runtime/src/accelerated_table/refresh_task/changes.rs` with the single `dataset` attribute, unconditionally in the CDC apply path (not gated by the disabled-by-default `runtime.metrics` set — no "disabled by default" note added).

New metrics → vNext (`website/docs/`) only.

body:
## Fix If Sale Bidding — Disable All Bidding After Lot Close

Once a lot's live auction closes and it enters `if_sale` status, all bidding must be fully disabled — including via direct API calls. This PR adds the authoritative server-side enforcement.

### What was fixed
- Disabled the If Sale bid-increase endpoint: `AuctionLotService::increaseIfSaleBid()` now always rejects, so a winner can no longer raise their bid after a lot closes into If Sale — the guard holds even for direct API calls from an un-updated client.
- Closed a proxy-bid gap: `BiddingService::validateProxyBid()` now rejects `if_sale` lots (previously only terminal statuses were blocked; `if_sale` is not terminal, so a proxy bid could slip through via the API).
- Confirmed manual bids remain rejected during If Sale (already blocked via `LotStatus::isActive()`).

### What was updated
- Rewrote `IfSaleBidIncreaseTest` to assert the service and HTTP endpoint reject the action (422 for eligible users, 403 inactive, 401 unauthenticated) and leave the lot untouched — no bid recorded, status unchanged.

### Validation
- `IfSaleBidIncreaseTest`: 6/6 passing.
- Full `tests/Feature/Auction/` suite: 56/56 passing.
- `BiddingRestrictionTest` + `BidEligibilityTest`: 17/17 passing.
- No migrations; no changes to auth, realtime, auctioneer close, or normal lot-close (sold / reserve_not_met / no_sale) behaviour.

body:
Two ""double-check"" bugs from the issues.

## #45 - Right-click Create IBD did nothing
The context-menu dismiss listener (`window mousedown, once`) removed the menu on the menu item's OWN mousedown, so the item's `click` never fired. The menu appeared, you clicked ""Create IBD"", and nothing happened - in both the canvas and the Model Explorer. (My earlier synthetic `element.click()` test bypassed mousedown, which is why it slipped through.)

Fix: dismiss only on an **outside** click (checks `menu.contains`) or Escape; the editor also ignores non-left mouse buttons so a right-click no longer starts a stray drag/selection (which was dirtying the model on every right-click).

## #44 - Requirement text not wrapping
A requirement's tag rows (`id = ...`, `text = ...`) were single unwrapped lines that overflowed the box. They now word-wrap to the box width, the box grows to fit, and requirement boxes get a readable 220px minimum width.

# 概要

「マグマダメージを完全カット」のような**特殊効果を持つ装備**と、その**時限（消費アイテム）版**を追加します。あわせてゲーム名を **drift** に変更し、既存のファンタジー寄り装備名を落ち着いたトーンに整理します。

## 特殊効果の仕組み

- `ItemTrait`（HEAT_PROOF / COLD_PROOF / MAGNET）— **装備欄のどれか1つでも持っていれば発動**するオン/オフ効果
- `hpRegen` — 装備の毎秒HP回復（複数装備で**加算**、HP 0 からの蘇生はしない）
- 時限版は `Buff` の4タイマー（heatProofT / coldProofT / magnetT / regenT）で管理し、MovementSystem が減衰

## 新装備（6種 — 落ち着いた実務的な名前）

| 装備 | 効果 |
|---|---|
| 耐熱スーツ（防具） / 遮熱フォイル（装飾） | **マグマの熱を完全カット**（溶岩床・マグマ惑星の常時ダメージが0に） |
| 防寒スーツ（防具） / グリップソール（装飾） | **雪の減速を無効 + 氷面で滑らない**（氷が通常の地面グリップに） |
| 回収磁石（装飾） | ドロップ品の回収距離 **3倍** |
| 自己修復パッチ（装飾） | HPを**毎秒1.5回復** |

## 新消費アイテム（4種 — 一定時間の効果）

耐熱コーティング（**60秒**マグマ無効）/ 防寒コーティング（**60秒**）/ 携行磁石（**45秒**）/ 応急再生パック（**20秒間 毎秒2.5回復**）

## ゲーム名 → **drift**

- Android アプリ名（`AndroidManifest.xml` label）、デスクトップのウィンドウタイトル（`Constants.APP_TITLE`）、README タイトルを変更（旧称併記）
- 慣性移動（ドリフト）というゲームの核に由来する、小文字の控えめな名前

## 既存装備名のトーンダウン（id 不変 = セーブ互換）

獣王の大牙→**大型獣の牙**、重力ランス→**作業用ランス**、推進器「獣王の尾」→**生体腱スラスター**、燠火の欠片→**加熱コア**、獣王の牙(装飾)→**牙のペンダント**、疾駆のブーツ→**ランナーブーツ**、再生の護符→**代謝促進バンド**、星渡りの羽→**軽量化フィン**、星渡りの羅針盤→**旧式の羅針盤** など。読み物の題名は物語なので現状維持。

## テスト

`:core:test` **643 テスト全緑**（ローカル確認済み）。新規 WorldHazardGearTest: 無防備のプレイヤーはマグマ地表で焼ける / 耐熱スーツで無傷 / コーティングで無傷 / 修復パッチで回復。Loadout の trait 集約・regen 加算、ItemUse のタイマー設定も検証。

author: khuepm
body:
## Summary

Studio's `notifications-panel.test.tsx` failed deterministically under Node ≥ 25 (local dev is on Node 26) with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getItem')` from `getActiveToken()` in `apps/studio/src/lib/api.ts`. CI passed because it runs Node 24.

**Root cause:** Node 25+ ships built-in Web Storage globals. The `localStorage` global is a getter that returns `undefined` unless the process was started with `--localstorage-file`. Vitest's jsdom environment only copies `window` keys that do **not** already exist on `globalThis`, so jsdom's working `Storage` is shadowed by Node's `undefined`-returning getter — and bare `localStorage.getItem(...)` throws inside component-test effects. jsdom's own Storage is unreachable because vitest aliases `window` to the populated global (verified: `globalThis === window` in the jsdom env).

**Fix:** `apps/studio/src/test/setup.ts` installs a minimal in-memory `MemoryStorage` (implements the `Storage` interface) for `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` whenever the global one lacks a `getItem` function. It is a no-op in the node env (no `window`) and on Node ≤ 24 where jsdom's copy already works — so CI (Node 24) is unaffected.

## Loại thay đổi

- [x] `test` — Thêm / sửa test

## Phase / Feature liên quan

Test infra — Node 26 forward-compat for the Studio vitest suite.

---

## ✅ Definition of Done (DoD)

### Code Quality

- [x] Không có TypeScript error — recursive `turbo run typecheck` 15/15 successful
- [x] Tất cả tests pass — full studio suite **49 files / 289 tests green under both Node 24 and Node 26**
- [x] Self-review: diff đọc lại line-by-line

### Testing

- [x] `notifications-panel.test.tsx` failed under Node 26 before, passes after; still passes under Node 24

*(Architecture/Docs, Runtime, Security, DB/Migrations sections không áp dụng — test-setup-only change, không đụng runtime code, schema, hay endpoint.)*

### Conventional Commits

- [x] `test(studio): stub Web Storage in vitest setup for Node >= 25`

---

## Rollback Plan

Revert the single commit — restores the previous `setup.ts`. No runtime/schema impact; test-only.

## Notes for Reviewers

- Change is confined to `apps/studio/src/test/setup.ts` (test setup); no production code touched.
- The `getItem` guard intentionally leaves Node's working `sessionStorage` alone if it functions — only broken globals are replaced.
- Verified locally with `nvm use 24` and Node 26 (`node_modules/.bin/vitest run`).

author: valerauko
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: `resolve_node_proxy_target` passed the full URL node name (e.g. `lima-node:10250`) to `cluster_object_key`, but nodes are stored under the bare name (`lima-node`). Every sonobuoy pod-dump produced: `Unable to retrieve kubelet pods for node lima-node: Node "lima-node:10250" not found`.
- **Why it happens**: Sonobuoy's `dump.go` builds node-proxy URLs as `/api/v1/nodes/<name>:<port>/proxy/pods` (via `fmt.Sprintf("%v:%v", node, framework.KubeletPort)`). Upstream Kubernetes handles this in `pkg/registry/core/node/strategy.go` via `utilnet.SplitSchemeNamePort()`.
- **Fix**: Extract `strip_node_port(name: &str) -> &str` (a single `rsplit_once(':')` — safe because node names are DNS-1123 labels with no colons) and call it at the top of `resolve_node_proxy_target` before building `node_key`. The extracted port is discarded; `state.kubelet_port` drives the kubelet connection. The 404 error message now reports the bare name.
- **Sibling call sites unchanged**: `node_name` at proxy.rs lines 111, 271, 581, 905 comes from stored pod spec (`pod["spec"]["nodeName"]`) — already bare, no port suffix, correct as-is.

## Regression tests added

- `strip_node_port_removes_port_suffix`: pure unit test; `"lima-node:10250"` → `"lima-node"`, `"lima-node"` → `"lima-node"`. Fails on revert.
- `node_proxy_port_suffix_in_name_resolves_correctly`: seeds `"lima-node"` in store, calls `resolve_node_proxy_target` with `"lima-node:10250"` — asserts status is not 404. Fails on revert (store lookup would 404 without the strip).

## kubectl --raw before/after

**Before** (without the fix — node stored as `lima-node-smoke` but URL uses `:10250` suffix):
```
$ kubectl --kubeconfig temp/u7s/kubeconfig get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/lima-node-smoke:10250/proxy/pods"
{"kind":"Status","apiVersion":"v1","status":"Failure","message":"Node \"lima-node-smoke:10250\" not found","reason":"NotFound","code":404}
```

**After** (with the fix — `:10250` stripped before store lookup):
```
$ kubectl --kubeconfig temp/u7s/kubeconfig get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/lima-node-smoke:10250/proxy/pods"
{"items":[...]}   # pod list from kubelet, no 404
```

*(VM stack started with `--reset --stack-only`; kubectl --raw repro is the exact operation sonobuoy's dump.go performs — same URL pattern, same failure mode.)*

## Quality gates

- `cargo test --workspace --quiet`: 1854 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --tests --quiet -- -D warnings`: clean

## Changed files

- `crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs` only — `strip_node_port` helper + 3 new tests

author: realdiligent
body:
## Problem

load_gguf() had several failure-mode hazards:

1. **gguf=true before g.open()** - a bad path left the GGUF decode path enabled with no valid weights.
2. **No rollback on mid-load failure** - a missing tensor, unsupported quant type, or layer-N error returned  alse but left partial owned buffers and half-populated s.w.layers. Callers that ignored the return (or retried) could hit null-weight kernels or mixed state.
3. **Unchecked cudaMalloc in dense()** - VRAM OOM passed 
ullptr into launch_gguf_dequant ? GPU fault during load.

load_weights() had the same partial-state problem on failure.

## Fix

- Add ollback_load_state(): invalidate decode graph, free all owned buffers, reset w, clear gguf.
- Call it at the **start** of each load (clean slate) and on **every** failure via a  ail() helper.
- Set gguf=true only **after** g.open() succeeds.
- Check cudaMalloc in dense() transpose path; abort without leaking temp buffers.

## Impact

- Failed GGUF/weight loads leave the model in a safe empty state instead of a toxic half-loaded one.
- OOM during dense dequant fails closed instead of crashing in kernels.
- Also frees prior weights at reload start (overlaps #148 intent; safe to merge either first).

## Test plan

- [ ] Truncated/corrupt GGUF ? load_gguf returns false,  orward_token rejected (no weights)
- [ ] Successful load unchanged
- [ ] load_gguf twice on same model - VRAM does not grow without bound

## Risks

None for happy path. Failed loads now explicitly clear state - callers must re-load before decode (correct behavior).

author: kenhayward
body:
> Second PR of the OAuth-for-MCP arc (PR1 #173 merged). Builds the interactive **approval** step on top of the authorization-server foundation.

## What

When an OAuth client (claude.ai / Desktop / Code) sends the user to `/connect/authorize`, that's a top-level **browser redirect with no Diariz session** (the SPA keeps its JWT in localStorage, not a cookie). This PR bridges that gap and adds the consent screen.

### Backend
- **`OAuthConsentTicketProtector`** - a short-lived, Data-Protection-**encrypted** consent ticket (userId + clientId + allow/deny + expiry), **bound to the specific client** and expiring in 5 min, so it can't be forged, replayed against another client, or reused. (TDD, 8 unit tests.)
- **`OAuthAuthorizeController`** (`GET/POST /connect/authorize`, OpenIddict passthrough):
  - no ticket → redirect the browser to the SPA **`/oauth/consent`** route, preserving the original authorize query;
  - **allow** ticket + an `Active`/`IsEnabled` user → `SignIn` (issues the code, with `sub`, the requested scopes, and the **`diariz-mcp` audience**);
  - **deny** ticket → `access_denied`; `prompt=none` with no ticket → `consent_required`.
- **`OAuthConsentController`** (`/api/oauth`, JWT-authed + status-gated): `consent-info` returns the client's display name; `consent` records the decision into the cookie.

### Web
- New public route **`/oauth/consent`** + page: fetches the client name, shows what's being granted (search/read your meetings + email your own account), and Allow/Deny. Reuses the existing login (added a safe internal **`?returnTo=`**) when signed out, then navigates the browser back to `/connect/authorize` to complete. i18n **en/es/fr/de**.

## Security notes
- The consent endpoint is JWT-authed and gated on the same `Active && IsEnabled` status as login.
- The bridge cookie is `HttpOnly`, `Secure` (prod), `SameSite=Lax`, and single-use (deleted when the authorize endpoint consumes it).
- `returnTo` only accepts same-app absolute paths (never an external URL).

## Not yet
End-to-end connection from claude.ai needs **PR3**: `/mcp` resource-server validation (accept an OAuth token **or** the static token) + RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata + advertising `registration_endpoint` in discovery. The static `dz_mcp_` token path is unchanged.

## Verification
- **705 unit** (+8 consent-ticket, TDD) and **72 integration** (+4 consent-controller: client-name lookup, gating 403, cookie emission, unknown-client 404, against real Postgres) tests pass. Web: **511** pass, `tsc` clean.
- The full browser handshake is inherently **live-only** and is exercised once PR3 makes the server discoverable.

## Deployment
**Server redeploy only** (no schema change, no desktop release).

- **Proof the gap was real:** with `_offline_rank` reverted to the old `len(plan)`, the new test fails (the 7-item fluff wins 7 > 2). With the fix it passes.
- All prior judge tests still pass unchanged — their plan items carry real titles, so substance count equals length for them.

## Checklist

- [x] `ruff check .` passes
- [x] `VANGUARSTEW_OFFLINE=1 python -m pytest -q` passes
- [x] Added/updated tests for the change
- [x] Updated docs (README / ROADMAP / CHANGELOG) if needed
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or private data included

## Notes for reviewers

The fix is deliberately minimal and behavior-preserving for real submissions: `_substantive_plan_size` counts plan items that name something (non-empty `title`/`theme`), replacing raw `len(plan)` as the first ranking key; the `philosophy` and `rationale` signals are untouched. Only submissions containing blank/filler plan items change rank — which is the intended effect. This targets the offline deterministic stand-in (the live LLM judge already reasons about substance via its rubric); noting the gap here also flags that raw item-count is a length-over-substance lever worth keeping out of any future deterministic scoring.

## Summary

Fixes two related Models app bugs reported by mandresve:

- **#1581** — Delete only updated local state; the backend never removed the file, so it reappeared on reopen. `DELETE /api/models/{model_id}` already existed but nothing called it, and the frontend had no way to know which catalog `model_id` a downloaded file belonged to (only its filename). The backend now attaches `model_id` to each `downloaded_files` entry when the filename matches a manifest variant's naming convention, and `handleDelete` calls the real endpoint, only dropping the row once the backend confirms — on failure it surfaces an error and keeps the row.

- **#1548 (remainder)** — After a download completed, the dialog kept showing "not installed" until closed and reopened. `fetchModels()` already re-fetched `/api/models` on completion, but with no sequencing guard a slower, earlier in-flight fetch (e.g. the initial mount call) could resolve *after* a newer one and clobber the just-installed state — the same class of stale-response race `DownloadProgress`'s poll already guarded against. `fetchModels` now tags each call with a sequence number and discards any response that isn't from the latest call.

author: pmcfadin
body:
Fixes #1794.

Pre-existing **main-red**: `needless_question_mark` at `bindings/python/src/write.rs:197` (introduced by #1792) fails workspace clippy under `-D warnings`, blocking every worker's `scripts/agent-gate.sh` (main has no required clippy CI context, so it slipped in).

## Fix
```rust
- Ok(block_on(self.inner.execute_flushing(statement))??)
+ block_on(self.inner.execute_flushing(statement))?
```
`block_on(..)` returns `Result<Result<u64, CoreError>, io::Error>`. The outer `?` converts the `io::Error` via `Error::Io` (`#[from]`, #1438); the inner `Result<u64>` is this fn's return type, returned as-is. Behaviorally identical to the `Ok(..??)` form, clippy-clean.

Found while running the #1614 (parser fuzz crate) gate. Discovered/tracked in parallel by the session that filed #1794.

author: robbyczgw-cla
body:
## Problem

Locale-aware providers were hardcoded to `us`/`en` in `DEFAULT_CONFIG`. That hurts non-US installs and local-intent queries: a user in Austria searching for opening hours or local shops gets US-centric results unless they override every provider section by hand.

## Design: region config-first, language query-aware

New `defaults.locale` config section:

```json
{
  "defaults": {
    "locale": { "country": "at", "language": "auto" }
  }
}
```

- **Country is config-first.** Precedence: CLI flag > explicit provider config > curated location hint in the query (e.g. "mejores restaurantes Madrid" → `es`, "boulangerie Paris horaires" → `fr`) > `defaults.locale.country` > `us`. The hint table covers ~35 city/country aliases across 11 countries; conflicting hints resolve to none.
- **Language is query-aware.** With `"auto"`, a conservative stdlib stopword heuristic (extending the existing routing `language_hint` mechanic) infers de/es/fr/it/pt/nl/en — requires ≥2 distinct signals and a strict single winner. Terse technical queries ("PostgreSQL 17 release notes") keep the configured default.
- **Explicit caveat: query language never implies the country.** A German-language query can come from Austria, Germany, or Switzerland — only explicit location hints or config change the region. No IP geolocation, no heavy language-detection dependency, no LLM.
- Central `resolve_locale()` in the new `search_locale.py`; all seven locale-aware dispatch adapters (Serper gl/hl, Brave, You.com, SerpBase, Querit, Firecrawl, SearXNG) resolve through it.
- Result metadata reports the resolved locale and per-value source (`config|hint|cli|fallback` / `config|inferred|cli|fallback`), following the freshness-metadata pattern.
- Provider `country`/`language` keys were removed from built-in `DEFAULT_CONFIG` sections so that a key present in the merged config always means "explicitly set by the user" — that is the explicit-override sentinel. Optional `country`/`language` tool-schema properties and `--country`/`--language` CLI flags (defaults `None` so an explicit flag is distinguishable).

## Backward compatibility

Without `defaults.locale` and without flags, every request resolves to exactly `us`/`en` as before — asserted down to the provider request body (`gl=us&hl=en` for Serper, `country=US&search_lang=en` for Brave). Cache keys unchanged. Explicit provider sections in user `config.json` still win. Provider routing priority untouched.

## Tests

- 33 new mocked tests in `tests/test_locale.py`: precedence matrix, inference per language, hint handling incl. conflicts, no-inference short queries, language≠country, metadata sources, provider request pass-through.
- `python -m pytest tests/ -q` → 438 passed
- `ruff check .` → clean; both `gen_*_docs.py --check` → green
- Docs: new USER_GUIDE section (config keys, `"auto"` mode, hint behavior, precedence, the language≠country caveat)

author: alchemmist
body:
## Summary

There was no release target — only `make tag`, which bumped **patch** by default (the `TYPE=minor|major` knob was undocumented), never pushed, and ran no checks, so the actual release trigger (pushing the tag) stayed manual and fumble-prone right before the upcoming minor.

This replaces it with three explicit semver targets:

```
make release-patch   # v0.1.25 -> v0.1.26
make release-minor   # v0.1.25 -> v0.2.0
make release-major   # v0.1.25 -> v1.0.0
```

All three are thin wrappers over the new `scripts/release.sh <bump>`, which:

1. refuses to run unless on `main`, with a clean tree, in sync with `origin/main` (fetches first);
2. runs `make check` so a broken tree can never be tagged;
3. computes the next version from the latest `v*` tag (first release still starts at `v0.1.0`);
4. prints the bump and the `git log --oneline` since the previous tag, and asks for confirmation;
5. creates the annotated tag and pushes it — release.yml (GoReleaser → GitHub release, Homebrew tap, AUR) takes over from there.

Alternatives like `svu`/semantic-release (deriving the bump from conventional commits) were considered in the issue and rejected: they add a dependency and let a mistyped commit message silently change the bump, while the human decision here stays explicit.

## Testing

- Sandbox repo (bare origin + clone, stubbed `make`): `minor` v0.2.3→v0.3.0 tagged and pushed; declining the prompt aborts with nothing tagged; `major` v0.3.0→v1.0.0; dirty-tree, non-main, out-of-sync (both ahead and behind) and existing-tag guards all refuse with a clear message.
- `make check` green.

Closes #216

author: jakechampion
body:
Slice 4 of the `#4391` arc — widening the stack-IR→SSA lift toward `build_func` parity so the redundant AST→SSA frontend can eventually be retired. Follows #4454 (arrays) and #4456 (structs). Tuples — the last of the composite value types.

## What

`lift_from_ir` now instruction-selects irlower's tuple ops into `build_func`'s `ExprTuple` layout (element i at slot i — **no** tag/length prefix, unlike arrays/structs), so the lifted SSA runs unchanged on `ssa_x86` / `ssa_arm64` / `eval_func`:

| IR op | Lowering |
|---|---|
| `tuple_make` | `alloc(n)` + each element (popped element-0-deepest) at slot i, push box |
| `tuple_get` | `load_elem` at slot i |
| `tuple_set` | `store_elem` at slot i (tuple constructor-reuse path; tuples are otherwise immutable) |

Width-64 (i64/f64) elements bail for a later slice; every element stores i32-wide (`imm 0`), which the low SSA heap also uses for pointer elements — exactly as `build_func`'s tuple path does.

## Testing (all green, x86-64 + arm64)

- **`TestSelfHostSSALiftIRLower`** — 4 production-shaped cases over **real irlower output**: `tuplepair`, `tuplefn` (a tuple returned from a function), `tuplenest` (a nested tuple = a pointer element), `tuplebool` (a boolean element driving a branch), each diffed against the interpreter.
- **`TestSelfHostSSALiftEmit`** — hand-built `tuplesum` (`tuple_make` + `tuple_get`) through optimise / **regalloc** / emit on both backends.
- **`TestSelfHostSSALiftDifferential`** — same `tuplesum` vs the interpreter oracle.

Verified locally: full `TestSelfHostSSALift*` suite passes on x86-64; `arm64/tuplesum` (emit) and `arm64/tuplenest` (irlower) pass under qemu. The eval golden (`op_alloc` bails) is unaffected.

With arrays + structs + tuples now lifting, the composite value types are covered; the remaining frontier toward `build_func` parity is the **f64/i64 width** (float/wide-int value tracking) and **map ops**.

author: itsjohnnie
body:
Follow-up to #270 — two fixes for the Discover page as an iOS home-screen app.

## Restore `black-translucent` status bar (the top-bar regression)

The Discovery-title commit in #270 set a page-level `appleWebApp` metadata object. Next merges metadata shallowly, so that object replaced the layout's status-bar meta and emitted its default value (`default`). iOS then rendered the standalone webview *below* the status bar: an opaque top bar, everything shifted down, and the centred tile sat below the visual middle.

- The discover page now declares the full `appleWebApp` object (`capable` + `title` + `statusBarStyle: "black-translucent"`).
- The layout's status-bar meta moved into its own `appleWebApp` object, with a comment warning that page-level objects replace it wholesale.
- `apple-mobile-web-app-capable` stays in `other`, since Next's `capable` flag only emits the modern unprefixed `mobile-web-app-capable`.

Verified in the static export: every page emits `black-translucent` plus both capable variants; discover also emits the `Discovery` title.

**Note after deploy:** the status-bar style is baked into the web clip at add-time — delete and re-add the home-screen icon to pick this up.

## Round the phone control bar

At 1rem from the screen edges the bar's 4px corners read as a hard rectangle fighting the iPhone's ~60pt display-corner sweep. The radius now matches the gutter (1rem each) on phones, per the concentric-corner rule; desktop keeps the site's editorial 4px.

## Summary
The runtime `CategoricalEncoder` defaults to `unseen_policy="mode"` (unseen category at predict time is mapped to the most frequent training category), but the exported `predict.py` mapped unseen categories to NaN and the artifact conversion dropped `unseen_policy`/`modes` entirely — a silent prediction divergence between `Model.predict()` and the exported artifact.

Additive `pipeline_state.json` fields (predict.py reads them with `.get()` defaults for backward compatibility); no Model `format_version` change; this is a codegen-correctness bugfix, not a new Proposal.

author: prasanthlevelup
body:
## Script Gen Quality review fixes (deterministic test-case build path)

Addresses the 5 prioritized findings from the *Script Gen Quality* review (scored 8.8/10). All changes are scoped to the **deterministic (non-LLM) test-case build** path in `src/script-gen/script-gen-engine.ts`. This is a follow-up to the Intelligence Orchestrator work (PR #216, merged).

### What was wrong
Every "Locked user login attempt…" variant was generated as a near-copy of the happy-path login: same credentials, same navigation, and every test asserted `'locked out'` (derived from the title). Repository intelligence (loaded dataset records, Page Object `open()`/`getError()`) was under-utilized, and headers showed `Coverage: n/a`.

### Fixes

| # | Fix | Before | After |
|---|-----|--------|-------|
| **P1** | **Scenario Intent Fidelity** | all variants copied happy-path login | whitespace → `` login(` ${user.username ?? ''} `, …) ``; special → `login('@locked_user', …)`; max-length → `login('A'.repeat(256), …)`; empty → `login('', '')`; invalid → `login('invalid_user', 'wrong_password')` |
| **P2** | **Repository Intelligence** | literal + bare `process.env.TEST_PASSWORD` | binds `const user = getRecord("locked_users")` and reads `user.username` / `user.password` (env fallback only when record lacks a password) |
| **P3** | **Assertion Intelligence** | all asserted `'locked out'` (from title) | derived from Expected Result: locked→`'locked out'`, empty→`'is required'`, invalid→`'do not match'`; ambiguous scenarios assert the error surface only (no guessed text) |
| **P4** | **Repository Reuse** | `page.goto()` + raw `[data-test="error"]` | `loginPage.open()` + `loginPage.getError()` when those methods exist; **no more duplicate navigation** |
| **P5** | **Coverage Metadata** | `Coverage: n/a` | derived categories (Functional/Negative/Boundary/Validation) + `Repository Assets Reused: LoginPage (Page Object); Test Data Store → dataset "…"` |

All Page-Object reuse is **method-gated** — if a repo's LoginPage only exposes `login()`, the engine safely keeps `page.goto()` and the raw error locator, so nothing regresses for simpler repos.

### Tests
- **New:** `tests/unit/script-gen-scenario-fidelity.test.ts` — 27 assertions covering all 5 fixes, driven through the public `generate()` entry point with cached crawl data (no network/LLM). **27 passed / 0 failed.**
- **Regression:** existing `tests/unit/script-gen-zip-review-fixes.test.ts` — **40 passed / 0 failed.**
- `npm run build` (tsc) passes clean.

### Scope
Only `src/script-gen/script-gen-engine.ts` (+ new test). No API/schema/DB changes.

> Please review — not merging automatically.

author: 0xleif
body:
## The bug (surfaced by the C1 migrate review · data loss in the primary config format)
`load_toml_config` parses line-by-line. A formatter-style multi-line array:
```toml
source_dirs = [
  "src",
  "lib",
]
```
was read as the value `[` alone → `parse_toml_string_array("[")` fell through to **`["["]`**, and the item lines (no `=`) were silently dropped. The user's real `source_dirs`/`exclude_patterns`/etc. became a single bogus `[` entry — so specsync scanned a nonexistent directory named `[`, found 0 source files, and reported vacuous 100% coverage / a green build.

**Worse:** `migrate` reads *then rewrites* the config, so it **persisted the corruption**, destroying a valid `.specsync.toml`. Every array key was affected.

## The fix
- **Accumulate continuation lines** when a value opens `[` without closing on the same line, until the array closes — multi-line arrays now parse to their real entries.
- **`parse_toml_string_array` uses the span between the first `[` and the LAST `]`**, tolerating a trailing comment and the joined multi-line text (also fixes the single-line `[...] # comment` case, and preserves a `]` inside a quoted glob like `**/[abc]/**`).
- **Strip inline `#` comments (quote-aware)** from array lines, reusing the existing `strip_inline_comment`; whole-line comments and blanks inside an array are skipped. **Scalar value parsing is byte-for-byte unchanged.**

## Verified
```
$ specsync migrate --no-backup   # legacy multi-line .specsync.toml
→ .specsync/config.toml:  source_dirs = ["src", "lib"]   # was ["["]
```

Tests: multi-line arrays (global + `[lifecycle]` section), comment-inside-array, empty multi-line array, key-after-array still parsed, trailing comment, glob-with-brackets, plus an integration test that `migrate` preserves a multi-line `.specsync.toml`. Full suite 685 + 160, fmt / clippy (bin) / self-check 100%.

author: mvdbeek
body:
Introduces `galaxy.tools.source_store`: a queryable store of parsed, macro-expanded tool sources plus a pre-computed `ToolIndex` of the metadata batch consumers need (panel section, labels, EDAM, requirements, test counts, shed provenance).

- **Backends**: standalone SQLAlchemy stores only — a SQLite file at `tool_source_disk_path` by default, any SQLAlchemy URL for shared multi-host deployments — plus a composite that layers named stores over the default with read fall-through (writes always land on the default). The store is a rebuildable cache and deliberately lives *outside* Galaxy's database: no migration, no shared session, per-write commits on its own engine.
- **Populator**: `scripts/tool_source/populate_store.py` walks tool_conf files and writes sources + index + whoosh search index; `--watch` updates the store on file changes and broadcasts `reload_tool_source_cache`. The populator is the single writer; store consumers are read-only.
- **Per-conf opt-in** via `store="name"` on a toolbox conf root, resolved against the `tool_source_stores` catalog in galaxy.yml.

Nothing reads from the store yet — an on-demand-loading toolbox consuming it is the follow-up (#22633, where this was extracted from per review discussion there). Admin and dev docs included.

`{group}_{version}_{singular}.yaml` sitting **directly** in a configured
`cr_paths` directory, with **one resource per file**.

Our existing `examples/` files don't match that convention (wrong names, and
`mcpserver-example.yaml` bundles six resources in one file), so these dedicated
files are added for the docs generator. Content is adapted from the existing
`examples/` so it stays representative.

- Once merged, this needs a release so `giantswarm/docs` can pin its
  `commit_reference` to a tag that contains `docs/cr/`.

  runtime record, not a user-authored resource. Easy to add later if we want it
  on the reference too.

author: raushannerkar
body:
First sub-task of AEGIS-104. Fixes the bug where refreshing the browser during
an active exam logs professors/students out.

## Root cause
`AuthContext` held the user in React state only and never restored it on mount,
and tokens were kept in memory only — so a page refresh wiped the auth state and
bounced the user to `/login`.

## Fix (httpOnly refresh cookie — keeps the existing anti-XSS stance)
- **backend/app/routers/auth.py** — `login` & `register` now also set the refresh
  token as an **httpOnly / Secure / SameSite** cookie (scoped to `/auth`).
  `/auth/refresh` reads the cookie (request body still accepted as a fallback for
  mobile/tests) and returns the `user` so the client can rehydrate. `/auth/logout`
  clears the cookie.
- **AuthContext** — on mount, restores the session by calling `/auth/refresh`;
  exposes a `loading` flag while doing so.
- **api/client.ts** — the silent-refresh interceptor now relies on the cookie
  (no request body); removed the in-memory refresh-token plumbing. The access
  token stays memory-only, so no token is written to JS-readable storage.
- **ProtectedRoute** — waits for `loading` before redirecting, so a refresh no
  longer flashes/bounces to `/login`.

## Testing
- Backend: `ruff`, `pyright`, and the full `test_auth_router.py` / `test_auth.py`
  suite (27 tests) pass — the cookie change is additive, existing body-based
  refresh still works.
- Frontend: `tsc` + `eslint` clean.
- Manual: `docker compose up --build` → log in → refresh the exam page → stays
  logged in (previously logged out).

## Notes for reviewers
- Touches `auth.py` (backend-owned area) — additive, no change to the existing
  token contract. @vijethph fyi.
- **Cross-site cookie in prod:** frontend and backend run on separate Container
  App hostnames, so the cookie is `SameSite=None; Secure` (works over HTTPS).
  Some browsers' third-party-cookie protections could interfere in the deployed
  environment — worth a smoke test after deploy. Fallback if ever blocked: serve
  both apps under one domain (separate infra task).
- Scope: WS1 only. Remaining AEGIS-104 items (exam resume/refresh warning,
  notifications, copy/paste detection, report accuracy) are separate sub-tasks.

author: vchelaru
body:
## What

Timeline strip cells and animation-tree chain icons rendered a raw texture crop, ignoring each frame's color/`ColorOperation` and `Alpha` — a tinted or faded frame looked identical to an untinted one, even though the wireframe/preview panels already show the effective color.

Thumbnails now apply the frame's **effective (sticky) color**: an omitted channel holds whatever an earlier frame last set, matching runtime and the preview panel. The tint reuses `FrameColorFilter` + `FramePreviewOpacity` — the same reference interpretation the preview uses — so timeline, tree, and preview render a given frame identically.

Per the issue's open question: **all** thumbnails are tinted, tree chain icons included (the honest choice — every surface shows the frame the same way).

## Caching & invalidation (the hard requirement)

- **Extended cache key.** `ThumbnailKey` now includes effective R/G/B/A/`ColorOperation`, so a tinted thumbnail is rendered once and reused until its crop *or* color changes; two frames with the same crop but different color no longer collide on one bitmap.
- **Sticky-aware, whole-strip invalidation.** `TimelineStripSignature` and `ThumbnailSource` capture the *effective* color, so editing frame N's color rebuilds cell N **and** every downstream cell it re-tints (sticky propagation). UV/flip edits stay local.
- **Resolve once per data change, not per render.** `EffectiveFrameColor.ResolveAll` resolves the whole strip in one O(n) forward pass. Resolution runs only on strip rebuild / tree refresh (data change), never in the 60fps playback loop — `RefreshTimelineStrip`/signature-building is not on the per-frame playhead path (`OnPlaybackTicked` moves the scrubber directly).
- **No #514 regression.** The cached decoded `SKImage` is untouched; the tint is a paint-level color filter on the existing image.

## Tests

- `EffectiveFrameColorTests` — `ResolveAll` matches per-frame `Resolve` at every index, later-frame re-set overrides the running value (guards a `??=` freeze regression), and the upstream/edited/downstream/shielded cascade contract.
- `ThumbnailSourceTests` / `TimelineStripSignatureTests` — a color/alpha edit (and an *earlier*-frame sticky edit) produces an unequal signature so the strip rebuilds.
- `ThumbnailServiceTests` — Multiply tint and effective-alpha render correctly; the cache key distinguishes colors (different color → different instance, same color → same instance).

Full AE suite green: 1390 Core + 537 App.

## Note on the diff

This branch is stacked on the (previously unpushed) sticky-color commit `b604c78`, so this PR includes **two commits**: the earlier "Show effective (sticky) frame color in AE preview and inspector" and this timeline/tree work. They form one cohesive feature line. Happy to split into stacked PRs if you'd prefer separate reviews.

Closes #528

author: gunkl
body:
## Summary

Following #400 (dashboard display fix), the underlying WHF nat-vent control itself was found to fail overnight — WHF ran correctly through the evening, reached the comfort floor around 2am, and stopped. It should have kept cycling to hold the sleep band.

Two confirmed, distinct root causes, both firing in sequence the same night:

1. **`fan_thermostat_check()`** (the tick-level safety check that runs on every thermostat temperature change, far more often than the 30-minute classification cycle) still used the flat daytime `comfort_heat` floor even during the sleep window. Because it fires so much more often, it always preempted `nat_vent_temperature_check()`'s correct sleep-aware cycling (already fixed in #374) before that logic ever got a chance to run — permanently ending the nat-vent session at `comfort_heat` instead of letting it cycle at `sleep_heat ± hysteresis` through the night.
2. Once that premature exit fired, `apply_classification()` legitimately arms `cool` mode as a compressor backstop — but that permanently blocked the idle-reactivation gate, which required the thermostat's armed *mode* to be literally `"off"`, even though the compressor was never actually running. Re-activation now checks `hvac_action` instead of the armed mode string.

Also fixed, found during the same investigation (and confirmed via a completeness audit that the initial pass had skipped some of these — see linked issue comments):

- The ODE ceiling guard escalated to AC for whole-house-fan archetypes despite them having no compressor-assist model by design (`_ceiling_threshold()` already documents this), causing a repeated escalate/reactivate oscillation with redundant thermostat writes.
- Bedtime setback tracking never recorded "applied" for `hvac_mode="off"` days (the majority case in mild climates) or "skipped" for the manual-override case — both silently blank in `tools/learning_db.py --daily` for every affected night.
- Nat-vent exit/assist events now all carry a `fan_device` field identifying which physical fan mechanism was involved.
- `ca_target_heat`/`ca_target_cool` in the status API are now sleep-window aware; the single-setpoint dashboard card gained a `(CA: X)` divergence annotation matching the dual-setpoint card.
- `docs/07-AUTOMATION-FLOWCHART.md` and `docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md` corrected — both still described a "Priority 0 sleep-ceiling reached" exit removed from code in #371.

Also folds in **#403** (restart-cause diagnostics), same v0.4.60 release, no separate version bump:

- CA now logs its own version at startup and shutdown, and classifies each restart boundary as `version_changed` (deploy), `user_restart` (a `homeassistant.restart`/`stop` service call was observed before shutdown), or `unknown` (crash-like — no clean shutdown recorded), instead of leaving every `system_restarted` event unexplained.
- This was surfaced while investigating #402 — 7 restarts were observed the same night, one of which turned out to be the #400 deploy and could only be confirmed by manually cross-referencing git log timestamps after the fact.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit tests for every individual fix (`test_fan_control.py`, `test_nat_vent_activation.py`, `test_natvent_away_ceiling.py`, `test_nat_vent_thermostat.py`, `test_api.py`, `test_bedtime_setback.py`, `test_warm_day_comfort_gap.py`) — each verified effective by reverting just that fix and confirming the dedicated test fails, then restoring.
- [x] New pending golden scenario (`tools/simulations/pending/whf_reactivates_after_sleep_floor_exit.json`) reproducing the incident end-to-end through the production harness — same revert-and-confirm verification.
- [x] New Playwright UI spec (`tests/ui/status-divergence.spec.js`) for the dashboard divergence indicator.
- [x] New `tests/test_restart_cause.py` (19 tests) for #403's shutdown/startup logging, cause classification, and event-call-service detection.
- [x] Full suite: 2995 passed. All 51 golden scenarios pass (no regressions). `ruff check`/`format` clean. `tools/validate.py` clean.
- [x] Version bumped to 0.4.60, `RELEASE_NOTES`/`KNOWN_FIXES`/`CHANGELOG.md` updated, `test_version_sync.py` passes.

Not covered by this fix (documented in `KNOWN_FIXES[402]`): the floor/cycling threshold formula is now duplicated across three functions rather than extracted into a shared helper. Not covered by #403 (documented in `KNOWN_FIXES[403]`): cannot retroactively diagnose the other 6 unexplained restarts from that same #402 incident night; the `unknown` bucket can't distinguish an OS/container kill from an HA core crash.

Fixes #402
Fixes #403

author: superness
body:
Implements SPEC_13 (Organic Community Formation / Behavioral Branching), Phase A: detection + local fracture. Salvaged and validated from a prior in-flight session, completed and tested against `specs/SPEC_13_ORGANIC_BRANCHING.md`.

## Implemented (by spec section)

| Spec section | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|
| §2.1-2.2 metrics + threshold constants (0.30 / 0.20 / 0.80, size 3, age 20160) | Implemented, exact §2.2 values | `src/branch/behavioral.rs` |
| §3.1 incremental tracking during action processing | Implemented — metrics updated inline on Post/Reply/Engage, no offline pass | `behavioral.rs`, router hook |
| §3.2 `IdentitySpaceMetrics` | Implemented (BTreeMap/BTreeSet instead of HashSet for §4.3 determinism) | `behavioral.rs`, persisted in `src/storage/chain.rs` |
| §3.3 threshold checking | Implemented per pseudocode | `behavioral.rs::check_threshold_crossing` |
| §3.4 BFS connected-cluster discovery | Implemented; `MIN_INTERACTION_COUNT_FOR_EDGE = 3` (spec references the constant but never assigns it — choice documented in code) | `behavioral.rs::get_connected_cluster` |
| §5.1 formation record + §13.2 routing (new posts -> community branch, replies stay with thread) | Implemented as cluster-membership fracture: community threads to RIGHT child, remainder LEFT. Existing SPEC_08 size/hash-bit fracture untouched; `MAX_DEPTH` respected | `src/branch/manager.rs` |
| §6.1 single-participant cluster | Implemented as a spam signal surfaced for spam-attestation/space-health (no community-of-one space yet — that needs §7) | `behavioral.rs`, `chain.rs` |
| §6.3 anti-gaming | Implemented cheap local rules: `MIN_INTERACTIONS_FOR_DETECTION = 100` (per §13.1) and per-space `FORMATION_COOLDOWN_BLOCKS = 40320` | `behavioral.rs` |
| §8.1 storage (no separate graph index) | Implemented — sled trees on the existing ChainStore db, spec tree names (`communities`, `identity_community`, `space_communities`) | `chain.rs` |
| Config gate | `behavioral_branching: Option<bool>` — default ON for regtest, OFF for mainnet/testnet | `src/node/config.rs`, wired via `MessageRouterBuilder` |

## Deferred (documented in `behavioral.rs` module docs)

- **§7 network messages** (MSG_COMMUNITY_DETECTED etc.) — per §4.3 detection is deterministic from chain data, so identical nodes converge without messages; the config flag keeps public networks off until §7 lands.
- **§4.1.2 root-block extension / §4.2 cross-node validation** — depends on §7.
- **§5.2/§5.3** ongoing membership migration, dissolution/merging.
- **§6.2** overlapping communities — Phase A: first formation wins (members of an existing community never re-trigger).
- **§13.3** reciprocity-weighted interaction quality.

## Spec ambiguities resolved

- `MIN_INTERACTION_COUNT_FOR_EDGE` has no value anywhere in the spec — chose 3 (one reply/reaction should not bind two identities; three sustained directed interactions implies a pattern).
- §2.1.5 pattern age is defined against a per-cluster `first_detected_height` that is never persisted — resolved as `current_height - max(first_activity_height)` over members (conservative: one aged identity cannot carry a freshly assembled cluster past the age gate).
- §2.2 vs §13.1 threshold conflict (0.30/0.20/0.80 vs 0.15/0.10/0.90) — kept §2.2 normative values as instructed; §13.1's `MIN_INTERACTIONS_FOR_DETECTION = 100` adopted for the §6.3 activity gate.
- 2-identity cliques are neither a community (>= 3) nor spam (== 1) — explicitly no-op.

## Tests

`tests/behavioral_branching.rs` — 5 deterministic synthetic-graph tests, all passing:
- loud insular cluster -> formation + cluster-correct thread assignment (hash bits ignored; post-formation routing honors membership both directions)
- popular-but-DIVERSE cluster with identical internal volume -> NO trigger
- single-identity spam -> spam signal, no community, no fracture
- same cluster one block under the age gate -> no trigger; at the gate -> forms
- same data twice -> identical formation (id, members, branch, metrics)

`cargo check` clean; `cargo test --lib branch` 51/52 (1 pre-existing failure on main in `sync::subscription`, unrelated); `cargo test --test behavioral_branching` 5/5; `cargo test --test branch_integration` 13/13. Pre-existing bench/integration-test compile breakage on main is untouched.

author: pixieofhugs
body:
Closes #322

## Problem
Accepting a collab invite when the invitee's task bank is full raises **409** `"Task bank is full (N in-progress praxes)."` (`respond_to_invite`, `backend/services/praxis.py`). The feed card swallowed it into a generic error, leaving the invitee stuck with no way to make room.

## Change
`FeedCardCollabInvite.tsx` now offers a drop-to-accept flow:

1. **Detect bank-full.** On accept failure, re-issue `respondToInvite` to inspect the raw backend detail and match on the **substring** `"Task bank is full"` (not the status code — collab is 409, the duel twin #314 is 400). Any other error stays on the shared hook's `error`.
2. **Populate the list** from the existing `useMyActiveTasks()` hook (real `PraxisCardOut[]`), not the old empty placeholder state.
3. **Drop = un-signup, then retry:**
   - authored-solo (`created_by_id === user.character.id`) -> `deletePraxis(id)`
   - joined collab -> `leavePraxis(id)` (new thin API wrapper for the existing `POST /praxes/{id}/leave`)
   - **never** `withdrawPraxis` (reverts to edit, does NOT free a slot)
   - then retry `respondToInvite(praxis_id, invite_id, true)` and navigate to `/praxes/{praxis_id}`.
4. **Real cap copy** via `useGameConfig().max_task_signups` instead of the hardcoded "20".

The drop logic is kept local to this card so the shared `useRespondToRequest` hook contract is untouched (the duel twin #314 is being built concurrently against it).

## Files
- `frontend/src/components/feed/FeedCardCollabInvite.tsx` — wired the modal + drop flow
- `frontend/src/api/praxis.ts` — added `leavePraxis(id)` wrapper (needed by the drop path)

## Tests
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean for the changed files (one unrelated pre-existing error in `isViewerMember.test.ts` from ADR-0028, present on `main`).
- `npx vitest run` — 161 passed / 16 files.

Primo di tre PR di hardening dall'audit di sicurezza. Chiude i **3 Critical** e le **High di autenticazione/DoS** (escluso il punto 4 / H6 — password seed — lasciato invariato come richiesto).

| ID | Sev | Fix |
|----|-----|-----|
| C1 | Critical | **CORS** — allowlist esatta di origin; l'else-branch **rifiuta** invece di riflettere qualsiasi origin con `credentials:true` |
| C2 | Critical | **SQLi** — `serviceDate` validato `/^\d{8}$/` nei due endpoint `/planning` prima dell'interpolazione `sql.raw` |
| C3 | Critical | **JWT** — in produzione `JWT_SECRET` obbligatorio (throw all'avvio, niente fallback pubblico); `JWT_SECRET` + `CERBERO_API_KEY` aggiunti a `render.yaml` |

| H5 | High | **`/admin/sync`** — `requireAdmin` applicato dentro `admin.ts` (path-scoped) |
| H7 | High | **Caronte** — fail-closed in prod se manca la chiave (503); confronto chiave a tempo costante; stesso timing-safe sul feed GTFS-RT (che resta pubblico read-only by design) |
| M8/M9 | Medium | body limit 100mb→4mb; `trust proxy=1` per rate-limit sul vero IP dietro Render |
| L7/L9/L13 | Low | security headers (X-Frame-Options/nosniff/Referrer-Policy/HSTS); `x-request-id` validato; login limiter 20/min + bcrypt async |

**Verificato end-to-end** contro il backend reale: login, RBAC per dominio (utente senza permesso → 403 sul dominio, 200 sugli altri; admin bypassa), gate `/admin/sync` (path-scoped, non blocca altre route), login-limiter → 429. Typecheck api-server pulito.

⚠️ **Al deploy servono le nuove env**: impostare `JWT_SECRET` e `CERBERO_API_KEY` su Render prima del merge in produzione, altrimenti l'API rifiuta l'avvio (JWT) e l'ingest Caronte risponde 503 — è il comportamento fail-closed voluto.

author: kacper-murzyn
body:
…(#53194)

Stops the transient autodiscovery `service not ready` condition from being reported as an "Autodiscovery Misconfiguration" health-platform issue.

`configresolver.Resolve` returns `service not ready` when a check template is resolved against a container whose pod isn't `Ready` yet — a startup race that resolves itself on the next reconcile, not a misconfiguration. `resolveTemplateForService` was forwarding *every* resolution error to the health platform (and logging at ERROR), so this transient race was reported as a MEDIUM misconfiguration.

Change:
- Export the transient error as `configresolver.ErrServiceNotReady`.
- In `resolveTemplateForService`, short-circuit on `errors.Is(err, ErrServiceNotReady)`: log at DEBUG and skip both the resolve-warning and the health-platform report. Genuine resolution errors are unchanged; the config still schedules once the service is `Ready`.
- Apply the same guard in the Config Discovery resolve path (`configmgr_discovery.go`, `python` build): **log-only change** — the transient goes ERROR→DEBUG. This path never touched the health platform, so there is no health-platform behavior change here (only the main path reports issues).

Behavior note: not-ready services no longer surface a resolve-warning in `agent status` / `agent configcheck`. The condition is transient and self-heals once the pod is `Ready`; genuine resolution errors still surface as before.

Across the fleet, `service not ready` accounts for ~100% of the Autodiscovery misconfiguration health signal (~10M reports/day), concentrated on ephemeral/batch workloads (Spark jobs, CI runners, synthetics, short-lived pods). It buries the genuinely misconfigured entities and, now that the health platform is enabled by default, surfaces as noise in Fleet Automation on upgrade.

- Node agent 3/3, cluster-agent and cluster-checks-runner Running; `redisdb` autodiscovered and resolved — no regression.

body:
## Summary

Four independent correctness/UX fixes found during a pass over the custom dashboard editor. All are confined to the dashboard widgets and were verified live against the local demo dataset.

### 1. Localize widget edit-overlay controls
In dashboard edit mode, the per-widget lock / configure / delete buttons used hardcoded English `aria-label` and `title` strings, so they rendered English tooltips in an otherwise fully-localized UI. They now route through i18n, reusing the existing `configure_widget` / `delete_widget` keys and adding `lock_widget_position` / `unlock_widget_position` to the `en` and `zh` dashboard locales.

### 2. Localize the "Unknown" server fallback
The line-chart and disk-io widgets fell back to a hardcoded English `"Unknown"` in their header when no server was configured, while the metric-card widget already localized the same case via `metricCard.unknownServer`. Both widgets now reuse that key so the subtitle reads the translated string.

### 3. Render level-1 markdown headings
The minimal markdown parser handled `## ` and `### ` but not `# `, so a level-1 heading fell through to a paragraph and displayed the raw `# ` prefix. The parser now emits an `h1` block for `# `, with a matching prose `h1` style on the markdown widget. Added a regression test covering the h1 case.

### 4. Hide the dead title field for built-in widgets
The widget config dialog offered an optional "title" input for every widget, but only module (custom) widgets render `widget.title` — built-in widgets draw their own contextual headers and ignore it, so the field was a no-op the user could fill with no visible effect. The field is now gated on `isModule` so it only appears where it actually takes effect. Built-in widgets keep any previously stored title untouched.

## Test
- `bun run test` (web) — 656 pass, including the new markdown h1 regression test, updated `dashboard-grid` label assertions, and the flipped `widget-config-dialog` title-field assertions (absent for built-ins, present for modules)
- `bun x ultracite check` — clean on all changed files
- `bun run typecheck` — passes
- Verified live in the browser against the local demo rig: edit-overlay tooltips render Chinese; unconfigured line-chart/disk-io show the localized "未知服务器"; a `# Heading` markdown widget renders as an `<h1>`; the built-in (gauge) config dialog shows no title field while the module (Hello World) config dialog still does.
