author: rodrisanchez1
body:
## Summary

Hardens the sync engine's board-deletion decisions around one rule: **a board is deleted locally only when the server confirms the deletion for that specific id**. Absence from the sync manifest is treated as a deletion *candidate*, never as proof. This closes the sync-zombie loop (#2259) and the stale-manifest data-loss vector (#2258), and removes two unbounded-retry loops.

### 1. Server-confirmed deletion candidates (PULL)

- `classifyRemoteBoards` no longer decides deletions. Boards with a server id, a `syncMeta` entry, not locally deleted, and absent from the manifest come back as `boardIdsToVerify` candidates.
- `syncBoards` re-reads all candidates in a single `POST /board/byids` request (`confirmServerDeletions`). Only ids **absent from that fresh response** are deleted (double signal: absent from the manifest AND absent from a fresh by-id read). Any request failure (network error, 5xx, unexpected shape) confirms nothing and retries next cycle: keeping a board the user deleted is recoverable; deleting a board the user just created is not. Failures are reported via `trackSyncException` (`phase: confirmDeletions`) — a chronically failing `/board/byids` would otherwise silently disable all remote deletions.
- The request is chunked to the server's 3000-id `MAX_BOARDS_BY_IDS` cap, so a mass-candidate cycle (e.g. every tracked board after a server-side account cleanup) confirms in a few requests instead of 400-ing forever. Ids that are not valid ObjectIds are never confirmed — the server filters them from the query, so their absence would prove nothing (the `isServerBoard` ≥14-char vs 24-hex ObjectId predicate gap is documented in `docs/sync-engine.md` §5.1).
- This deterministically fixes the #2258 mechanism (a stale manifest snapshot — e.g. a concurrent tab classifying against a manifest that doesn't yet list another tab's just-created boards): the omitted board still exists, the fresh read returns it, the board is kept.
- It supersedes the manifest-watermark guard from earlier commits on this branch. The watermark only protected the strictly-newest boards and could strand genuinely deleted boards above it (the most-recently-edited board deleted elsewhere became a permanent local zombie). No timestamp inference remains in the delete decision; the manifest watermark survives only as a telemetry property (the stale-manifest detector in App Insights).
- In a healthy cycle the candidate list is empty, so the confirmation costs no requests.

### 2. Untracked zombies & edit-vs-delete conflicts via the push 404 (#2259)

- Untracked boards (no `syncMeta`, pre-dating the sync engine) deleted server-side out-of-band are invisible to PULL (the `localHasSyncStatus` guard), so Pass 2 kept `PUT`-ing them forever, always failing with 404.
- On a push PUT **404**, when the board is **also absent from this cycle's manifest AND a fresh `POST /board/byids` read also omits it** (triple signal, same `confirmServerDeletions` helper as PULL), hard delete it locally via `deleteApiBoardSuccess`. A transient/spurious PUT 404 deletes nothing — it won't reproduce on the independent by-ids read, so a `PENDING` board's unsynced local edit can't be lost to a flaky response.
- The hard-delete path is explicitly update-only (`!needsCreate`): a board being *created* never existed on the server, so its absence from the by-ids read proves nothing — previously this was only protected accidentally by `createApiBoard` wrapping errors (stripping `.response`).
- Tracked edit-vs-delete conflicts (edited locally, deleted on another device) are now mostly resolved earlier, in the PULL confirmation pass; the push-loop path remains as the same-cycle fallback and the only path for untracked boards.
- `updateApiBoard` rethrows the original error instead of wrapping it, so the push loop can inspect `e.response.status`.

### 3. Telemetry

- New `Sync_PushNotFoundDelete` event on the (now triple-confirmed) push-loop delete path, with `boardId`, `tracked`, the board's `lastEdited`, the manifest watermark, and manifest size. Firings for boards that still exist in the DB would mean the by-ids confirmation itself is unreliable — a server-side investigation trigger.
- New `confirmDeletions` phase on `trackSyncException`, fired from the per-chunk catch in `confirmServerDeletions` (see §1).
- `Sync_RemoteDeletions` now counts only server-confirmed deletions; `manifestWatermark` is kept on the sync events as the fleet-wide stale-manifest signal.

Docs updated: `docs/sync-engine.md` (§5.1–5.2 confirmation rationale, predicate-gap note, flow diagram, §14 edge-case tables) and `docs/sync-telemetry.md`.

Fixes #2259
Mitigates #2258

## Test plan

- [x] `classifyRemoteBoards`: manifest-absent tracked server boards → `boardIdsToVerify` (including with an empty manifest); short-id, untracked, and locally-deleted boards excluded
- [x] `syncBoards` (PULL): candidate absent from the by-ids read → hard deleted; candidate returned by the by-ids read (stale manifest) → kept
- [x] `syncBoards` (PULL) fail-safe: confirmation request fails → candidate kept, cycle still succeeds; unexpected response shape → candidate kept; non-ObjectId candidate → excluded before any request; 3001 candidates → chunked into 3000 + 1 by-ids calls
- [x] Push loop: untracked zombie PUT 404 + by-ids absent → hard delete; tracked `PENDING` PUT 404 + by-ids absent → hard delete (edit-vs-delete, delete wins); PUT 404 while the manifest still lists the board → kept, no confirmation request; spurious PUT 404 with the board still in the by-ids response → kept
- [x] `npx react-scripts test src/components/Board/__tests__/Board.actions.test.js --watchAll=false` — 114 tests passing; `confirmServerDeletions` at 100% statement coverage

author: incognick
body:
Adds ADR-0042. Burrow installs and requires ingress-nginx today, the app Ingress, the cert-manager HTTP-01 solver, and the capability check all hardcode the `nginx` class. But k3s and k3d ship **traefik** by default (and k3s is hugely popular for self-hosting, homelab, and edge, dead center of the ICP), so those users are told to install a redundant second controller.

Standard `networking.k8s.io/v1` Ingress is served by every major controller and cert-manager HTTP-01 is controller-agnostic, so the only real barrier is the hardcoded class. The ADR decides to **use whatever controller the cluster already has**:

- **Detect** the running controller and its IngressClass (the orphan-class fix stands: a class alone is not a controller).
- **Bind expose and the HTTP-01 solver to the detected class** instead of hardcoding nginx.
- **Install ingress-nginx only when no controller exists**; adopt an existing one otherwise.
- **Stay portable** (standard Ingress; controller-specific annotations applied only for the controller in use).

This refines ADR-0022's "detect what the cluster supports and use it" from the Ingress-vs-Gateway axis to the which-controller axis; the expose surface does not change. Supported set is small (ingress-nginx, traefik) with others best-effort via standard Ingress.

Open for review; the implementation follows once the decision is settled.

author: augusdn
body:
### Description of PR

`ssh/test_ssh_stress.py::test_ssh_stress` fails intermittently on the **t1-lag-vpp** KVM baseline (on `master` it runs only on `asic_type == 'vpp'`, skipped on other asics via `conditional_mark`). The post-test system check reports a false failure although the DUT is healthy:

```
Failed: CPU usage increased by more than 20 points during test and did not reduce from raised value
Initial Value: 0.25252525252525254, Max value: 0.47, Post-Test Value: 0.47
```

Root cause (two parts):
1. `get_system_stats` read bare `vmstat`, which reports CPU **averaged since boot**. Over a ~5 min test that average barely moves, so the in-test peak (`max_cpu`) and the single post-test sample (`post_cpu`) end up nearly identical.
2. The check asserted `max_cpu - post_cpu > 0.1`. When the late `post_cpu` sample lands `>= max_cpu` (a measurement artifact -- note `Max == Post == 0.47` above), the difference is `<= 0` and the assertion fails even though CPU never actually stayed elevated.

Fixes the failures tracked in ADO PBI 38650838.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Test case improvement

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
`run_post_test_system_check` verifies that CPU/memory return toward their pre-test baseline after the SSH stress load, but it fails intermittently on shared VPP KVM hosts even though the DUT is healthy, for the two reasons above.

#### How did you do it?
- Sample **instantaneously** with `vmstat 1 2` (the 1-second delta row) so the peak and post-test readings are meaningful instead of since-boot averages.
- **Poll** several post-test samples, keep the best (lowest), and compare it against the **pre-test baseline (`init`)** rather than the in-test peak. A genuinely stuck-high process still fails; a normal spike-then-recover (even with a noisy first sample) passes. The 20-point sensitivity is unchanged, so this does not introduce new false positives from benign page-cache growth.

#### How did you verify/test it?
- Reproduced the exact failure end-to-end on the VPP KVM baseline (`vms-kvm-vpp-t1-lag`, master KVM build): 1/20 repeats failed with the signature above.

author: simonhull
body:
## Avatar cluster fix (#4 / #9 / #10 / #11)

`UserAvatar` resolved every user through `UserProfileRepository.observeProfile`, which read the `user_profiles` Room table. But the *only* writer of `user_profiles` is `ProfileRepositoryImpl.refreshMyProfile()` — the current user. So for any **other** user, `observeProfile` emitted `null` forever → indefinite `Loading` → grey circle. The all-users roster (with `displayName`, `avatarType`, `avatarUpdatedAt`) already lives in the server-synced `public_profiles` table used by the leaderboard; the UI just never read it.

### Changes

**Step 1 — resolve any user from `public_profiles` (#4, enables #9/#11)** — `sharedLogic`
- `UserProfileRepositoryImpl` now depends on `PublicProfileDao` instead of `UserProfileDao`. `observeProfile`/`getById` read the synced roster (tombstoned rows → `null`).
- New `PublicProfileEntity.toDomain()` maps `avatarUpdatedAt → updatedAt` (load-bearing: versions the `"$userId-avatar-$updatedAt"` Coil cache key on avatar-byte changes) and leaves `avatarColor` blank so `parseAvatarHexColor` falls back to the stable per-user color.
- `SocialModule` + `UserProfileRepository` KDoc updated (now serves **all** users, incl. self).
- Fixes the blank grey circle at every fallback-less site (Admin, activity feed, book readers, discover, book card, admin collection detail).

**Step 2 — reactive file presence + version-keyed cache (#11, #9)** — `sharedUI`
- `rememberUserAvatarState` replaces the fire-and-forget `ensureUserAvatarCached` + non-reactive `hasLocalAvatar` with a completion-driven re-check: a `downloadTick` bumps when `downloadUserAvatar` actually lands a file, and disk presence is re-checked on `userId` / `avatarUpdatedAt` / tick. A synced avatar change re-emits a new cache key (Coil re-decodes) and re-runs the download effect. Avatars now flip from initials to the real photo the moment the file appears — no revisit, no manual refresh.

**Step 3 — tap-to-profile (#10):** no code change needed. The leaderboard and book-readers rows are already fully clickable and navigate to `UserProfile(userId)`; the avatar sits inside that clickable row. Adding a nested `onClick` would be redundant. With Step 1 making avatars actually resolve, tapping through works. No new screens; Admin users-list avatar and decorative badges intentionally unchanged.

### Tests
- New `UserProfileRepositoryImplTest` (jvmTest): another user's name/type from `public_profiles`, `avatarUpdatedAt → updatedAt`, blank color, tombstone → `null`, avatarUpdatedAt bump re-emits.
- Extended `UserAvatarStateTest` (androidHostTest): public-profile-derived profile never maps to `Loading`; blank color → stable opaque per-user color; cache key folds `updatedAt`.

### Follow-up (out of scope)
After Step 1, the `user_profiles` table / `UserProfileDao` is still **written** by `refreshMyProfile()` but no longer **read** anywhere — a newly orphaned read left in place for a surgical follow-up cleanup.

### Verification
`./gradlew :sharedLogic:jvmTest :sharedUI:testAndroidHostTest spotlessCheck detekt --no-daemon` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**. (commonMain/sharedUI changes; iOS keeps its own `ensureUserAvatarCached` path and builds in CI.)

body:
Every released APK shipped with `versionCode=1` / `versionName="0.1.0"` because the values were hardcoded and never bumped. Android rejects installs where `versionCode` doesn't strictly increase, breaking installation of any release after the first.

## Changes

### `app/build.gradle.kts`
- Defaults bumped to `versionCode=3` / `versionName="0.3.0"` (current release)
- Both values read from Gradle project properties, falling back to the hardcoded defaults:
  ```kotlin
  versionCode = (project.findProperty("versionCode") as String?)?.toInt() ?: 3
  versionName = (project.findProperty("versionName") as String?) ?: "0.3.0"
  ```

### `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- Added a **Compute version from tag** step before the Gradle build that validates the tag matches `vX.Y.Z`, then derives and injects `versionCode` / `versionName` via `-P` flags — no manual bumps needed going forward:

  | Tag | versionCode | versionName |
  |-----|-------------|-------------|
  | v0.3.0 | 300 | 0.3.0 |
  | v1.2.3 | 10203 | 1.2.3 |

  Tags not matching `vX.Y.Z` fail fast with an explicit error.

author: xpiredruby
body:
## Summary

Implements item 3 as a separate PR after PR #20 and PR #21 were reviewed and merged.

This hardens `ghost_sim_ros2/analysis/observability_crlb.py` into a pure-Python/NumPy observability and CRLB module that consumes the merged measurement-covariance API without ROS, rclpy, Pi, camera-driver, OpenCV, or live hardware dependencies.

## What changed

- Adds 2D CV and CA motion-model support:
  - `cv_state_transition(dt)` for `[x, y, vx, vy]`
  - `ca_state_transition(dt)` for `[x, y, vx, vy, ax, ay]`
  - `position_measurement_matrix(state_dim=4|6)`
- Adds R-weighted finite-horizon observability Gramian:
  - `weighted_observability_gramian(f, h, r, horizon_steps)`
  - `gramian_report(...)` with rank, observability, singular values, and condition number.
- Keeps `fisher_information_matrix(...)` as the observed-measurement linear alias for the R-weighted Gramian.
- Adds labeled CRLB outputs with runtime-visible caveats:
  - `assumption_label = "ASSUMES_WHITE_NOISE"`
  - `validity_status = "INVALID_IF_NOISE_IS_COLORED"`
  - caveat strings describing the R source.
- Adds `linear_crlb_from_covariance_estimate(...)` and CV/CA convenience wrappers that consume `CovarianceEstimate` from PR #21.
- Adds `empirical_raw_cv_crlb(...)` as the default empirical path.

## Raw vs detrended R discipline

The default empirical CRLB path uses:

```python
estimate_empirical_stationary_r(csv_path, sample_mode="raw", dimensions=("x", "y"))
```

This is intentional and matches PR #21: raw empirical R preserves the actual single-measurement uncertainty seen by a filter, including drift/colored components if present.

Detrended R is allowed only as an explicitly labeled diagnostic. CRLB caveats differ depending on the R source:

- Raw empirical R:
  - `RAW_EMPIRICAL_R_DEFAULT_MAY_INCLUDE_COLORED_COMPONENTS`
  - CRLB remains invalid as a final bound if temporal correlation remains.
- Detrended empirical R:
  - `DETRENDED_R_DIAGNOSTIC_NOT_DEFAULT_FOR_FILTER_R`
  - caveat says detrended R suppresses linear drift and is not the default filter R.
- Pinhole/Jacobian analytical R:
  - `ANALYTICAL_WHITE_R_REFERENCE`
  - caveat says internally consistent only under the white/local residual assumption.

## Tests added/expanded

`ghost_sim_ros2/test/test_observability_crlb.py` now covers:

- CV observability after two position measurements.
- CA observability after three position measurements.
- Hand-computable 1D CV R-weighted Gramian:
  - `G = [[2, dt], [dt, dt^2]] / sigma^2` for a two-step position-observed CV system.
- CRLB improvement with longer horizon.
- CRLB reduction with lower measurement noise.
- Raw empirical R default flowing through CRLB with colored-noise caveat.
- `empirical_raw_cv_crlb(...)` using raw mode by default.
- Detrended empirical R labeled diagnostic/not-default.
- Pinhole covariance estimate producing analytical white-reference CRLB caveat.
- Existing range/bearing Jacobian checks.
- Markdown report includes white-noise/colored-noise caveat fields.

## CI wiring

The focused `GHOST Software Regime` workflow now includes:

```bash
pytest -q ... ghost_sim_ros2/test/test_observability_crlb.py
```

## Simulation vs hardware scope

Validated in synthetic/simulation only:
- CV and CA finite-horizon observability rank behavior.
- Hand-computable R-weighted Gramian case.
- CRLB monotonic behavior with horizon and measurement noise.
- R-source caveat routing for raw empirical, detrended empirical, and analytical pinhole R.

Still dependent on real hardware R / Pi validation:
- Whether the controlled Pi stationary log remains colored after camera-control lock.
- Whether raw empirical R should be used directly, inflated, whitened, or augmented in the eventual estimator if temporal correlation remains high.
- Any report-grade use of CRLB against real GHOST data.

## Claim discipline

This PR does not claim the live tracker reaches the CRLB. The CRLB is explicitly a simplified observed-measurement, white-noise reference bound and is labeled `INVALID_IF_NOISE_IS_COLORED` at runtime.

author: copilot
body:
The `pages build and deployment` workflow was intermittently failing in the `deploy` job despite successful artifact creation, with `actions/deploy-pages` returning transient backend errors. This change makes deployment behavior explicit and resilient to one-off Pages deploy failures.

- **Workflow ownership and deployment path**
  - Added a repository workflow at `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` to define build/upload/deploy behavior directly in-repo.
  - Uses the standard Pages sequence: checkout → configure pages → upload artifact → deploy.

- **Deploy resilience**
  - First deploy attempt runs with `continue-on-error: true`.
  - A second deploy attempt runs only when the first attempt is `failure` or `cancelled`.
  - Job fails only if the retry also fails/cancels.

- **Deployment serialization**
  - Added `concurrency` for Pages (`group: "pages"`) with `cancel-in-progress: false` to avoid interrupting in-flight deploys.

```yaml
- name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
  id: deploy
  continue-on-error: true
  uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5

- name: Retry deploy to GitHub Pages
  id: deploy_retry
  if: ${{ steps.deploy.outcome == 'failure' || steps.deploy.outcome == 'cancelled' }}
  uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5

- name: Fail if retry did not succeed
  if: ${{ steps.deploy_retry.outcome == 'failure' || steps.deploy_retry.outcome == 'cancelled' }}
  run: exit 1
```

## What
`statistics.py` only (+ tests). Added `_fill_missing_interior_hours(existing, repairs)`: for each consecutive present pair in `sorted(existing.keys())` with a gap, insert a flat `StatisticData(start=H, state=P, sum=P)` for every absent hour strictly between them. Combined into the single import `_import_statistics(missing_rows + stats)`, after the `existing` read and after `_repair_zero_filled_hours`. Real data for these flat hours lands on the **next** poll via the existing adjacent-pair repair path (deferred, matching the zero-fill contract). The anchor math from 38f1d18 is unchanged: missing rows are `< last_db_hour` with zero delta, so they never touch the anchor.

## The guard (da HIGH) and why in-memory over a re-read
`_repair_zero_filled_hours` runs first and its `async_adjust_statistics` cascades each delta forward (`sum += adj WHERE start >= start_time`), **including onto the gap's left neighbour `prev_hour`**. If the flat value `P` were computed from the pre-repair `existing` snapshot, the inserted flat sum would sit **below** the now-cascaded neighbour — a downward monotonicity dip that never converges (the next poll sees `existing[gap] - existing[prev] < 0`, classifies it as "has data" at the `!= 0` check, and never repairs it).

**Fix:** `P` must be the post-repair sum at `prev_hour`. I compute it **in memory** — `existing[prev_hour] + Σ(delta for repaired hours <= prev_hour)` — using the `(hour, delta)` pairs `_repair_zero_filled_hours` now returns. I deliberately did **not** re-read the DB: `async_adjust_statistics` and `async_add_external_statistics` *queue* work on the recorder thread, while a `statistics_during_period` re-read runs on the DB executor pool — so the re-read can race ahead of the queued adjustment flush and return stale pre-repair sums, reintroducing the exact bug. The in-memory computation is deterministic and independent of flush timing.

**Multi-repair correctness:** the cascade is additive and order-independent, so the final sum at `prev_hour` equals its initial value plus every delta applied at an hour `<= prev_hour`; multiple repairs before one gap each contribute independently. Covered by `test_repair_before_gap_stays_monotonic_multi_repair` (two repairs before the gap).

## VISION decision filter
1. **Helps get consumption into the Energy Dashboard / keep it correct?** Yes — fills real gaps so the cumulative chain is complete and monotonic.
2. **Without re-implementing Helen API logic `oma-helen-cli` owns?** Yes — pure chain bookkeeping over already-fetched data.
3. **Keeps the six-file shape understandable in one sitting?** Yes — one new private method plus a small threading change; no new files or surface.
4. **Could it corrupt or erase existing statistics on failure?** No — gated behind a successful `existing` read (`StatisticsQueryError` → return, nothing written); flat rows carry post-repair sums so the chain stays monotonic; existing rows are never modified; nothing is written outside the rolling window.

## Rules involved
- STACK.md: never a code path that can corrupt/erase already-imported history on a transient failure (the read-gate + in-memory post-repair value).
- STACK.md executor discipline: no blocking I/O added to the loop; no DB re-read.
- CLAUDE.md golden rule: smallest correct change; window sizing / backfill (#10) / config flow untouched.

## Verification
`uv run ruff check custom_components && uv run pytest tests/` → ruff clean, **38 passed**. Also ran `-W error::Warning` (38 passed) — no blocking-call warning. New tests: (1) missing interior hour flat-filled this poll, not adjusted, chain monotonic; (2) that hour converges next poll (adjacent-pair adjust, repaired delta reflected in the tail anchor, no lost energy); (3) da's multi-repair regression — two repairs before a gap stay monotonic with no dip (**fails against a naive pre-repair-snapshot implementation**, verified: it yields 1.0 instead of 2.2); (4) transient read failure → nothing imported even with a gap present; (5) `missing_rows` (< last_db_hour) and appended `stats` (>= last_db_hour+1h) are disjoint and the combined batch is ordered.

## States handled
Interior gap flat-filled (this poll), gap converged (next poll), repair-before-gap (post-repair flat, no dip), transient read failure (nothing written), combined batch (disjoint/ordered).

Closes #6

body:
## What

Adds first-class support for running Strix on [Groq](https://console.groq.com/). `GROQ_API_KEY` is now accepted as the LLM key alongside `LLM_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`, so users can point Strix at Groq's fast inference with their
provider-native key and a `groq/<model>` model string.

Resolved #656 

## Why

Groq offers fast, low-cost inference for open models (Llama 3.x, etc.), but there was no documented, first-class way to use it. Strix only looked for `LLM_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`, so a user with a `GROQ_API_KEY` had to fall back to
undocumented workarounds (custom `LLM_API_BASE`, `openai/` model names). This makes Groq work the same way OpenAI already does.

## How

Groq models already route correctly through the existing stack — `StrixProvider` forwards non-OpenAI prefixes to LiteLLM, and `_mirror_api_key_to_provider_env` copies the configured key into `GROQ_API_KEY` (verified: `litellm.validate_environment("groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile")` reports `GROQ_API_KEY` as the required key). The only missing piece was accepting the provider-native key, so this change is intentionally minimal:

- `strix/config/settings.py` — add `GROQ_API_KEY` to the `api_key`
  `AliasChoices`. It's listed **after** `LLM_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`, so
  those keep precedence when multiple are set.
- `tests/test_config_loader.py` — two tests (alias populates the LLM key;
  `LLM_API_KEY` wins over `GROQ_API_KEY`) plus `GROQ_API_KEY` added to the
  env-reset list.
- `README.md` — document the Groq config in the Configuration section.

## Before / After

**Before** — no supported path; had to improvise:
```bash
export STRIX_LLM="openai/llama-3.3-70b-versatile"
export LLM_API_BASE="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1"
export LLM_API_KEY="gsk_..."   # undocumented, loses provider-native handling

author: ch4r10t33r
body:
Closes #63.

Ports the channel parked-chunk buffer and GC from ethp2p [`broadcast/channel.go`](https://github.com/ethp2p/ethp2p/blob/main/broadcast/channel.go) (`handleChunk` / `handleSessionOpen` / `cleanup`). `ChannelRs` previously had no parked map or TTL handling — chunks arriving before their `SESS` open had nowhere to go, and stale sessions were never reaped.

## What it does
- **`parkChunk`** buffers a chunk that arrived before its session exists; per-message cap **`max_parked_chunks = 32`** (new chunk dropped → `.dropped_full` when full, matching Go cancelling the stream).
- **`attachRelaySession`** replays and frees any parked chunks into the now-open session (Go `handleSessionOpen` flush).
- **`disposeSession`** also drops the message's parked chunks.
- **`cleanup(now_ms)`** disposes sessions older than `active_session_ttl_ms` and drops parked buckets older than `pending_chunk_ttl_ms`.
- Adds the constants `channel_inbox_cap` (1024), `max_parked_chunks` (32), `active_session_ttl_ms` (5m), `pending_chunk_ttl_ms` (10s), `cleanup_interval_ms` (30s), `routing_tick_interval_ms` (25).

## Adaptations
- Go parks the **QUIC stream** and lets flow control back-pressure the sender; the Zig ingest path already holds the read bytes, so `ParkedChunk` owns a copy of the peer id + data.
- `cleanup` is poll-driven with an explicit `now_ms` (no ambient clock / ticker goroutine). `SessionRs.created_at_ms` carries the creation time — `0` means unset and is skipped, set by the driver that owns the clock. (Go's `cleanup` currently drops parked chunks unconditionally with a TODO to use `pendingChunkTTL`; this implements that intent.)

## Tests (leak-checked)
- replay-on-attach (verified via a recording observer's `chunk_rcvd`),
- cap enforcement (33rd park → `.dropped_full`),
- `cleanup` drops stale parked chunks + disposes expired sessions (and leaves fresh ones).

Verified on stock Zig 0.16.0: `zig fmt --check`, `zig build test`, `zig build test-broadcast` (TSan). README updated.

author: conormccarter
body: Advancing the retention floor makes sub-floor WAL GC-eligible, but advancement only parsed the target manifest — a metadata segment lost after checkpoint publication would surrender the replay promise that could still have rebuilt it. Floor advancement now existence-probes every referenced segment first and refuses to move past a missing one. The base rebuild — the one production point that materializes every row of every family — now cross-checks the index families against their canonical tables, giving the spec's index-corruption rule a production enforcement point instead of a test-only one. Spec wording updated to promise exactly what is enforced.

body:

The #311/#312 framing asks the designer to *justify each serial edge* in the schedule, and asks
`design-audit`'s schedule-efficiency dimension to *check the justification*. In practice
(restriction-sweep-1, hours after #312 merged, same day) this produced a circular justification —
"serial edge justified: single shared GPU is the resource limit" — where the single GPU was itself a
discretionary one-pod choice made a line earlier. The design-audit's schedule-efficiency dimension
PASSED it, because both sides were in justification-mode: defending/checking the plan as drawn instead
of generating alternatives. The researcher had to catch it in conversation, again — the same failure
mode #311/#312 were meant to close.

Replace justification with **enumeration** at both ends of the same seam (design + design-audit), with
the researcher's concrete numbers landing verbatim in spirit:

<details>
<summary>Design record</summary>

## Problem

The #311/#312 framing asks the designer to *justify each serial edge* in the schedule, and asks
`design-audit`'s schedule-efficiency dimension to *check the justification*. In practice
(restriction-sweep-1, hours after #312 merged, same day) this produced a circular justification —
"serial edge justified: single shared GPU is the resource limit" — where the single GPU was itself a
discretionary one-pod choice made a line earlier. The design-audit's schedule-efficiency dimension
PASSED it, because both sides were in justification-mode: defending/checking the plan as drawn instead
of generating alternatives. The researcher had to catch it in conversation, again — the same failure
mode #311/#312 were meant to close.

Justification-mode is asymmetric in a way that invites this: it is always easier to justify a choice
already on the page than to independently generate the max-fan-out alternative and compare. The author
writes the schedule, then writes a one-line reason for each serial edge already in it; the auditor reads
the schedule with the same anchor. Neither side is ever forced to produce the parallel alternative and
show why it was rejected.

## Approach

Replace justification with **enumeration** at both ends of the same seam (design + design-audit), with
the researcher's concrete numbers landing verbatim in spirit:

1. **`design-experiment` SKILL.md** (`plugins/experiment-lifecycle/skills/design-experiment/SKILL.md`):
   remove the "justify every serialization" cost-section bullet and the "every serial edge you *do* keep
   must justify itself" line in the schedule-brainstorm bullet. Replace with an enumeration instruction:
   while sketching the schedule, list each step's max sensible fan-out and price it, not just note that
   parallel is allowed. State the researcher's defaults directly (not as escalation thresholds, as norms):
   - 5-10 pods is the NORMAL fan-out for parallelizable GPU work — not a special case needing permission.
   - API concurrency starts at ~50.
   (These are stated as this researcher's/instance's current defaults, adjustable to a design's actual
   execution profile / provider quota — not a universal product constant — same pattern the skill already
   uses for `AAR_STYLE_GUIDE`.)
   - Per-wallclock cost is linear in pod count, so pod-count conservatism buys nothing under that billing
     model — the only real caps are (a) setup/warmup fraction (fan out until setup is roughly 20-30% of
     the unit of work — e.g. ~15-20 min pod warmup against a 1h generation unit is fine at one pod per
     unit), (b) GPU stock/quota or a real, documented API/provider rate limit, and (c) a true data
     dependency or validation gate.
   Keep the per-compute vs per-wallclock billing distinction (Tinker-style parallel-is-free vs a rented
   pod) — that framing correctly caught the 2026-07-03 hereditary-ccp-platform incident and isn't part of
   what broke.

2. **`verify-claims` `audit_experiment.sh --design`, dimension 7 (schedule efficiency)**
   (`plugins/verify-claims/skills/verify-claims/scripts/audit_experiment.sh`): reframe the dimension from
   "does every serial edge justify itself" to "enumerate the parallelizable steps and their max sensible
   fan-out; is the design at max fan-out for each, or did the researcher explicitly decline it?" State
   explicitly that a resource limit which is itself a discretionary design choice (e.g. "only one pod") is
   NOT a valid reason to serialize — that's the exact circular pattern that slipped through. Keep the
   per-compute vs per-wallclock billing check (still correct, still the thing that caught the earlier
   incident).

3. Update the matching one-paragraph summary of dimension 7 in `verify-claims` `SKILL.md`
   (`plugins/verify-claims/skills/verify-claims/SKILL.md`) so the two descriptions of the same dimension
   don't diverge — one says "justify," the other says "enumerate."

Companion runtime ticket #323 (API concurrency 50 + watchdog GPU-utilization tracking) touches
`run-experiment`'s runtime concurrency/watchdog text and `design-experiment` SKILL.md for the same reason
(shared serialization language); it is a separate PR, dispatched right after this one merges, to avoid two
concurrent edits to the same file.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep justification, add a stronger auditor prompt ("be suspicious of resource-limit justifications").**
  Rejected: still asks the auditor to evaluate a justification for a plan already drawn, which is exactly
  the anchor that let the circular case through. Doesn't change the generative/adversarial asymmetry.
- **Require the researcher to co-sign every serial edge.** Rejected: reintroduces per-decision human gating
  that the design stage already avoids elsewhere (the whole point of the audit gates is to let the AAR self-
  correct before consuming the researcher's attention); the enumeration reframe gives the auditor a concrete,
  falsifiable check (is the enumeration complete, is fan-out at the max or explicitly declined) without adding
  a human step.
- **Numeric fan-out floor enforced by tooling (e.g. a checklist gate that fails under N pods).** Rejected as
  out of scope for this issue: the fix here is a documentation/prompt-framing change to two already-existing
  gates, not new tooling; a mechanical floor can't tell a genuine stock/quota cap from under-parallelization
  and would need its own design work.

## Blast radius

Product-scaffold only, in `automated-researcher`: `plugins/experiment-lifecycle/skills/design-experiment/
SKILL.md` (prose), and `plugins/verify-claims/skills/verify-claims/SKILL.md` (prose) + its
`scripts/audit_experiment.sh` — a behavior-affecting change to the prompt text the cross-family design-audit
reads, not just documentation, since it changes what the auditor is asked to check. Both changed plugins
(`experiment-lifecycle`, `verify-claims`) get a `plugin.json` version bump + a `CHANGELOG.md` entry per repo
convention, checked by `.aar-ci/checks.sh`'s version-bump gate. No other skills, no schemas. Affects every
future experiment design and design-audit pass; does not touch `run-experiment`'s runtime text (companion
issue #323, landing right after this PR merges) or any in-flight experiment.

## Rollout + rollback

Doc-only change, takes effect on the next `design-experiment` invocation after merge — no migration, no
staged rollout needed. Rollback is a plain revert of the merge commit if the enumeration framing turns out
worse in practice; low risk given the change narrows rather than removes a check (the billing-distinction
check that caught a real incident is left intact).

</details>


Design record: `proposals/322-parallelism-enumeration.md`. It lands in the repo when this PR merges.

author: dyascj
body:
Provider default base URLs were duplicated across **six** places — the chat client, the chat server route, the models client, the models server route, the local-endpoint helpers, and the registry. A drift between any two of them recreated the old Ollama base-URL bug class (e.g. one table gets `/v1` appended, another doesn't).

This moves them into one `provider-defaults.ts` module and points every consumer at it. Rather than collapsing to a single map, it keeps the three sets that legitimately differ:

- **`DEFAULT_CHAT_BASE_URLS`** — chat/streaming endpoints (Google uses its OpenAI-compat path `/v1beta/openai/` here)
- **`DEFAULT_MODELS_BASE_URLS`** — model-listing endpoints (Google uses its native path `/v1beta`; also includes the TTS providers that expose a model list)
- **`DEFAULT_LOCAL_BASE_URLS`** — local providers, before per-provider normalization in `local-endpoints.ts`

Values are unchanged from what each consumer used before, so this is behavior-preserving. The registry's LLM `defaultBaseUrl` fields now reference the chat map too, so the display/fallback value can't drift from the resolution value.

## Verification
- `pnpm test` — 104/104 pass (existing registry + local-endpoint tests exercise the resolution paths)
- `pnpm check` — 0 errors; `pnpm build` — succeeds
- Manual against the running app:
  - Cloud model fetch via the server route (OpenAI) → 98 models

author: jspinak
body:
Plan: runner-session-restore-windows-path-shim-fix

Follow-up to the session-restore redesign (#648). **Live production diagnosis on the rebuilt primary** found the deterministic-capture path is not fully engaging: operator sessions are recorded with `origin:"authoritative"` but the recorded ids are largely **phantom** (no matching transcript), and **zero** SessionStart confirmations fire — restore currently leans entirely on the Phase-4 reconcile backstop.

## Honest scoping — what this PR does and does NOT fix

**Fixes (tested):**
- **Unify the runner-launched pinned id.** Direct-command claude spawns (agent-runtime, e.g. `claim:pr:…` sessions) minted a fresh seam id `Q` while claude actually ran under a different explicit `--session-id` `P`, so `Q` was recorded as a phantom. `apply_identity_seam` now **adopts the command's explicit `--session-id`** (`explicit_session_id_from`), so the recorded id == the id claude runs under == the id the hook confirms. Eliminates the phantom for the direct-command class.
- **PATH hardening (defensive).** Inject the shim under the canonical `Path` key on Windows and remove inherited case-variants (`set_child_path`). NOTE: `portable-pty` 0.8.1 already case-folds env keys on Windows (verified against the pinned crate source), so this is **hardening, not the operative fix** — it guards against a future portable-pty that stops folding. (This corrects an earlier hypothesis that a `Path`/`PATH` duplicate was shadowing the shim; it is not, on 0.8.1.)

**Does NOT fix (needs the diagnostic below to pin down):**
- The **account-launcher / typed-into-shell** class (`buildAiLaunchCommand` types `claude --session-id <aiUuid>` into a shell, `TerminalPage.tsx:919`). The mechanism by which these end up phantom / never confirm is **not yet empirically proven** — code-reading alone proved unreliable here, so this PR adds instrumentation instead of guessing.

## Diagnostic beacon (`POST /control/shim-beacon`)
The identity shim now POSTs one fire-and-forget line on **every** invocation — including the don't-double-pin passthrough that sends no session-open — reporting `{terminal_id, tool, user_session_id, settings, pinned}`. The runner logs it (log-only, no store write). After the next primary rebuild, the logs will reveal **empirically** whether the shim runs for organic account launches and whether it delivers `--session-id`/`--settings` — nailing the account-shell class instead of inferring it.

## Verification
- `cargo check` clean; `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` clean on all touched files (the pre-push `--all-targets` trips only on pre-existing lints in unrelated test files — `flywheel_e2e_tests.rs`/`spec_authoring.rs` — which CI's non-`--all-targets` clippy does not gate).
- 23 `terminal::session` tests + the new `shim_beacon_request_parses_full_and_defaults_missing` + `session_open` tests pass; `cargo fmt` clean.
- Built as a release binary and booted on an isolated temp runner (git_sha `2e88b5e9`) — healthy.

## Next step (owner action)
Rebuild the primary from this once merged; the beacon logs then reveal the account-shell truth, and I'll fix that class precisely from evidence.

author: n716739x
body:
Recalibrates the Mean Reversion `scale` from 25 to **12.5**, derived from two live IA-Mean-Reversion chart samples.

## Evidence
Reading (smoothed RSI, Mean-Reversion) pairs off the 4H / regular-hours chart and solving `scale = (RSI − 50) / MR`:

| Ticker | Smoothed RSI | Mean-Rev | Implied scale |
|--------|--------------|----------|---------------|
| MRVL | 48.09 | −0.1491 | 12.81 |
| NVDA | 38.05 | −0.9720 | 12.29 |

- Both straddle **12.5**.
- Raw RSI is ruled out — it gives wildly inconsistent scales (67.7 vs 10.2), while the **smoothed** RSI gives a consistent ~12.5.
- `scale=12.5` maps RSI to a ±4 range, with the ±2 OB/OS bands landing at RSI 75/25.
- The old `scale=25` was provably ~2× too large: MR could never reach the +2 peaks clearly visible on the chart (that would require a smoothed RSI of 100).

Applied consistently across `marketwatch-dev.html`, `index.html`, and `worker.js` so analyzers and dashboard cards stay in agreement.

## Deploy impact
- Frontend (analyzers): redeploys via Netlify on merge.
- Dashboard cards are server-scored, so **`worker.js` needs a manual Cloudflare redeploy** for the cards to reflect the new scale. This is a one-constant change with no DB/binding involvement — unrelated to the prior D1 outage.

body:
A Notion-style wiki after the Grove mock, seeded when the "wiki" template is chosen at repo creation, plus the onboarding and FAB changes it rides in on. ### Wiki template (`wiki.yaml`, worker seed, create-wizard card) Everything is branch data: - **concepts**: `wiki/page` (tree via parent+order), `wiki/block` (typed inline-HTML blocks), `wiki/comment`, `wiki/link` (wikilinks as facts, so backlinks are queries, not HTML parses), plus single-field projections for partial upserts and delete retractions - **commands + rules** for page/block/comment/link mutations; every command reads verb-specific detail attributes (`dom.event.detail/activate` vs `/delete` …) because commands match structurally — a shared attribute would fire sibling rules on the same event - **three web components** (`wiki-tree`, `wiki-editor`, `wiki-panel`) shipped as `component!:` rows: they read invisible `data-row` directory views, build their own DOM, and dispatch CustomEvents wired to commands; the editor covers typing, Enter-split/Backspace-merge, markdown prefixes, slash + `[[` menus, block menu, comments, jump-to-block - empty block text travels as `
` — an empty string reads as "blank = omit" and would silently drop the command Verified end to end in the sealed guest: navigate, create/rename/delete page, block create/edit/turn, comment + resolve, backlinks. ### Onboarding: default new spaces to this sync server Replace the manual "Sync server (optional)" input and "Use this server" button with a hidden `remote` field auto-filled by ``: new spaces default to syncing with this server, falling back to local-only when the URL can't be resolved. Applied to both the Hub onboarding wizard and the FAB create-space modal. Adds the Wiki template card (with preview artwork) alongside Sheets and Blank; the template grid grows 2 → 3 columns. ### FAB: move to lower-right corner Reposition the floating app pill; drop the now-unneeded wiki-tree top inset. --- ## PR-Codex overview This PR introduces a `wiki` template for the `tonk` project, enhancing the application with a wiki-style structure. It adds new functionalities and tests related to the wiki template, alongside some adjustments to existing components and layouts. ### Detailed summary - Added `wiki.yaml` template for a Notion-style wiki. - Introduced `WIKI_LIBRARY` constant for the new template. - Implemented tests for the `wiki` template's functionality. - Modified `index.html` to include the `wiki` template link. - Updated `repository.rs` to handle `WIKI_LIBRARY_URL`. - Adjusted UI components to support the `wiki` template. - Enhanced documentation to describe the new `wiki` features. > The following files were skipped due to too many changes: `rust/tonk-core/assets/library/wiki.yaml` > ✨ Ask PR-Codex anything about this PR by commenting with `/codex {your question}`

author: omersamuk
body:
This PR fixes the M5-S1R gate blockers identified after the exact audit rerun. It adds native StereoMIS manifest validation, enforces the no-depth photometric densification path, generates the canonical train panel artifact, and updates evaluator/dry-run guards so invalid schema workarounds or depth-residual selection cannot pass the M5-S1 gate.

## Official status
- SERV-CT: metric-depth reference / closure benchmark
- StereoMIS: GO — primary real-pose generalization dataset
- M5-S0: PASS
- M5-S1: CONDITIONAL FUNCTIONAL POSITIVE / AUDIT-GATE MARGINAL FAIL
- M5-S1R: INVALID_FOR_GATE / FUNCTIONAL SIGNAL POSITIVE
- M5-S1B: schema/no-depth/panel fix only
- M5-S2: blocked until M5-S1R2 PASS

## Explicit non-scope
- no VM run
- no training run
- no M5-S1R2 rerun
- no hyperparameter ablation
- no M5-S2 design
- no output artifact commit
- no tag

## 1. Branch
m5-s1b-schema-nodepth-panel-fix

## 2. Head commit
6352e2720cedff05729b127dfdeee4eaf1b4f539

## 3. Test result
523 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failures

## 4. Changed files (10)
- surgtwin/data/manifest.py
- scripts/run_m5_s1_stereomis_densify_smoke.sh
- surgtwin/training/uncertainty_trainer.py
- surgtwin/training/densification.py
- scripts/train_uncertainty.py
- scripts/evaluate_m5_s1_stereomis.py
- tests/test_stereomis_manifest_schema_validation.py
- tests/test_m5_s1_no_depth_path.py
- tests/test_evaluate_m5_s1_stereomis.py
- tests/test_m5_s1_panel_artifacts.py

## 5. Schema validation fix
- native StereoMIS manifest validation added
- accepts intrinsics / c2w / w2c schema
- does not require SERV-CT-only K_left/K_right/c2w_left fields for StereoMIS
- validates depth_semantics="none"

## 6. No-depth path fix
- StereoMIS no-depth runs must use gt_depth=None for densification selection

author: briananderson1222
body:
## What

Fixes the trust-ledger defects that made any session which ever recorded a `fail` critique permanently unreconcilable, and that collapsed check/critique identity through the bundle round-trip (catastrophically under `--flow-id`).

### #267 — supersede-by-critique-id
`record-critique` no longer carries every prior write forward unconditionally. The latest write per critique id wins for reconcile/status/validator purposes; each prior **live** write for that id is retained as history (`status: superseded`, first-class `metadata.superseded_by`) but excluded from evaluation. A reviewer recording a resolving pass for a previously-failed id **closes** it.

Supersession is **reviewer-scoped** (anti-gaming): a write may only supersede a prior live critique of the same id written by the **same reviewer**, so a worker cannot bury a reviewer's disputed finding — a cross-reviewer fail stays live and continues to block.

### #282 — first-class `superseded_by` affordance
A resolved session retains historical fail critiques **structurally**. The validator rule ("critique pass cannot include fail members") now tolerates superseded historical fails; only a **live** fail blocks. `trust-reconcile` excludes superseded critique history from evaluation, **scoped to non-`test_output` claims** so a command-backed claim can never launder a real failure by carrying `superseded_by`.

### #268 — lossless, type-stable round-trip
`buildTrustBundle` stamps a stable `metadata.origin` (`check` | `acceptance` | `critique`) and `metadata.check_kind` on every claim. `checksFromBundle` / `critiquesFromBundle` classify by `origin` (authoritative) with legacy claimType fallback, so:
- a critique claim is **never** re-absorbed as a command-less `test_output` check, and
- a session-local check kind **never** flips to `test_output`,

even under `--flow-id`, where check/acceptance/critique all collapse onto one declared claimType. `record-evidence` now **preserves** existing critique claims instead of hardcoding `critiques: []` (which silently dropped the entire finding history).

## Tests (first, as regression repros)
`evals/integration/test_critique_supersession_roundtrip.sh`:
- **(a)** `record-critique` fail→pass (same reviewer) → live state = pass, history retained + superseded, no duplicate claim ids, `trust-reconcile` exits 0.
- **(b) HEADLINE** — a `--flow-id builder.build/verify` session (`ensure-session` → `record-evidence` mixed kinds → `record-critique` → `trust-reconcile`) exits **0**. This exact flow could never converge before.
- **(c)** `record-evidence` after a critique preserves history.
- **(d) ANTI-GAMING** — a different reviewer cannot supersede a reviewer's fail (stays live; reconcile exits 1).
- **(e)** validator tolerates a superseded historical fail, still rejects a live fail.

## Validation
- Anti-gaming & trust suite: **24/24 PASS**
- Static eval suite: PASS; sidecar unit tests: 35/35
- Trust/reconcile/producer integration lanes: green (`test_trust_reconcile`, `test_reconcile_soundness`, `test_flowdef_session_history_preservation`, `test_builder_step_producers`, `test_dual_emit_flow_step`, `test_publish_delivery`, `prove-capture-teeth*`, …)
- Baseline lanes: `validate:source`, `check:content-boundary`, `check:decisions`, `context-map:check` all pass
- Pre-existing environmental failures `test_goal_fit_hook` (1) / `test_goal_fit_escape_hatch` (5) fail identically on clean `origin/main` — not caused by this change.
- **Live dogfood**: a real `--flow-id` session with a critique reconciles at exit 0 (3 commands RECONCILED, critique ATTESTED). Delivery bundle committed.

## Anti-gaming note (documented gap)
Reviewer identity is currently the free-form `--reviewer` string. There is no cryptographic worker-vs-reviewer distinction yet — that lands with the runtime actor-identity slice (#287/#290). Same-reviewer-string scoping is the strongest honest enforcement available today and matches the granularity the critique record already carries.

## Coordination
Work claimed via the repo's liveness selection machinery (`workflow-sidecar liveness claim`) for subjects `kontourai-flow-agents-267/268/282`; liveness stream was empty (no other holder). No overlap with the concurrent actor-identity slice: this PR touches only `workflow-sidecar.ts` trust-bundle producers/round-trip helpers, `validate-workflow-artifacts.ts` critique rule, `trust-reconcile.js`, plus new test + delivery artifacts; it does not modify liveness/actor/assignment-provider code. Does not touch release PR #263.

author: jamierthompson
body:
## What

Retires the test-only mock project machinery and swaps the lorem-ipsum seed dataset for the garden's **real content** — the seven planned entries (5 projects + 2 essays, all honestly `stage: sketch`) plus a real "now" update announcing the launch and the design-engineering job search.

- **Mock purge (#109):** `src/projects/engine-board/` and `src/projects/first-light/` deleted, along with the `sunrise-meter` embed (owner call — nothing renders it and real embeds are coming). `COMPONENT_KEYS` and `EMBED_KEYS` are now both empty; the first real module lands with #70. All key-drift tests reconciled to assert retired keys miss cleanly; falsified doc examples fixed.
- **Schema — let a sketch be a sketch:** `componentKey`/`fontKey` are now required only for a project *past* the sketch stage (`requiredForNonSketchProject`, extracted to `entryValidators.ts` with a full branch-matrix test). `brandColor` stays required for every project — the card plates consume it. A sketch-stage project is real content with no coded module yet; the maturity badge is the honesty signal.
- **Routing fix:** `/[slug]` 404'd any project without a resolvable module — which would have 404'd every sketch entry. A project with **no** `componentKey` now renders prose-only; a *declared-but-unresolvable* key still 404s as drift.
- **CI canary fix:** the published-keys vacuous-green canary hard-coded "any published project has a componentKey", which the relaxation falsified — it would have gone red on the live all-sketch dataset. It now counts only non-sketch projects (`nonSketchProjectCount`), with an all-sketch-garden regression test.

## Why

The seed data was throwaway test fixtures; the site goes public with real content this week. The dataset swap itself already happened in production (owner-approved: 12 lorem docs deleted, 8 real docs published, relaxed schema deployed) — this PR lands the code that makes that data first-class: sketch entries render, the CI nets stay meaningful, and no mock module ships.

## How it was tested

Full gate green on the tip (CI order): lint · lint:css · lint:keys · lint:docs · format:check · typecheck · **1189 tests** · studio typegen with no `sanity.types.ts` drift · build (all 8 slugs prerendered). Published-keys net verified green against live production data (`componentKey=0, entries=8, nonSketchProjects=0`). Route sweep on a clean production build: all 11 routes 200 with real titles, zero mock leftovers, sketch project renders prose-only, backlinks resolve bidirectionally.

## Adversarial QA record (fresh reviewer, no prior context of the build)

**Verdict: SHIP.** Probed and passed:
- **Hypothesized schema hole disproven** — a stage-less published project cannot escape: the validator requires a componentKey whenever `stage !== 'sketch'` (undefined included), and an empirical GROQ probe confirmed `stage != "sketch"` matches null-stage docs, so the canary counts them too.
- **Empty-registry zero boundary** — resolvers return typed NotFound, `EmbedBlock` renders a graceful fallback, `ComponentKey=never` compiles, all key nets behave (no vacuous passes).
- **Live-data audit** — slugs unique + CSS-safe, blurbs under cap, every project has a parseable brandColor, `related` graph bidirectional with zero dangling refs, featuredRank 1–7 gapless.
- **Browser soft-nav pass** (home → cards → detail → browse → now, both color schemes): console error-free, no lorem/mock strings on any rendered route, focus rings visible, keyless sketch project confirmed prose-only in-browser.

**Defect → fix → re-check:** QA's one in-scope finding — the slice's core validator had no regression test — was fixed by extracting both conditional-required validators to `studio/schemaTypes/documents/entryValidators.ts` (type-only imports, zero Sanity runtime) with an 11-case branch matrix, auto-discovered by the root Vitest jsdom project with zero config change. QA re-checked and proved the tests fail on regression by mutating the validator (both directions: lost exemption and over-broad exemption). Loop closed.

**Filed as follow-ups, pre-existing (not introduced here):** #121 soft-404s under the PPR shell (unknown slugs return HTTP 200); RSS ships project-kind entries only (documented design — flagged to the owner since 2 of 7 featured entries are essays); footer link under the 24px target floor (noted for the #120 treatment family).

Closes #109.

author: chelseakr
body:
Add a signed HttpOnly session-cookie flow so a phone/desktop browser (which
can't attach an Authorization header on plain navigation) can reach the
dashboard, without weakening the existing fail-closed bearer-token auth.

- app/auth.py: sign_session/verify_session (stdlib hmac+hashlib HMAC-SHA256,
  keyed by an HMAC of expected_token() over a fixed salt — no new secret or
  config), 12h TTL, constant-time signature comparison, and a pure/testable
  LoginLockoutTracker (5 failures / 15min per IP, reset on success).
- app/server.py: require_auth now accepts a valid Bearer header OR a valid
  stacks_session cookie. GET /login renders an accessible sign-in form
  (label-linked input, skip link, one landmark). POST /login — the one
  deliberate exception to the app's GET-only routes, since a GET query-string
  token would leak into browser history/logs — exchanges the token for a
  signed HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict/Secure cookie and 303-redirects to /;
  failed attempts are rate-limited per client IP, with 429 while locked out.
  GET /logout clears the cookie and redirects to /login.
- pyproject.toml: add python-multipart to the app extra — Starlette's
  Request.form() requires it even for urlencoded (non-multipart) bodies.
- tests/test_auth.py: sign/verify round trip, tampered/expired-cookie
  rejection, the lockout tracker in isolation, and the full browser flow via
  FastAPI's TestClient (login sets cookie -> dashboard access, logout clears
  it -> 401, lockout -> 429), plus a Bearer-header regression check.
- docs/ideation/02-large-scale-fixes.md: mark FIX-04 done with an
  implementation summary.

The TLS assumption behind Secure is documented in app/auth.py's module
docstring: the cookie is only ever sent over HTTPS, so deployment must
terminate TLS in front of the app or otherwise ensure the browser reaches it
only over a secure/loopback channel.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: dgriffith
body:
Closes #959. First step of the packaging epic #958 — a signed DMG is shippable on its own.

## Problem

`release.yml` ran `pnpm build` with only `NODE_OPTIONS` in its env, so `forge.config.ts` took its unsigned path (`wantSign` is false without creds). The CI DMG was unsigned + un-notarized → Gatekeeper-quarantined on any other Mac.

## What changed

- **New "Prepare macOS signing" step** (before build): imports the Developer ID Application cert into a throwaway keychain and adds it to the search list so `codesign` / `find-identity` can see it; decodes the App Store Connect `.p8`; exports `APPLE_API_KEY` / `APPLE_API_KEY_ID` / `APPLE_API_ISSUER` via `$GITHUB_ENV`. The existing build step then takes forge's already-wired signed + notarized + stapled path.
- **Gated** on a `HAS_SIGNING` env flag (`secrets` can't be referenced in a step `if:` directly). A secretless run — e.g. a fork — still builds, just unsigned.
- **Cleanup step** (`if: always()`) removes the keychain and staged key so signing material never lingers on a reused runner.
- Refreshed the stale "builds are UNSIGNED" header comment.

## ⚠️ Action required before this signs anything

Add these repo secrets (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions):

| Secret | How to produce |
|---|---|
| `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64` | `base64 -i DeveloperIDApp.p12` |
| `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | the `.p12` export password |
| `APPLE_API_KEY_BASE64` | `base64 -i AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8` |
| `APPLE_API_KEY_ID` | the key's 10-char Key ID |
| `APPLE_API_ISSUER` | App Store Connect Issuer ID (UUID) |

## Verification (per issue acceptance — needs the secrets + a run)

- `workflow_dispatch` run → download the DMG →
  - `spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature <dmg>` passes
  - `codesign -dv --verbose=4` on the mounted `.app` shows the Developer ID
  - opens on a *different* Apple-Silicon Mac, **offline** (staple works)

I can't run these from here — no access to the secrets or a second Mac — so leaving the boxes for you. The workflow YAML validates and follows the standard temp-keychain pattern.

author: orangepeachpink
body:
Refs #577, #567, #565, #486. ADR-0023 v2 §3.

## What this does

#565's ambient line renders interior temp/RH + tag; #567 completed the pressure **data plane** but nothing displayed it. This renders the **exterior-family** pressure quantity, keeping ADR-0023 v2's two-family separation visible in the UI.

- **`build_context`**: a `pressure` field on the sensor dict, populated only when the last reading carries **both** `pressure_context_hpa` and `pressure_context_source` — the same value+tag-together honesty as the interior ambient block, kept **separate** from it.
- **template**: a `pressure` meta line tagged **"· exterior"**, visibly distinct from the interior ambient tag — a reader sees temp/RH come from the plant's own air, pressure from outside (the ADR-0023 §3 physics). Uses only the existing `muted` class — **no new design token invented**.
- **Honest-empty** inherited from the data plane: when the pressure cache ages out (#567's staleness bound) the fill writes nothing → `pressure` stays `None` → the line doesn't render. Offline = blank, never stale-presented-as-fresh.

## Independent of #572's merge

The render reads only **already-merged** parse properties: `pressure_context_hpa` (CANONICAL column) and `pressure_context_source` (payload property, on `main` since #565 — not #567). So a row renders pressure whenever its data carries it, however produced — this slice doesn't stack on the still-open #572.

## On the #575 binding

The #575 Multi-Device Dashboard spec defines the per-device card **grouping** (that's the separate #486 grouping build), but **no** pressure/exterior treatment. Rather than invent a token, I marked pressure exterior with plain existing markup and **flag Design**: if a dedicated exterior-family color/token is wanted, that's an optional follow-up. When the grouping build lands, this line moves under the device-header chrome with it (it's on the same card meta).

## Evidence

- **300 passed (4 new)**: tagged pressure reaches the card; an untagged pressure value never renders (same no-untagged-display fence as interior); a pre-#567 log exposes `None`; interior + pressure render **independently**, each with its own tag (the two families never merge into one display).
- Verified the rendered JSON payload end-to-end (a real `dashboard.py` render — ambient + pressure both present, correctly shaped). The template `add()` structurally mirrors the already-browser-verified #562 ambient line.
- Note: the preview harness is bound to the main repo, not this worktree, so a live browser screenshot wasn't cleanly reachable without polluting main — verification was via the rendered payload + unit tests.
- `ruff` clean.

author: suthinxn
body:
## Summary
- **ระบบจัดการ Catalog (Master Data ในคลังสินค้า) พัฒนาขึ้นมาใน 3 ส่วนหลัก:**
  1. **Master Category (หมวดหมู่สิ่งของ):** ระบบจัดเก็บและจำแนกประเภทของสินค้า/สิ่งของที่อยู่ในคลัง (เช่น ยารักษาโรค, เครื่องนุ่งห่ม, เครื่องนอน)
  2. **Item Master (รายการสิ่งของหลัก):** ระบบจัดการรายละเอียดสิ่งของหลัก การจัดหมวดหมู่ การแปลงหน่วย UOM (Unit of Measure) การตั้งค่าสิทธิ์ต่อหัว และการระบุกลุ่มเป้าหมายผู้รับตามมาตรฐาน Sphere Standard
  3. **Recipe (สูตรอาหารมาตรฐาน):** สูตรอาหารอ้างอิงวัตถุดิบและส่วนประกอบ (Ingredients) จาก Item Master พร้อมกำหนดจำนวน Portions (สัดส่วนการผลิต) และระยะเวลาการจัดเตรียมเสร็จสิ้น

## Reason
- เพื่อเป็นระบบฐานข้อมูลหลัก (Master Data) สำหรับบริหารจัดการคลังสินค้าและทรัพยากรส่วนกลางของศูนย์พักพิง (Smart Shelter)
- เพื่อให้สามารถคำนวณการใช้ทรัพยากรและปริมาณความต้องการเบิกจ่ายวัตถุดิบ/สินค้าล่วงหน้าได้อย่างถูกต้องตามมาตรฐานบรรเทาทุกข์

## Impact
- **UI:** เพิ่มเมนูตั้งค่าและแคตตาล็อกที่เส้นทาง `/back-office/catalog` โดยแยกการทำงานออกเป็น 3 แท็บบนหน้าจอ
- **API/Feature:** นำ TanStack Query Hooks และระบบ Live Query เข้าไปเชื่อมโยงใน `+layout.svelte` เพื่อให้ข้อมูลมีการอัปเดตแบบเรียลไทม์ข้ามแท็บการใช้งาน
- **Database:** เริ่มใช้งานฐานข้อมูล PouchDB แยกเฉพาะชื่อ `catalog` เพื่อเก็บแคตตาล็อก

## Database
- **CouchDB Schema & Doc Type:** ใช้งานเอกสาร 3 ประเภทภายใต้คีย์หลัก `{type}:{ulid}` ได้แก่:
  * `item_category` (เก็บโครงสร้างหมวดหมู่สิ่งของ)
  * `item_master` (เก็บโครงสร้างสินค้าหลัก, อัตราแปลงหน่วย UOM, อัตราการแจกจ่าย, และข้อจำกัดทางเป้าหมาย)
  * `recipe` (เก็บโครงสร้างสูตรอาหารมาตรฐานและส่วนประกอบวัตถุดิบอ้างอิง Item Master)
- **Transform & Provisioning:** มีการระบุคำสั่งซิงค์ PouchDB สำหรับฐานข้อมูล `catalog` เพิ่มเข้ามาใน layout หลักของเว็บเพื่อทำ Replication
  
## Spec/UI

author: bryanfawcett
body:
## Summary

Four independent onboarding/UX bugs, each investigated and root-caused separately:

- **Random location instead of the user's actual location** — the IP-geo fast path (`GET /api/py/geo?autoCreate=false`, used by the home page's server-side detection) called `find_nearest_location(lat, lon, max_km=20_000)` — effectively unbounded. A coarse/wrong IP-derived lat/lon would therefore always match *some* seed location, even one on another continent, and `HomeLanding` would auto-redirect there within 2 seconds. Capped to `150km` (roughly IP-geolocation accuracy) so a genuinely distant "nearest" match now falls through to the city chooser instead of silently mislabeling the user.

- **No welcome screen** — `WeatherDashboard` called `completeOnboarding()` on mount for *every* first-time visitor and never rendered `<WelcomeBanner>` anywhere, so the fully-built banner component was permanently dead code. It's now rendered inline (it self-gates on `hasOnboarded`), with its "Personalise" action wired to the My Weather modal — which already calls `completeOnboarding()` on Done/Apply.

- **AI not working (stuck on caching)** — fallback text (no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, an open circuit breaker, or an Anthropic API error) was cached with the *exact same* tiered TTL (up to 2 hours) as a real Claude-generated summary. One transient failure therefore served the generic fallback for up to 2 hours per location. Cached docs now carry a `source: "ai" | "fallback"` tag, and fallback responses get a 60s TTL so real generation is retried almost immediately after recovery.

- **Activities always show "fair"** — the client-side RxDB offline cache persisted each suitability rule's `conditions` but silently dropped its `fallback` rating, and a cache-freshness bug stamped "now" as the fetch time on every page load — so once a device had any cached copy (even an incomplete one), it always looked fresh and the missing field was never restored from the network. Every rule with no matching condition therefore hit the hardcoded generic "fair" rating. Schema bumped to v1 (`fallback` now persisted; a migration drops incomplete v0 docs so they get re-fetched), and cache freshness now tracks the actual fetch timestamp instead of read time.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 1962 tests passing
- [x] `python -m pytest tests/py/ -v` — 920 tests passing (1 new test added)
- [x] `npm run lint` — 0 errors (pre-existing warnings only, unrelated to this diff)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npm run build` — compiles and generates all pages successfully
- [x] Added/updated tests for each fix: geolocation radius cap, welcome banner rendering, AI fallback TTL/source tagging, suitability RxDB schema migration + cache freshness

author: robertobasile84
body:
## The bug (found by a fresh-user dry run)

Running the published stack as a stranger would (`cp .env.example .env && docker compose up -d`), the collector crash-looped:

```
RuntimeError: token request failed (400): invalid_client / Client not found
```

`.env.example` shipped **placeholder** credentials (`HUSQVARNA_CLIENT_ID=your-application-key`) even though the comment said "leave blank to stay in DEMO mode". Non-empty values make the collector attempt the real API instead of demo mode.

## The fix

Ship `HUSQVARNA_CLIENT_ID` / `HUSQVARNA_CLIENT_SECRET` **blank**, so copying the example verbatim runs in demo mode. Verified: with blank creds the collector logs `falling back to DEMO mode` and the dashboard fills with synthetic data.

author: jonathancrawford05
body:
## What
Adds `AssumptionSet.valuation_mortality: MortalityTable | None = None` — a prescribed statutory valuation mortality table (e.g. 2001 CSO) that the statutory reserve bases value on. When set, CRVM and the VM-20 NPR floor value on the prescribed table on both TermLife and WholeLife (WL to the valuation table's own omega); the statutory valuation q is static (the improvement scale is never applied) and carries per-policy substandard rating. `NET_PREMIUM` and the VM-20 deterministic reserve (anticipated experience by definition) always stay on the projection best-estimate assumptions. Default `None` reproduces today's behaviour byte-identically. ADR-125.

**Also included (review P2, folded in at maintainer direction):** the per-(sex, smoker) masked mortality lookup is now single-source — `BaseProduct._lookup_qx_column` with per-engine cached `_sex_smoker_masks` — replacing all six former copies (Term projection + statutory builders, WL projection + valuation builders, UL and Disability mortality builders). Pure refactor, verified byte-identical (empty byte-level golden JSON diff pre- vs post-refactor); the GAAP slices will call the helper instead of adding a copy.

## Why
Selected from PRODUCT_DIRECTION_2026-06-18.md — **IMPORTANT** ("Statutory valuation mortality table (2001 CSO) for CRVM", ADR-089 Out of scope). Exact reproduction of a cedant's US statutory CRVM reserve — the point of the reserve-basis epic — requires valuing on the prescribed table, not the pricing basis.

Slice 1 of 4 — this PR **opens the new active Epic** `docs/PLAN_reserve_basis_exactness.md` / `docs/CONTINUATION_reserve_basis_exactness.md` (2001 CSO valuation table + GAAP FAS 60 basis), started per the active-epic rule: all prior epics (A1–A3, C0 Asset/ALM, B3) are COMPLETE as of PR #123.

**Core-contract note (flagged for human review):** this adds an optional field to `AssumptionSet`. The default `None` preserves backward compatibility on every path (all 1925 pre-existing tests green, goldens byte-identical).

## Changes
- `src/polaris_re/assumptions/assumption_set.py` — `valuation_mortality` field
- `src/polaris_re/products/base_product.py` — shared `_lookup_qx_column` + cached `_sex_smoker_masks`
- `src/polaris_re/products/term_life.py` — `_valuation_q` / `_build_statutory_valuation_q`; CRVM + VM-20 NPR dispatch; builders use the shared lookup
- `src/polaris_re/products/whole_life.py` — table-parametrised `_build_valuation_mortality` / `_valuation_months_to_omega`; CRVM wiring; builders use the shared lookup
- `src/polaris_re/products/universal_life.py`, `src/polaris_re/products/disability.py` — mortality builders use the shared lookup (pure refactor)
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md` (ADR-125 incl. shared-helper bullet), PLAN/CONTINUATION (new), session log

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `types.ts` | The local `Artist`/`Song`/`Project`/`Release` view-model interfaces (previously inlined in ArtistPage), imported by page + tabs. |

| `ReleasesTab.tsx` | Releases tab (upcoming + released). |
| `AnalyticsTab.tsx` | Analytics tab (streams tables). |
| `ManagementTab.tsx` | Management tab (relationship, quick actions). |

The shell (`ArtistPage.tsx`, now 361 lines) keeps the two data-loading `useEffect`s, the loading/error early returns, and the derived values. Derived values (`avgQuality`, `archetypeInfo`, `moodStatus`, `insights`) are now wrapped in `useMemo` and the child callbacks (`handleArtistMeeting`, `handleNavigateToArtist`, `handleToggleExpand`) in `useCallback`. These were hoisted above the early returns to respect the Rules of Hooks and null-guarded on `artist`.

Removed unused `analytics`, `qualityFilter`, `sortBy` state (declared, never applied to any filter/sort/render). Also dropped the now-dead `getTotalMarketingCost` helper and dead `totalStreams`/`totalRevenue`/`releasedSongs` locals surfaced during extraction, and pruned unused imports. Zero behavior change.

## Avatar-crop block untouched

The avatar overlay `<div className="absolute -top-40 -right-20 z-10 h-56 overflow-hidden">` with its coupled clip-height math (and the explanatory inline comment) and the surrounding Tabs header were left verbatim in the shell. No wrapper hierarchy around it was changed.

Added `@testing-library/react` render smoke tests (jsdom, no DB) for each extracted tab under `client/src/components/artist/__tests__/` (shared `testFixtures.ts`; `ArtistCard`/`ReleaseWorkflowCard` stubbed). 12 tests, all passing. author: bobinska-dev
body:
## What & why

The Studio **Review changes** pane failed to render diffs for `richTable` fields (SYS-168): with no custom `diff` component, Studio's generic field differ walks the deeply nested `rows → cells → Portable Text` structure and can throw, blanking the diff behind an error card.

This registers a custom `diff` component on the `richTable` type (inherited by `richTableBlock`) that renders a readable, self-contained before/after grid.

## Highlights

- **Grid diff mirroring the editor**: empty corner, `A/B/C…` column headers, `1/2/3…` row labels; real titles shown when set (old title struck through when changed).
- **Structural detection**: rows aligned by `_key`, columns by `columnHeaders[]._key`; add / remove / **move** detected. Moves use an LCS so a deletion doesn't falsely flag shifted siblings.
- **Cell content diff**: old → new text per changed cell; empty cells render blank.
- **Click to inspect**: any cell opens a dialog with the full before/after text and the raw Portable Text JSON — useful for image / custom-block cells whose plain-text label looks unchanged.
- **Summary badges**: rows/columns reported only when wholly added/removed/moved; content edits reported as “cells changed”.
- **Robustness**: the diff model never throws; an error boundary falls back to a safe message. Also fixes the `richTableRow` preview crash (`cells.length` on rows without cells) — the original SYS-168 throw.

## Scope / follow-up

Native **inline Portable Text diff** inside cells (word-level highlighting via Sanity's `ChangeList`) is intentionally left as a follow-up for the Sanity **v6** line (tracked in SYS-181's description). The diff API is identical across v5/v6, so v6 is the right place to build it against the shipping `@portabletext/editor` v7 stack.

## Testing

- `pnpm test` — 225 pass (new: model add/remove/move/title cases; render + click-to-inspect).
- `pnpm lint` — clean; `pnpm build` (`pkg-utils --strict --check`) — passes; pre-commit `tsc --build` — passes.
- Manually verified in the dev studio: grid renders, coordinates map to the editor, deleted/added/moved rows & columns show, and the cell inspector opens with raw content.

Base: `main` (v5 / 1.x line) — flows forward into the v6 branch via the existing merges.

body:
## Summary

`AgentFieldClient` built its default `async_config` with `AsyncConfig()`, which ignores the `AGENTFIELD_ASYNC_*` environment overrides that `Agent` already honors. This initializes the default from `AsyncConfig.from_environment()` so client-level async behavior (timeouts, event stream, poll intervals, etc.) can be tuned via env vars, while any explicitly passed `async_config` is preserved unchanged.

`from_environment()` starts from `AsyncConfig()` defaults and only overrides fields when the corresponding env var is set (falling back to the default on unparseable values), so this is fully backward-compatible for callers that set no env vars.

Fixes #621.

## Changes

- `sdk/python/agentfield/client.py` — default `async_config` now uses `AsyncConfig.from_environment()`.

Supersedes **#632** (original change by @liuzemei / neooosky). That PR is approved by the maintainer but stuck on an outstanding CLA signature from an unsigned committer. Re-authored here so it can land cleanly; thanks to the original authors for the fix.

body:
Follow-up to ADA-387 (which shipped only the weekly deadline). Adds the monthly analogue end-to-end.

## What
- **Config (v10→v11)** — `monthlyDeadlineDay` (Nth working day of the *following* month, default 3) + `monthlyDeadlineTime` (default 18:00). New normalizer clamps the ordinal to 1–20 and reuses the `HH:MM` validator; `normalizeConfig` fills defaults for pre-v11 blobs; migration note added.
- **`computeMonthlyDeadline(year, month, nthWorkingDay, time)`** in `onTimeStatus.ts` — the Nth weekday (Mon–Fri) of the month after the reported one, handling weekend skips and Dec→Jan rollover. Pure + tested.
- **Monthly Reports view** — the snapshot shows *"Timesheets due by <date>"*, and `OverviewTable` derives a **per-member on-time badge** against the cutoff.
- **Settings** — a *"Monthly deadline"* control in Reports Scope paralleling the weekly one (working-day select + time), wired through `SettingsForm`.

## Design note
The monthly aggregate carries no per-worklog timing, so *"met by the deadline"* reads as **on-time** (there's no false *"late"*) — the weekly RAG history stays the finer-grained signal. Badges ride the green/amber/red completeness ramp, **never** the ember brand accent (brand rule). **Field parity kept** — this only *adds* fields.

## Testing
`computeMonthlyDeadline` (offset, weekend skip, year rollover, sub-1 clamp), config defaults + normalizer bounds, and the ScopeSection control (working-day + time binding). Full suite: **no new failures** (1072 pass); typecheck + biome clean.

Closes ADA-549.

body: Fixes following issues: Prefix match: Open-tag search for (e.g. were treated as nesting opens because / is a valid name terminator. Fixed by detecting /> and skipping without incrementing depth. Empty tag UB: s_load_node_decl read ptr[(size_t)-1] on input <>. Fixed with a len == 0 early-return. CDATA/comment/PI handling: Both the child-scan loop (aws_xml_node_traverse) and the close-tag search (s_advance_to_closing_tag) treated , , and as element tags. Fixed by detecting and skipping them in both paths. This prevents false close-tag matches inside CDATA and false open-tag matches inside comments. O(N²) on nested same-name elements: The inner open-tag search scanned the entire remaining document when no opens existed before the close tag. Fixed by limiting the search region to bytes before the found close tag. Boundary condition: When an open-tag match filled exactly the remaining search region with no byte after it, the name-terminator check was skipped. Fixed by treating boundary matches as non-matches.
