author: grzanka
body:
Closes #228 — the three cleanups collected from the "Quick review from Niels/Codex." approval on #217. All non-functional: comments, docs, and one mechanical ternary rewrite. No behavior change.

## Why

#217 (periodic & on-demand partial-result dumps) merged with an APPROVE plus three small review nits worth tidying in a follow-up. This is that follow-up.

## What

1. **`src/apps/osh/osh_signals.c` — soften the SIGUSR1 read-and-clear comments.**
   The two comments claimed exactly-one-dump-per-signal ("so one signal yields exactly one dump", "never lost for good"). That overstates what the code guarantees:
   - a `SIGUSR1` delivered after `if (g_dump)` reads true but before `g_dump = 0` is cleared and lost, not deferred to the next poll;
   - standard (non-realtime) POSIX signals coalesce, so N rapid signals need not yield N dumps.

   Reworded both to best-effort / edge-trigger semantics. This is fine for a dump-and-continue hint — the user re-signals, and a scheduled cadence bounds latency.

2. **`src/apps/osh/osh_run.c` — replace the ternaries this PR introduced with explicit `if`/`else`,** per DEVELOPER.md **§7.2** (which landed on `main` after #217 branched and asks that *new* non-macro ternaries be treated as review findings). The two touched sites are the periodic-dump report source labels (`--dump-every-primaries`/`NSTAT step`, `--dump-every`/`DUMPEVERY`) and the saturated shadow-footprint calc. Scoped to the newly-added ternaries only — §7.2 explicitly does not want a tree-wide sweep of pre-existing ones.

3. **Soften "can never OOM mid-run" → "budgeted up front"** across `osh_run.c`, `src/transport/osh_run_control.h`, `docs/user/command-line.md`, and `docs/dev/architecture.md`. The shadow is only *reserved against the budget* up front; it still allocates lazily at the first dump and fails soft under external memory pressure, so the absolute claim was inaccurate.

## Testing

- `cmake --build --preset debug` — warning-free.
- Focused suite from the review, all green:
  ```
  ctest --test-dir build_debug -R "unit::(test_osh_run_control|test_osh_signals|test_osh_cli|test_osh_checkpoint_policy|test_osh_run_dump|test_osh_simulation)$|unit::cli::help" --output-on-failure
  ```
  `test_osh_run_dump` (periodic-dump report + shadow-reservation accounting) and `test_osh_signals` (SIGUSR1 edge trigger) cover the changed lines.
- `clang-format --dry-run --Werror` clean on all changed C/H files.

author: shubochandrosarker
body:
## Summary

Closes **3 correctness gaps** from the Phase-10 audit doc in one PR:

1. **Shooter Insights** → real data instead of hard-coded segments.
2. **AI Insights** — Approve / Dismiss buttons are functional.
3. **Business Gaps** — "Create task" button is functional.

New `/tasks` page centralises every operator work item (AI-insight approvals + business-gap tasks + BridGistic-created tasks + manual tasks) so the operator has one place to work them.

## 1. Customer segments

- **`Providers\Segments_Provider`** — computes 7 segments against real Woo + Memberistic + Booking tables:
  - range regulars (≥ 2 lane bookings / 30d)
  - CCW graduates (completed CCW class)
  - **ammo bulk buyers** (WC line-item name matches `N rd` pattern, sums ≥ 1000rd over 60d)
  - Ladies Tuesday attendees (last 90d)
  - members expired 30-90d (win-back)
  - first-time last 14d
  - lapsed 90d
  Plus scalars: known shooters, repeat rate, first-time this month, lapsed 90d.
  Each subquery falls back to `0` when its source table is absent — payload shape stays stable.
- **New REST route**: `GET /analytics/shooter-insights` (2 min transient cache).
- **Dashboard `ShooterInsights`** page swaps its hard-coded segments for the live payload.

## 2. Tasks store

- **`Tasks\Tasks_Store`** — persistent `{ id → task }` in `g2aba_tasks`, capped at 500 with resolved/dismissed entries evicted first so **open tasks are never silently displaced**. `task_*` ids, `open → done | dismissed` state machine, terminal-state protection.
- Tracks **source** (`ai_insight` / `business_gap` / `bridgistic` / `manual`) and `sourceId` so the queue shows why each task exists.
- **Migrates legacy Phase-6 `g2aba_bridgistic_tasks`** option on read.
- **`REST\Tasks_Controller`**:
  - `GET /tasks?status=open`
  - `POST /tasks` (admin, manual create)
  - `POST /tasks/{id}/resolve`
  - `POST /tasks/{id}/dismiss`
- `BridGistic\Executor::handle_create_task` now writes via `Tasks_Store` instead of the ad-hoc option — one queue for everything.

## 3. Insight decisions

- **`Tasks\Insight_Decisions`** — records approve / dismiss per insight id in `g2aba_insight_decisions`. `Insights_Controller::list` applies these before responding so **dismissed insights disappear** and **approved insights carry `converted=true` + `taskId`** for the frontend.
- **`REST\Insights_Controller`**:
  - `POST /ai/insights/{id}/approve` (admin) — creates a task with `source=ai_insight`, records the decision + audit entry, returns the task.
  - `POST /ai/insights/{id}/dismiss` — records the decision + audit entry.
- **`REST\Gaps_Controller`**:
  - `POST /insights/business-gaps/{id}/create-task` (admin) — recomputes the gap list, finds the gap by id, creates a task with `source=business_gap` + `owner` from the gap, audit logs.

## 4. Dashboard

- `api.ts` — `analytics.shooterInsights`, `insights.approve/dismiss`, `gapActions.createTask`, `tasks.list/create/resolve/dismiss`. New `Task`, `ShooterInsights` types.
- **New sidebar item** under System group: **Tasks**.
- **AI Insights** — real approve + dismiss; optimistic update; converted cards show "**Converted to task task_… — Track it in Tasks**."
- **Business Gaps** — Create task POSTs the endpoint; per-row optimistic state shows the created task id.
- **Shooter Insights** — full rewrite consuming `/analytics/shooter-insights`. Fallback copy when opportunity list is empty.
- New `Tasks` page with Open / All filter, `open → resolve | dismiss` actions, and source + status pills per row.

## Tests

**204 PHPUnit tests / 455 assertions, all passing.**

New coverage:

- **`Segments_Provider::compose_opportunities`** — singular vs plural on shooters, zero-segments omitted, all-4 nonzero produces the full list in order.
- **`Tasks_Store`** — create persists + generates `task_*` id, open filters terminals, resolve stamps + refuses double-resolve, dismiss is terminal, `normalize_source`, `counts_by_source`, legacy Phase-6 option migration.
- **`Insight_Decisions`** — apply hides dismissed, marks approved with `taskId`, leaves undecided untouched, reset clears, apply skips entries without id.
- **`Insights_Controller::compose_task_body`** — includes every present field, skips missing.
- **`Gaps_Controller::compose_body`** — label + ordering, skips empty fields.

Phase-6 `ExecutorTest` updated: task now lives in `Tasks_Store`'s `g2aba_tasks` with `source=bridgistic`.

Dashboard `vite build` clean (656 kB / 186 kB gzip).

## Test plan

- [ ] Activate on staging. Load the dashboard's Shooter Insights page → confirm numbers reflect real bookings + orders + members (or all zeros if no data yet).
- [ ] Load AI Insights. Click Approve on any insight → confirm the card flips to "Converted to task …". Visit Tasks → the new task is at the top with `ai_insight` source.

author: jsv4
body:
## What

Closes the DocxDiff header/footer comparison gap: header/footer differences were **silently ignored** — the output carried the LEFT document's parts verbatim, `accept(Compare(l,r))` did not reproduce the right's headers, and nothing was reported in revisions or the edit script. DocxDiff now compares header/footer **stories** the way Word Compare does (its default-on "Headers and footers" granularity), gated by **`DocxDiffSettings.CompareHeadersFooters` (default `true`)**.

## How

- **Word-faithful story pairing.** Stories pair per (section ordinal × occurrence kind) over each side's *effective* story grid — explicit `w:headerReference`/`w:footerReference` plus Word's previous-section inheritance rule — never by positional part order (`hdr1` labels aren't stable across files). The reader now records each part's section references (`IrHeaderFooterRef`).
- **Edit script + JSON.** New `IrEditScript.HeaderFooterOps` (`IrHeaderFooterDiff`, reusing `IrEditOp`); additive `headerFooterOps` array in `GetEditScriptJson` (omitted when empty — earlier scripts serialize byte-identically).
- **Native markup inside the parts.** Matched stories rebuild with fine per-word `w:ins`/`w:del` via the shared block-op dispatch (shared revision-id counter; per-part media/hyperlink relationship import — rels are part-scoped). Right-only stories become a fresh part + typed reference with `w:titlePg`/`w:evenAndOddHeaders` ensured; left-only stories are marked deleted (part + reference stay; accept leaves an empty story — Word's own behavior, empty ≡ absent). **The round-trip contract (`accept ≡ right`, `reject ≡ left`) now extends to header/footer scopes**, enforced corpus-wide by the renderer battery's new story projection.
- **Revisions.** `Fine` reports hdr/ftr-anchored revisions (`p:hdr1:…`) appended after notes; `WmlComparerCompatible` excludes them (its contract is the legacy comparer's revision set, which has none) — so the 179-count parity scoreboard holds by construction. The differential harness filters hdr/ftr revisions with the oracle-cannot-produce rationale (the WC004 pair's real footer change otherwise drops Match, for reporting a change the oracle drops).
- **Wire.** `compareHeadersFooters` in the Ops settings JSON (both bridges) + npm/python types. Default-on needs no client change.
- **Inspector.** `headersFooters` catalog entry → `Covered`; `revisionsInInput` text updated (the verbatim carry-over leak now applies to *unchanged* stories only).

## v1 ceilings (documented + pinned)

Sections pair by ordinal; sectPr/settings visibility flags are ensured, not `w:sectPrChange`-tracked; unreferenced parts aren't compared; **`Consolidate` does not merge header/footer scopes** — `IrCompositeMerger` forces the scope off (explicit, deterministic, pinned by test; follow-on = `MergeHeaderFooterScopes` mirroring `MergeNoteScopes`).

## Proof (smoke)

`DocxDiffHeaderFooterSmokeTests`:
- **Synthetic battery** — edited default header, edited PAGE-field footer (field plumbing intact), untouched first-page header (verbatim), added even footer (`evenAndOddHeaders` ensured): markup in the right parts, per-story accept/reject round-trip via the client byte primitives, hdr/ftr revisions (Fine) + none (compatible), `headerFooterOps` JSON, `OpenXmlValidator` clean on redline/accepted/rejected.
- **Real corpus pair** — `WC004-Large` ↔ `WC004-Large-Mod` (the corpus' one differing footer, previously silent): ftr-anchored revisions now surface; footer round-trips; no new schema errors.
- **Headless LibreOffice render oracle** (`tools/diffharness/lo/lo_headerfooter_check.py`, soft-skips when unavailable): an independent renderer surfaces "Draft 2"/"(Reviewed)"/"Even-page" on the accepted view and "Draft 1" (with "Reviewed" absent) on the rejected view — all four oracle runs green locally.

## Tests

Full .NET suite **2553 passed / 0 failed** (3 usual manual skips); differential ratchet (96/66 floors), markup scoreboard (39), parity scoreboard (179/179/Deviation==0), revisionsInInput pins, composite suites all green; Release build warning-clean (library + tests; the WASM project needs the `wasm-tools` workload not installed locally and has no changes here).

author: jomcgi
body:
Implements Phase 3 of ADR 036 (orchestrator brief-compiler tier) and prepares the live rollout. Builds on the merged Phase 1 (OpenRouter client) and Phase 2 (baked context bundle).

## Task 3.1 - Telemetry table
- Migration `20260703210000_chat_orchestrator_brief.sql` and the `OrchestratorBrief` SQLModel per spec section 5 (id, created_at, thread_id, model, route, brief_json, directive_version, latency_ms, prompt/completion/cached tokens, error).
- `route` CHECK IN ('chat','goose','failopen') is mirrored in `__table_args__`; DB-level route-CHECK tests added. `brief_json` uses the JSONB-with-sqlite-JSON variant so `create_all` builds cleanly in tests.

## Task 3.2 - Orchestrator module (`chat/orchestrator.py`, TDD)
- `assemble_prompt`: byte-deterministic. `system` = baked bundle + versioned channel directive; `user` = volatile tail (KG results, channel context, request). No volatile data in `system`, so the provider prefix cache hits across consecutive escalations.
- `parse_brief`: strict-JSON, route-partitioned. `goose` -> `Brief`; `chat` -> `ChatVerdict` carrying `reply_guidance` (context + direction required, redirect optional). Unknown keys tolerated; missing required keys for the active route raise a typed error the caller turns into fail-open. A `repo` outside the invoker's ADR 029 scopes is discarded and flagged, then replaced by the invoker scope in `compile`.
- `compile`: checks `enabled()` then the `orchestrator` consent grant FIRST (no client call, no key read, no telemetry row when disabled/ungranted, per spec section 1). Otherwise calls the client once and writes exactly one telemetry row per path (goose/chat/failopen). Timeout, HTTP error, and parse failure all fail open.
- Tests cover: ungranted -> no call/no row; disabled -> no call/no row; happy goose; happy chat; timeout -> failopen row; parse-failure -> failopen row; repo-out-of-scope replacement.

## Task 3.3 - Flow wiring (`chat/bot.py` `start_agent_flow`)
The **flow-wiring refactor**: `start_agent_flow` now runs the orchestrator verdict up front and returns an `AgentFlowOutcome(thread | chat_reply)` instead of a bare `Thread | None`. This keeps the method surface-agnostic (it produces the reply, callers post it), matching its existing "caller owns origin-channel acks" contract.
- **chat**: no thread, no session, no checklist. Reply authored by local Qwen via `conversational_agent_reply(channel_id, summary=raw prompt, details=reply_guidance block, llm_call=build_llm_caller())`. Raw prompt stays ground truth; a `redirect` never itself submits a session.
- **goose**: opens the session thread as today, seeds the guest with `render_brief(brief) + raw prompt`, and pre-renders the checklist from `brief.stages` (synthetic all-pending `Progress` through `render_checklist`).
- **failopen**: byte-for-byte today's behaviour (direct submit of the raw prompt). `_orchestrator_verdict` short-circuits to FailOpen when the tier is disabled, so the disabled/failopen path does no extra gathering (no directive seeding, no context fetch).
- `start_agent_session` gains a `task` kwarg so the submitted task (brief + prompt) can differ from the transcript/echo, which keep the raw prompt. Both callers (`/agent` slash command and the mention/ambient engage) updated to post `chat_reply` or announce the thread.

## Task 3.4 - Secret-source correction, chart bump, live enable
- **Secret-source correction (please note):** the task brief said to point at `{fullname}-goosecracker`, but the goosecracker OnePasswordItem syncs into a Secret named literally **`goosecracker`** (not fullname-prefixed, because the fc-agentd egress sidecar references it by that exact name). The deployment `secretKeyRef.name` is therefore `goosecracker`, `key: OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `optional: true`, gated on `orchestrator.enabled`. The redundant `onepassworditem-orchestrator.yaml` is deleted and `orchestrator.onepassword` removed from values. Render confirmed: the orchestrator env references the `goosecracker` Secret and no `-orchestrator` OnePasswordItem renders.
- **orchestrator.enabled: true** in `deploy/values.yaml`.
- **Chart bump 0.265.1 -> 0.266.0** (Chart.yaml + `application.yaml` targetRevision). Note: main had already advanced to 0.265.1, past the brief's assumed 0.264.0, so I bumped to the next free minor 0.266.0 rather than 0.265.0.
- **Consent grant (seeded, in-repo):** grants are seeded in-repo by `acl.bootstrap_defaults()` (called from `app/main.py` on startup), the same mechanism as the `/agent` and `/artifact` grants. Added `(home_server, subject="", feature="orchestrator", scope="")` there, so the home server (guild `1501965852042330302`, from `agent.discord.defaultServerId`) gets the tier server-wide (all channels). No manual DB insert needed. `acl_test` updated (grant count 5 -> 6, new assertions).

## Things to flag
- **conversational_agent_reply framing:** per the task I reused `conversational_agent_reply` for the chat verdict, but its prompt is framed as "the coding agent just finished, relay what it did." For a chat verdict no agent ran, so the framing is a mismatch and may read oddly in prod. Worth a dedicated chat-reply prompt as a fast-follow; flagging since orchestrator.enabled is flipped on here.
- **KG grounding deferred:** `compile` receives `kg_results` via the request context, but the flow currently passes only the channel directive and channel context window (both cheap/in-process); wiring the KG search (needs the embedding client + a session) is a fail-open-safe fast-follow. The assembler renders "(none)" for empty KG results.
- **Prompt/bundle updated:** to make the chat-enrichment path non-dead, `orchestrator_prompt.md` now asks for `reply_guidance` on the chat route and the baked bundle was regenerated. The generated bundle is now prettier-ignored (generator is the sole authority) to stop a prettier-vs-generator race in the format hook.
- **Commit-boundary slip:** the `onepassworditem-orchestrator.yaml` deletion landed in the 3.1 commit rather than 3.4 (it was staged via `git rm` before 3.1's commit). Final branch state is correct; only the commit boundary is off.

author: cwaits6
body:
## Problem

The `Set image metadata` step derives the image tag from the branch name but only replaces `/` with `-`. Any other character that is illegal in a Docker/OCI tag is left intact.

Renovate group branches such as `renovate/major-github-actions-(major)` therefore produced tags like:

```
ghcr.io/<owner>/<image>:renovate-major-github-actions-(major)
```

`buildah manifest` rejects this with `invalid reference format`, failing the **Create & Push Manifest** job. This breaks the container build on every Renovate major-group PR (observed in cwaits6/apk-datasource#21).

## Fix

Collapse any character outside `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]` to `-` for both the `pull_request` and `refs/heads/*` cases:

```bash
BRANCH="${BRANCH//[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]/-}"
```

Docker tag grammar is `[a-zA-Z0-9_][a-zA-Z0-9._-]{0,127}`, so this yields a valid tag regardless of branch name.

author: robotsix-mill[bot]
body:
Gap: The periodic security_posture agent generates drafts for GitHub Action SHA pin updates, but every SHA it resolves does not match the actual upstream tag commit. Across the 2026-07-01 batch on robotsix-modules, all four action types (actions/checkout, setup-uv, upload-artifact, and the consolidation rollup re-applying the same data) had incorrect SHAs. The implement stage independently re-resolved each tag via git ls-remote, incurring roughly $0.28 and 900s of wasted trace cost and latency across the batch.

Root cause: The periodic agent's tag-to-SHA resolution logic systematically returns commits that do not exist in upstream repos. The 100 percent failure rate (4-for-4 across distinct action types in one batch, plus the consolidation re-application) indicates a systematic defect rather than a transient network issue.

Recommended fix (choose one):
1. Have the periodic agent validate its resolved SHAs against the upstream repo via git ls-remote (or equivalent) BEFORE committing the draft, rejecting mismatches at draft time.
2. Alternatively, delegate SHA resolution entirely to the implement stage, which already does the correct git ls-remote resolution (as evidenced by every implement round correcting the draft's wrong SHAs).

body:
## In-app self-update (Windows + Linux) — the client half

Wires the Wails v3 `pkg/updater` (already in the pinned `v3.0.0-alpha2.108`,
no framework bump) into the **About dialog**: Check → SHA256SUMS-verified
download → in-place binary swap → Restart, headless. macOS, dev builds,
server mode, and unwritable installs fall back to the existing "Open release
page" via a single `can_self_update` gate.

This is **PR B** of two. **PR A (#563, merged)** froze the asset-name contract
this PR hard-codes (raw `recall-<v>-windows-amd64.exe`, raw
`recall-<v>-linux-amd64`, combined `SHA256SUMS`) and cut Windows over to
per-user install. **Both must ship in the same release** — the per-user
installer and the self-updating client arrive together; that release is the
floor from which users self-update onward.

### What's in it
- **`pkg/app` seam** (`SelfUpdater`, wails-free) so the `serveronly` build
  never links the updater. `StartSelfUpdate` is single-flighted on a
  background goroutine; `RestartToApply` delegates.
- **`pkg/cmd` adapter** (`!serveronly`) — gates on dev/macOS/unwritable-exe,
  matches the raw per-platform asset by exact suffix with a `-server-`
  exclusion, `updater.WindowNone`. `Init` does no network I/O (boot stays
  offline).
- **Wire**: `POST /api/v1/system/self-update` + `.../restart` (202, or 409
  `self-update-unavailable`), `can_self_update` on `UpdateInfo`.
- **Frontend**: `wails:updater:*` → phase/pct/error state machine in the app
  store (survives About close/reopen); About renders Install / progress /
  Restart / error, with the release-page fallback always present.

### Automated tests (all green locally)
- Go unit under **both** build tags: seam single-flight/delegation, asset
  matcher over the real inventory, `dirWritable` probe, 409/202 handlers.
- Vitest: store state machine (`stores/app.test.ts`) + AboutModal branches.
- New e2e `update-self-install.spec.ts`: pins the gate + transport (the
  serveronly harness can't run a real updater).
- `task lint`, `task test`, `task test-e2e`, `task cover` (Go 76.4% ≥ 67%,
  frontend lines 70.9% / branches 61.4% ≥ 60%), gen-types in sync.

### Manual smoke checklist — DO NOT MERGE until these pass
The real binary swap can only be proven on a released build, not in CI. Please
run before merging:

- [ ] **Windows migration**: machine-scope v(N−1) installed → run the new
      per-user installer → exactly one UAC prompt → old copy + HKLM key gone,
      app now under `%LocalAppData%\Programs\Recall` with `Reset-Database.bat`.
      Decline-UAC path warns and still installs (temporary dual install).
- [ ] **Windows swap**: against a scratch repo (temp `Repository`, v0.0.1 →
      v0.0.2 with raw exe + SHA256SUMS) → Install → progress → Restart →
      relaunched on the new version.
- [ ] **Linux swap**: `~/bin` binary swaps cleanly; tmpfs-`/tmp` machine
      fails safe (backup restored, EXDEV, no relaunch — known upstream gap);
      `.deb` install reports `can_self_update:false`.
- [ ] **Unchanged**: dev build + macOS still show only "Open release page".

### Ledger

author: philmichel
body:
## Summary

Runs the container as a dedicated non-root user (`genmon`, uid/gid 1000) instead of root.

- **Patch upstream's root check**: `genloader.py` and `genmon.py` hard-require `euid == 0` via `MySupport.PermissionsOK()`, but nothing in a TCP-serial deployment actually needs root (no serial devices, no GPIO, web UI on 8000, MQTT out). The check is relaxed at build time with a `grep` guard that fails the build if upstream moves or rewords the line.
- **`USER 1000:1000`** with ownership of the paths genmon writes: `/app/genmon`, `/etc/genmon`, `/var/log/genmon`, `/var/log/genmon.log`.
- **`start.sh` drops sudo**: calls `genloader.py -s` directly with the virtualenv python — `startgenmon.sh` wraps the identical call in `sudo`, which is unavailable (and unnecessary) as non-root. Also recreates `/var/log/genmon` at startup in case a volume is mounted over `/var/log`.
- **`sudo` purged** from the final image (still present during build for `genmonmaint.sh`).

Known trade-off: the web UI's restart/update buttons shell out to the sudo-based scripts and won't work — updates are handled by image rebuilds anyway (`update_check = false` is already set).

## Test plan

- Build the image and run it: container should start as uid 1000, genloader should load all modules, web UI reachable on 8000.
- In k8s, pair with `runAsNonRoot: true` / uid 1000 pod securityContext and an emptyDir over `/var/log`.

author: ezraellette
body:
Fixes #4845

## What was broken

Three related defects left the Windows a11y walk budgeting system effectively inoperative (a11y+input cohort telemetry: **117% avg CPU vs 72%** for others):

1. **No mid-walk wall-clock timeout** — the walk timeout was only checked *before* the walk started. Once started, the Chromium/Electron per-element TreeWalker fallback (~2 cross-process COM round-trips per element, serviced synchronously on the target app's UI thread) was bounded only by node count (5,000–10,000 nodes).
2. **Fragile-provider exemption missing on the value-producing path** — `is_fragile_uia_tree_provider` (Outlook Classic crash vector) was only checked in the periodic worker; the paired-capture walker that actually persists text had no such check.
3. **Walk budgets + terminal-OCR throttle were dead code on Windows** — they depend on `get_focused_metadata_lightweight`, which was a stub returning `None` on Windows, so per-app walk budgets, the heavy-OCR-app throttle, and lock-screen detection never engaged for non-AppSwitch triggers.

## Walk timeline, before → after

```
BEFORE (Chromium/Electron window, per capture trigger)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 cache attempt      per-element TreeWalker fallback (unbounded duration)
 ├────┤├──────────────────────────────────────────────────── ⋯ ────────┤
 0     ~10 titlebar nodes → rediscover fallback, walk up to 10,000 nodes
       └─ serviced ON the target app's UI thread → foreground freeze

AFTER
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 walk 1: cache attempt → ≤10 nodes → fallback (shares 250ms deadline)
 ├────┤├──────────────────┤ truncated=true, reason=Timeout
 0                     250ms   └─ hwnd memoized as "needs walker"

 walk 2+: straight to TreeWalker with the FULL wall-clock budget
 ├─────────────────────────┤ deadline checked before every element fetch
 0                      250ms  (adaptive tiers shrink this to 100–150ms
                                for apps that repeatedly walk slow)
```

## Changes

### 1. In-walk wall-clock deadline (`platform/windows_uia.rs`, `tree/windows.rs`)
- New `capture_window_tree_bounded(hwnd, max_elements, timeout)` returns the tree **plus a `TruncationReason`**. A `TreeBudget` threads through both tree-build paths; the deadline is checked before every element fetch in the **per-element TreeWalker fallback** (the unbounded-freeze path this issue is about), so a walk overruns it by at most one element.
- The **cached path is deliberately node-cap-only**: its single `ElementFromHandleBuildCache` call is synchronous (can't be interrupted), and once it returns the subtree is already materialized in-process — truncating the local build on the deadline would discard data the target app already paid to produce without shortening its freeze. (A live run proved this matters: a 163ms cached call under a 50ms budget would have yielded 1 node out of a 768-node tree.)
- **Both pipelines honor it**: the paired-capture walker passes its remaining `effective_walk_timeout()` budget (250ms default, 100–150ms for heavy-tier apps), and the periodic worker (`capture_and_send`) uses a 250ms cap.
- The paired path now reports real `truncated`/`truncation_reason` values instead of hardcoded `false`/`None` — so `record_walk` sees truncation and the adaptive budget escalates tiers correctly, and the `ax_*` telemetry counters (`truncated_timeout`) become meaningful on Windows.
- **Per-hwnd "needs walker fallback" memoization** (5-min TTL, process-wide): Chromium/Electron windows skip the pointless cached attempt on subsequent walks and give the TreeWalker the full budget. TTL + eviction handles HWND recycling; a window whose cached path starts working clears its memo entry.

### 2. Fragile-provider exemption on the paired path (`tree/windows.rs`)
`walk_focused_window` now skips apps in `FRAGILE_UIA_TREE_PROVIDERS` (Outlook Classic — crashes its own host process when an external client materializes its Sent Items grid), matching the periodic worker. OCR still captures these apps' content.

### 3. Windows `get_focused_metadata_lightweight` (`event_driven_capture.rs`, `platform/windows.rs`)
- New `get_focused_app_window_lightweight()`: `GetForegroundWindow` + cached process-name lookup + `GetWindowTextW` — no UIA/COM. Skips transient shell windows (MSCTFIME UI etc.) so throttle state isn't poisoned with explorer.exe. App names go through `get_effective_app_name`, so walk-budget keys line up across `should_walk` (trigger app) and `record_walk` (snapshot app).
- Engine-side implementation mirrors the macOS 1s-TTL `ArcSwap` cache.
- This single change reactivates three existing systems on Windows: **per-app adaptive walk budgets**, the **terminal/Obsidian OCR throttle**, and **lock-screen skip**.
- Follow-on fixes required by app names now flowing on Windows:
  - `is_lock_screen_app` recognizes `LockApp.exe`/`LogonUI.exe` — without this, a `Some(app)` at the lock screen would have *cleared* the global screen-locked flag.
  - `is_ocr_heavy_app` matches `Obsidian.exe` (Windows process names carry the extension).

### Drive-by
- Fixed stale `test_incognito_detection` assertion (`"Enter Password - Chrome"` stopped matching when incognito keywords were tightened in 6b45f9609 for false-positive reduction; the Windows-only test was missed).

## Testing

- `cargo test -p screenpipe-a11y --lib` — **all pass** (190 + new tests), including new unit tests:
  - `test_tree_budget_max_nodes` / `test_tree_budget_deadline` — truncation reason recording, first-hit-wins
  - `test_walker_fallback_memo_roundtrip` — memo insert/hit/forget
  - extended `test_fragile_uia_provider_detection`
- `cargo test -p screenpipe-engine --lib event_driven_capture` — **all pass**, including extended `lock_screen_app_detection` / `ocr_heavy_app_detection` for Windows process names.
- **Live bounded-capture test** on a real Windows 11 desktop (`test_live_bounded_capture_truncates`, `#[ignore]`d like the other live UIA tests). Two runs against real windows:

```
# deadline enforcement (mid-development, deadline applied to both paths):
full walk:    768 nodes in 252ms (truncation: None)
bounded 50ms: 1 nodes   in 163ms (truncation: Timeout)   <- walk stopped at deadline

# final semantics (deadline binds the fallback; cached path node-capped):
full walk:    335 nodes in 224ms (truncation: None)
bounded 50ms: 335 nodes in 124ms (truncation: None)      <- materialized tree kept
```

The first run proves the deadline machinery fires mid-walk. It also exposed why the cached path must not be time-truncated: the 163ms was one uninterruptible `ElementFromHandleBuildCache` COM call that had *already* materialized the full tree — discarding it saved the target app nothing. Final semantics: cache-path windows keep their (node-capped) tree; Chromium/Electron fallback walks stop at the deadline.

## Impact

- A single Electron/Chromium window can no longer take an unbounded-duration walk per capture trigger; the paired-capture walk is now hard-capped at the adaptive budget (250ms default), directly capping the foreground-freeze class measured in #4835.
- Windows machines now get the same per-app cost caps as macOS: expensive apps decay to Heavy/Critical tiers (walks at most every 5s/60s with 1000/500-node caps), terminals cap at 1 OCR capture per 30s.

Related: #4835 (orphaned periodic walker — this issue caps the remaining paired-capture walks).

author: kristofferr
body:
## What & why

PR #411 deliberately **excluded** six remote codes that resolve through the same FurniMove handset backend but use an incompatible command layout ("DOT PROTOCOL" / RF1058 / RF34 / RF6707: 90167, 91983, 93558, 97450, 97544, 98035). This PR implements them.

Stacked on #411 (`feat/okin-all-remote-codes`) — it builds on the generated 216-code remote table and the handset-layout-derived control exposure added there.

## What "DOT PROTOCOL" actually is

Traced through the FurniMove APK (`com.okin.okinsmartcomfort`):

- **DOT boxes are CB24-family receivers.** `BluetoothLeService.setCharacteristics` flags a connection as DOT when the GATT exposes the Nordic UART write characteristic `6E400002` — the app's constant is literally named `CB24_WRITE_CHARACTERISTIC`. There is no Okin `62741523` service on these boxes.
- **Framing:** 7-byte `[0x05, 0x02, <keycode BE>, 0x00]` (`HexValueConverter.toByteArray` with `isDOTProtocol=true`) instead of the Okimat 6-byte `[0x04, 0x02, <keycode BE>]`.
- **Handshake:** the app writes ASCII `affirm` to the characteristic immediately on discovery; mirrored once per connection before the first command.
- **Timing:** held buttons re-send ~every 100ms; release sends keycode `0` (`DisobeyStandbyTime`). No pairing, no known position feedback.

Same keycode space, different transport — so the implementation is a thin transport subclass, not a new protocol stack.

## Implementation

- **New bed type `okin_dot`** with its own `OKIN_DOT_VARIANTS` dropdown.
- **Section-mapped motors.** DOT motor keycodes are renumbered per handset (whichever channels exist start at `0x1/0x2`, then `0x4/0x8`) but keep their section meaning (FurniMove: M1=Head, M2=Back, M3=Legs, M4=Feet). The table maps them to the standard section fields, so the layout-derived controls carry the right names: RF1058 beds get **Head + Feet** covers, RF34 **Back + Legs**, RF6707 **Head + Back**.
- **`OkinDotController(OkinUuidController)`** (`beds/okin_dot.py`): Nordic UART, write-without-response, affirm handshake, no pairing/position paths. The six codes live in the shared generated remote table flagged `dot: True`, so all config-driven capabilities (massage, memory, zero-g) come from the existing flows.
- **Factory rescue:** Okimat/Okin UUID entries whose connected box lacks `62741525` but exposes Nordic UART are switched to DOT framing automatically (mirrors the RF-Gateway sniffing from #402).
- **Authoritative per-code data** (fetched live from `GET /mobile-data/button/{code}`): renumbered memory layouts (RF34 Memo1 = `0x10000`, the standard *save* keycode), hold-to-save timing via `OkinUuidComplexCommand` (5s @ 200ms on RF1058, 2s @ 200ms on RF34), zero-gravity, quiet-sleep, and a new **anti-snore** preset field wired to the existing anti-snore button.
- **Why these couldn't be folded into the Okimat profile:** DOT Flat is `0x08000000` — the standard Okimat *child-lock* keycode.
- **Pipeline:** `build_master.py` gains `DOT_CODES` handling (`protocol: "dot"` records, kept out of the csv-inherit pool so standard codes never inherit DOT keycodes); generators emit the split variant dicts. New protocol doc at `docs/beds/okin-dot.md`, including the one known unknown: FurniMove sends a raw `00 B0` write ~400ms after stop (not implemented; suspected standby-timer re-arm — first thing to try if a tester reports motor creep).

## Testing

- Full suite: **2066 passed**, including 30 new DOT tests (framing incl. trailing `0x00`, affirm-once-per-connection, per-code section-mapped keycodes for all six codes, cover exposure, factory routing incl. the no-demotion case for real Okimat boxes).
- ⚠️ No hardware confirmation yet — protocol is APK + live-backend verified; the README row is marked accordingly.

Ref #406

body:
## What
The perf/memory pass from the /goal (*"Fix memory issues and optimize everything for loading times"*). Driven by an exhaustive multi-perspective audit with each finding independently verified and a final review pass on the fixes. Applied the confirmed findings; dropped false positives.

## Fixes
- **RemoteStore** (memory/security, HIGH): `saveDebridConfig` clears the transient plaintext secret in a `finally`, so a failed credential PUT can't leave a token in memory until profile-switch/restart.
- **App.tsx** (bundle/loading): 8 rarely-opened overlays (onboarding wizards, guide, shortcuts, profile picker, nudge) are `React.lazy` + Suspense — out of the first-paint chunk, including ServerSetupWizard's QRCode dep. CommandPalette stays eager (owns the global ⌘K listener).
- **genreArtwork** (network/memory): Browse-tile artwork fetch capped at **4 concurrent** TMDB requests (was ~15 at once on Search open — free-tier rate-limit risk), plus a **30-min TTL** so a "no backdrop" result stops blocking retries forever.
- **MediaCard** (large-grid render): wrapped in `React.memo`, handlers moved to `useCallback`, motion variants/transitions hoisted to module constants — a grid re-render no longer re-runs 100+ unchanged cards. `contain: layout` on the card + `contain: layout paint` on the already-clipped poster (paint omitted on the card so its hover lift/scale isn't clipped).

## Dropped as false positives (after verification)
The AppStore `useMemo` "missing serverSession dep" — `serverSession` isn't exposed in the context value, so adding it would **regress** (re-render all consumers on every session change). The prior sweep confirmed the codebase was already well-optimized (visibility-gated intervals, suspend-on-hidden animations, memoized context, bounded caches).

## Tests
App overlay tests await the now-lazy chunks. **Full suite green (2644), tsc clean.**

body:
## What & why

`remotehelp_start` could never open Quick Assist on target PCs. The tray helper launched it with `std::process::Command::new("quickassist.exe").spawn()`, assuming Quick Assist registers an app-execution alias on the user's PATH.

On the modern MSIX/Store package (`MicrosoftCorporationII.QuickAssist`) that fails two ways:

- The alias `quickassist.exe` is a zero-byte reparse point (`IO_REPARSE_TAG_APPEXECLINK`) that a plain `CreateProcess` does not resolve → *"not found"*.
- The packaged binary under `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\...\QuickAssist.exe` denies direct execution by ACL → *"Zugriff verweigert" / access denied* (the reported symptom).

The Start menu — which works — activates the app by its **Application User Model ID**. This change does the same: packaged apps are activated via `IApplicationActivationManager::ActivateApplication`, which also returns the real process id for the `pid` field. The launch happens in the interactive-session tray helper (as before), since the activation manager needs the caller's session/foreground rights that the session-0 service lacks.

The launch allow-list — still the trust boundary — becomes a small table keyed by the same bare exe name. An entry carries an AUMID for a packaged app, or `None` for a classic desktop binary (a future `msra.exe` / `mstsc.exe`), which still uses a plain spawn.

The wire contract is unchanged: `remotehelp_start` still answers `{launched, pid, note}`; `docs/protocol.md` and the fixtures are untouched. Docs (ADR-0022) and the stale "app-execution alias" comments are updated.

author: 0xergod
body:
Adds an on-the-fly reachability/safety checker in `stratum-logic` that evaluates the property DURING lazy exploration and stops at the first witness/counterexample, without building the full `Lts`. Closes #11.

## API (`stratum_logic::onthefly`)
- `find_reachable(start, bound, goal) -> Reachability{ witness, explored, exact }` — `EF goal`, returns the path to the first goal state.
- `check_safety(start, bound, invariant) -> Safety{ counterexample, explored, exact }` — `AG invariant`, returns the run to the first violation.
- `Run`/`RunStep` genuine reduction sequences; `*_prop` labelling-phrased variants matching the existing checker.

## How
A shared `explore_until` does lazy BFS driven directly by `stratum_core::step_labeled` + `canonicalize`, **byte-for-byte mirroring `Lts::explore`** (nominal reps stepped, canonical dedup keys, identical `>= bound` state-count truncation rule), with a stop-predicate checked on `start` and each newly-discovered state → early return. Runs are reconstructed from BFS back-pointers exactly like `shortest_path` (shortest run). Exactness follows the `Checked` polarity: a positive witness / a counterexample is definitive even under truncation; a negative reachability verdict or "safety holds" is definitive only if exploration completed within the bound.

## Agreement (verified)
Because the exploration engine is identical up to the early-exit, the on-the-fly verdict provably matches the denotational checker: a witness exists iff `holds(ef(prop))`, a counterexample iff `counterexample(...)` (≡ `!holds(ag(inv))`), with equal shortest-run lengths. Adversarial review confirmed this with an **80,000-combination** sweep (2000 random systems × bounds 1..40) asserting verdict + run-length + exact-flag equality against the full `Lts` oracle at every truncation boundary — APPROVE.

## Tests
`tests/onthefly.rs`: 300-system differential (both polarities + truncating cases, non-vacuity asserted, runs validated against the built `Lts`), empty-run edges, and an acceptance benchmark — a 1-Comm `bad` violation beside an unbounded replicator: full `explore(500)` truncates at ≥100 states while on-the-fly explores **2** (and succeeds at `bound=8`), demonstrating detection without full state-space construction.

author: anton-vinogradov
body:
## Problem
Sessions lived only in an in-memory map, so every restart/deploy logged everyone out
("the site forgot my token").

## Fix
No server-side session store. On login the validated TeamCity token is encrypted (AES-GCM)
into the HttpOnly session cookie (`SessionCodec`), keyed by a stable `session.secret`
(`SESSION_SECRET`, generated once by `install.sh`). Each request decrypts the cookie; a bad
secret, tampering (GCM tag) or expiry just fails to `401`. The token stays confidential in
transit (HTTPS), invisible to JS (HttpOnly), and off disk.

## Trade-off
Without a server-side store, a specific session can't be force-revoked before its TTL — but the
user can revoke the TeamCity token itself, and the 8h TTL bounds it.

## Verified
- Unit: encode→decode round-trip; **survives a fresh instance with the same secret** (== restart);
  rejects a different secret, tampering, and expiry.
- On the server: logged in, **restarted the app**, and the same cookie still returned the user
  and analysed PR 13316 (200).

author: independentvar
body:
## Summary

Fixes the crash reported upstream in Kalejin/DCSB#161: playing an MP3 throws

```
NAudio.MmException: NoDriver calling acmFormatSuggest
  at NAudio.Wave.Compression.AcmStream.SuggestPcmFormat(...)
  at NAudio.Wave.Mp3FileReader..ctor(...)
  at DCSB.SoundPlayer.FileReader..ctor(String fileName)
  at DCSB.SoundPlayer.AudioPlaybackEngine.PlaySound(...)
```

`AudioFileReader` decodes MP3s through the Windows ACM MP3 codec, which is absent on Windows N/KN editions and some stripped-down installs. `PlaySound` only caught `COMException` (the Ogg fallback), so the `MmException` escaped and the sound errored out.

## Fix

- New `MediaFoundationFileReader` implementing `IAudioReader` over NAudio's `MediaFoundationReader`, which uses the Media Foundation MP3 decoder instead of ACM.
- `AudioPlaybackEngine.PlaySound` catches `MmException` and retries with the new reader.

No new DLLs are shipped (MediaFoundation support is inside the existing NAudio.dll), so no installer script changes are needed.

## Testing

- `msbuild DCSB.sln /p:Configuration=Release` builds clean.
- Exercised `MediaFoundationFileReader` directly against a generated MP3: correct IeeeFloat output, full sample reads, `Position = 0` reset (loop support), and clean dispose.

Note: on systems where Media Foundation itself is also missing (Windows N without the Media Feature Pack), MP3 playback still cannot work; the error message will now point at Media Foundation instead.

Every fix went through the mandatory workflow: `make build` (lint + tests) → `make deploy` → `make verify` → live API/Playwright verification against the running daemon, plus a CHANGELOG entry. Closes #164, closes #165, closes #166, closes #167, closes #168, closes #169, closes #170, closes #171, closes #172, closes #173, closes #174, closes #175, closes #176, closes #177, closes #178, closes #179, closes #180, closes #181, closes #182, closes #183, closes #184.

## Live verification highlights (192.168.20.21, test jobs only)

- **#165** GC triggered mid-backup queued behind the run (log-ordered), swept 0 packs; backup completed 5/5
- **#167** synthetic `skipped` run with due retry was claimed and dispatched end-to-end (`retry_of` chain visible in history)

author: johnny-liou
body:
## Background
- **RFC:** [vllm-project/vllm#47572](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47572).
- **Project:** ReplaySSM, caching recent SSM inputs instead of writing the recurrent state back to HBM every step.
- **Collaboration:** [Dao AI Lab](https://dao-lab.ai) × NVIDIA.
 - **Blog (full derivation + figures):** [ReplaySSM](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/)
- **Fork / branch:** [`Johnny-Liou/ReplaySSM`](https://github.com/Johnny-Liou/ReplaySSM)
- **Concurrent cross-framework work:** [TensorRT-LLM PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/14203)
- **AI assistance:** AI assistance was used for parts of this work. The human authors have reviewed the kernel design and most of the code; since this is a draft PR, we will finish reviewing every changed line and run the tests before marking it ready.

## Core concept
- SSM decode is memory-bound: each step loads and stores a `(nheads, d, n)` recurrent state; the state store dominates traffic.
- ReplaySSM keeps a small ring buffer of recent inputs and a periodic checkpoint state; it reconstructs the state (or reads the output directly) from the checkpoint + buffer, and writes the full state back only on periodic flushes.
- Three benefits from one change:
  - **Less memory traffic:** halves the dominant state traffic in standard decode (state store replaced by a small input append most steps).
  - **Cheap rollback:** vLLM's current spec path stores a per-draft state snapshot to undo rejected tokens; ReplaySSM makes rollback a ring-buffer pointer move, so no per-step state snapshots are kept or restored.
  - **Parallel verification:** most steps only need the output, not the state: the output-only form computes all `T` draft outputs from one checkpoint + buffer in a single GEMM (removing the length-`T` serial recurrence), and materializes the full state only at a flush.
- **Additional benefit (numerical precision):** reconstruction runs in FP32 and the state is written back only on flushes, so storing the checkpoint in low precision (e.g. FP16) re-quantizes it at most ~`L`× less often than the baseline, which re-quantizes on every per-step state store to HBM. Reference: [NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Ultra Technical Report](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/nemotron/files/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-Technical-Report.pdf), Section 4.5.
- **Regime (hybrid models):** the win is largest at short-to-medium output lengths (where the SSM layers dominate the step) and at large batch size (at small batch the MLP layers dominate). ReplaySSM shows largest kernel-level speedup at large batch size, where the SSM kernel is purely memory-bound.

## What this PR adds (scope + opt-in)
- **New Triton kernels** (files under `vllm/model_executor/layers/`):

  | Component | Entry point | File |
  |---|---|---|
  | Mamba2 standard | `selective_state_update_replayssm_output_only`, `…_state_and_output` | `mamba/ops/selective_state_update_replayssm_output_only.py`, `…_state_and_output.py` |
  | Mamba2 spec | `selective_state_update_replayssm_spec` (+ `commit_replayssm_spec` / `reset_*`) | `mamba/ops/selective_state_update_replayssm_spec.py` |
  | GDN standard | `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_replayssm` | `fla/ops/fused_recurrent_replayssm.py` |
  | GDN spec | `gdn_replayssm_spec_decode` (+ `commit_gdn_replayssm_spec` / `reset_*`) | `fla/ops/gdn_replayssm_spec_decode.py` |
  | Shared launch config | `get_replayssm_config` (hardware auto-detected) | `mamba/ops/replayssm_config.py` |
- **Config flags (all default off ⇒ baseline path byte-for-byte unchanged):**
  - `--use-replayssm`: Mamba2/GDN standard cached decode.
  - `--replayssm-route`: Mamba2 standard route `output_only` (default) or `state_and_output` (GDN ignores it).
  - `--use-replayssm-spec`: speculative cached decode; requires speculative decoding + `--mamba-cache-mode none`.
  - `--replayssm-buffer-len`: history block `B` (default 16).
- **Note (route):** `output_only` (default) outperforms `state_and_output` in every setting we measured. We keep `state_and_output` and the `--replayssm-route` flag only for upcoming numerical-precision experiments; both the kernel and the flag will be removed in the production-ready version.
- **Note (staging):** this draft shows the complete design; we plan to land it in the stages proposed in the RFC.
- **Integration:** `mamba_mixer2` / `qwen_gdn_linear_attn` dispatch to the cached kernels under the flags; `mamba_attn` / `gdn_attn` metadata builders carry the ring cursors; `MambaStateShapeCalculator` sizes the caches; the hybrid reuses vLLM's `causal_conv1d_update`.

## Design notes (the non-obvious parts)
- **What the baseline stores (for contrast):**
  - Standard decode: the baseline advances the recurrent state and writes the full `(nheads, d, n)` state back to HBM every step.
  - Speculative decode: vLLM stores a separate state snapshot for every draft token (to enable rollback of rejected tokens); even the improved prior works still advance the state and write at least one full state back to HBM per step.
- **What ReplaySSM caches instead (per step):** a small input append, no state store.
  - Mamba2: the per-step SSM inputs `(v, Δ, k)` (i.e. `x`, `dt`, `B`).
  - GDN: `(u, k, g)`, where `u = β(v - Sk)` is the corrected update vector (cached instead of `v`) because it depends on the state; caching the already-corrected `u` keeps replay free of the serial dependency.
- **What ReplaySSM keeps in HBM (the state):**
  - A single checkpoint state `S₀`, loaded every step and written back only on flushes (see below), replacing the baseline's per-step state store.
  - Conv state reuses vLLM's `causal_conv1d_update` unchanged; in spec decode the window is `conv_kernel-1+num_spec` and rollback is a shift keyed on `num_accepted_tokens`. ReplaySSM never touches the conv path.
- **When we flush (write the checkpoint):** `B` (`--replayssm-buffer-len`, default 16) is the maximum number of history tokens (past SSM inputs) the buffer holds. A flush reconstructs the recurrent state from the cached history tokens and writes it back as the new checkpoint `S₀` in HBM; the history window then restarts.
  - Standard: each step appends one input to the size-`B` buffer, so we flush every `B` steps.
  - Speculative: a verify step consumes a window of `T = num_spec_tokens + 1` tokens at once, so we flush whenever `history_tokens + T > B` (the next window would not fit). This guarantees every verify step has room for a full `T`-draft window, preventing window collapse / truncation.
- **Ring-buffer sizing (spec):** the ring holds `L = B + T` slots. A flush step carries at most `B` history tokens (from the flush rule above) and appends the current window of up to `T`, so `L = B + T` always has room for a full `T`-draft window on top of the history, so the window never collapses or truncates.
  - **Physical size:** we currently round the logical size up to `next_pow2(L)` so wraparound indexing is a cheap bit-mask (`& (N-1)`) instead of a `% L`. Sizing the ring to exactly `L = B + T` (dropping the pow2 slack to save cache memory) is future work.
- **Why a ring buffer (spec):** the number of accepted tokens is only known after the whole step, so rejected drafts must be discarded cheaply. Rather than relocate accepted tokens to the front of the buffer every layer/step, the kernel indexes the cache circularly and moves cursors instead of data.
  - **Circular indexing (in-kernel):** every cache access maps to physical slot `(post_origin + write_pos + offs) & (buf - 1)`, driven by two block-keyed cursors: `post_origin` (the window's circular base) and `write_pos` (committed-history offset).
  - **Commit / rollback (device-side, no data movement):** a normal step does `write_pos += num_accepted` (rejected drafts are never committed, which is the rollback); a flush advances `post_origin` past the committed history and resets `write_pos`.
- **Full decode step (end-to-end integration):**
  - Standard: `write_pos

author: usirin
body:
## What

Add an `http(s)`-only **protocol allowlist** to pano's submit-URL persistence gate.
`parseSubmitUrl` (`apps/web/worker/features/pano/post-operations.ts`) previously only
guarded against `new URL()` *throwing*, so a `javascript:` / `data:` / `file:` URL parsed
successfully and persisted to `post_record.url` unguarded.

The exact protocol gate already lived next door in `isSafeFetchUrl`
(`link-metadata.ts`). Rather than duplicate it, this factors the parse + http(s)-scheme
check out as a shared exported `isHttpUrl(raw): URL | null` helper. `isSafeFetchUrl` now
layers its SSRF host screen on top of it, and `parseSubmitUrl` reuses it directly — one
source for the http(s) rule. A non-http(s) or unparseable URL rejects with the existing
typed `UrlInvalid` (following the vote/pano error idiom); the prior throw-guard behavior is
preserved (a malformed URL still rejects the same way).

`isHttpUrl` is deliberately **not** the full `isSafeFetchUrl`: the submit gate wants the
protocol allowlist without the fetch-time private-IP/localhost host block, which is a
broader SSRF policy that would wrongly reject legitimate public submit URLs.

## Severity — defense-in-depth, not a live exploit

This closes a **stored-invariant gap at the persistence layer**, it is **not** a live SPA
XSS. The render sinks (`PanoPostCard.tsx`, `PanoPostHeader.tsx`) are React JSX `<a href>`
with no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, and React 19 neutralizes `javascript:` hrefs at render —
so there is no live exploit today. The fix keeps a non-http(s) href from ever reaching the
store, so no future non-React consumer can read one back out.

## Tests

`submit-validation.unit.test.ts` (the off-DB wiring tier, driven through the mutation over a
throwing `Drizzle`) gains, for both `submitPost` and `saveDraft`:
- `javascript:` / `data:` / `file:` URLs reject with `UrlInvalid` before any DB call
- an `http(s)` URL passes the allowlist and reaches the DB (proven by the die-on-DB-reach)
- the existing malformed-URL throw-guard still rejects with `UrlInvalid`

`link-metadata.unit.test.ts` (38 cases over the refactored `isSafeFetchUrl`) stays green.
`pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint:worktree` clean.

Fixes #1890

author: flavia-vale
body:
## Resumo
Depois do PR #1191 (janela curta de 5min pra dedup de cupom), mensagens de cupom **reais continuaram bloqueadas** — prints anexados pela cliente mostrando cupom Amazon e Shopee com "Link já enviado — bloqueado para não duplicar" bem depois do deploy.

**Causa raiz:** das 4 camadas de dedup, **duas gravam um TTL/`expiresAt` "congelado"** no momento da escrita, que continua valendo mesmo depois do código já rodar com a janela curta nova:

1. **`SendDedupKey.expiresAt`** era `Date.now() + effectiveDedupWindowMs`. O `create()` conflita (P2002) pela **existência** da linha no índice único, não pelo seu `expiresAt` — só o `deleteMany` libera o slot, e só libera quando esse `expiresAt` (calculado com a janela de QUANDO a linha foi criada) já passou. Uma reserva de cupom criada sob a janela antiga (24h) prendia o slot por até 24h.
   - Fix: essa tabela existe só pra fechar a corrida de **milissegundos** entre o `findFirst` diagnóstico e o `create` do `MessageLog` — nunca precisou representar a janela lógica inteira. Passa a usar um TTL fixo e curto (`SEND_DEDUP_RESERVATION_TTL_MS`, default 5min), independente do `linkKind`.
2. **`globalDedupCheckAndSet`** gravava `SET dedup:<userId>:<key> '1' PX ttlMs NX` — o TTL **nativo** da chave no Redis fica congelado no valor de quando foi criada. Uma chave de cupom criada sob a janela antiga continuava bloqueando no Redis por até 24h, mesmo com chamadas novas passando `ttlMs=5min`.
   - Fix: o valor guardado passa a ser o **timestamp** do envio (não mais `'1'`), com um TTL nativo fixo de segurança (24h, só pra não vazar memória). A decisão de duplicata compara esse timestamp contra o `ttlMs` do **chamador** em tempo de leitura — igual à dedup local/DB (que já eram corretas). Caminho comum (chave nova) continua `SET NX` atômico, sem round-trip extra.

Também corrigido: o texto do painel ("Link já enviado nas últimas 2 horas") era uma string fixa **já desatualizada antes desse fix** (o valor real já era 24h, não 2h) — atualizado em 3 lugares pra explicar que a janela varia por tipo de link, sem prometer um número fixo que erra a cada ajuste futuro.

body:
⚡ Bolt: Correct IOMUX and SPI configuration bitfields

💡 What:
- Updated IOMUX configuration constants to use correct bit positions: MCU_SEL (bits 4:2), FUN_IE (bit 9), and FUN_DRV (bits 11:10).
- Set SPI_WR_BYTE_ORDER (bit 10) to 0 to ensure Big-Endian/standard SPI transmission.

🎯 Why:
- The previous IOMUX configuration used incorrect bit offsets (e.g., bit 0 for MCU_SEL), which failed to correctly select the direct peripheral path (Function 1), resulting in higher latency via the GPIO matrix.
- The mismatch between SPI_WR_BYTE_ORDER=1 and MSB-shifting logic (cmd << 24) caused incorrect data transmission.

📊 Impact:
- Correctly bypasses the GPIO matrix for CLK and MOSI signals, reducing signal propagation delay.
- Restores correct SPI data integrity for all display commands and data transfers.

🔬 Measurement:
- Verified syntax and integration using:
  gcc -c -DTEST_HARNESS -Iinclude src/lcd_fast.c -o /dev/null

author: masamoto1982
body:
## Summary

Lifts the function-table proposal (`docs/dev/ajisai-functional-foundations.md` §3, approved via #1237) into `SPECIFICATION-NEXT.html` as normative draft-canon text — Ajisai's lambda-free abstraction mechanism, specified.

- **§5.6 Function tables**: a table with declared **parameter columns** (machine-readable column metadata; header presentation is host) defines a pure n-ary function. Bodies are ordinary column formulas; the **default output column is the rightmost formula column** (overridable, and any formula column is callable by name — one table, several named results). **Example rows** are simultaneously the live visible definition, the test fixture, and a memo table; zero example rows is allowed. Table names and word names share one document-unique namespace.
- **§6.6 Application**: naming applies (the concatenative rule — deferral is quotation; **no function-reference value kind**). `a1 … an TABLE@COL` binds positionally, evaluates the named column in a call context with on-demand sibling-column evaluation (each sibling at most once), and yields one atomic value. Calls are pure, deterministic, and metered against the calling cell's step budget. **Memo soundness condition**: an implementation may answer from an example row only when every argument's equality with the row's parameters is *exactly decided* (always true within domain D); memoization is never observable in values.
- **§9.6 Call recursion vs reference cycles**: self/mutual application is well-formed and budget-bounded (Turing completeness without LAMBDA); §9.4's static cycle detection governs cell-value dependencies only. The self-memo loop (an example row whose evaluation applies its own table with that row's own parameters) is identified as a genuine value cycle.
- **§10.3 `EXPECT`**: an optional literal column asserting, per example row, that the output equals the expected value — checked as a fail-loud table invariant under the same regime as `CONSERVE` (mismatch, NIL/U output against a definite expectation, or unprovable equality ⇒ machine-readable integrity failure).
- **Syntax**: §3.5 adds the application form `TABLE@NAME`, disjoint by shape from cell (`TABLE@B3`) and range (`TABLE@[NAME]`) forms; §3.6 adds the infix projections `TABLE(args…)` (default output) and `TABLE.COL(args…)`. §8.2 adds the word/table collision rule; §13.3 serializes function-table metadata; §16 gains a conformance item.

This resolves the design note's open items 1, 2, and 4 as: metadata-based parameter declaration (presentation-independent), rightmost-formula-column default output, and quotations retained in the initial release. Item 3 (`EXPECT`) is resolved as canonical. Item 5 (future of Script-surface `DEF`) remains open — `DEF` stays for now.

Documentation/draft-spec only — no code or shipped-runtime behavior changes.

## Quality Classification

- Highest impacted level: QL-D (draft specification text; shipped runtime canon unchanged)

body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The `isUnsafeVelocityAST` validation check for `velocityjs` templates previously checked only for literal string access to `constructor` or `__proto__` (e.g. `$object['constructor']`). However, it failed to block dynamically constructed string indices resulting from concatenation or interpolation (e.g. `$object['cons' + 'tructor']`), which bypasses the SSTI protection.
🎯 Impact: Attackers can execute arbitrary JavaScript on the server (RCE) by leveraging Sandbox Escape or Prototype Pollution through Velocity template injections.
🔧 Fix: Updated the `isUnsafeVelocityAST` AST validation utility to explicitly block nodes where `id.isEval === true` inside an index access node. Also removed a duplicated implementation of `processConcurrent`.
✅ Verification: Ran unit tests via `npx jest` and native test runner `tsx --test`. Manually validated via node scripts to ensure standard and dynamically interpolated blocklisted properties are trapped by the AST scanner.

Signed-off-by: Sentinel

author: mdheller
body:
## What

Closes the verified gap (2026-07-03) where the mount-intent taxonomy from the storage architecture was **design-only** (`grep -rn 'canonical_data|derived_index|MountIntent'` → zero hits). Workloads now declare storage by **intent**; the library resolves each to the backend **and** the retention/egress/caching **policy** — by construction.

## The invariant it encodes

**Only `canonical_data` + `curated_corpus` may ever egress** (to the cloud twin). Everything else stays on the device:

| intent | layer | retention | egress | vendor-cache |
|--------|-------|-----------|:------:|:------------:|
| canonical_data / curated_corpus | canonical (L1) | durable | ✅ | ✅ |
| derived_index | derived (L2) | rebuildable | ❌ rebuild at twin | ❌ |
| cache | vendor-cache (L3) | ttl | ❌ | ✅ |
| scratch | ephemeral (L6) | ephemeral | ❌ | ❌ |
| secrets | ephemeral | ephemeral | ❌ **never** | ❌ |
| config_ro / ipc_bridge | config / node-local | managed / ephemeral | ❌ | ❌ |

This is the storage-side counterpart to the ER plane's egress-masking / fog-scope discipline.

## Grounded in the two diagrams

- **Layered store model** (canonical L1 / derived-rebuildable L2 / vendor-cache-TTL L3 / tool-runtime-ephemeral L6) → `Layer` + `Retention`.
- **Policy Engine gates** (egress / caching / deletion, records events) → `may_egress` / `may_cache` / `may_delete` + auditable `PolicyDecision`.
- **Artifact lifecycle** (`IngestedRaw → … → Served → {VendorMaterialized, FlaggedRetention, LegalHold} → Deleted`) → `mount_intent.lifecycle`, where `transition()` refuses illegal moves and **blocks deletion under a legal hold**.
- **Per-runtime backends** (K8s PV/PVC·emptyDir·Secret·configMap / Docker volume·tmpfs·bind·npipe / Podman volume·tmpfs·`:O` overlay·secret·bind) → `resolve(intent, runtime)`.

## Enforcement (not just a library)

`tools/validate_mount_intent_egress.py` gates the build: every edge→cloud-twin sync Job/CronJob must declare `mount-intent.socioprophet.io/egress: <intent>[,...]`, and every declared intent must be egress-allowed — **fail-closed** on a missing annotation. Adding `derived_index` or `secrets` to a sync job fails CI. Annotated the existing hellgraph `edge-twin-sync` CronJob (egresses `canonical_data` only); the validator confirms it.

## Tests / CI

**45 tests** (intent×runtime resolution, the egress invariant, policy-decision auditing, lifecycle incl. legal-hold-blocks-deletion, and the validator's pass/fail-closed/reject-non-egressable behavior). New `mount-intent.yml` runs tests + the egress enforcement.

Follow-up (spawned): unify the two edge↔cloud-twin sync stacks so the twin's live graph comes from the hellgraph super-peer federation and rclone→S3 is cold-DR only.

## Summary
The ACA half of Phase F, built to the locked scope decisions: **historical 1095s = archive retrieval only; e-filing deferred.**

author: ajnunezg
body:
## What

Ports the macOS **Pretext** text-**layout** engine to Windows. On macOS it is an offscreen `WKWebView` running a bundled JS layout library (`pretext.bundle.min.js`) behind a JSON bridge (`OpenBurnBarCore/.../Pretext/PretextEngine.swift`). Here it becomes an **offscreen WebView2** loading the **same bundle byte-verbatim**, with a C# engine that mirrors the Swift protocol **method-for-method**.

This is **W6-DS-PRETEXT** — it blocks all of Chat (StreamingBubble height/shrink-wrap depend on these measurements) and carries top risk **R22** (Chromium-vs-WebKit metric drift).

## Architecture: portable engine + Windows-only transport

The engine, protocol, handle cache, and metric-parity harness talk only to an `IPretextWebHost` seam, so they **compile and unit-test on the macOS authoring host** against an in-memory fake host — no browser. Only the real WebView2 transport (and the live measurement run) needs Windows.

- `windows/pretext/OpenBurnBar.Pretext/` (**net8.0**, portable): `PretextTypes` (value-type mirror), `PretextBridge` (`{id,method,params}`↔`{id,ok,value,error}` codec + the exact Swift JS-string escaping), `IPretextWebHost`, `PretextEngine` (method-for-method port + `prepare`/`prepareWithSegments` handle cache), `MetricParity/*` (corpus + golden + runner).
- `Resources/Pretext/pretext.bundle.min.js` — **byte-verbatim** copy (cmp invariant). `Resources/Pretext/index.html` — WebView2 bridge shell mirroring the WKWebView shell method-for-method (`chrome.webview` transport) + a commented `@font-face` pin seam.
- `corpus/pretext-corpus.json` (10 Chat-critical cases) + `corpus/golden.mac.json` — a **real headless-WKWebView capture** (`capturedOn: macos-webkit`), regenerable via `tools/pretext-golden/capture_golden.swift`.
- `windows/app/OpenBurnBar.App/Pretext/WebView2PretextHost.cs` — Windows-only real offscreen-WebView2 transport (`CoreWebView2.WebMessageReceived` + `ExecuteScriptAsync`).
- `docs/windows-port/design/0005-pretext-webview2-metric-parity.md` (R22) + READMEs.

### Protocol map (Swift ⟷ C#) — method-for-method

| JS method | Swift | C# |
|---|---|---|
| `prepare` / `prepareWithSegments` | `prepare` / `prepareWithSegments` | `PrepareAsync` / `PrepareWithSegmentsAsync` |
| `layout` / `layoutWithLines` | `layout` / `layoutWithLines` | `LayoutAsync` / `LayoutWithLinesAsync` |
| `measureLineStats` / `measureNaturalWidth` | same | `MeasureLineStatsAsync` / `MeasureNaturalWidthAsync` |
| `prepareRichInline` / `layoutRichInline` | same | `PrepareRichInlineAsync` / `LayoutRichInlineAsync` |
| `releaseHandle` | `release(_:)` | `ReleaseAsync` |
| (client bisection) | `shrinkWrapWidth` | `ShrinkWrapWidthAsync` |

Same request envelope, same readiness heartbeat (`id: 0`), same escaping order (backslash-first, then `"` `\n` `\r` `\t` U+2028 U+2029), same handle cache keyed on `(text, font, options)`.

## R22 mitigation

Same JS + same bundle ⇒ identical layout math; only the font-metric backend can differ. Mitigated by: the committed corpus, the authoritative Mac golden, the parity runner (field-by-field within per-case tolerance), and font pinning (**Arial**, on both OSes; `@font-face` woff2 seam for exact parity). Tuning guidance is in the design doc — prefer bundling the exact woff2 over widening tolerances.

## Validation (macOS authoring host)

- `dotnet build windows/pretext/OpenBurnBar.Pretext` → **succeeded, 0 warning / 0 error**.
- `dotnet test windows/pretext/OpenBurnBar.Pretext.Tests` → **38 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed**. Covers: escaping + reply parsing (incl. U+2028/U+2029 round-trip), full engine round-trip, handle-cache elision, separate prepare/segments caches, sparse options serialization, `break:never` chips, rich-inline fragment mapping, shrink-wrap bisection, bridge-error + execute-script-failure + readiness-gating + dispose paths, and the parity harness (loads corpus + golden, **golden is a real capture not a scaffold**, every case covered, identity passes, injected drift + line-count mismatch fail, and `MeasureAsync` drives the whole corpus end-to-end via a golden-replay host).
- `cmp` macOS bundle vs Windows copy → **identical (verbatim)**.
- `scripts/debt/check-windows-tree-budget.sh` → **pass** (`windows/pretext/` is not a ratcheted area; the one app-area file is well under the 800-line target).
- Mac golden was **captured live** here via headless WKWebView from the verbatim bundle (all 10 cases, real numbers, zero JS errors).

### Windows-only / honestly deferred (macOS-gated)

- The **WinUI app + `WebView2PretextHost`** build on Windows only (WinUI/WebView2 are Windows-only) — consistent with the existing `VAL-P0-WINUI` "authored; build unproven until WINUI-017" status.

author: cahaseler
body:
## Summary

Two codegen fixes plus small ergonomic additions, branched off `main` (v3.0.0).

## Codegen fixes (`scripts/generate.ts`)

`tsType` was collapsing **every** array to `string[]`/`number[]` and **every** object to `Record<string, unknown>`, ignoring the declared element/property shapes in the spec.

1. **Array-of-object & object params render their real shape.** Bulk params — storage `deposit`/`withdraw`/`jettison` `items`, market `create_buy_order`/`create_sell_order`/`modify_order` `orders`, transfer `offer_items`/`request_items`, mission `objectives` — are arrays of `{ item_id, quantity, ... }` objects in the spec but were generated as `string[]`, forcing `as unknown as string[]` casts in consumers. `OpenAPIProperty` is now recursive and `tsType` descends into array items and object properties, emitting inline object types with correct optionality and nested enums. Shapeless object arrays (`craft`/`recycle` `jobs`, whose spec `items` declare no properties) correctly stay `Record<string, unknown>[]`.

2. **Array-of-enum elements are parenthesized.** The recursion first emitted `types?: "chat" | "combat" | "system"[]` — postfix `[]` binds tighter than `|`, so TS parsed that as `"chat" | Array<"system">` (valid syntax, wrong type, invisible to `tsc`). Enum element unions are now wrapped: `("chat" | ... | "system")[]`. Only `spacemolt/get_notifications.types` hits this.

Regenerated `commands.gen.ts` / `actions.gen.ts` / `COMMANDS.md` are included. `tests/generated.test.ts` gains assertions pinning the object-array and enum-array shapes.

## Other commits on this branch (v3 reconciliation)

- `feat: expose Account.id` — the managed store key / username.
- `fix: connectIds tolerates a per-account connect failure` — one bad/blocked account no longer aborts the whole fleet connect; it's skipped with a warning. Test adapted to the v3 harness (`failToOpen` + `connectRetry: false`).
- `chore: add prepare script` — installs build `dist/` automatically.

## Verification

- `bun test` — **75 pass / 0 fail**
- `bun x tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit` — clean (shipped code)
- `bun run build` — dist rebuilt with the new types

(The 5 pre-existing `tsc` errors in the untracked `examples/play.ts` are unrelated — out-of-date example against v3, excluded from the build tsconfig.)

author: cozy-corner
body:
Closes #44

## 何を変えたか

ETL スパイク（`scripts/etl-spike/`）を **標準 ETL 形**に寄せた。属性を発見時に**一度だけ**抽出して `raw-*.json` に永続化し、外国人剪定・養子分離を **WDQS 再訪ゼロ**のローカル変換にする。

**トポロジ（辺の存在）は truthy `wdt:` のまま不変**。reified `p:/ps:/pq:` は「属性付与」と「重複クエリの統合」だけに使う（＝挙動保存リファクタ。truthy を reified で再現し直すような再設計はしない）。

### E（抽出・一度だけ）
- `raw.ts` — 生スキーマ（`RawNode`: sex/nationality、`RawParentEdge`: 両端 rank・P1039・P1480、`RawEdge`: 養子）
- `attrs.ts` — **ノード属性スイープ**（旧 label / P21(add-sex) / P27(traverse・filter-foreign) の3スイープ→1つ）、**reified 親辺スイープ**（旧 `fetch.ts` EXCLUDE_ADOPTIVE ＋ `fetch-adoptions.ts` の2パス→1つ、`wikibase:rank` は UNION 各ブランチ内）、**養子スイープ**（P1038 ＋ P22/P25/P40）
- `fetch.ts` / `traverse.ts` — 全属性を raw へ。traverse のフロンティア判定は raw 国籍からローカル計算（P27 sweep 廃止）

### T（変換・ローカル・WDQS ゼロ）
- `transform.ts` — 外国人剪定（broad ルール）＋養子分離を1つのローカルパスで。**旧 `filter-foreign.ts` ＋ `fetch-adoptions.ts` を統合・置換**

### L
- `load.ts` — `sex` を raw から SET（**`add-sex.ts` 廃止**）

削除: `add-sex.ts` / `filter-foreign.ts` / `fetch-adoptions.ts`。

## 検証

- **seed parity ガード**（`parity-seed.ts`、新規・再利用可能）: 種近傍で新旧の load 入力を突合 → **完全一致**
  - kept nodes 137 / PARENT_OF spine 129 / ADOPTIVE_PARENT_OF 8（P1038 含む）/ sex 137
- **reified 属性取得を実データで確認**: 140 辺すべてに rank、P1039・P1480 も取得（#43/presumed の土台が機能）
- `tsc` / `eslint` green

## 意図的な挙動差（養子を整合的に扱う）

旧実装は fetch と traverse で養子の扱いが**非対称**だった。本 PR で整合化:

1. **traverse 由来の養子辺**も spine から除外し `ADOPTIVE_PARENT_OF` のみに（旧: fetch 由来のみ除外、traverse 由来は spine に漏出）
2. **養子だけが唯一の家族リンクのノード**を `:Person` に含め、その養子辺も保持（旧: 丸ごと drop）

実データ影響はほぼ皆無だが、いずれもノード membership を変えうるため明記。`parity-seed.ts` は固定ノード集合上のデータパス等価性を証明するもので、この membership 差は非対象（ヘッダに明記）。

## スコープ外（issue の非スコープ通り）

- **#43**（deprecated 父辺の除去そのもの）: raw が両端 rank を持つので後続のローカル変換で対応
- **P1480 presumed 抑制**: raw に捕捉するのみ、抑制ポリシーは将来

## self-review 対応

`/code-review medium` を実施。適用: 重複ヘルパ統合（`chunk`/`sparqlValues`）、古い参照修正、`role` を非 deprecated 文のみから採取。却下（理由付き）: ノード属性の OPTIONAL 統合（cross-product 爆発回避）、reified 2スイープ統合（spike・キャッシュ済・リスク>便益で PR6 送り）、raw 辺属性の削除（issue が明示的に要求する #43 の土台）、sex 多重 P21 の非決定性（旧 add-sex から不変・pre-existing）。

author: g-varhan
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: Image operations (`RemoveImage`, `PullImage`, `InspectImage`) in `pane-api/panespec/images.go` used user-supplied input to construct file paths. While `/` and `:` were replaced, inputs like `.`, `..`, or `""` bypassed this, allowing path traversal. Specifically, `RemoveImage("..")` would delete the entire parent directory (`/var/lib/pane`) via `os.RemoveAll`.
🎯 Impact: Arbitrary file and directory deletion, leading to catastrophic system data loss and denial of service.
🔧 Fix: Introduced `validateImageName` to explicitly reject empty strings, `.`, and `..`. Added regression tests to ensure robust validation.
✅ Verification: Ran `go test ./...` successfully. Verified the fix in tests providing traversal strings.

author: nivintw
body:
## Why

A `/dev-kit:template-reconcile` audit against `gh:nivintw/copier-everything` at the pinned `v1.4.0` (template rendered with copier from the repo's recorded answers, then byte-diffed) found **zero missing template infra** — but 15 intentionally divergent template-owned files and 2 deliberately deleted placeholder tests, none documented anywhere. Every `copier update` conflict on those files has required re-deriving which differences are intentional; that archaeology is where deliberate customizations get accidentally reverted.

## What

- **`tests/template-divergences.txt`** — the registry: one line per intentional divergence with its reason (e.g. the pre-push vm-smoke stage in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, the installer jobs in `ci.yml`, release-please-owned files), plus `deleted:` entries for the superseded placeholder tests. Documentation sits below the entries because hawkeye rewrites a leading comment block as the license header.
- **`tests/template_sync.bats`** — two cases:
  1. Renders the template at the pinned `_commit` with the repo's own answers (`uvx copier copy --force --defaults --trust --skip-tasks`), walks the rendered tree, and fails on any file differing from the repo without a registry entry. The candidate set is derived from the render — nothing hand-curated, so a template release adding or dropping files is picked up automatically after `copier update` bumps `_commit`. Skips cleanly offline; CI always has network, so drift can't pass the gate.
  2. A network-free registry-hygiene check: an entry pointing at a nonexistent file must carry a `deleted:` reason, so the registry can't rot into stale documentation.

## Verification

- `bats tests/template_sync.bats` — 2/2 pass against the current tree (the registry exactly covers today's divergences; 22 files verified byte-identical to the rendered template).
- `prek` clean on the new files; full pytest suite unaffected (414 passed).

Closes #125

Integrated a comprehensive code execution system into the Hypenosys Neural Chat environment. 

Key features:
1. **Python & Javascript Runners:** Added a frontend bridge that hooks into `marked.js` to inject execution buttons on Python and JS code blocks. These buttons trigger a confirmation modal where users can inspect code, provide CLI arguments or stdin, and execute the script in a sandboxed Docker environment via n8n.
2. **AI REPL Mode:** A new "Runners" mode in the chat interface allows users to provide natural language instructions. The AI generates the corresponding Python or Javascript code and automatically opens the execution workflow.
3. **Enhanced Configuration:** Updated the Repo Admin Settings and AI Configuration modal to manage new runner endpoints, the n8n base URL, and an optional Embedding Model per profile.
4. **Robust Security:** Execution is restricted to isolated containers with no network access and hard resource limits. Code integrity is maintained by executing snippets byte-for-byte as retrieved from SVN or AI.
5. **UI/UX Polishing:** Fixed bugs in settings loading and markdown rendering to ensure a smooth, persistent experience across sessions.
