author: briankeegan1
body:
## What

Watcher flexibility for long-pending deps. Builds on the shipped dispatch/deps schema (`herd depend`/`deps` + `.herd/deps` + `dep-watcher.sh`) so a slow enterprise upstream is a **status line, never a workspace freeze**.

### `scripts/herd/dep-watcher.sh`
- **Richer dep STATES** derived from the upstream PR/issue's live state: `open | in-progress | in-review | stalled | closed`. New pure `_dw_derive_state` maps raw upstream state + pending-age onto the surfaced state.
- **STALLED + TTL**: a dep still open/in-progress/in-review with no upstream movement past `DEP_STALE_TTL` (default 86400s, `0` disables) surfaces as `stalled` — warned loudly but **still polled** (never auto-unblocks, never freezes).
- **Capped exponential backoff** factored into pure `_dw_next_interval`: while every open dep sits unchanged the poll interval doubles (capped at `DEP_POLL_MAX`) so a long-pending dep is polled less aggressively over time; any change resets to `DEP_POLL_MIN`.
- Each tick writes a `<ref> <state> <age>` console-surface file (`<lock-stem>.states`) for the watcher console to read.

### `scripts/herd/agent-watch.sh`
- New **"blocked on"** console section (`build_blocked`) painting one status row per live dep; `stalled` is the only loud (red) row. Absent/stale file → no section. Purely informational — never gates a merge.

### `tests/test-dep-states.sh` (hermetic)
A dep transitions through states from a **stubbed upstream state**; a stalled dep is surfaced; backoff **widens and caps** the poll interval; `build_blocked` renders the surface.

## Notes
- TTL/backoff use hardcoded defaults with a code comment noting the follow-up `capabilities.tsv` config key (that file is owned by another builder this cycle and is left untouched here).
- Healthcheck: **CLEAN** (hermetic suite pass, tab-leak-guard clean, caps-sync clean).
- Scope limited to `dep-watcher.sh` + `agent-watch.sh` + the new test; none of the excluded files touched.

## TL;DR Clean up the @generaltranslation/react-core public API surface for the next major by removing dead helpers and internal plumbing from public entrypoints. ## Code Changes - Removed the dead react-core dictionary utility exports, modules, and tests. - Stopped exporting JSX serialization internals from @generaltranslation/react-core/pure while keeping the internals available to react-core modules. - Removed the requested singleton/plumbing exports and useShouldTranslate from public react-core entrypoints. - Kept only internalInitializeGTSRA in react-core /pure and aliases it locally as initializeGT in gt-react RSC. - Repointed gt-next type consumers of removed react-core legacy types to local equivalents. ## Notes / Flags - Downstream grep found gt-next consumers of RenderMethod, CustomLoader, and _Messages from @generaltranslation/react-core/pure; those were repointed locally instead of keeping the react-core exports. - components-rsc still exports getPluralBranch, but now sources it directly from the module file instead of ./pure. - Sibling PRs touch packages/react/src/index.rsc.ts and react-core hooks.ts/pure.ts; trivial merge conflicts are expected.

Greptile Summary

Cleans up the `@generaltranslation/react-core` public API surface by deleting dead dictionary utilities (source files, tests, and exports), removing JSX serialization internals and singleton-plumbing exports from `/pure`, and dropping `useShouldTranslate` from the hooks entrypoint. Downstream consumers in `gt-next` and `gt-react` are updated to local type equivalents or direct module aliases. - **`react-core/pure.ts`**: Removes ~17 exports (dictionary helpers, `initializeGT` alias, `setI18nConfig`, `setReadonlyConditionStore`, `WritableConditionStore`, `DictionaryLookup`, `TranslateLookup`, and several types); retains only the minimal surface needed by sibling packages. - **`gt-react`**: Re-aliases `internalInitializeGTSRA as initializeGT` in its own RSC entrypoint so the public API is unchanged for consumers. - **`gt-next`**: Replaces the now-removed `_Messages`, `RenderMethod`, and `CustomLoader` imports from `react-core/pure` with structurally identical local type definitions.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 The code changes themselves are safe — all internal callers were verified and the migrated types are structurally identical to the removed originals. The only concern is the changeset version type, which is a process issue rather than a runtime one. All type migrations check out, no internal react-core module still imports from the deleted dictionary source files, and the `initializeGT` alias is correctly re-created in gt-react. The single flag is the changeset marking multiple public API removals as `patch`; depending on the team's pre-release exit strategy this could produce an incorrect final version bump. `.changeset/clean-react-core-api-surface.md` — the version bump type warrants a second look before the pre-release is finalized.

Important Files Changed

author: calcooper
body:
# Learn tab revamp, phase 1

One PR, stacked commits: structure first, then each learning path lands as its content is approved. Restructures docs.vendasta.com/learn from a flat course pile into sequenced learning paths that tell the AI Workforce story, plus product libraries organized by the customer lifecycle. Every old URL redirects; no content is deleted.

## What this does

**Structure (commits 1-7):**
- The sidebar pill is now **DOCUMENTATION / LEARN** (was TRAINING)
- New Learn home with path cards and two libraries
- All lesson files renamed to kebab-case; 61 client-redirect entries + 2 nginx server-side redirects preserve every old URL
- Near-duplicate lessons parked in `docusaurus/training-retired/` (outside the plugin path, not built)
- /learn pages indexed by site search; training content joins the article-freshness review rotation

**Content (subsequent commits, one path at a time):**
- **Get started** (6 steps, complete): steps 1+2 merged into The Vendasta Platform, get-set-up-to-get-paid and growth-engine written, growth engine promoted to its own path. New lesson component system: LessonHeader, LessonFooter, PathRoadmap, redesigned FlipCard
- **AI foundations** (6 steps + 3 SVG diagrams, complete): how AI Employees actually work — models, knowledge, capabilities, tools, and automations. Six critique rounds; every claim verified against partner and Business App docs
- **Hire your AI Workforce** (restructured 10 planned steps to 7; step 1 written): compliance, roster-growth, and first-customer material folds into neighboring steps; the four retired receptionist lessons consolidate into put-a-receptionist-to-work
- **Your growth engine / Build with Vibe / The builder track**: scaffolded stubs so the build-out plan is visible in the repo; content lands on this PR path by path
- **Library-wide voice sweeps**: you-voice, no activity markers, no community mentions, platform-scope rule

**The working system:**
- `.claude/skills/learning-path-writing/SKILL.md` — ~38 editorial rules earned line by line through critique; loads automatically in Claude Code when learning path content is touched
- `learn-revamp/` — implementation plan with execution log, IA spec, partner-call evidence, lesson outlines, per-lesson review records, and the handoff doc for the remaining build-out

## Why

Partner call analysis (14 calls) and a full repo/content recon showed the Learn tab still teaches the 2023 platform story while the website sells the AI Workforce. The IA spec and evidence base now live in this repo under `learn-revamp/`.

## Verification

- `npm run build` green; zero broken links or anchors touching /learn or training content
- All seven AI Workforce steps, six Vibe stubs, and seven builder stubs render; retired receptionist URLs redirect to put-a-receptionist-to-work (spot-checked in the build output)
- Redirect spot-checks pass, case-sensitive
- Pre-existing on master and untouched: 2 typecheck errors (Root.tsx, TOC) and broken links in main docs

## What reviewers should look at

1. Click through the preview build: `/learn` home, the Get started and AI foundations paths end to end, the AI Workforce roadmap
2. Skim the redirect block in `docusaurus.config.ts` (comment-fenced section) and `nginx.conf`
3. Read one AI foundations step against `.claude/skills/learning-path-writing/SKILL.md` — the rules are the review checklist

Remaining paths (growth engine, Vibe, AI Workforce steps 2-7, builder track) land as stacked commits on this PR after per-path approval, per `learn-revamp/HANDOFF.md`.

author: jmilne22
body:
Stacked on #101 (merge that first; this retargets to main automatically).

The two features from the second research pass — the only ones that survived the evidence review:

## Self-explanation prompt
After the solution reveals, the rating buttons stay locked until you write one or two sentences answering "why does this solution work?" (or click skip). Meta-analysis across 64 studies puts self-explanation prompts at g = 0.55 — the best evidence-per-effort ratio available. Explanations persist in localStorage per exercise.

## Calibration tracking (test-backed challenges only)
Cards with a practice workspace ask "will your code pass `go test`?" before you run it, and "what did it say?" after. The card shows a running hit rate — *when confident: 8/12 pass*. Self-assessment accuracy is reliably poor and corrupts study decisions; outcome-vs-judgment feedback is how it improves. All localStorage, delegated listeners (survives shuffle/easier/harder re-renders), no backend.

## Module 0
Documents both features + one working-with-AI rule: AI explains and reviews, never writes milestone code (per the 2024–25 overreliance findings).

## Verification
- `node --check` on both JS files, `node validate.js`, full build green
- dist ships the new renderer/progress/css
- Manual check: open a module 4 challenge → reveal solution → rating locked until text/skip; calibration widget cycles predict → record → stats

author: bushidocodes
body:
## What

A full-width rule line on the **bottom row** of a panel (e.g. the ISPF Primary Option Menu's closing rule) fills through the very last buffer cell. The RA (Repeat to Address) order emitted for it used a stop address of `cols*rows` — **1920** on a 24×80 screen — which is one past the last valid address (1919).

The 3270 buffer is circular: a run that fills through the last cell stops at address **0**, not one-past-the-end. This PR takes the RA stop address modulo the buffer size, and threads the screen `depth` into `Text.render` so the alternate (model-3/4/5) presentation space wraps against its own larger buffer too.

## Why it wasn't caught

`ws3270`/`wc3270` **v4.4** rejects the stray address and refuses to paint the screen:

```
Host write error:
RA address 1920 > maximum 1919
```

`s3270` **v4.1** (what CI installs via apt) and ws3270 v4.4 share `Common/ctlr.c`, and **both detect the out-of-range address and abort the write** — neither actually draws the RA. The difference is only how *visible* the abort is:

- v4.1's `ABORT_WRITE` macro is **trace-only** (`trace_ds(...)`, no popup); with `-trace` off the abort is completely silent.
- v4.4 hardened the same check to call `popup_an_error("Host write error: RA address %d > maximum %d", ...)`, which surfaces to the scripting layer.

Because the offending RA is the panel's **last** order (the bottom rule), v4.1's silent abort still left everything the assertions check already on screen — so the two smoke tests that navigate *through* the menu (`test_ws3270_model_3_browse_uses_the_alternate_screen`, `test_ws3270_invalid_option_keeps_typed_input`) passed on CI while the rule line was **silently never drawn**. Under v4.4 the popup makes the follow-up read fail, which is what surfaced the bug locally.

## Verification

- The ISPF menu now emits `RA` stop **0** instead of **1920** (in range for its 1919-max buffer).
- Two regression tests added: bottom-row rule wraps to 0 on both a 24×80 primary screen and a 32×80 alternate screen.
- Golden byte-identity tests (`load_panel(x).render() == build_x().render()`) still pass — both paths share `Text.render`.
- Full suite green against the real emulator (ws3270 v4.4): `474 passed`.

body:
## What (updated — now two related features)

### 1. Day schedule
Family members and the coordinator can build a day/week schedule for the person they support — once-off items or weekly-recurring ones. The recipient (plus family/coordinator) sees a colourful timeline: a live "Happening now" / "Up next" banner, per-item notes scoped to that specific date, and a done/not-done checkmark per occurrence.

### 2. Visual countdown timer (recipient-only)
A Time Timer-style tool: drag the dial or pick a duration, and a coloured wedge visibly shrinks as time passes — concrete and intuitive rather than a number ticking down. Chime + vibration + pulsing glow on completion. Integrates with the schedule: the "up next" banner and the current item's card show the same shrinking disk, and any item gets a one-tap "Start a timer for this".

**Background alerts**: opting in lets the alert reach the recipient even if the app is backgrounded, via a new `timer_alerts` table + pg_cron job + `timer-alert-notify` edge function. This required implementing real Web Push payload encryption (RFC 8291 aes128gcm + RFC 8292 VAPID) in a new shared module, since the existing `push-notify` function only ever sent bare pings with generic notification text — left that working path untouched to avoid regressing it.

## Database — action required before merging (same as before)

Three new tables from the schedule feature, plus `timer_alerts` from the timer feature — all in `supabase/migrations/033_schedule.sql` and `034_timer_alerts.sql`. Run both manually (SQL Editor or `supabase db push`); I don't have direct database access from this environment.

**Additional one-time step for 034**: pg_cron needs the service_role key to call the edge function. Rather than repeating the mistake in `017_push_notify_trigger.sql` (hardcoded key in a migration), 034 reads it from Supabase Vault instead. Run once in the SQL Editor with your real key:
```sql
select vault.create_secret('<your-service-role-key>', 'service_role_key');
```
Also requires the `pg_cron` and `pg_net` extensions to be available on your Supabase plan.

**Known blocker**: as of this writing, applying 033 hit a Supabase platform incident (schema cache not picking up new tables after `NOTIFY pgrst`/dashboard reload) — see https://status.supabase.com. If still unresolved, 034 will likely hit the same issue.

## Testing

- `tsc && vite build` passes clean on every commit.
- Could not click through live — no Supabase credentials/CLI in this sandbox, and didn't want to test destructively against production. The Web Push encryption code was hand-verified against RFC 8291/8188 but not exercised end-to-end against a real push service; recommend a manual test (subscribe on a device, start a timer with background alert, background the app) once deployed.

author: nallenscott
body:
Replaces the single `undertow_on_drain` handler with named sinks via `undertow_sink(name, max_batch_size: nil, &handler)`. A model can now register more than one, e.g. a search index reindex and a Kafka publish, and each gets called independently with the same `(model_name, upserted_ids, deleted_ids)`.

Pop size stays `Undertow.configuration.max_batch`, unrelated to any sink, so one sink's tighter downstream limit never throttles another sink's batch. A sink that does specify a smaller `max_batch_size` just gets its own block called multiple times, chunked to that size, via a small `each_sink_chunk` helper in `DrainJob`. `drain.undertow` now fires once per chunk per sink, tagged with `sink:`; if any sink raises, the whole popped batch restores and everything retries next tick (including sinks that already succeeded), same whole-batch semantics as before, with `error.undertow` now tagged with whichever sink raised.

Breaking, no shim, same as the earlier `ids` → `upserted_ids` rename. Migration documented in `UPGRADING.md`.

author: basilsuhail
body:
Closes #304. Part of #282.

## What

`make baselines` gains a head-to-head table on **common support**: eval-window rows where the composite has a value (2,239 at k=1 — 18% coverage after the #303 backfill), with B0–B2 recomputed on identical rows. Coverage share stated in the report so partial coverage can't masquerade as the full claim.

## The result (k=1, common support)

| contender | AUROC | AUPR | Brier |
|---|---|---|---|
| B0 random | 0.487 | 0.508 | 0.341 |
| B1 persistence | 0.844 | 0.833 | 0.156 |
| **B2 base rate** | **0.900** | **0.911** | **0.136** |
| **B6 composite v1.0** | **0.493** | 0.518 | 0.262 |

**The composite is a coin flip.** Same story at k=3 and k=6.

## Why this is the right kind of bad news

The current ground truth is P1–P3 — **geopolitical only**. This composite carries **market + hazard** signals (geopolitical domain still pending). So what was actually measured is: *do equity drawdowns and earthquakes predict armed conflict?* Answer: no — which is reassuring rather than damning, and it sharpens the roadmap:

1. **Geopolitical signal backfill** (GDELT bulk) — give the composite the domain the labels test
2. **P4/P5 labels** (market crises, hazard disruptions) — give the market/hazard signals the truth they're supposed to predict

Both were already planned; this number makes them the priority. A pre-registered protocol that surfaces a clean negative before the test window was ever touched is the methodology working as designed.

## Tests

score_composite unit tests (NaN/None skip); full suite 610 passed. Ruff clean.

author: artyhoo
body:
## What

The `npm-eslint-declarative` capability-matrix carried a hand-written `evidence.toolchain` eslint version (`"9.39.4"`) that **no mechanism** checked against the eslint that actually resolves. This is the stale-version-string MINOR flagged in the MT 3b PR-1 review, addressed as an executable gate rather than a re-read.

Verified **under vitest** (not just raw node) that `packages/core` resolves eslint **10.4.0** — it declares `^10.4.0` (since #460); the root-hoisted 9.39.4 comes from `preset-react-spa` (`^9.0.0`) and does **not** satisfy core's range, so npm nests 10.4.0 under core (deterministic under `npm ci`, identical in CI). The committed `"9.39.4"` + `nodeType` diagnostic was **mislabeled at birth**: `nodeType` is an eslint-9-only shape (eslint 10 emits none), i.e. a 9.x capture that never actually fired here.

## Changes (2 files, scope-clean)

- `capability-matrix.test.ts`: pure `checkToolchainFreshness(matrix, resolvedVersion)` + `parseEslintVersion`. **No version literal in the test** — the resolving eslint is derived at runtime via `createRequire(import.meta.url)`, the same bare-`eslint` resolution `firing-runner.ts` uses, so the gate cannot itself rot. Paired negatives: **N8** (stale version → violation), **N9** (toolchain stops naming eslint → violation).
- `capability-matrix.json`: regenerate the `syntax` cell evidence honestly against eslint 10.4.0 (drops the eslint-9-only `nodeType`; `date` → 2026-07-04).

Bumping eslint later turns the gate **RED** until the live-fired evidence is regenerated — the version string is no longer trusted on attention.

## Verify-trace

- RED-first: gate fails on the old 9.39.4 evidence → `cell "syntax": evidence.toolchain claims eslint 9.39.4, but the resolving eslint is 10.4.0`.
- GREEN after evidence correction: `backends/npm/capability-matrix.test.ts` → 13 passed.
- Gates: backends 63/63 (pre-push), typecheck clean, principles 282/282.
- Independent cold review (adversarial, own probes): **GO** — confirmed 10.4.0 resolution + honest diagnostic + discriminating negatives.

## §1.7 self-reflexive check

**Forward-check:** complies with `no-paid-llm-in-ci.md` (gate is deterministic vitest, zero API calls); `attention-is-not-a-mechanism.md §1` (replaces a hand-written version string with a runtime-derived error-gate — the exact promotion this rule prescribes); `build-first-reuse-default.md` (no new capability — hardens an existing honesty test, REUSE of eslint's own resolution, `capability-matrix.test.ts:137`); `dual-implementation-discipline.md §2(iv)` (TypeScript test under `packages/`, not a delivery-channel artefact — non-trigger).

**Backward-check:** class of change = *evidence-freshness enforcement for a live-fired capability cell*. Sibling surface: the cargo backend's `backends/cargo/capability-matrix.test.ts` carries the same mechanized-honesty contract but its toolchain is an external `cargo`/`clippy` invocation (not an in-process resolvable module), so a `createRequire`-style freshness gate does not transfer 1:1 — SWEPT, no parallel gap introduced here (the cargo toolchain-freshness question is out of this PR's scope; noted for the maintainer). No other cell in the npm matrix carries live-fired evidence (`type-aware`/`dep-graph` are `no`).

## Observation (out of scope — not fixed here)

Monorepo eslint version-skew: `packages/core` → `^10.4.0`, `preset-react-spa` → `^9.0.0` (root hoist 9.39.4). Pre-existing (since #460), unrelated to this hardening. Flagged for maintainer decision; not resolved drive-by.

author: averagejoematt
body:
## What & why

CI's `cdk diff --all` compares the CDK app to the deployed **template** — it is blind to drift that happens **out of band**: a resource edited in the console, a stack resource deleted, a Lambda config hand-mutated, a bucket policy loosened. This adds a read-only **weekly** sweep that a human never has to remember to run, and lands its findings in the remediation agent's existing curated report.

Closes the gap cited in the issue: `.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml` runs `npx cdk diff --all` (template-only), and there was no active `detect-stack-drift` usage anywhere in the repo.

## How it maps to the acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — CFN drift across all 8 stacks.** `deploy/drift_sentinel.py::check_cfn_drift` runs `detect_stack_drift` per stack, polls to completion, and reports every `MODIFIED`/`DELETED` resource via `describe_stack_resource_drifts`. (Web stack handled in us-east-1.)
- **AC2 — reuse the human-invoked checks + no-functions-outside-IaC.** Reuses `session_postflight`'s layer-uniformity / config-drift / asset-completeness checks, and re-asserts the invariant by diffing live `list_functions` against the authoritative set from `cloudformation:ListStackResources` (minus a small CDK-toolkit allowlist).
- **AC3 — delete-protection intact.** Verifies the live bucket policy still `Deny`s `s3:DeleteObject` on every protected prefix (`raw/*`, `config/*`, `uploads/*`, …) against the source of truth `deploy/bucket_policy.json`.
- **AC4 — lands in the curated report; loud clean.** Findings write to `s3://…/drift-log/{latest,<date>}.json` (mirrors the Coherence Sentinel's `coherence-log`). `remediation/drift_report.py` (shared by both email paths) surfaces real drift as a **needs-human** signal and renders a status line on **every** report — a clean week reports explicitly clean, never silence.
- **AC5 — no new always-on infra.** Runs as a **Monday-gated step in the existing** remediation workflow, under the remediation role's read-only access. CloudFormation drift-detection API calls are free.

## Files

- `deploy/drift_sentinel.py` (new) — the read-only sweep + S3 persistence + stdout summary
- `remediation/drift_report.py` (new) — the report seam (`as_signal` + `status_html`)
- `remediation/agent.py`, `remediation/automerge.py` — ingest the drift signal + render the status line on both email paths
- `.github/workflows/remediation-agent.yml` — the Monday-gated, non-gating drift step, before the agent
- `deploy/setup_remediation_role.sh` — CFN drift APIs + `s3:GetBucketPolicy` + `drift-log/*` write (⚠️ **operator-run IAM** — see below)
- `tests/test_drift_sentinel.py` (new) — 12 hermetic tests (bucket-policy clean/drift/missing/error, sweep aggregation, orphan allowlist, report seam)

## Deploy note (not self-deployed)

The drift step runs under `github-actions-remediation-role`, which needs the new permissions before the step can succeed. That IAM change is operator-run:

```bash
bash deploy/setup_remediation_role.sh
```

Until it's applied, the step is **non-gating** (`continue-on-error`) and each check fail-soft — so the workflow stays green and the drift record simply reports the checks it couldn't run as `degraded`.

## Verification (local)

- `tests/test_drift_sentinel.py` — 12 passed (fake-cred hermetic)
- `black --check` + `ruff check` clean on the in-scope files (`deploy/`, `tests/`)
- workflow YAML valid; drift step verified to precede the agent step
- both heredoc IAM JSON blocks parse; full suite collects (2613 tests)

author: leejmorel
body:
## Problem

A fresh install that follows the documented least-privilege path (`DATABASE_URL` = `app_provisioner`) fails on modern Postgres — twice:

1. **Postgres 15+** made `CREATE` on the `public` schema owner-only. The baseline migration, running as `app_provisioner`, creates `alembic_version` and the shared tables there, and also runs `COMMENT ON SCHEMA public` (which requires ownership). First failure: `permission denied for schema public`.
2. **Postgres 16+** allows only BYPASSRLS holders to create — or even *name in `ALTER ROLE`* — the BYPASSRLS attribute, and `app_provisioner` is deliberately `NOBYPASSRLS`. Second failure: `permission denied to create role` … `Only roles with the BYPASSRLS attribute may create roles with the BYPASSRLS attribute` on `CREATE ROLE app_admin WITH LOGIN BYPASSRLS`.

Installs whose `DATABASE_URL` is still a superuser mask both, which is why existing deployments and CI never hit this. Found deploying the initiative_infra Helm chart against a fresh Postgres 17.

## Changes

- **`docker-compose.example.yml` (initdb config)** — everything that needs superuser now happens once, at first volume init: hand the `public` schema to `app_provisioner`, and pre-create `app_user`/`app_admin` with their env passwords plus `WITH ADMIN OPTION` grants to the provisioner so it can keep syncing passwords.
- **Baseline migration** — the exists-path `ALTER ROLE app_admin` only names `BYPASSRLS` when the attribute is actually missing (naming it at all requires holding it on PG16+); new `_role_bypassrls()` helper. The create-path is unchanged (still works under a superuser `DATABASE_URL`; under the provisioner the role now always pre-exists via initdb).
- **`backend/scripts/create-provisioner.sql`** — same `public`-schema ownership handover for existing installs (step 2b), so future provisioner-run migrations can create shared tables.
- **CHANGELOG** — entry under `[Unreleased]` → Fixed.

No schema changes to app data; env vars unchanged (the initdb config reuses the existing `APP_USER_PASSWORD`/`APP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` interpolations).

## Testing

Exercised via the initiative_infra Helm chart on kind (fresh Postgres 17 volume, image built from this branch):

```
docker build -t initiative:dev-fix .
kind load docker-image initiative:dev-fix --name initiative
helm upgrade --install initiative charts/initiative -n initiative -f values/public.yaml \
  --set image.repository=initiative --set image.tag=dev-fix --set image.pullPolicy=Never --wait
```

- Baseline + guild-template provisioning complete under `app_provisioner` (no superuser in any `DATABASE_URL`); `Application startup complete`.
- Registered first user (owner), created a guild (`guild_<id>` schema provisioned), uploaded a file through the S3 backend, verified authorized download (200) and unauthorized download (401).
- Before the fix, the same fresh install reproduced both failures in order.
